dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels for families in Sobha Hartland and the central corridor. Each works from the student's own marked papers and reports which component is losing marks rather than giving a general impression.

intro.heading: Cost the course by component, because that is how the grade is built
paragraphs: Diploma maths is not a single thing a tutor can be good at. It is a set of named components with published weightings, and a student losing marks in one of them is not helped by hours spent on another. At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 40% each and the internal exploration carries 20%. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 30% each, the shorter Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration carries 20%. Those numbers are the spending plan, if anyone bothers to use them.

Almost nobody does. The standard approach in this market is to sell hours and let the content sort itself out, which works when a student's weakness happens to coincide with what the tutor likes teaching and wastes money when it does not. A Sobha Hartland family paying a specialist rate for general revision while their child's actual losses sit in Paper 1's non-calculator algebra is buying attention rather than improvement.

The market rates themselves are worth stating plainly, since most competitor pages will not. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with budget online tutors advertised from about AED 33 to 65 and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 because the figure includes travel. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and they are market context rather than IB Gram's price list.

What this page adds is the second half of the calculation. Given those rates, which component should the money go to, how many hours does each realistically need, and how would you know within six weeks whether it worked? Those questions have answers, and the answers differ for a Standard Level student with a weak exploration and a Higher Level student who cannot touch Paper 3. Treating them as the same problem is how a family spends a year's fees on tutoring and watches a 5 stay a 5.

IB Gram delivers Diploma maths tuition to Sobha Hartland as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the course and level rather than to the postcode. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and that is also why no travel premium sits inside our pricing. The sections below cost the course component by component, name the three purchases that never pay back, and give you the verification test to apply at six weeks. Nothing here promises a grade; it gives you an order to spend in and a way to check the spending, which is more useful than a promise.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.programmesIntro: The component argument applies differently at each stage, because the assessment structure changes. These are the three contexts that matter for a Sobha Hartland maths decision, and each has a distinct answer to the question of what is worth funding.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, one of two maths courses, and a published component structure that makes spending decisions tractable. Standard Level sits two papers at 40% each plus a 20% exploration. Higher Level sits three papers, at 30%, 30% and 20%, plus the same 20% exploration. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator in Analysis and Approaches, which is the structural fact that most often decides where a student's marks are going missing.
programmes.countryNote: Near Sobha Hartland, Diploma maths is taught at several schools within a short drive, and the course combinations offered differ. Some timetable both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels; others offer less. That constrains choice before a tutor is involved, so the first question in a Hartland consultation is what the school actually runs.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with no examination papers, which is exactly why the component argument matters at the transition. A student can earn a 7 in MYP Mathematics on strong investigations and then meet a non-calculator paper they have never sat. The cheapest maths tutoring a Diploma family buys is a short block before DP1 that secures algebraic speed, because speed is examinable and MYP does not test it.
programmes.countryNote: Several central-corridor schools run MYP and then offer both the Diploma and A Levels. For a Hartland family the useful spend at this point is one session testing readiness for Higher Level rather than a term of general support, because the Higher Level misplacement is the single most expensive error available in Diploma maths.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.description: Individual Diploma subjects taken for certificates rather than the full Diploma. In maths this arises when a student needs Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level for an engineering or economics application but cannot carry Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay alongside. The components, the weightings and the exploration are identical, so the costing on this page applies unchanged.
programmes.countryNote: Business Bay and Hartland see a steady flow of mid-year arrivals, which is where the certificate route most often comes up. What a certificate carries for Ministry of Education equivalency is a question for the ministry's attestation channel rather than for a tutoring service, and we point parents there rather than guessing.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.subjectsIntro: Maths is the subject here, and the component logic generalises. These are the courses our tutors cover for Hartland families, each noted for the component where marks are actually lost, because that is what determines whether a session is worth a specialist rate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 without a calculator is where algebraic fluency is exposed and where most of the recoverable marks sit. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is a separate skill in extended problem solving and needs its own sessions rather than more Paper 2 practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, with calculator competence examinable. Losses concentrate in interpreting output the student can generate, and in Paper 3's extended investigation at Higher Level, which rewards a structured write-up.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where a maths weakness shows up second. Equation rearrangement and uncertainty treatment cost Physics marks that have nothing to do with physics, which means one maths block can be charged against two grades.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Logarithms in pH work and rearrangement in equilibrium problems are maths problems in chemical dress. Worth checking before booking two separate tutors, because one underlying fix often serves both subjects.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries real quantitative work and the internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles. Students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside it gain from shared statistics work rather than duplicated sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Discrete mathematics and algorithmic reasoning overlap with Analysis and Approaches content, so a student strong in one usually finds the other less alien than expected. Thinner coverage in the market, so book earlier.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A frequent pairing with Applications and Interpretation. The quantitative tools are modest and the evaluation marks are not, so a student applying a framework without weighing it sits mid-band regardless of arithmetic.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Included because the exploration is a written document worth 20% of the maths grade. A student who cannot justify a method in prose loses exploration marks that have nothing to do with their mathematics.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and essay land in the same term as the maths exploration for most students, which is a scheduling cost rather than a teaching one. Our support is structural: reading the title, building an argument, finding the marks.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Occasionally written in mathematics, which is harder than students expect because the research question must carry genuine mathematical content. One early session narrowing the question is the best value available here.

sections.heading: What Diploma maths tuition costs here, and how to check you are getting it
paragraphs: Start with the market, because most competitor pages refuse to. The table below gives the Dubai bands with the provider that published each figure and the month we read it, alongside the thing that matters more: the specific behaviour you should be able to observe at that price. These are market rates rather than IB Gram's prices, which follow a free trial lesson and a count of the sessions genuinely needed.

The behaviour column is the point. Price in this market tracks delivery model and claimed credentials, not teaching quality, because quality is not observable at the point of purchase. What is observable is what happens in a lesson. A tutor who explains the question the student is stuck on and moves to the next one is delivering the budget tier faithfully, whatever they charge. A tutor who arrives having read the marked mock, names the component where marks are going, and sets practice aimed at that component is delivering the specialist tier.

So the test is not whether a rate is reasonable but whether the behaviour matches the rate. A family paying AED 350 an hour for homework supervision is being overcharged regardless of the tutor's qualifications, and a family paying AED 60 an hour for competent content re-teaching after a fortnight of illness is getting a bargain. Read the table across rather than down, and use the right-hand column as a specification for what you are buying. If a tutor cannot deliver the behaviour in that row, the rate attached to the row is the wrong rate for them whatever their qualifications say.

sections.heading: Funding by component: where the hours actually pay back
paragraphs: Here is the calculation nobody in this market performs. Each maths component has a published weighting, a characteristic failure mode and a rough number of hours needed to shift it. Put those three together and you have a funding order that is defensible rather than intuitive, and it frequently contradicts what a worried parent would choose.

The highest return is the exploration, because 20% of the grade sits in a document the student controls entirely, and the difference between a mediocre and a strong exploration is often a topic choice made in one conversation. Three to five sessions, once, no repetition needed. The second highest is Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches, because no-calculator algebra is a mechanical skill that improves with drill and students never drill it voluntarily. The third is Paper 3 at Higher Level, 20% of the grade and a skill almost nobody has been taught.

The lowest return, and the thing most often bought, is general topic revision across the whole syllabus. It consumes the most hours, addresses no specific failure, and produces the feeling of progress without the evidence of it. If a tutor proposes going through the course from the start, ask which component that is aimed at. There is usually no answer, because the proposal is a plan for filling sessions rather than for recovering marks.

One qualification on the funding order. It assumes the student is in roughly the right course at roughly the right level, and when that assumption fails nothing else on the list applies. A student holding a 3 in Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is not short of Paper 3 strategy; they are in the wrong place, and the useful intervention is a conversation with the department rather than a block of sessions. A tutor who notices that and says so has saved you more than any amount of component-level work would have earned them.

sections.heading: The three purchases that never pay back in Diploma maths
paragraphs: Having named where the money works, here is where it does not. These three are so consistent that we will talk a Hartland family out of them, and losing the sale is the correct outcome in each case because the alternative is a parent concluding, reasonably, that tutoring does not work.

The first is open-ended revision of the whole course with no component named. It is the most commonly sold product in this market and the least accountable, because nothing in it can be shown to have worked or failed. It also consumes the budget that should have gone to the exploration and to Paper 1. If a proposal cannot name the component it targets, it is not a plan.

The second is a second weekly session in the same subject. A student already carrying six subjects, three core components and school homework does not have two hours a week of maths attention to give, and the second session typically becomes supervised homework at a specialist rate. One good session with practice between is better and cheaper. The third is Paper 3 work for a Standard Level student, which does not exist on their course, and its mirror image: a Higher Level student receiving no Paper 3 work at all because the tutor's experience is Standard Level. Both are matching failures and both are avoidable by naming the level in the first email.

What these three share is that none of them can be shown to have failed. An unbounded revision programme always has more syllabus to cover, a second weekly session always has homework to supervise, and a level mismatch is invisible until results. That is why they persist in a market where everyone means well. The protection is the same in each case: name the component before you buy, set a date to check it, and be willing to end the arrangement when the check comes back empty.

sections.heading: What Hartland specifically changes about the arithmetic
paragraphs: Most of this page would be true anywhere in Dubai. Three things are different about Sobha Hartland, and all three affect cost rather than content, which is why they belong on a cost-led page rather than in a description of the community.

The first is timing. Two schools sit inside the community, so a proportion of students are home before three o'clock without a car journey. That makes a genuine 4pm session possible, and an alert student at four is worth more per dirham than a tired one at six. It is the only local factor on this page that reduces cost directly, and families who have it should use it rather than defaulting to an evening slot.

The second is competition for slots. Hartland has a high concentration of Diploma families relative to its size, and the better local tutors are generally committed by October. A family asking in February is choosing from what is left, which is a quality cost rather than a price one. The third is the group alternative: Al Quoz and Downtown are both close, so a shared topic gap can be addressed in a group class far more cheaply than one-to-one. That only works when you can name the topic, which brings the argument back to diagnosis.

There is a fourth Hartland feature worth naming, which cuts the other way. Because the community is dense and the schools are close, recommendations circulate fast and families end up using the same tutors on the strength of a neighbour's experience. A recommendation is useful information about reliability and manner. It is not information about course fit, because the neighbour's child may be sitting Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level while yours sits Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and those are different jobs with different components to attack.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session: the maths-specific milestones
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and the maths calendar has its own shape because the exploration deadline is internal and movable while the papers are not. Planning backwards is more useful than planning forwards, and it tells you when each of the components in the funding table should be bought.

Two cautions. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those, and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal deadlines, including the exploration draft and submission dates, which are the ones that constrain spending. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including this one, and treat an internal deadline as firm from the moment it is announced.

Read for spending, the calendar produces a clear sequence. Secure algebraic fluency in DP1, when it is cheap. Buy the exploration block before the topic is chosen, not after the draft is written. Buy Paper 3 support in the first half of DP2, early enough for the skill to settle. Buy whole-paper practice in the final six to ten weeks. Anything bought outside that sequence is buying comfort rather than marks, and the most expensive version is an open-ended arrangement started in the final term when there is no time for it to work.

One scheduling point parents rarely anticipate. The exploration deadline tends to fall near the Extended Essay deadline and near at least one other subject's internal assessment, so the weeks when maths most needs attention are the weeks the student has least to give. A coordinator can usually say where those collisions fall for a given cohort, and knowing it in DP1 lets you move the exploration block earlier rather than bidding for evenings that are already committed. That is a scheduling saving rather than an academic one, and it is free.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Hartland schools and judging whether the money is working
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Annual inspection runs on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, published school by school, and the secondary mathematics commentary inside a report is a free second opinion on whether a weak grade reflects the student or the provision.

The cost context is unusual this year and worth using. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

With the fee line flat, tutoring is more visible in a household budget than usual, so here is the test to apply. At six weeks you should be able to see three things: a written statement naming the component that was losing marks, marked practice in that component showing movement, and a mark trend in the relevant paper. If all three are absent, the spend is not working whatever the sessions feel like. The test needs no mathematics from you, which is precisely why it is the one worth using.

On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any service describing its tutors with that phrase is referring to something else or saying something untrue, which for a parent comparing quotes is a quick filter.

sections.heading: The exploration: 20% of the grade a tutor may never write a word of
paragraphs: The exploration is the highest-return component in the funding table and the one where tutoring most often crosses a line. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Presented as a purchase it looks like a solution with a known cost. It is academic misconduct under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the Diploma, and the website that took the money bears none of it.

What a tutor legitimately does is substantial, which is why the component ranks where it does. They may explain the criteria in the language the examiner uses. They may push a topic until it carries mathematics at the right level for the course rather than reading as a school project. They may point out that a planned approach will not generate enough mathematics to assess. They may teach the mathematics the exploration depends on. They may read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin, where the notation is wrong and where a conclusion outruns the working.

What a tutor may not do is choose the topic, supply the mathematics, generate the data, or write or edit the report into its final form, nor hand over a worked example close enough to the student's own topic that copying becomes the obvious next step. We state this to the student in the first session, not in small print, because a sixteen-year-old under deadline pressure deserves to know where the line is before they are standing on it. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the official source, which is lawful and more useful, since the official version is the current one.

sections.heading: Getting started from Sobha Hartland, with a component in mind
paragraphs: Send four things. Which course, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. The latest grade, labelled as mock or classwork. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than summarised. And a photograph of one marked paper, which is worth more than the other three combined because it shows which component the marks are leaking from.

We propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis. Afterwards ask for the component in writing: not that your child needs to practise more, but that the losses sit in Paper 1's non-calculator work, or in method marks on Paper 2, or in an exploration topic that will not reach the higher criteria. If the answer does not name a component, do not book the block at any rate, because without it there is nothing to check at six weeks.

And the honest part. Diploma maths capacity is finite, and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with Paper 3 experience is thinner than Standard Level in this market. When the right tutor is not free at the time you want, we say so and offer a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course to Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level Paper 3 student and charge the specialist rate for it. If none of the alternatives suits, nothing has been lost, because the trial lesson is free and comes first.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the component if you can
process.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses, Higher and Standard are different jobs, and Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level. A photograph of a marked paper tells us the component faster than any description of the problem does.

process.title: Fund the exploration before the topic is chosen
process.description: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in a document the student controls, and the difference between a weak and a strong exploration is often a topic decision made in one conversation. We will suggest this before suggesting weekly tuition, even though weekly tuition is the larger sale.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then ask for the component in writing
process.description: The first session costs nothing. Ask which component the losses sit in and expect a specific answer naming a paper and a failure mode. Without that there is nothing to measure at six weeks, so a vague answer is a reason not to book at any price.

process.title: One session a week, with practice between
process.description: Each session ends with named timed questions in the target component and the next begins with them marked against the published criteria. A second weekly session in the same subject usually becomes supervised homework at a specialist rate, so we will advise against it.

process.title: Check the three signals at six weeks
process.description: A written statement of the component, marked practice in that component showing movement, and a mark trend in the relevant paper. If all three are missing the spend is not working, and the test requires no mathematics from you.

process.title: Buy Paper 3 early at Higher Level, then stop
process.description: Six to eight bounded sessions in the first half of DP2 is usually enough, because the skill is strategic rather than content-heavy. Once it is working the block ends rather than continuing because stopping feels risky.

whyPoints.title: Costed by component, not by the hour
whyPoints.description: The Diploma maths grade is built from named components with published weightings, so we fund them in order of return rather than selling undifferentiated hours. No competitor page in this market performs that calculation.

whyPoints.title: The exploration funded first
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, controlled entirely by the student, and decided largely by a topic choice. Three to five sessions, once, before the topic is fixed. It is the highest return available and the most commonly bought too late.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: A fifth of a Higher Level grade sits in an extended investigation most students have never been taught to approach. We block it separately and we will tell a Standard Level family they do not need it.

whyPoints.title: Three purchases we talk families out of
whyPoints.description: Open-ended course-wide revision, a second weekly session in the same subject, and level-mismatched Paper 3 work. Losing those sales is better than a parent concluding that tutoring does not work.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with named sources
whyPoints.description: Every rate here carries the provider that published it and the month we read it, next to the behaviour you should be able to observe at that price. Price tracks delivery model in this market, not quality, so the behaviour column is the useful one.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA does and link to its own material. We do not describe IB Gram or any tutor as KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, because none of it is true of us and the phrase is the commonest untruth in this market.

faqs.question: Which part of IB maths is actually worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: In order of return: the exploration, because 20% of the grade sits in a document the student controls and the outcome is largely decided by a topic choice made in one conversation. Then Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches, because no-calculator algebra is a mechanical skill that improves with drill nobody does voluntarily. Then Paper 3 at Higher Level, a fifth of the grade and a skill almost nobody is taught. Course-wide revision with no named component comes last, and it is the most commonly sold product in this market.

faqs.question: How are the IB maths components weighted at each level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 40% each and the internal exploration carries 20%. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 30% each, the shorter Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration carries 20%. The consequence for spending is direct: a Higher Level student has an entire additional paper with its own style of extended problem, and hours spent on Paper 2 practice do not prepare for it. Confirm the current structure with your child's teacher, since course documents are revised periodically.

faqs.question: What should a tutor charging AED 300 an hour do that one charging AED 60 does not?
faqs.answer: Observable things, not attitudinal ones. A specialist arrives having read the student's marked work, names the component where marks are going, sets practice aimed at that component, and talks about method marks rather than answers. A budget tutor correctly explains the questions the student brings and moves on, which is genuinely useful for a missed topic. If a tutor at the higher rate is doing the lower-rate job, you are being overcharged regardless of their qualifications, and that is testable in one lesson.

faqs.question: Is two maths sessions a week better than one?
faqs.answer: Usually worse, and more expensive. A Diploma student carries six subjects, three core components and school homework, so there is rarely two hours a week of genuine maths attention available. The second session typically becomes supervised homework at a specialist rate. One well-used session with named practice between, marked before the next session, achieves more. The exception is a bounded pre-examination block of six to ten weeks, where the intensity is justified because the window is short and the targets are specific.

faqs.question: My child is in Higher Level and has never attempted Paper 3. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It is a fifth of their grade, so yes. Paper 3 is a long structured investigation requiring the student to carry a line of reasoning across many parts, and most lose marks by stopping rather than by making errors. Six to eight bounded sessions is usually enough to change that, because the skill is strategic rather than content-heavy: knowing how to make progress on a later part when an earlier one has not resolved, and how to write enough to earn partial credit. It is worth buying in the first half of DP2.

faqs.question: How much does Diploma maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026: budget online tutors advertise from about AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified subject tutors online sit at roughly AED 150 to 300, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 because the figure includes travel. Monthly packages seen are around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures, attributed in the table here, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration and stay within the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may explain the criteria, push a topic until it carries mathematics at the right level for the course, warn that an approach will not generate enough mathematics to assess, teach the mathematics involved, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the mathematics, generate data, or write or edit the report into its final form. Submitting work that is not the student's own is misconduct under IB rules and the student bears the consequence.

faqs.question: When is it too late to buy exploration support?
faqs.answer: Once the draft has been submitted for feedback, most of the value has gone. The decisive intervention is the topic conversation, which happens before any mathematics is done: a topic too thin to reach the higher criteria cannot be rescued by polishing the write-up. After the draft, what remains is honest process advice on structure and notation, which is worth something and is not worth a specialist block. Ask your coordinator when the internal deadlines fall and buy the session before the first of them, not after.

faqs.question: How do I know within six weeks whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: Look for three things. A written statement from the tutor naming the component that was losing marks. Marked practice in that component showing movement over several weeks. And a mark or grade trend in the relevant paper. If all three are present the spend is working even if the grade has not moved yet. If all three are absent, it is not working however pleasant the sessions are. The test requires no mathematics from you, which is why it is the one worth applying.

faqs.question: Does Sobha Hartland itself change anything about the cost?
faqs.answer: Three things, all practical. Two schools sit inside the community, so some students are home before three without a car journey, which makes a genuine 4pm session available and an alert student is worth more per dirham than a tired one. Local demand is high relative to the community's size, so the better local tutors are generally committed by October. And Al Quoz and Downtown are close, so a group class on a named shared topic is a cheap and real alternative when you can identify the topic.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation cheaper to support?
faqs.answer: Neither inherently, but the spending shape differs. Analysis and Approaches needs regular no-calculator drill for Paper 1, which is weekly work across a term, so the cost is spread. Applications and Interpretation needs calculator efficiency and interpretation practice, which tends to respond to shorter targeted blocks. The genuinely expensive scenario in either course is a student placed above their foundation, who may need weekly support for two years to hold a 4. Checking that fit early is the cheapest intervention available.

faqs.question: Should a tutor's permit show up anywhere in what we are quoted?
faqs.answer: They need one and it should not affect the price, because it costs them nothing. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Are school fees rising in Dubai, and how does that affect a tutoring decision?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. With the largest education line flat, a tutoring figure is more visible in the household budget than usual. Practically, that makes this a good year to insist on the component-level diagnosis and the six-week check rather than absorbing an undifferentiated monthly payment into a general increase.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan, mock weeks or travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is what makes it straightforward rather than a favour. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, with no journey to renegotiate at either end. In mock weeks a session can pause or redirect to whatever the mocks have just exposed, which is often the most useful single session of the year. When a family travels the lesson follows the student. Agree the time zone the session is pinned to if you are leaving the Gulf, and give notice so the slot is held.

faqs.question: What happens if the Higher Level maths tutor we want is booked?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting quietly. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with genuine Paper 3 experience is thinner in this market than Standard Level, and the early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots Hartland families want fill first. The options are a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course to Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level Paper 3 student at the specialist rate, and the trial lesson is free so asking costs nothing.

faqs.question: What single thing should I send to get the most useful recommendation?
faqs.answer: A photograph of one marked paper, with the course and level written alongside it. It tells us more than any description of the problem, because it shows which component the marks are leaking from: blank later parts suggest Paper 3 strategy or pacing, correct answers with no working suggest method marks, slow early arithmetic suggests non-calculator fluency. Add the teacher's last comment quoted rather than paraphrased, and the time the school day ends, and we can usually propose a tutor the same day.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingHeading: Name the component, then spend the money
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingBody: Diploma maths has published weightings, so the spending question has an arithmetic answer rather than an intuitive one. Fund the exploration before the topic is chosen, fund Paper 1 drill through DP1, fund Paper 3 early at Higher Level, and fund whole papers in the last six to ten weeks. Send the course, the level, the latest grade and a photograph of one marked paper, and we will propose a tutor and run the first session free. Then ask which component the losses sit in, and check the three signals at six weeks.

intro.heading: The Barsha Heights week, and where an hour of mathematics fits in it
paragraphs: Start with the logistics, because in this community they decide everything. Barsha Heights, still universally called TECOM, is a cluster of towers between Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai Internet City and Al Barsha, and it contains no large school campus. Secondary students living here are bussed outward in the morning, to Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Sufouh and occasionally further, and they come back on a route that collects from several communities. The practical consequence is that a parent in a villa in Al Barsha 2 knows within five minutes when their child will be home, and a parent in a tower in Barsha Heights does not.

That single difference is why a generic afternoon tutoring slot does not work here. A 16:00 session, which is standard in parts of Dubai, is unusable for most Barsha Heights families. A 17:00 session works for some and not others. A 17:30 or 18:00 session works for nearly everybody, and in the second term those are the most heavily booked hours of the year across the whole city, which means a family that waits until February to arrange them will not get the time they want. Planning around the bus is not a detail; it is the first thing to settle.

The second thing to settle is which mathematics course your child is actually taking, because there are two and they are genuinely different subjects. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route, and it includes a paper sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology route, and every paper allows a calculator. Each runs at Higher and Standard Level. Four combinations, four different sets of weaknesses, and a tutor matched to the wrong one wastes the hour you worked so hard to schedule.

Third is the exploration, which carries a fifth of the grade in every version of the course and which, in a Dubai school week, has nowhere obvious to live. A student carrying six Diploma subjects plus Theory of Knowledge plus the Extended Essay plus the mandatory UAE subjects does not have a free afternoon in which to design an original piece of mathematics. It gets written in evenings and on weekends, which is exactly when a Barsha Heights child is also recovering from a commute. Protecting a fixed weekend slot for it is worth more than any amount of weekday tutoring.

On what we actually provide: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the paper, the graphical display calculator screen and the student's own working shared live. For a community whose children are already in a vehicle for an hour a day, the absence of a fourth journey is not a compromise. It is most of the argument.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-tecom.programmesIntro: Four combinations, and a tutor has to be matched to one of them rather than to mathematics in general. Here is what each demands.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
programmes.description: The most demanding mathematics on the Diploma. Three written papers: Paper 1 without a calculator, Paper 2 with one, and Paper 3 as two long structured investigative problems. Proof, complex numbers, vectors and a substantial calculus load. Paper 3 is the component students prepare least for and underestimate most, because nothing earlier in their schooling resembles it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students heading for engineering, computer science, physics or mathematics at competitive universities are commonly advised into this course. Admissions requirements are set by each institution, so check the published requirements on the specific programme page at Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah, Zayed University or whichever overseas university is in view.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
programmes.description: Two written papers of equal weight, one without a calculator and one with, plus the exploration. The content is narrower than Higher Level but the algebraic demand is still real, and students who arrived from an IGCSE Core or Foundation route frequently find the first term harder than expected. The no-calculator paper is where that shows first.
programmes.countryNote: A common landing place for Dubai students who want a quantitative course without the Higher Level load, and for those keeping options open in economics and the sciences. Check each university programme's own published mathematics requirement, because Standard Level acceptance varies by subject and by institution.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
programmes.description: Three written papers, all allowing a calculator, with modelling and statistics at the centre and the graphical display calculator integral rather than incidental. The statistics, matrices and graph-theory content is denser than the course's reputation suggests, and Paper 3 again asks for sustained work on an extended problem rather than recall.
programmes.countryNote: Frequently chosen by Dubai students heading for business, economics, design and some social sciences. Because programme requirements differ, and some engineering routes specify Analysis and Approaches, the course choice should be checked against the published requirement of the actual programme rather than assumed.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level
programmes.description: Two written papers of equal weight, both with a calculator, plus the exploration. Technology use is assessed rather than tolerated, so marks are lost by producing a correct answer with no indication of the method or the tool used. Students treat this as the easy option and then meet statistics content they have genuinely never seen before.
programmes.countryNote: The most commonly taken mathematics route in Dubai Diploma cohorts. The risk is reputational: because it is widely described as the lighter course, students arrive expecting to coast and discover that the exploration still carries a fifth of the grade and still has to contain real mathematics.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics splits into topic areas that behave very differently under tutoring. These are the ones Barsha Heights students most often need, with where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Algebra and functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: The foundation everything else stands on, and the place an under-powered IGCSE route shows first. Rearranging, factorising, laws of logarithms and transformations of graphs. Students who cannot manipulate confidently spend their calculus lessons doing algebra badly, which is why diagnosis almost always starts here regardless of the stated problem.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.levels: AA SL and HL, AI HL
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules at Higher Level, implicit differentiation and related rates. Marks are lost less on the differentiation itself than on what the question wanted it for: a maximum, a rate of change, a gradient at a point. Reading the question for the purpose of the derivative is the teachable step.

subjects.name: Integral calculus
subjects.description: Definite and indefinite integration, areas and volumes of revolution, and at Higher Level substitution, integration by parts and partial fractions. The Higher Level content is dense enough that late intervention works poorly, which makes this the clearest case on the whole course for starting in DP1 rather than DP2.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample. A distinct skill that most students meet for the first time here, and one where the marks sit in the structure of the argument rather than in the result. Students who write a correct conclusion without the inductive step earn very little, which surprises them.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and circular functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Identities, equations, radian measure and modelling with sinusoidal functions. Radians rather than degrees is a recurring source of lost marks on calculator papers, and solving a trigonometric equation over a stated domain is routinely answered with one solution where the domain contains several.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AI SL and HL, AA SL and HL
subjects.description: Heavier in Applications and Interpretation, where distributions, hypothesis testing and correlation carry real weight. Students lose marks by reporting a statistic without interpreting it in the context of the question, which is precisely what the course assesses. Calculator output pasted without comment earns nothing.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Lines and planes in three dimensions, scalar and vector products, intersections and angles. Spatially demanding and hard to self-teach from a textbook, which makes it a strong candidate for one-to-one work where a shared screen can hold a diagram that both people are drawing on.

subjects.name: Matrices and graph theory
subjects.description: Transformations, eigenvalues, adjacency matrices and algorithms on graphs. Content that students taking Applications and Interpretation often did not expect from a course described as the lighter route, and which they meet late enough in DP1 to be under-practised by the time Paper 3 arrives.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator skills
subjects.description: Assessed rather than assumed. Solving numerically, finding intersections, regression, distributions and sketching from a window that actually shows the feature in question. Marks are lost when a student produces the right number and writes nothing about where it came from, which the mark scheme requires.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.levels: All four combinations, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: Marked out of 20 across five criteria, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation. The most common failure is a well-presented exploration using mathematics below the student's own course level, which caps the heaviest criterion before anybody reads the argument.

subjects.name: Paper 3 structured problems
subjects.description: Two extended, scaffolded investigations rather than a set of independent questions, which rewards persistence and reading ahead. Students who treat each part as a separate question lose the thread the paper is built on. It is the least-practised component in Higher Level mathematics and the easiest to improve with deliberate work.

subjects.name: Bridging from IGCSE or MYP
subjects.description: Different gaps by route. An IGCSE Extended student usually needs confidence with proof and with sustained problems. An MYP student usually needs timed answering against a mark scheme. A Core or Foundation route student usually needs algebra rebuilt before anything else, and in the summer rather than in October.

sections.heading: The Barsha Heights school run, and the session times it actually permits
paragraphs: Here is the practical table this page exists for. Barsha Heights students travel outward in four broad directions, the return journeys differ by twenty-five minutes or more, and that difference decides which tutoring slot a family can hold through a term rather than abandon in week five. Find the row that matches your child's bus and the answer to when should we book is in the last column.

The pattern across the table is consistent. Short northern runs towards Al Sufouh and the coast sometimes permit a 17:00 start. Runs south into Al Barsha cross the interchange at its worst and land closer to 17:30. Runs inland to Al Barsha South are longer still and realistically need 18:00. And a second sibling, whatever the route, works better an hour after the first rather than immediately after, because two consecutive sessions in one household compete for the same quiet room.

There is a seasonal complication that catches families out every year. Those 17:30 and 18:00 slots are the most heavily demanded tutoring hours across the whole Dubai school system, and demand peaks in the second term when mocks and Internal Assessment deadlines arrive together. A family that decides in February to start weekly mathematics is competing for the scarcest hour of the year. The same decision made in September gets the slot without difficulty and costs the same.

The other seasonal factor is Ramadan, when school days shorten and the useful tutoring window moves to after Iftar entirely. For a Barsha Heights family that is often easier rather than harder, because the commute compresses and the evening opens up. We keep the same tutor with the same student through that change rather than reshuffling, since continuity in mathematics matters more than in most subjects.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice and its consequences
paragraphs: Two courses, four combinations with level, and a decision usually made in Year 11 with less information than it deserves. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route, and it includes a paper sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology route, and every paper allows a calculator. Both run at Higher and Standard Level, and both carry an exploration worth a fifth of the grade.

The no-calculator paper is the most practical distinguishing fact and the one families find most useful. An Analysis and Approaches student has to be fluent enough to work without technology for a whole paper: exact values, surds, logarithm laws, differentiation by hand. A student who has leaned on a calculator since Year 9 will find that paper brutal, and the problem is diagnosable at the point of choosing the course rather than in DP2. If your child cannot do a page of algebra without reaching for a device, that is information about the course choice.

University expectations are the other half of the decision, and here the honest answer is that they vary by institution and by programme rather than following a universal rule. Some engineering, computer science, physics and mathematics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Many business, economics, design and social-science programmes accept either. Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and Zayed University each publish their own requirements, as do overseas universities, and the only reliable method is to read the specific programme page rather than to accept a general claim from anybody.

What a tutor can usefully contribute to this decision is evidence rather than opinion. A diagnostic on Analysis and Approaches material tells you whether the algebraic fluency is there. A look at the student's statistics work tells you whether the Applications route plays to a genuine strength or simply avoids a weakness. Avoiding a weakness is sometimes the right call and sometimes stores the problem for a first-year university course, and that is a conversation worth having with data in front of you.

sections.heading: Paper weightings, durations and calculator rules
paragraphs: This is where a family decides how to spend the one evening hour the bus schedule allows. A component worth 40% deserves more of that hour than one worth 20%, and students routinely split their revision evenly because nobody has shown them the proportions. The table sets out the published structure for all four combinations, and the figures should be confirmed against the current subject guide through your school's Diploma coordinator, because the IB revises its guides.

Read the Higher Level rows carefully, because the structure is the thing students misunderstand. Higher Level does not take the two Standard Level papers and make them harder. It redistributes the weight across three papers and introduces a distinct format in Paper 3: two long, scaffolded investigative problems that reward reading ahead and persisting rather than recall. Students meet that format late, often in the second Diploma year, and prepare for it less than for the papers they have been sitting since DP1.

The exploration row is the same in every combination and is the one most often misread. Twenty per cent of the grade, produced over months, with feedback available and no time pressure, is the most controllable mark on the course. A student who treats it as homework and the papers as the real assessment has the priorities inverted. Every mark lost in an exploration was available under near-perfect conditions and was given away, which is a harder thing to accept than a mark lost in an examination hall.

The calculator column is practically useful for planning a session. An Analysis and Approaches student needs some sessions with the device put away entirely, because fluency without it is a separate skill that does not develop by accident. An Applications and Interpretation student needs the opposite: deliberate work on using the graphical display calculator well, including writing down what was entered and why, because the mark scheme asks for the method and not only the number.

sections.heading: When the exploration actually gets written in a Dubai school week
paragraphs: A fifth of the grade has to be produced somewhere, and in a Dubai Diploma timetable there is no obvious somewhere. Six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, creativity activity and service, and the mandatory UAE subjects that every Dubai private school runs regardless of its licensed curriculum. For a Barsha Heights student add an hour a day in a vehicle. The honest arithmetic is that the exploration gets written on weekends and in a few late evenings, and planning for that reality beats pretending otherwise.

Which means the sequencing matters more than the effort. Topic choice first, and early, because the heaviest criterion rewards use of mathematics at or above the student's own course level and a topic that cannot carry that mathematics caps the piece before a word is written. Students pick topics they find interesting and then discover the mathematics available in them is Year 10 material. Testing a topic against the criterion takes twenty minutes and saves a month.

Then the mathematics, then the writing, in that order and not simultaneously. A student who writes as they explore produces a narrative of their own confusion, which reads badly against the communication criterion. A student who establishes the mathematics first and then writes it up produces something coherent. Personal engagement and reflection, the two smaller criteria, are earned by genuine decisions recorded as they happen, which is another argument for fortnightly work rather than a single heroic weekend.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and worth stating. Explain the criteria, test whether the topic can carry course-level mathematics, check the mathematics for correctness, ask why a choice was made, and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. Not choose the topic, not write the mathematics, not draft the text, not revise prose until the words are no longer the student's. The student and the school declare the work authentic, and a breach is a malpractice finding against your child rather than against anybody else.

sections.heading: Where Diploma mathematics marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The list is short and stable, which is why a tutor who has marked enough scripts can usually predict a student's weak areas from a single paper. Publishing it is more useful than describing a teaching philosophy, so here it is in the order the marks disappear.

First, working not shown. Diploma mathematics mark schemes award method marks, and a student who writes an answer with no intervening steps forfeits them even when the answer is correct. On a calculator paper this is worse, because the mark scheme explicitly wants an indication of what was entered. Students who have been praised for being quick at mental arithmetic are the most prone to it, and the fix is a habit rather than a concept, which makes it the fastest gain available.

Second, the wrong fluency for the paper. An Analysis and Approaches student who cannot work exactly without a calculator loses marks across the whole of Paper 1, regardless of understanding. Exact values in surds, logarithm laws, differentiation by hand. This is not a content gap and it will not appear in a topic test with a calculator on the desk, which is why it is often discovered first in a mock.

Third, the question's purpose missed. A derivative is calculated correctly and then not used for the maximum the question asked for. A statistic is produced and not interpreted in context, which is exactly what the Applications course assesses. A trigonometric equation is solved for one value when the stated domain contains three. Fourth and last, Paper 3 treated as a set of separate questions rather than one developing investigation, which loses the thread the whole paper is built on and is the single clearest case of a component that improves rapidly with deliberate practice.

sections.heading: What two hours a week costs across a Diploma, and whether it is worth it
paragraphs: Dubai tutoring is usually priced by the hour and bought by the year, so the honest frame for a Diploma family is the two-year total rather than the hourly figure. Take a weekly session through DP1 and DP2, roughly thirty-two teaching weeks a year, and the arithmetic at published Dubai market rates becomes a real number that deserves a decision rather than a drift.

The published bands, all read in October 2026 and all published by other providers: budget online and university-student tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International Baccalaureate from AED 200. Specialists across IB, IGCSE and A Level at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors published as high as AED 650 by BartyED. In-home visits at AED 180 to 350 from Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors.

Run that across two years at one hour a week and a mid-market online rate produces a four-figure annual commitment, while a specialist rate produces a materially larger one and an in-home specialist larger again. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions put budget at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-market at AED 600 to 1,200 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, which is the same arithmetic from the other direction. None of these figures is IB Gram's price list.

Seeing the total changes the sensible shape of the purchase, which is the point of writing it down. For most Barsha Heights families the better pattern is not two hours every week for two years. It is one weekly hour in DP1 while there is runway, a fortnightly weekend slot for the exploration, and then a concentrated paper-specific block before each major assessment. That costs less, lands where the marks are, and respects a week that already contains a commute. We would rather sell that shape than a flat retainer, and we will say so at the consultation.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects and why the week has no slack
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. One of KHDA's requirements has a direct effect on whether a Diploma student has time to practise mathematics, and it is rarely connected to tutoring in anything a family reads.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's guidance setting the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the implementation point. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes are required by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs strictly prohibited.

Add those lessons to six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the supervised core, and the independent study time that a Diploma mathematics course assumes is largely notional. For a Barsha Heights student with an hour of daily commuting on top, the week genuinely does not contain the practice time the syllabus imagines. When a family says their child has no time to do past papers, that is usually literally true rather than an excuse.

Which changes what a tutoring hour should be for. If the week contains no independent practice time, the session cannot be a place where work is reviewed; it has to be the place where the work happens, under supervision, with immediate correction. That is a different session design from a review tutorial, and it is the right one for most students in this community. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA and claims none of those things; we explain the framework because it changes how an hour should be spent.

sections.heading: Booking, scheduling and what we will not do
paragraphs: Send the course, the level and the paper causing the problem: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 1, or Applications and Interpretation Standard Level Paper 2, and so on. If you have a marked script or a draft exploration, send that instead of a description. The first session is free and is spent on a timed section of real paper, marked, with a written note afterwards naming where the marks went and what the remaining window realistically allows.

Then tell us the bus. Which direction your child travels, roughly when they get home, and whether a sibling needs a slot too. That determines the session time, and the session time determines whether the arrangement survives past week five. Barsha Heights families generally settle at 17:30 or 18:00, and those are the hours that disappear first in the second term, so arranging them in term one is worth more than it sounds.

Three things we decline. We will not write, draft or revise any part of an exploration to completion, whatever the request is called when it arrives. We will not distribute International Baccalaureate subject guides, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because they are the IB's copyright; we reference them, link to the official source and work from them inside a session. And we will not claim International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA or Ministry accreditation, because IB Gram holds none.

One more honest limit. No International Baccalaureate examination or results date appears anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from source. The May session is the one UAE schools sit, and your Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative dates together with the internal deadlines that actually bind a student's term. IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai and no office, centre or branch in the UAE; every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths session start for a family in Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:30, and 18:00 for many. Barsha Heights contains no large school campus, so secondary students are bussed outward and return on multi-stop routes rather than at a school bell. Children travelling north to Al Sufouh and the coast sometimes manage 17:00; those travelling inland to Al Barsha South realistically need 18:00. A second sibling works better an hour after the first rather than immediately following, because two consecutive sessions in one apartment compete for the same quiet room.

faqs.question: Why are evening tutoring slots so hard to get in the second term?
faqs.answer: Because the whole city wants them at once. The 17:30 and 18:00 hours are the most demanded tutoring times across the Dubai school system, and demand peaks in the second term when mocks and Internal Assessment deadlines arrive together. A family deciding in February to begin weekly mathematics is competing for the scarcest hour of the year at exactly the worst moment. The same decision made in September secures the slot without difficulty and at the same rate, which is the cheapest piece of planning available.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between IB Maths AA and AI?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route and includes one paper sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology route, and every paper allows a calculator. Both run at Higher and Standard Level and both carry an exploration worth a fifth of the grade. The no-calculator paper is the most practical test for a family choosing: if your child cannot do a page of algebra without reaching for a device, that is real information about which course fits.

faqs.question: Which maths course do UAE universities expect?

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why do students struggle with it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 appears at Higher Level in both mathematics courses and consists of two long, scaffolded investigative problems rather than a set of independent questions. It rewards reading ahead, persisting through a developing argument and carrying earlier parts into later ones. Students meet the format late, usually in the second Diploma year, and practise it less than the papers they have been sitting since DP1. That combination makes it the single component in Diploma mathematics that improves fastest under deliberate, short, concentrated work.

faqs.question: How much of the maths grade is the exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four combinations of course and level. It is produced over months, with feedback available from a teacher and no time pressure, which makes it the most controllable mark on the whole course. The most common failure is not laziness but topic choice: a well-presented exploration using mathematics below the student's own course level caps the heaviest criterion before anybody assesses the argument. Testing a topic against that criterion takes twenty minutes and saves a month of work.

faqs.question: When should my child start the maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most Dubai schools require it, because the week has no slack later. A realistic pattern is topic selection and testing in DP1, the mathematics established in a fortnightly weekend slot across the following months, and the writing done once the mathematics is settled rather than alongside it. Students who write as they explore produce a narrative of their own confusion, which reads badly against the communication criterion. Personal engagement and reflection are earned by decisions recorded as they happen, and cannot be convincingly backfilled late.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may explain the criteria, test whether a topic can carry course-level mathematics, check the mathematics for correctness, ask why a particular choice was made, and mark the student's own draft against the published criteria. A tutor may not choose the topic, write the mathematics, draft the text, or revise prose until the words are no longer the student's. The student and the school both declare the work authentic, and a breach is a malpractice finding against your child rather than against the tutor.

faqs.question: Where do IB maths students lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Working not shown, by a clear margin. Diploma mark schemes award method marks, and an answer written with no intervening steps forfeits them even when correct. On calculator papers the scheme explicitly wants an indication of what was entered. After that: the wrong fluency for the paper, meaning an Analysis student who cannot work exactly without a calculator; the question's purpose missed, where a derivative is computed and not used for the maximum asked for; and Paper 3 treated as separate questions rather than one developing investigation.

faqs.question: Does my child need no-calculator practice?
faqs.answer: If they are taking Analysis and Approaches, yes, and it needs to be deliberate rather than incidental. Paper 1 in that course is sat without a calculator, which demands exact values in surds, fluent logarithm laws and differentiation by hand. A student who has leaned on a device since Year 9 will not discover the gap in a topic test with a calculator on the desk; they discover it in a mock. The fix is sessions with the device put away entirely, which is a habit rather than a concept and responds quickly.

faqs.question: What does two years of weekly maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Enough to deserve a decision rather than a drift, which is why the two-year arithmetic is worth doing. Published Dubai bands read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. intro.heading: The real price of two years of Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: Families in The Greens tend to discover the cost of Diploma mathematics in the wrong order. The first number they see is an hourly rate, quoted by whoever answered the phone. The number that matters is the total across two years, and that depends on three decisions taken long before any tutor is hired: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level or Higher Level, and whether the exploration is handled early or in a panic in the spring.

Published Dubai rates in 2026 make the arithmetic visible. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised between roughly AED 150 and 300 an hour, and a Diploma specialist from about AED 200 to 450 and upwards. At one session a week that is between AED 600 and 1,200 a month at the middle of the market, and between AED 1,000 and more than AED 2,000 a month in an exam year, according to Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026. Across twenty-two teaching months, the gap between a sensible plan and a drifting one runs into tens of thousands of dirhams.

Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the expensive end of that range for a structural reason rather than a commercial one. It carries a third examination paper, Paper 3, which is a one-hour guided investigation worth a fifth of the grade and the component students are least able to practise alone. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so algebraic fluency has to be rebuilt by hand rather than checked on a screen. Both of those take hours, and hours are the unit that is actually being purchased.

Applications and Interpretation prices differently. The graphic display calculator is assumed throughout, so fewer hours go on by-hand technique and more go on modelling, statistics and the written interpretation that the mark scheme rewards. Many Greens families paying specialist rates for AI are paying for the wrong thing: they buy algebra drill when the marks are being lost in the sentence after the answer.

The waste in this market is predictable and it is almost always one of four things. Paying a generalist to cover Paper 3. Buying weekly sessions in Year 12 for a student who needed a six-session exploration block instead. Starting in March of Year 13 at exam-season rates for work that cost half as much in October. And paying the in-home travel premium, quoted in Dubai from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, for a format that consumes part of the only usable evening window The Greens has. The sections below put numbers on each of them.

Read the tables before the prose if you are comparing quotes this week. The first prices every sensible plan across the full Diploma, the second shows what the route choice does to the number of hours you buy, the third puts the component weightings next to the places marks actually go missing, and the fourth sets out the five exploration criteria with the mark allocation beside each one. Taken together they answer the question an hourly rate never does, which is how many hours your child's specific course and specific weakness are going to require.
