dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Four things get called "IB maths" by parents in this community, and they cost different amounts to support. Separating them before you ask for a quote is the single cheapest thing you can do.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebra, functions, calculus and proof route. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which makes by-hand manipulation a graded skill rather than a convenience. Higher Level adds a third paper and a markedly deeper calculus and proof requirement, and it is the course most often chosen by students heading for engineering, mathematics, physics or quantitative economics.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates Living cluster, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is where tutoring spend concentrates, because the schools that offer it near The Greens run small HL cohorts and a student who falls behind has few classmates at the same level to work alongside. Two sessions a week through the second year is the common pattern, and it is the plan with the largest total cost in this table.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling, statistics and financial mathematics route, with the graphic display calculator assumed in every paper. The technical demand is lower and the communication demand is higher: marks come from choosing a model, justifying it, and interpreting the output in context. Higher Level adds a third paper and substantially more statistics.
programmes.countryNote: Applications and Interpretation is frequently the better route for Greens students heading into business, design, psychology or the health sciences, and it is cheaper to support well. The mistake families make here is buying specialist exam-year rates for help with technique when what the student needs is a few hours on writing a conclusion that the mark scheme can credit.

programmes.name: The mathematical exploration
programmes.ageRange: Written in Year 12 or early Year 13
programmes.description: An independent piece of mathematics, usually twelve to twenty pages, assessed against five criteria worth twenty marks in total and carrying a fifth of the final grade on both routes and at both levels. It is the only component where a student controls the question, and the only one where good support is a block of a few sessions rather than a weekly commitment.
programmes.countryNote: Handled in Year 12, an exploration block of around six sessions is a one-off cost. Handled in the spring of Year 13 it competes with examination revision at the most expensive point in the calendar. For families in The Greens this is the clearest example of timing being worth more than rate negotiation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics into the Diploma
programmes.description: The years before the Diploma, assessed against criteria rather than examination papers. Students arriving in Year 12 from MYP standard mathematics frequently find Analysis and Approaches a harder step than their report grades suggested, because criterion-based assessment measures different things from a timed non-calculator paper.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses near The Greens run the full IB continuum, so a child can move from MYP into the Diploma without changing school. That continuity is an advantage academically and a trap financially: parents assume the transition is smooth in content terms and buy support only after the first set of Year 12 Paper 1 marks arrives.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics is one subject on a timetable and five distinct skills in a mark scheme. These are the areas Greens families most often end up paying to repair, with the component each one actually shows up in.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms and, at Higher Level, complex numbers and proof by induction. On Analysis and Approaches this is Paper 1 territory and has to work without a calculator, which is why it absorbs more tutoring hours than any other topic in the first year.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, rational functions, inverse functions and composite notation. Marks go missing in the unstructured questions that give a graph and ask for the function, because the student recognises the shape but cannot write the algebra that produces it.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, equations and, at Higher Level on Analysis and Approaches, vectors. Students who learned trigonometry as triangle work in the Middle Years Programme struggle with it as a function, and that gap is the usual cause of a weak Paper 1 in the first year.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: SL and HL, heavier on AI
subjects.description: Distributions, correlation, hypothesis testing and regression. On Applications and Interpretation this is the core of the course and the heart of Paper 2, and it is tested as much on interpretation as on calculation. Precise wording earns marks that a correct number alone does not.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: SL and HL, deeper on AA
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and, at Higher Level, techniques such as substitution and differential equations. Higher Level calculus is the single largest reason an Analysis and Approaches student needs a second weekly hour in Year 13.

subjects.name: Proof and the Higher Level toolkit
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and counterexample. Unlike every other topic, it cannot be drilled through repetition because each question is new. It is the part of the course where a specialist and a generalist produce visibly different results.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: A one-hour paper of extended guided investigations worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade. The difficulty is structural: later parts depend on earlier ones, so a single early error cascades. It is the most tutored component in the whole course and the hardest to practise unsupervised.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The two smallest criteria, personal engagement and reflection, are where capable students lose the most, because strong mathematics with no reflective commentary scores well below its apparent quality.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.levels: SL and HL, essential on AI
subjects.description: Regression, distributions, numerical solving and graphing on the permitted handheld. Schools teach the mathematics and often assume the device, which leaves students slow in Paper 2 where speed converts directly into marks.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.levels: SL and HL, Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Exact values, surd and index manipulation, and arithmetic done by hand under time pressure. Paper 1 assumes it, and students arriving from a calculator-permitted lower-school course have usually never been tested on it.

subjects.name: Physics HL alongside Maths AA HL
subjects.description: A common Greens combination for engineering applicants. The two courses share kinematics, vectors and calculus, so a single tutor who covers both can convert overlapping content into fewer paid hours rather than more.

subjects.name: Economics and business quantitative work
subjects.description: Students on Applications and Interpretation often take Economics or Business Management, where the same statistical reasoning is assessed in prose. Support that connects the two is cheaper than treating them as unrelated subjects.

sections.heading: What two years of Diploma mathematics actually costs here
paragraphs: The table below converts published Dubai market rates into the figure a household budget feels: the monthly cost, and the total across the Diploma. The hourly bands behind it are the ones advertised across the emirate in 2026, with qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150 to 300 and Diploma specialists from about AED 200 to 450 and upwards. The monthly estimates are from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table. Nothing here is an IB Gram price.

Read the first two rows against the third and the shape of the decision becomes obvious. Standard Level on either route, supported by one weekly hour, is a four-figure annual commitment. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches at two hours a week in the second year is a five-figure one. The difference is not a markup; it is an extra examination paper, a non-calculator paper and a calculus requirement that genuinely takes twice as long to teach.

The two block rows are the ones families usually omit from their planning and then pay for anyway. An exploration block is a fixed, one-off purchase of around six sessions. A final block before the May session is eight to twelve sessions at the most expensive point in the year. Budgeting for the first makes the second smaller; skipping the first guarantees the second is large.

One honest caveat about every figure in this table. These are market observations, not quotations, and the ranges are wide because the market is. Treat them as a yardstick for judging any quote you receive, including ours. What IB Gram offers first is a free trial lesson with no card details, after which a rate is quoted for the specific route, level and session length your child needs.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets the bill
paragraphs: Parents in The Greens usually meet this decision as a form to sign in the spring of Year 11, with twenty minutes of explanation attached. It deserves more, because it determines both what the student studies for two years and roughly how much support that will take. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. They assess different mathematics.

Analysis and Approaches is algebraic. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which means index laws, surds, exact trigonometric values and algebraic rearrangement all have to be reliable by hand. Students who have spent the Middle Years Programme or IGCSE with a calculator permanently available often arrive fluent in method and slow in execution, and closing that gap is measured in weeks of practice rather than in explanations.

Applications and Interpretation assumes the graphic display calculator throughout and asks for judgement instead. A typical Paper 2 question gives real data, asks for a model, and awards marks for choosing it, fitting it and saying what it does and does not tell you. The failure mode is a correct number followed by a sentence the mark scheme cannot credit, and the fix is written technique, not algebra drill.

The expensive error is buying support for the wrong route. An Applications and Interpretation student given weekly algebra practice will improve at something that is barely assessed on their papers. An Analysis and Approaches student given modelling work will enjoy it and gain very little in Paper 1. Confirming the route and level before the first paid session costs nothing and removes the most common source of wasted spend in this subject.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: what you are paying to fix
paragraphs: Hours are only worth buying when they are aimed at a component. The weightings below show where the grade actually sits, and they explain why two students on the same course with the same report grade can need very different amounts of help. A student losing marks in Paper 1 has a technique problem. A student losing them in Paper 3 has a stamina and structure problem. The second costs more to fix.

Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry forty per cent at Standard Level and thirty per cent at Higher Level. At Standard Level they run an hour and a half each; at Higher Level, two hours each. The non-calculator constraint on Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is the single most under-prepared feature of the course, because school practice tends to happen with a calculator on the desk out of habit.

Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, lasts one hour and carries a fifth of the grade. It consists of extended guided investigations where later parts build on earlier ones, so one early mistake propagates through the rest of the question. No amount of topic revision prepares a student for it; the only thing that does is working through complete investigations under time pressure with someone who can see where the thread was dropped.

The exploration carries the remaining fifth on both routes and at both levels. Its criteria are explained in the next section, but the budget point belongs here: a fifth of the grade is decided by a document written months before the examinations, and it is the only component where a student can bank marks early at a predictable, one-off cost.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, and where the money goes wrong
paragraphs: The exploration is an independent piece of mathematics of around twelve to twenty pages, assessed against five criteria worth twenty marks in total. Presentation carries four marks, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. That distribution is the whole reason capable students underperform on it: the mathematics is worth less than half the marks, and the six remaining marks for engagement and reflection are the ones strong mathematicians skip.

The cost implication is specific. A student who understands the criteria before choosing a topic needs a small block of sessions. A student who writes twenty pages of good mathematics and then discovers that personal engagement and reflection are separately assessed needs a rewrite, usually during the term when examination revision should be starting. The second scenario costs two or three times the first and buys a worse grade.

The boundary on what a tutor may do here is not a matter of taste. A tutor can explain each criterion, discuss a plan the student has drafted, teach a technique the student has decided to use, read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short, and ask the questions that force a genuine reflective paragraph into existence. No tutor at IB Gram will write the exploration, produce a draft for submission, or edit one until the words are no longer the student's.

That line protects the candidate rather than us. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under the board's rules and the consequence lands on the student. Providers in this market do advertise completed Internal Assessments at fixed prices; what they are selling is the risk, transferred.

sections.heading: Where Greens families waste money on Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: The first waste is paying a generalist specialist rates. A tutor comfortable with IGCSE mathematics and willing to attempt Higher Level Paper 3 will produce sessions that feel productive and change very little, because Paper 3 rewards a particular kind of structured exploration that has to be taught by someone who has marked or taught it repeatedly. Asking directly which route and level a tutor teaches, and when they last taught it, filters this out in one question.

The second is buying weekly hours when the student needed a block. A Year 12 who is keeping up in class but has not started the exploration does not need thirty-six weekly sessions; they need six focused ones and then nothing until the spring. Weekly standing arrangements are easier to sell and easier to forget to cancel, and they quietly become the largest line in a family's education spending.

The third is starting late and paying exam-season prices for foundational work. Rates in this market firm up as the May session approaches, and the work available in six weeks is narrower than the work available in six months. A student with a non-calculator weakness in October has a technique problem that practice solves; the same student in April has a grade problem that practice cannot fully solve.

The fourth is the travel premium. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly packages of four two-hour visits advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799, and the difference against online rates at the same qualification level buys transport. In The Greens, where the usable weekday window runs from about four o'clock to half past seven, that premium also costs evening minutes twice over. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are an India-only service.

Front-load foundational work into the autumn term
Do not pay a travel premium out of a ninety-minute evening window

sections.heading: How many hours Higher Level actually takes
paragraphs: A straight answer is more useful than a range, so here is the pattern that recurs among students who move from the middle of the Higher Level cohort to the top of it. Year 12 runs on one hour a week, aimed at the non-calculator technique that school practice tends to skip, plus a six-session exploration block in the second half of the year. Year 13 runs on two hours a week from September: one on technique and content, one on complete timed papers with Paper 3 treated as a separate skill.

Expressed in sessions rather than months, that is roughly thirty to thirty-six hours in the first year and sixty to seventy in the second. At the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour, the two-year total lands somewhere between the mid-twenty thousands and the high forty thousands of dirhams. Those are market figures rather than ours, and the range is wide because the market's is.

Standard Level is close to half of that on both routes. One weekly hour across two years, plus the same exploration block, covers most students who are keeping pace in class. Students who are not keeping pace need a short diagnostic block first, because adding hours to a weekly arrangement rarely fixes a gap that opened a year earlier.

The number that changes these totals most is not the rate. It is the month you start. Every family who began in the spring of Year 13 paid more per week, bought fewer usable weeks, and had less of the course left to influence. Starting in Year 12 at one hour a week is the cheapest version of a serious plan.

sections.heading: Which schools near The Greens run Diploma maths, and why cohort size matters
paragraphs: Dubai's private school market held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of enrolment and the UK curriculum thirty-seven. That seven per cent share is the relevant number for a Diploma mathematics parent in The Greens, because it explains why Higher Level groups are small even in large schools.

A Diploma cohort of a hundred students might produce fifteen taking Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and five taking Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. In a class of five, a student who falls behind has almost nobody to compare working with, and the teacher has little room to run two paces at once. That is a structural argument for one-to-one support rather than a criticism of any school, and it is worth asking the question before Year 12 rather than after the first Paper 1.

KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports. The subject-level commentary is where the useful information is: a school can be strong overall and thin in Higher Level mathematics, and that is exactly the situation in which private support changes an outcome. Dubai is also adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, three of them International Baccalaureate, which should ease cohort sizes over time.

On fees, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting two years of Diploma mathematics support, a flat school fee is the one fixed point in the calculation.

sections.heading: Does the route choice matter for UAE university entry?
paragraphs: It matters for course access rather than for admission in general, and the honest answer is that the requirement sits with the individual programme rather than with the country. Engineering, computer science and quantitative economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, design, psychology and most health science programmes accept Applications and Interpretation. Check the published entry requirement for the specific programme and the specific intake year, because these change.

Separately from admission there is equivalency, which is the Ministry of Education process that recognises a foreign school certificate in the UAE. The published requirements differ by curriculum. On the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying, and English proficiency is satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

No equivalency points threshold for the International Baccalaureate is published on this page, because none has been read from a Ministry of Education source. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a subject count for IGCSE that does not match the Gulf Today report of the Ministry's clarification; inheriting that error would be worse than saying nothing. Take the Diploma figure from moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly.

Equivalency is also not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or accelerates. IB Gram describes the process and points to the official channel; the application itself is between the family and the authority. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: Six weeks out: what a final block can and cannot buy
paragraphs: Families in The Greens ask this every spring, usually after a mock result. The answer depends almost entirely on what already exists. With sound technique and weak exam execution, six weeks of timed papers and targeted review moves a grade, sometimes more than one, because the marks being lost are recoverable through practice. With a genuine content gap in calculus or in non-calculator algebra, six weeks closes part of it and the rest shows up in the hall.

What a sensible final block looks like is unglamorous. A full past paper under timed conditions first, marked properly, to identify the two topics costing the most marks rather than the two that feel worst. Then eight to twelve sessions alternating between those topics and complete timed papers, with Paper 3 treated separately at Higher Level because it is a different skill from the other two papers. No new content after the halfway point.

What it cannot buy is a rewritten exploration. A fifth of the grade was settled when that document was submitted, and the time spent trying to improve the remaining components is better spent on them. This is the moment families most regret not having bought an exploration block eighteen months earlier, and it is why that block appears so early in this page.

Nobody honest will promise a specific grade from a specific number of sessions, and any provider willing to do so should be questioned rather than hired. What a final block can promise is that the student will have sat complete papers under time, had them marked against the real criteria, and been told plainly which topics are still costing marks. On IB session dates, work from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org, because no Diploma examination or results date is published on this page.

process.title: Name the route and the level first
process.description: Send four facts: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard or Higher Level, the school, and whether the exploration has been started. Those four decide which tutors are relevant and roughly what the two-year commitment will cost, before any rate is discussed.

process.title: Get a diagnostic read, not a sales call
process.description: The free trial lesson is one full session with no card details taken to book it. The tutor works through a past-paper question with your child and reports back on which topics are genuinely weak, whether the problem is technique or practice, and which component is costing the most marks.

process.title: Choose the plan that matches the diagnosis
process.description: A practice problem is a weekly hour. A content gap is a short intensive block first. An unstarted exploration is a six-session block with a deadline. Buying the wrong one of these three is the most common way money disappears in Diploma mathematics, and the diagnosis is what prevents it.

process.title: Fix the slot against the real evening
process.description: Secondary school days around The Greens finish between about 15:00 and 15:30, and buses and clubs push arrival later. Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time at a time the student is actually free, usually between 16:15 and 18:00, and they move rather than vanish when a fixture overruns.

process.title: Review against the calendar, in writing
process.description: Each session produces a short written note, and before each reporting period you get a view of which components are improving and which are not. Where the evidence says the plan should shrink, we say so. A weekly hour that is no longer needed is a cost rather than a safety net.

whyPoints.title: Rates on this page are the market's, not ours
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here comes from published Dubai rate cards and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, and is labelled as such. You can judge any quote against them, including ours. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Route and level stated before money moves
whyPoints.description: A tutor tells you whether they teach Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at which level, and when they last taught it. That one answer removes the most expensive mismatch in this subject, which is paying Higher Level rates for someone who last taught Standard Level two years ago.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own component
whyPoints.description: At Higher Level, Paper 3 is one hour and a fifth of the grade, and it is the component students can least prepare for alone. It gets its own sessions and its own timed practice rather than being folded into general revision, which is where most of its marks are quietly lost.

whyPoints.title: The exploration bought once, early
whyPoints.description: A block of around six sessions in Year 12 covers topic choice, the five criteria and feedback on the student's own drafts. Handled then, a fifth of the grade is banked at a predictable one-off cost instead of competing with examination revision in the spring of Year 13.

whyPoints.title: A line around assessed work that is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria and respond to drafts the student wrote. No one here writes the exploration or supplies a draft for submission. In a market where finished Internal Assessments are advertised at fixed prices, that boundary is what protects the candidate from a malpractice finding.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram has no office in Dubai and makes no home visits in the UAE; home visits exist only in India. The in-home rates quoted on this page belong to other providers and are shown so the premium is visible.

faqs.question: How much does IB maths tutoring cost for a family in The Greens?
faqs.answer: On published Dubai rates for 2026, qualified subject tutors online are advertised at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and Diploma specialists from about AED 200 to 450 and upwards. At one session a week that is around AED 600 to 1,200 a month in the middle of the market, rising to AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000 in an exam year according to Bestimate's Dubai cost table. Higher Level at two sessions a week roughly doubles it. None of those figures is an IB Gram price; they are here so you can judge any quote.

faqs.question: What does two years of DP maths support add up to in AED?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level on either route, one weekly hour across two years plus an exploration block lands somewhere in the mid-teens to mid-twenties of thousands of dirhams at published market rates. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, with one weekly hour in the first year and two in the second, the total runs from the mid-twenties into the high forties of thousands. The spread is wide because the Dubai market's hourly spread is wide, and because the month you start changes the number of weeks you buy.

faqs.question: Is Maths AA or Maths AI cheaper to tutor through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation is usually cheaper to support well, because the graphic display calculator is assumed throughout and fewer hours go on rebuilding by-hand technique. Analysis and Approaches has a non-calculator Paper 1 at both levels, which takes sustained practice rather than explanation. At Higher Level the gap widens again, since Analysis and Approaches carries a deeper calculus and proof requirement. The exploration costs the same on both routes, since it is twenty marks and a fifth of the grade either way.

faqs.question: Where do Greens parents waste money on IB maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four places, in order of cost. Paying specialist rates to a generalist who cannot teach Higher Level Paper 3. Buying thirty-six weekly sessions when the student needed six focused ones on the exploration. Starting in the spring of Year 13, when rates firm up and there is less course left to influence. And paying the in-home travel premium, quoted in Dubai from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, out of an evening window that is only about ninety minutes wide in this community.

faqs.question: Is a maths tutor charging AED 450 an hour worth it for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is specific rather than general. At the top of the published specialist band you should be buying something a mid-market tutor cannot do: Paper 3 investigations taught as a distinct skill, unstructured proof at Higher Level, and diagnosis precise enough to name two topics rather than describe a weakness. If the sessions look like homework help, the premium is buying nothing. Ask what the hour will contain before agreeing the rate, and ask when the tutor last taught that exact level.

faqs.question: How many IB maths sessions a week does an HL student actually need?
faqs.answer: One a week through the first year is usually enough if it is aimed at non-calculator technique rather than at homework, with a six-session exploration block in the second half of that year. Two a week from September of the second year is the realistic plan: one hour on content and technique, one on complete timed papers with Paper 3 handled separately. Students who try to compress all of that into the spring buy fewer usable weeks at higher prices and influence less of the course.

faqs.question: Can one maths tutor cover both Paper 3 and the IA?
faqs.answer: Yes, and there is a saving in it, because the same person already knows the student's working. The two jobs are different though. Paper 3 is timed, structured investigation practice where early errors cascade into later parts. The exploration is a written document assessed on five criteria, two of which reward reflection rather than mathematics. A tutor who treats them as one activity usually under-serves the exploration, so ask how the sessions will be split before booking a block.

faqs.question: Do IB maths tutoring rates rise closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: Quoted rates in the Dubai market tend to firm up as the session approaches, and availability tightens first. The larger cost is not the rate though. In February a tutor can only work with the course that remains, so the same money buys narrower work: timed paper technique and two topics rather than the foundational fluency that practice can still fix in October. Families who book the autumn pay the lower rate and get the wider job, which is why starting early is a pricing decision as much as an academic one.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths IA support block typically cost?
faqs.answer: Around six sessions covers topic choice, the five criteria letter by letter, the mathematics the student has chosen to use, and feedback on drafts the student has written. At published Dubai rates of roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour for a Diploma specialist, that is a one-off commitment of about AED 1,200 to 2,700. Run in Year 12 it is the best-value purchase in the course, because a fifth of the grade is settled early and does not compete with revision later.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student maths tutor a false economy at HL?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, often not. A capable graduate can run useful practice sessions for a student who understands the method and needs repetition, and the budget end of the Dubai market is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. At Higher Level the picture changes, because Paper 3 and unstructured proof reward someone who has taught or marked that specific component repeatedly. The cheap hour is good value for practice and poor value for technique, and most Higher Level students need both.

faqs.question: Does an in-home maths tutor in The Greens cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Yes, on published rates. In-home one-to-one visits in Dubai are quoted from about AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel built into the price, and monthly packages of four two-hour visits have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Online rates at the same qualification level sit lower. The extra buys transport rather than teaching, and in a community where the usable weekday window is roughly four o'clock to half past seven, it also costs evening minutes. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai.

faqs.question: Which Greens-area schools run Maths AA HL, and does that change the price?
faqs.answer: Several Diploma campuses within fifteen to thirty minutes of The Greens offer both mathematics routes, and the schools in the Emirates Living, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha clusters are the ones Greens students most often attend. Cohort size matters more than the school's name. The International Baccalaureate accounted for about seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, which is why Higher Level groups stay small, and a small group is precisely the situation where one-to-one support changes an outcome.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities care whether my child sat AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Individual programmes care, countries do not. Engineering, computer science and quantitative economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level; business, design, psychology and most health science programmes accept Applications and Interpretation. Check the published requirement for the specific programme and intake year. Separately, Ministry of Education equivalency on the American track specifies at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and no Diploma points threshold is published here because none has been read from a Ministry source.

faqs.question: We have six weeks until the maths exam. What can that money buy?
faqs.answer: If technique is sound and execution is weak, six weeks of timed papers and targeted review can move a grade, because the lost marks are recoverable through practice. If there is a genuine gap in calculus or non-calculator algebra, six weeks closes part of it and the rest appears in the hall. What it cannot touch is the exploration, which is a fifth of the grade already submitted. Start with one full timed paper, marked properly, then spend the block on the two topics it identifies.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy a block of maths sessions than to pay weekly?
faqs.answer: It is usually cheaper in total, because a block has an end date and a weekly arrangement does not. The honest comparison is not rate against rate but purpose against purpose. A block suits a defined job: the exploration, a bridging gap before Year 12, or a final push before the session. A weekly hour suits sustained practice through a difficult year. Families overspend by running a weekly arrangement past the point where it was needed, rather than by paying too much per hour.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-greens.closingHeading: Price the two years, then book the trial
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-greens.closingBody: Send the route, the level, the school and whether the exploration has started, and we will come back with tutors who teach that exact course, the hours they can hold in Gulf Standard Time, and a plan that says which of a weekly hour, a block, or both the diagnosis actually supports. The first session is free and needs no card details. Every figure quoted on this page is a published Dubai market rate rather than ours, and they are here so the quote you receive can be judged against something. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; there is no UAE office and no home visit.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are IB Mathematics teachers who work by course and component rather than by year group: Analysis and Approaches HL algebra and calculus, Applications and Interpretation statistics and modelling, Paper 3 problem sets, and exploration supervision. Pick on the component your child is losing marks in, not on proximity to The Lakes.

intro.heading: The cost question, answered before anybody pitches you
paragraphs: Most Lakes parents arrive at this search after a DP1 report that says "working below potential in Mathematics" and a WhatsApp group that has produced four numbers between AED 120 and AED 650 an hour. The spread is real, and it is not random. It tracks three things: whether the tutor teaches the exact course your child sits, whether the rate carries somebody's car across Dubai, and how close the May session is. Understanding those three variables is worth more than any list of tutor photographs, because it tells you which number on your shortlist is a fair price and which is a markup on convenience.

Start with the published market. Dubai providers who show their rates put a budget or university-student tutor between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour online, a qualified subject tutor between AED 150 and AED 300, an IB or IGCSE specialist between AED 200 and AED 450, and a premium named tutor at AED 500 to AED 650. In-home visits sit higher again, roughly AED 180 to AED 500 depending on distance and subject, because an hour of teaching inside a villa in Emirates Living costs the tutor two hours of their evening. None of those figures is our price list; they are what the market says, each attributable to the provider that published it, and they are the benchmark any quote you receive should be measured against.

The expensive mistake is not paying AED 300 an hour. It is paying AED 300 an hour for the wrong hour. A student who cannot reliably differentiate a quotient does not need three hours a week; they need four targeted hours on the chain and quotient rules, then a return to school homework. A student sitting Analysis and Approaches HL who has never seen a Paper 3 investigation under timed conditions is not helped by more Paper 2 practice, however cheap. Every dirham that goes into generic revision when the loss is diagnosable is a dirham that buys nothing, and in a two-year Diploma that compounds into five figures.

The second expensive mistake is the package bought before the diagnostic. Monthly bundles advertised in Dubai run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. A bundle is excellent value once the tutor is right and the plan is agreed. Bought in week one, it locks a family into a pairing nobody has tested, and the cancellation terms are where the goodwill goes. Pay for one or two diagnostic hours, read the written outcome, then commit.

The third is geography. Searching for a maths tutor within driving distance of The Lakes limits the pool to whoever happens to live between Al Barsha, The Greens and Emirates Hills and happens to be free at 17:00. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai - tutors travelling to homes is a service we run only in India - so the pool for a Lakes family is every available IB Mathematics specialist on Gulf Standard Time instead of everyone inside a twenty-minute drive. That is the practical argument for online delivery here, and the rate table further down shows what it saves.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.programmesIntro: Mathematics in an IB school is a twelve-year sequence, and a Lakes family usually meets it at three points: a PYP child who has stopped enjoying number work, an MYP student hitting the criterion-based mark scheme, and a DP student choosing between two courses that cost different amounts to support.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two separate courses, each at Higher and Standard Level. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route; Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology route. Standard Level is assessed by Paper 1 at 40%, Paper 2 at 40% and the exploration at 20%. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-part investigation, and the split becomes 30%, 30%, 20% and 20%.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the route choice is frequently made on timetable availability rather than on the degree the student wants, because not every IB school in the Emirates Living catchment can run four maths courses at once. One paid hour spent on AA versus AI before DP1 begins is the highest-value money in this entire price list.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Standard and Extended mathematics, assessed against four criteria each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student can be fluent in technique and still sit on a 4, because two of the four criteria reward explanation and investigation rather than answers.
programmes.countryNote: MYP mathematics is where Lakes families most often overpay, because the obvious fix - more practice questions - targets criterion A while the marks are being lost in B and C. A tutor who has read the criteria and marks against them is worth the qualified-tutor band; a tutor who sets worksheets is not.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Number, pattern and function, measurement, shape and space, and data handling, taught through transdisciplinary units rather than as a separate subject. Assessment is continuous and teacher-designed, so there is no paper to revise for and no mark scheme to drill.
programmes.countryNote: Primary maths support for a Lakes child is usually a short, cheap engagement - six to eight sessions on place value, fractions or times tables - and should be priced at the lower market band. Paying a Diploma specialist rate for a Year 4 number gap is the clearest waste in the Dubai tutoring market.

programmes.name: The IGCSE to Diploma maths bridge
programmes.description: Many students in the Emirates Living catchment sit Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE mathematics at 16 and then enter the Diploma. The gap is not content coverage; it is the jump from a mark scheme that rewards method to one that rewards reasoning, plus unfamiliar notation and a far heavier algebraic load in the first term of Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: A six-session summer bridge between Year 11 and DP1 is the single cheapest intervention on this page. Bought in August at the mid band it costs roughly what two months of panic tutoring costs in DP2, and it removes the term-one confidence collapse that generates most of the emergency calls we take from Dubai in October.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.subjectsIntro: Maths tutoring is sold by subject name and bought by component. The list below is organised the way a quote should be written: the course, the level, and the specific thing the hours are for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form, integration by substitution and parts, differential equations, Maclaurin series. Marks go missing in the algebra of a correct method rather than in the method itself, which is why timed non-calculator practice matters more than new content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Functions and transformations, sequences and series, trigonometry, differentiation and integration, probability and statistics. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so students who have done every exercise with technology are often a grade below their understanding.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Matrices, graph theory, Voronoi diagrams, non-linear regression, chi-squared and t-tests, and modelling with differential equations. The hardest marks are interpretive: stating whether a test's conditions are met, and what a coefficient means in the context given.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Descriptive statistics, correlation and regression, probability distributions, financial mathematics, and modelling with technology. Students lose marks by reporting output without interpreting it, and by rounding at intermediate steps instead of at the end.

subjects.name: Paper 3 investigations
subjects.description: Two extended problems, each building from a guided start to an open generalisation. This component rewards stamina and structured conjecture rather than recall, and it is the one place where a block of four or five tutored hours reliably changes a grade.

subjects.name: The Mathematics exploration
subjects.description: A twelve to twenty page individual piece of mathematics worth twenty per cent of the grade, marked against five criteria. The student chooses the topic and writes every line; a tutor's role is questions, deadlines and feedback on one draft within the school's internal policy.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.description: Regression, numerical solving, distributions, and sketching from a table of values. Calculator fluency is worth whole marks in Applications and Interpretation and in Analysis and Approaches Paper 2, and it is cheap to teach in two focused sessions.

subjects.name: MYP Extended Mathematics
subjects.description: The route into Analysis and Approaches HL, covering function families, algebraic manipulation and proof-shaped reasoning earlier than Standard mathematics does. Criterion B investigations are the usual mark loss: students find the pattern but do not justify the general rule.

subjects.name: MYP Standard Mathematics
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, assessed against four criteria out of eight each. The practical tutoring task is translating a 5 in criterion C into clearer written explanation, which is a writing problem wearing a maths hat.

subjects.name: Year 11 to DP1 maths bridge
subjects.description: Surds and indices without a calculator, function notation, the factor and remainder theorems, radian measure, and the early differentiation that DP1 assumes in week three. Six sessions over a Dubai summer, priced at the mid band, is the standard shape.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor in The Lakes actually costs
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor working with a family in The Lakes costs between roughly AED 150 and AED 450 an hour online in the Dubai market as of October 2026, with university-student help below that and named premium tutors above it. In-home visiting rates run higher, roughly AED 180 to AED 500, because the hour you pay for carries the travel either side of it. Those are market figures published by providers in this city, not an IB Gram price list; our own rate is quoted after a trial lesson and depends on course, level and frequency.

The reason the bands exist is specificity. A tutor who can teach GCSE maths accurately is not automatically able to teach Analysis and Approaches HL, where the content includes complex numbers, Maclaurin series and proof by induction and where Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. The pool of people who can teach that course well in any city is small, and small supply is what the specialist band is paying for. Applications and Interpretation HL has the same effect from the other direction: the statistics is genuinely university-level in places, and a tutor who has never run a chi-squared test on real data cannot teach the interpretation marks.

Read the table below as a benchmark rather than a menu. If a quote sits in the premium band, ask what in your child's situation requires it - a specific HL component, a six-week deadline - and if the answer is vague, the band is wrong for you. If a quote sits in the budget band for HL work, ask which course and which papers the tutor has taught, and ask it in those words. The gap between the honest answer and the confident answer is where most of Dubai's wasted tutoring money sits.

sections.heading: Four ways Emirates Living families overpay for maths
paragraphs: The first is buying hours instead of buying a diagnosis. A family forwards us a quote for twenty sessions and no written statement of what the student cannot currently do. Twenty sessions of unfocused support at the mid band is AED 3,000 to AED 6,000, and a two-hour diagnostic that produces a ranked list of recoverable topics costs a fraction of that and changes what the twenty sessions are for. Ask for the diagnosis in writing before you agree to the block.

The second is paying the specialist band for primary and lower-MYP work. A Year 5 child who has not secured place value, or an MYP 2 student stuck on negative indices, needs careful, patient teaching at the qualified band. The Diploma specialist whose value is Paper 3 and exploration supervision is not better at times tables; they are simply more expensive. Match the band to the problem.

The third is paying twice for the same hour through travel. An in-home tutor crossing Dubai to reach the Emirates Living gates at 17:00 has to recover that time, and it appears either as a higher rate or as a quiet surcharge nobody itemises. The fourth is the automatic renewal: a monthly bundle that made sense in November and is still running in March after the original gap closed. Diary a review date when you start, and treat the bundle as something that ends by default rather than continues by default.
None of these is a reason not to spend money on maths. They are reasons to know what each dirham is for, which is the difference between a tutoring budget and a tutoring habit.

The useful question is not whether AED 250 an hour is expensive in the abstract, but what a year of it looks like beside everything else a Lakes family already pays for a Diploma student. KHDA's announcement of 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, made under the emirate's second economic incentives package, is the right anchor: for most families the fee line is flat this year, which is precisely when a maths plan can be funded deliberately rather than in a panic.

The table below converts hourly bands into the periods families actually budget in. The two-year figures are the ones worth sitting with. One session a week for the whole Diploma at the mid band is a serious commitment, and a family who sees that total up front usually makes a better decision than one discovering it a month at a time. Frequently the better plan is a lighter year in DP1 with a bridge in the summer, then a heavier final term - the same total money, spent where it converts.

Exam entry costs are worth a note of their own. A student entered through their school pays through the school; a private candidate pays the centre directly and the figure varies by centre, so no single number belongs on a page like this. Ask the school's examinations officer for the written schedule rather than relying on a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets the bill
paragraphs: No decision in a Lakes family's Diploma affects the tutoring budget more than which maths course the student takes, and very few are made with less information. The two courses are not harder and easier versions of each other. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic: proof, calculus, trigonometric identities, and a Paper 1 sat with no calculator at all. Applications and Interpretation is interpretive and technological: modelling, statistics, graph theory, and a calculator in every paper. A student who thinks numerically but dislikes abstraction will spend fewer tutored hours on the second course than the first, and vice versa.

The university dimension matters and is often overstated by both sides. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses in the United Kingdom and the United States list Analysis and Approaches, usually at Higher Level, in their published entry requirements. Business, psychology, design and several life-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation comfortably. The honest position is that the requirement belongs to the specific university and the specific course, in writing, on that institution's own admissions page - and that a tutoring site is the wrong place to learn it.

What this page can tell you is the cost consequence. A student placed in Analysis and Approaches HL against their grain is the most expensive configuration in Dubai tutoring: they need weekly support for two years, then an intensive before the session, and the total runs well into five figures. The same student in Applications and Interpretation HL frequently needs a short block each term. One consultation before DP1 subject selection, paid at the specialist band, is the cheapest hour on this entire page.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty per cent of the grade, and the strict limits on help
paragraphs: The Mathematics exploration is worth twenty per cent of the final grade in every DP maths course, at both levels, and it is marked against five criteria totalling twenty marks. It is also the component where parents most often ask what a tutor is allowed to do, and where the wrong answer ends a Diploma. The boundary is not subtle: the student chooses the topic, does the mathematics and writes every word. A tutor teaches technique, asks questions, holds deadlines and gives feedback on a draft within the school's own internal policy. Anybody offering to supply finished text is offering the student an academic-honesty investigation.

Within that boundary the gains are real and cheap. Most explorations lose marks in presentation and communication rather than in mathematics: undefined variables, graphs without axis labels, a twenty-eight page document where twelve focused pages would score higher, and a reflection section that summarises rather than evaluates. Those are coachable in three or four sessions, and because criteria A, B, C and D account for fourteen of the twenty marks, they are better value than another pass through the content.

Timing is the other lever. A student who starts the exploration in the spring of DP1 has time for one proper draft and one round of feedback. A student who starts in the final term is paying specialist rates for crisis management while also revising for papers. The cheapest exploration is the early one, and the table below shows where the marks sit.

sections.heading: Online versus a tutor at the gate: the Emirates Living arithmetic
paragraphs: This comparison is usually presented as a question about learning style. In The Lakes it is mostly a question about time and supply. The community is a gated villa estate off Sheikh Zayed Road with internal cluster roads, and a tutor arriving for a 17:00 session from Al Barsha or the Marina is committing ninety minutes of driving to deliver sixty minutes of teaching. That cost is in the rate whether it is itemised or not, and it also decides who is available: only tutors who live close enough and are free in that window.

IB Gram delivers to The Lakes as one-to-one live video, and the reason is not cost alone. A Lakes family wanting Analysis and Approaches HL with strong Paper 3 teaching should be choosing from every available specialist on Gulf Standard Time, not from the subset who can reach Emirates Living before dinner. Home visits are not something IB Gram sells anywhere in the UAE - that is an India-only service - and the page would be dishonest if it implied otherwise. The trade is real: a parent cannot sit in the next room and overhear the lesson. What replaces it is a written note after each session, a shared screen the student can revisit, and a recording policy agreed in advance.

For maths specifically, online delivery has a technical advantage worth naming. Mathematics is written, not spoken, and a shared whiteboard with both parties writing keeps the working visible in a way a notebook on a dining table does not. Calculator teaching is easier too: the tutor can display the same model the student is holding, which is awkward across a kitchen table and trivial on screen.

sections.heading: The May session counted backwards from a Lakes kitchen table
paragraphs: Dubai IB schools sit the May session, and the budgeting mistake families make is treating May as the deadline. It is not; it is the last in a chain of deadlines that start in the previous calendar year, and the expensive tutoring is always the tutoring bought after one of the earlier ones has passed. Working backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today changes what a given month's money should buy.

A DP2 student's internal deadlines - exploration drafts, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge - are set by the school, not by the IB, and they cluster in the autumn and early winter term. That clustering is why November and December are the months when Lakes families most often double their tutoring spend: three internal deadlines and a mock series land inside six weeks. A plan that funds exploration coaching in DP1's summer term removes most of that collision for the price of four sessions.

We do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages. The IB's own site is the only acceptable source for them and it cannot be checked reliably by an automated process, so a specific date here would be a guess dressed up as a fact. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the school's dated internal calendar and the official session timetable, and build the plan on that document. Cambridge and Pearson publish their International GCSE timetables openly, which is why those dates appear on our IGCSE pages and IB dates do not.

sections.heading: Paying a maths tutor legally in Dubai, and what to ask for
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, which is useful information when you are comparing quotes. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists a two working-day completion time and is applied for through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences for a Lakes family. First, a tutor who tells you no permit exists or that it is optional is wrong: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. Second, the code of conduct attached to the permit, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff, bar a teacher from tutoring students enrolled at their own school. If the plan under discussion is your child's own classroom teacher, privately, that is the arrangement to decline.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram is an online matching platform, not a licensed Dubai training institute, and holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, IB or Cambridge accreditation. Any page telling you its tutors are regulator-approved is telling you something that cannot be true of an online platform.

sections.heading: What a trial lesson should tell you before you spend anything
paragraphs: The first lesson is a diagnostic, and it should be treated as the cheapest piece of market research available. IB Gram offers one trial lesson at no charge - thirty minutes, one per family, no card details taken and nothing to cancel - and the point is not to be charmed. The point is to find out whether this tutor can name, by the end of the session, the two or three specific things standing between your child and the next grade. A tutor who finishes a trial with 'we will build confidence' has not done the job. A tutor who finishes with 'she can integrate but she cannot choose a substitution, and her Paper 1 algebra breaks under time pressure' has.

Ask three questions in the trial. Which papers have you taught for this exact course, and in which years? What is the first topic you would work on with my child, and why that one? What will I receive in writing after each session? The answers tell you whether you are buying a specialist or a generalist, and whether the band you are being quoted matches what you are getting.

Then decide on a short commitment. Four sessions is enough to see whether the diagnosis was right and whether the student turns up willingly. If it works, extend; if it does not, change tutor without having prepaid a term. A family in The Lakes who spends two trial lessons and four paid sessions choosing carefully will usually spend less across a Diploma than one who commits to twenty sessions in October on a recommendation from a neighbour.

faqs.question: How much should an IB maths tutor for a family in The Lakes cost per hour in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates put a qualified online maths tutor at AED 150-300 an hour and an IB specialist at AED 200-450 or more; university-student help starts around AED 45-65 and named premium tutors reach AED 650. In-home visiting rates run roughly AED 180-500 because travel is inside the hour. Those are market figures from providers in this city as of October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our rate is quoted after the trial lesson and depends on the course, the level and how often you want sessions. Judge any quote by asking what in your child's situation justifies the band.

faqs.question: Is an online maths tutor genuinely cheaper than a home tutor for Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: On published market bands, yes, and the gap is mostly travel rather than teaching quality. Online one-to-one in Dubai runs AED 150-450 an hour; in-home one-to-one runs AED 180-500 for the same level of tutor, because a visit to a gated villa community costs the tutor roughly ninety minutes to deliver sixty. The second difference is supply: online you choose from every specialist on Gulf Standard Time rather than those who can reach The Lakes by 17:00. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so for a Lakes family the comparison is between our online delivery and a local in-home provider.

faqs.question: Why do IB maths rates sit above IGCSE maths rates in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: Supply. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, and the pattern holds across providers. The content is the reason: Analysis and Approaches HL includes proof by induction, complex numbers and Maclaurin series, Paper 1 is sat with no calculator, and Paper 3 is an open investigation. Far fewer tutors can teach that reliably than can teach IGCSE Extended maths, and scarcity sets the band. If a quote prices HL Diploma work at IGCSE rates, ask which papers the tutor has taught and in which years before taking it as good value.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an Analysis and Approaches HL student actually need?
faqs.answer: One a week through DP1 is the usual shape, rising to two in the final term if the mock series shows several unrecovered topics. That maps onto Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates of AED 600-1,200 for a weekly hour and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. More than two is rarely productive, because the student also needs time to attempt problems alone. The exception is a short component block, four to six sessions on Paper 3 or on non-calculator algebra, run at higher intensity over a fortnight and then stopped.

faqs.question: Should we buy a package of ten or twenty sessions up front?
faqs.answer: Not before a diagnostic. Bundles advertised in Dubai run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and they are good value once the tutor is right and the plan is agreed. Bought in week one they commit you to a pairing nobody has tested, and the cancellation terms are where families lose money. Take the trial, agree a block of four to six sessions with a stated end date, and only then consider a bundle. Diary a review date on the first invoice so the arrangement ends by default rather than continuing by default.

faqs.question: Is the rate in The Lakes quoted per hour or per lesson, and does it include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask both questions in writing before the first paid session, of us or of anybody else. A rate quoted per hour against a ninety-minute lesson is a different number from a rate quoted per session, and the two are mixed up constantly in this market. On tax, the only thing a tutoring page should state is whether its own quoted figure is inclusive; the VAT treatment of tuition in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not something to take from a tutoring site. Our quotes state the session length, the figure and whether tax is included.

faqs.question: Do we keep paying through Dubai school holidays and the summer break?
faqs.answer: Only if you want sessions. Billing per session rather than per term means a pause costs nothing, and for most students a genuine break is more useful than continuity for its own sake. The exception is the summer between Year 11 and DP1, where six sessions on surds, indices, function notation and early differentiation is the cheapest intervention available - it prevents the term-one collapse that generates most of the emergency calls we take from Dubai families in October. Short summer work before a transition year is worth funding; holiday cover for its own sake usually is not.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths AA and Physics to save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Analysis and Approaches and Diploma Physics overlap in calculus, vectors and graph interpretation, and a tutor strong in both can cut scheduling and sometimes the effective rate. The caution is depth: a physics teacher who is comfortable with SL maths is not automatically able to teach Paper 3 at Higher Level, and a maths specialist may not know the current physics assessment structure. Ask which of the two they have taught to examination and in which years. If the answer is one of them, use two tutors for the component that matters most.

faqs.question: Is the Mathematics exploration worth paying a specialist to support?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, and in a small number of sessions. The exploration is twenty per cent of the final grade, and fourteen of its twenty marks sit in presentation, communication, personal engagement and reflection rather than in the mathematics itself. Those are coachable: an undefined variable, an unlabelled graph, a reflection that summarises instead of evaluating. Three or four sessions in the spring of DP1 typically do more than the same hours spent on content. The limits are strict - the student chooses the topic, does the mathematics and writes every line, and a tutor gives feedback on one draft within the school's policy.

faqs.question: Does a private maths tutor working with Dubai families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through the MoHRE app, website or e-services system, and MoHRE's service page lists a two working-day completion. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts as unverified.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest route from a 4 to a 5 in Applications and Interpretation SL?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic, a ranked list, and four to six sessions on the top two items. At Standard Level in this course the recurring losses are predictable: reporting calculator output without interpreting it, rounding at intermediate steps, missing the conditions for a chi-squared test, and losing marks on financial mathematics through unit errors. Those are fixable in a short block rather than a term-long engagement. Add one session on calculator fluency, which is worth whole marks in both papers. The expensive route is open-ended weekly support that never names a target; the cheap route starts with a written diagnosis.

faqs.question: Do Dubai tutoring rates climb in the run-up to the May session?
faqs.answer: Effective prices do, for two reasons. Specialist availability thins through the final term, so the tutors still free are often the ones at the higher bands, and families booking in March usually want two sessions a week rather than one. Bestimate's monthly estimates reflect that pattern, with specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month against AED 600-1,200 for a weekly hour earlier in the year. The practical answer is to book the specialist you want in the autumn at the frequency you can sustain, rather than paying for intensity in April because nothing was done in November.

faqs.question: What should I send a tutoring provider to get an accurate quote rather than a range?
faqs.answer: Five things: the exact course and level, the school and year group, the most recent report with its grade or criteria scores, one marked piece of work that went badly, and the days and times that genuinely work around your school run. A marked paper is the most valuable of these, because it shows whether marks are lost in method, in algebra or under time pressure. With those five, a provider can name a band and a first target. Without them, any figure quoted is a guess, and guesses in this market drift upwards.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if the first tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: With per-session billing, nothing beyond the sessions already taught. That is the practical reason to avoid prepaying a term: a mismatch in week two should cost you two sessions, not twenty. Tell us what did not work - pace, explanation style, the time slot, the subject depth - and we propose a different tutor from the same course specialism. Say it early rather than politely waiting. A student who has quietly disengaged for a month is a more expensive problem to solve than a swap made after the second lesson.

faqs.question: Is a small group class in The Lakes better value than one-to-one maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether everyone in the group shares the same gap. Group rates in Dubai run roughly AED 60-200 an hour per student against AED 150-450 for one-to-one, so the saving is real. It evaporates when the group covers a topic your child already has and skips the one they do not, which is the common outcome with Diploma maths because the losses are individual. Groups work for broad revision and for younger students building fluency. For a diagnosed topic gap at Higher Level, four one-to-one sessions usually beat twelve group hours.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingHeading: Start with one hour that tells you what the next ten are for
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingBody: If you are weighing quotes for an IB maths tutor in The Lakes, the useful next step is not another recommendation from the community group. It is thirty minutes with a tutor who teaches your child's exact course, followed by a written note naming the two or three specific gaps and what to do about them. That costs nothing, takes one per family, and needs no card details. From there you can price a block of four to six sessions honestly, against the market bands on this page, and decide with numbers rather than hope. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, around the Emirates Living school run.

intro.heading: Buying maths tutoring by the hour is how families here lose money
paragraphs: The usual sequence in Emirates Living runs like this. A Diploma report in January shows a 4 in Mathematics where a 6 was expected. A tutor is found through a school-gate recommendation, a rate per hour is agreed, and a weekly session begins. Four months and roughly nine thousand dirhams later the grade has moved by half a band, because the sessions worked through topics while the marks were being lost somewhere the topics never touched. Nothing in that sequence was dishonest. It was simply priced on the wrong unit.

The unit that matters in Diploma maths is the component. Your child's final grade is assembled from two or three written papers plus an internally assessed exploration worth twenty per cent at both Standard and Higher Level. At Higher Level there is a third paper worth another twenty per cent. Each of those components rewards a different thing and fails for a different reason, and an hour of tutoring aimed at one of them does almost nothing for another. Before you agree a rate, it is worth knowing which component your money is meant to buy.

There is a second piece of arithmetic specific to this subject. There are four Diploma maths courses, not two: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. They have different content, different papers, different calculator rules and different university consequences. A tutor who says they teach "IB maths" has told you nothing. A family paying specialist rates for Higher Level support when the right answer was a change of level is paying for the problem rather than the solution, and in this neighbourhood that happens every year.

This page is therefore written as a pricing exercise rather than a pitch. It sets out the four courses side by side, the weighting of every component, the five lettered criteria that make up the exploration's twenty marks, the published Dubai market rates with the provider and date attached to each figure, and a straightforward table of what each kind of spend can and cannot realistically address. Where the honest answer is "do not buy tutoring for this", the page says so.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one live video tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses in The Meadows or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service our India operation runs, and the in-home rates quoted on this page belong to other providers in the Dubai market, not to us. What removing the drive buys a family in Meadows 6 is access to a tutor who has taught Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3, rather than the nearest adult who teaches maths.
