dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: Maths support means different things along the route through a Dubai international school, and the handover points are where the cost spikes. These four stages cover almost every enquiry that reaches us from Emirates Living.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across four strands, with extended and standard mathematics streams separating in the later years. Marks come from criteria rather than percentages, which confuses parents arriving from a percentage-based system and obscures a genuine algebra gap behind a respectable criterion score. The transition into Diploma maths is where that gap becomes visible and expensive.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills both run MYP, so a Meadows family may have one child on criteria and another on IGCSE grades in the same term. MYP extended mathematics is the usual feeder into Analysis and Approaches; students from standard mathematics who choose AA HL are the group that most often asks for help by November of Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one of four maths courses: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Two written papers at SL, three at HL, plus the exploration at twenty per cent. Content, calculator permissions and Paper 3 differ by course, and the choice is made in the first weeks of Year 12 with consequences that reach into university applications.
programmes.countryNote: The IB carried 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25 and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three further IB-curriculum schools. For a Meadows family the practical point is that the maths course is chosen on campus, often quickly, and reversing it later is a conversation with a school deadline rather than with the IB.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The route the majority of students around Emirates Living take at 16, with Cambridge 0580 tiered into Core and Extended and Pearson 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher. Two written papers, no coursework. A student finishing Extended or Higher tier with a grade 7 has the content base for Diploma SL maths; the gap to Analysis and Approaches HL is in unprompted reasoning rather than topics.
programmes.countryNote: Because IGCSE and the Diploma run in different schools within a few kilometres of each other here, families comparing notes across the community often compare incomparable things. A grade 9 at IGCSE and a 7 in AA HL are not adjacent achievements, and expectations set by the former are a common reason a Year 12 student is judged to be underperforming when they are not.

programmes.name: AS and A Level mathematics
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in the British-curriculum schools around The Meadows, with Mathematics and Further Mathematics as separate qualifications and no internally assessed component. Students choosing between A Level Maths and Analysis and Approaches HL are choosing between depth in fewer subjects and breadth across six, and the maths content overlap is substantial but the assessment style is not.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Emirates Living frequently hold this decision open into the spring of Year 11, and the maths question is usually the deciding one. The honest input a tutor can give is a diagnostic view of how the student handles unscaffolded problems, because that predicts AA HL performance better than an IGCSE grade does.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: The four maths courses are listed first because the distinction between them is the single most consequential thing on this page. The subjects after them are the ones most often paired with maths in a Diploma timetable, where a shared tutor sometimes makes sense and sometimes does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers at 30, 30 and 20 per cent plus the exploration at 20. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. The content runs deep into calculus, complex numbers, proof and series, and Paper 3 sets two extended problem-solving questions that reward sustained reasoning rather than recall. This is the course that generates the most tutoring demand in Dubai and the thinnest supply of genuine specialists.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers at 40 per cent each plus the exploration. Paper 1 is calculator-free, which is the detail most students underestimate: algebraic fluency has to be good enough to survive without a graphing display. Suits students who need recognisably algebraic mathematics for a university route but do not need the Higher Level content load.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Three papers at 30, 30 and 20 per cent plus the exploration, with a graphing calculator permitted throughout. Content leans into statistics, modelling, graph theory and matrices-based work, and Paper 3 sets extended data-led investigations. It is not an easier Higher Level; it is a different one, and students who move here from AA HL expecting relief are often surprised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Two papers at 40 per cent each with a calculator permitted throughout, plus the exploration. Statistics, functions and financial modelling dominate. The common failure is treating calculator availability as a substitute for understanding: the papers ask candidates to interpret output and justify a model, which a calculator cannot do for them.

subjects.name: Physics HL and SL
subjects.description: The most natural pairing with Analysis and Approaches, because the algebraic manipulation, graph interpretation and unit handling transfer directly. A tutor comfortable in both can genuinely save a family money. The limit is the scientific investigation, which has its own criteria and needs someone who has supervised one.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL and SL
subjects.description: Quantitative chemistry, energetics and equilibrium all depend on maths that a maths tutor can shore up, but the subject's grade is usually decided by organic mechanisms and the investigation, which are not maths problems. Pairing works for the calculation-heavy topics and stops there.

subjects.name: Economics HL and SL
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and quantitative work at HL make the maths overlap real, particularly in elasticity and market analysis. The grade, however, sits largely in evaluation and in the internal assessment commentaries, which reward a judgement supported by evidence rather than a correct calculation.

subjects.name: Computer Science HL and SL
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, logic and complexity sit close to Applications and Interpretation content, and students strong in one are often strong in the other. The internally assessed solution is a substantial independent project with its own criteria and timeline, and it is the component that most often slips.

subjects.name: Business Management HL and SL
subjects.description: Financial and quantitative tools, break-even analysis and ratio work give a maths tutor something concrete to help with. Everything else in the subject, and most of the grade, is case-study analysis and the internally assessed project, which need a subject specialist rather than a mathematician.

subjects.name: Biology HL and SL
subjects.description: The statistical and data-handling demands have grown, and students who cannot read error bars or interpret a correlation lose marks that look like biology marks. Beyond that the subject diverges completely from maths, and sharing a tutor across the two is rarely a saving worth making.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Not a maths course, but the exhibition and essay are assessed and mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge students write about. Support means teaching how the assessment instrument works and giving feedback on the student's own argument, never supplying the argument.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay in mathematics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay, supervised by the school. Choosing mathematics as the subject is harder than students expect, because a mathematically trivial question cannot earn the higher bands and an overambitious one cannot be completed. A tutor's role is process coaching and feedback; the research and the writing are the student's.

regions.note: The densest population of private tutors within reach, and where the highest local rates are quoted. Families from Emirates Living who drive here for maths sessions are paying twice: once in fees and once in the commute.

schoolClusters.city: IB schools within reach of a Meadows address
schoolClusters.note: Where Diploma maths is actually taught near Emirates Living. The course offer differs by school: not every campus runs all four maths courses at both levels, which is itself a reason a student ends up on the wrong one.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools in the same catchment
schoolClusters.note: The alternative post-16 route for the same neighbourhood, and the reason parents here compare A Level Maths against Analysis and Approaches HL at Year 11 options evenings rather than at results.

schoolClusters.city: The newer Al Barsha South and Motor City campuses
schoolClusters.note: Growth-corridor schools with expanding sixth forms. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven private schools and 16,846 places across the emirate, three of them IB-curriculum, so the local Diploma cohort is still growing.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.modesIntro: Each format below is one tutor to one student over live video, and each is priced for a different component of the grade. Choosing the format is the decision that controls the bill; choosing the rate barely moves it.

modes.title: Component diagnostic
modes.description: Two sessions whose only purpose is to establish which component is losing the marks. A timed Paper 1 section without a calculator, a timed Paper 2 section with one, and a look at the exploration draft if there is one. The output is a written allocation of the lost marks across components, which is what every later decision should be based on.

This is the cheapest money per mark in Diploma maths because the content is still being delivered in class, and it leaves marked timed evidence behind in time for the level decision to be made properly.

sections.heading: Which of the four Diploma maths courses is your child actually taking?
paragraphs: Before any rate is discussed, settle this. Every Diploma student takes one of four maths courses: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher or Standard Level, or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher or Standard Level. They differ in content, in the number of papers, in whether a graphing calculator is permitted, and in what universities make of them. A tutor who describes themselves as an IB maths tutor without naming one of those four has given you no information at all, and a quote offered on that basis cannot be evaluated.

The calculator rule alone changes the work. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which makes algebraic fluency a graded skill in its own right. In Applications and Interpretation, a graphing calculator is permitted in every paper, which shifts the examined skill towards selecting a method, interpreting output and justifying a model. A student who has spent a term rehearsing calculator-free manipulation for the wrong course has spent that term usefully in general terms and wastefully in exam terms.

The exploration is the one component common to all four. It is internally assessed, externally moderated and worth twenty per cent of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level, and it is marked out of twenty raw marks across five lettered criteria. Those twenty marks are the largest single block of the grade available outside an examination hall, they are earned over months rather than hours, and they are also the component with the strictest rules about what help is permitted. The table below sets the four courses out side by side.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: where the marks are, and therefore where the money goes
paragraphs: A component-level view changes what a sensible tutoring plan looks like. At Standard Level, eighty per cent of the grade sits in two ninety-minute papers and twenty per cent in a document written over several months. At Higher Level the examined share is split three ways, with Paper 3 carrying twenty per cent on its own across just two extended questions in sixty minutes. Paper 3 is the component most frequently ignored by tutors and most frequently decisive for students aiming at a 6 or a 7.

Each paper fails differently. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 punishes weak algebraic manipulation, because there is no calculator to rescue a line of working. Paper 2 punishes poor calculator technique as much as poor mathematics: students lose marks entering a function incorrectly, failing to sketch what they are solving, or quoting a display value to the wrong accuracy. Paper 3 punishes students who have only ever answered short questions, because it requires a line of reasoning sustained across a long structured problem with unfamiliar framing.

This is why an hour of generic topic revision is poor value late in the course. If the diagnostic shows that a student understands the content but is losing method marks and accuracy marks, the fix is a short technique block, not thirty weeks of teaching. If the loss sits in Paper 3, the fix is extended-problem practice with marked feedback, which is a specific and scarce skill. The table below gives the component structure and what each one repays.

sections.heading: The calculator-free paper is a separate subject
paragraphs: In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 at both levels is sat without a calculator, and students in Dubai schools arrive at it after years of permanently available technology. The consequence is predictable and specific: candidates who can solve a problem correctly with a graphing display cannot reliably manipulate the same expression by hand, and the marks lost are not conceptual. They are arithmetic slips, abandoned surds, mishandled indices and fractions left in forms that make the next line impossible.

The fix is mechanical and cheap, which is why it is worth identifying early. Four to six sessions spent exclusively on calculator-free manipulation, with short timed sets marked for accuracy rather than understanding, typically moves more marks than a term of topic teaching. The diagnostic signal is easy for a parent to read: if your child's school marks show a consistent gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 performance, you have found the problem and it is a technique problem.

Applications and Interpretation has the mirror-image version of this. A graphing calculator is permitted throughout, and students lose marks precisely because they assume the tool removes the need for judgement. The papers ask candidates to choose a model, interpret output and justify a conclusion in context, and a correct number with no interpretation earns a fraction of the available marks. A short block on tool use and on writing the interpretation sentence is, again, the cheapest intervention available in the course.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The exploration is the only part of a Diploma maths grade that is produced outside an examination hall, and it carries twenty per cent at both levels. It is marked out of twenty raw marks across five criteria, each with its own letter and allocation: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Students routinely lose marks in the first four while concentrating entirely on the fifth, because nobody has explained to them that half the available marks are for how the work is presented, communicated and reflected upon.

Two failures dominate, and both are about timing rather than mathematics. The first is topic choice: a question that is mathematically trivial cannot reach the higher bands no matter how neatly it is written, and a question that is wildly overambitious cannot be completed to a standard. Deciding this in week two rather than week eight is worth several marks and several weeks. The second is reflection, which has to be woven through the work rather than appended as a paragraph at the end, and which students almost always treat as a conclusion.

The boundary on help is strict and worth stating in writing before any session is booked. A tutor may explain each criterion and its mark allocation, discuss whether a proposed task carries enough mathematics for the course, teach the mathematics the student needs, teach what good notation and reflection look like, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the topic, perform the mathematics that appears in the report, supply the reflection, or rewrite or edit the work to completion. The qualification belongs to the student, and crossing that line risks the qualification rather than the fee.

sections.heading: Price per mark: the cost question families here never ask
paragraphs: Start at the cheapest end and work upwards, asking what each additional hundred dirhams actually buys. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is published from the low double digits an hour: EdFlik advertises AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. What that money buys is a competent graduate who can answer questions on homework. What it generally does not buy is somebody who knows that Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is calculator-free or that the exploration is marked out of twenty across five lettered criteria, and for a Diploma student those two facts are worth more than a term of homework help.

The next step up, AED 150 to 300 an hour, is where qualified subject tutors sit; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the band in which a tutor can reasonably be expected to name the components, mark timed work against published criteria and produce a written diagnostic. Above it, IB and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and more, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table showing AED 200 to 450 and upwards for specialist exam-year support. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500, on Bestimate's AED 180 to 350 band plus independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and the premium end runs higher still, with BartyED published at AED 650.

Monthly figures make the commitment legible. Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 a month for a weekly hour at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, while published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure here belongs to the named provider and was read from its published material in October 2026. None is an IB Gram price: we offer a free trial lesson and a consultation instead of a rate card, because the course, the component and the number of weeks change the answer entirely. sections.heading: The level change that saves more than any discount
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in Diploma maths is not an hourly rate. It is a student sitting a course that was never the right fit, supported by increasing quantities of tutoring that are buying ground rather than gaining it. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is the usual case. A student arrives from a strong IGCSE grade, chooses it because the engineering ambition seemed to require it, and spends Year 12 at a 3 while a family in Meadows 5 spends AED 1,200 a month holding the line.

The alternatives are real and they are not failure. Analysis and Approaches Standard Level keeps the algebraic character of the course with a far lower content load. Applications and Interpretation Higher Level keeps a Higher Level on the transcript with a different content emphasis, which suits data-facing degrees. Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is the right answer for a number of students who took AA SL because somebody told them it looked better. In every case the change has to go through the school, has a deadline set by the school rather than by the IB, and gets harder the longer it is left.

The honest input a tutor can give here is diagnostic rather than commercial, and it is worth noticing that the incentive runs the other way. Two sessions of unscaffolded problem work will tell you whether a student is struggling with the content of the course or with the course itself. If it is the course, say so and act early. The money saved by a well-timed level change is measured in thousands of dirhams and a far better final grade, and no rate negotiation in this market comes close to it. University prerequisites should be checked on each programme's own published entry requirements rather than assumed, because the assumption that Higher Level is always required is the belief that keeps students in the wrong course.
bullets: Four courses, so a change of emphasis is available without dropping a level

sections.heading: Mock season and the predicted grade: the weeks that decide university offers
paragraphs: For a Diploma student the mock examinations are not a rehearsal. They are, in most schools, the main evidence base for the predicted grade that goes out with university applications, and a predicted grade sets which offers are available long before a final result exists. That makes the autumn and winter of Year 13 the highest-leverage weeks in the two-year programme, and it makes work scheduled into them qualitatively different from work scheduled in the spring.

The planning consequence runs backwards. If predicted grades are formed on mock performance, then the term before the mocks is the term in which tutoring changes an offer, and the term after them is the term in which tutoring changes a final grade. Those are different objectives and they justify different spending. Families in Emirates Living who start in January of Year 13 are buying the second one and assuming they have bought the first, which is the single most common misallocation we see in Diploma maths.

Exact dates belong to your child's school rather than to this page. Mock windows, internal deadlines for the exploration and the Extended Essay, and the school's own deadline for predicted grades are all set on campus, and the IB's published session dates should be confirmed against ibo.org or with the school's IB coordinator before anything is planned around them. What is safe to say is the shape: the examined session UAE schools sit is the May one, the internal deadlines land months earlier, and the mocks sit earlier still. Ask the coordinator for all three dates in one email at the start of Year 13 and plan from that, not from a tutor's calendar.

sections.heading: What tutoring cannot buy, and what to do about those gaps instead
paragraphs: Three common problems in Diploma maths are not maths problems, and paying maths rates to solve them is poor value. The first is reading the question. A student who consistently answers an adjacent question, or who misses a condition stated in the stem, is losing marks to a comprehension habit. It is fixable, often quickly, but the fix is a rehearsed reading routine applied to every question, which a parent can enforce at home for nothing once a tutor has demonstrated it.

The second is writing method down. Diploma mark schemes allocate method marks, and a student who writes only answers forfeits them even when the thinking was correct. This is behavioural rather than conceptual, and it responds to short, frequent, marked practice with the mark scheme visible. Paying a specialist AED 300 an hour to repeat the instruction weekly is expensive; having the student self-mark five questions against the published scheme twice a week is free and works better.

The third is exam timing. Students who leave a fifth of a paper unattempted are not short of knowledge; they are short of pace, and pace comes from sitting full papers under timed conditions, which schools do too rarely. The useful tutoring contribution is to mark those papers properly and categorise the losses. The sitting itself can happen at a kitchen table in The Meadows on a Saturday morning with a timer, and it costs nothing at all. A tutor who tells you this is giving you better value than one who sells you the hour.
bullets: Reading the question: a routine, demonstrated once, then enforced at home

sections.heading: Paying a tutor properly in Dubai, and the equivalency question behind it
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE operates on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a stated two working days, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any amount circulating in a parents' group is rumour.

A second rule constrains the arrangement families most want. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify against the current policy document, but do not plan around hiring your child's own maths teacher. A specialist who has taught the same course elsewhere brings the same knowledge without the conflict.

The equivalency question arrives later and is worth knowing early. For Ministry of Education certificate equivalency on the British track, reporting in July 2026 set the requirement at five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is set at IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Math. That reporting states no IB points threshold, so none is published here: verify any IB figure on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it.

sections.heading: Starting maths support from The Meadows, with the costs stated first
paragraphs: The first thing we will ask is which of the four courses your child sits and at which level, followed by the most recent marked evidence you have: a school assessment, a mock paper, an exploration draft. The second is what time a session can realistically start given which part of The Meadows you live in, because a Meadows 7 bus arriving at 4:20pm makes a 4:30pm slot a fiction. Then a free 45-minute trial with the tutor who would actually teach, not a consultant, and no card details are required to book it.

Our recommendation will sometimes be to spend less rather than more. If the diagnostic shows the loss is calculator-free technique, we will say four to six sessions and a stop date rather than a term. If it shows the student is in the wrong course, we will say so and suggest you take that to the school before buying anything. If the issue is exam pace, we will tell you to sit papers at home under a timer and pay us only to mark them. None of that is generosity; it is what makes the recommendation worth listening to on the occasions when it is to spend more.

The limits, stated before you book. Availability for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and for Paper 3 preparation is the thinnest in this subject, and in the weeks before the May session it thins further because demand across Dubai peaks at once; where no UAE-based tutor covers the course and slot, the match may be an experienced Diploma maths specialist teaching from elsewhere on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time slot, and we say so in advance. No tutor will promise a grade. No tutor will produce any part of the exploration. No tutor will come to a villa in Emirates Living, because in-home visiting is not a service we sell in the UAE. And nothing here claims approval, accreditation or partnership with the IB, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, because IB Gram holds none and describing a tutor as an IB examiner without evidence is a claim we do not make.

process.title: Name the course, not the subject
process.description: Tell us whether it is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. Those four combinations have different papers, different calculator rules and different Paper 3 situations. A quote given without that information cannot be compared against anything, and a tutor who does not ask is not reading the assessment.

process.title: Send the most recent marked evidence
process.description: A school assessment with marks, a mock paper, a returned past paper, or an exploration draft. Marks out of a known total are worth more than any description of how the term has gone, because they let a tutor allocate the loss across components before the first session rather than after the fifth.

process.title: Buy the diagnostic before the package
process.description: Two sessions that produce a written allocation of lost marks by component and cause, plus a recommendation on where the next ten hours should go. This is the cheapest money in the subject and the step most often skipped, because it feels like a delay before the help starts rather than the thing that aims it.

process.title: Choose the component, then the format
process.description: Calculator-free technique, graphing-calculator fluency, Paper 3 extended problems and exploration feedback are four different purchases with different session counts and end dates. Deciding which one you are buying controls the total bill far more than negotiating the hourly rate ever will.

process.title: Review against the diagnostic monthly
process.description: Once a month, compare the error log against the original component allocation. If a named loss has not moved in four weeks, change the method or the tutor. Agreeing that trigger before the first invoice converts a difficult conversation into an administrative one, and avoids the term-long drift that costs more than any rate.

process.title: Get the three school dates in one email
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator for the mock window, the internal exploration and Extended Essay deadlines, and the school's own deadline for predicted grades. Those three dates determine what tutoring is for in each term. Session dates for the examined session should be confirmed with the coordinator or on ibo.org, not taken from a tutor.

whyPoints.title: Priced by component, not by the hour
whyPoints.description: The plan starts from which component is losing marks, because an hour aimed at Paper 1 technique does almost nothing for Paper 3 or for the exploration. That is the difference between tutoring that moves a grade and tutoring that fills a weekly slot with competent teaching.

whyPoints.title: Every rate attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page belong to EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, Bestimate, TutorChase and BartyED, read from their own published material in October 2026. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you to spend less
whyPoints.description: Where the fix is a short technique block, a level change or sitting timed papers at a kitchen table for nothing, we say so. A recommendation to spend more is only worth hearing from somebody who has previously recommended spending less.

whyPoints.title: The exploration boundary in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains the five criteria, teaches the mathematics and gives feedback on drafts. The student chooses the task, does the mathematics and writes every word submitted. That line is published because the opposite is openly sold in this market and it is the student's qualification at stake.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of a Higher Level grade sits in two extended questions in sixty minutes, and almost nobody prepares for it specifically. Where a tutor with that experience is not available at the time you need, we tell you before you book rather than after.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credibility
whyPoints.description: No IB session dates are published here, because the IB's own site could not be verified for this project; confirm them with your coordinator. No tutor is described as an IB examiner without evidence. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB, KHDA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education and runs no UAE office.

faqs.question: How do I tell which of the four Diploma maths courses my child is taking?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the subject title in full, which will be either Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, plus the level. The distinction matters because it sets the calculator rules, the content and whether a Paper 3 is sat. Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without a calculator at both levels; Applications and Interpretation permits a graphing calculator in every paper. Higher Level in both courses adds a Paper 3 worth twenty per cent. A tutor who offers a quote without asking which of the four applies is not reading the assessment your child faces.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 worth paying for separately at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It carries twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade across two extended questions in sixty minutes, and it is the component tutors most often skip. If a student is losing marks there specifically, a short block of extended-problem practice with marked feedback is one of the better-value purchases in the course, because the skill, sustaining a line of reasoning through an unfamiliar problem, is not built by answering short questions. At Standard Level the question does not arise, since Paper 3 is not sat. The diagnostic should tell you which situation you are in before you buy anything.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well on Paper 2 and badly on Paper 1?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches that pattern almost always means technique rather than content, because Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Paper 2 is not. Students in Dubai schools have had technology available throughout, so manipulation by hand is the skill that atrophies: surds, indices, fractions and algebraic rearrangement. The fix is mechanical and cheap, typically four to six sessions of short timed sets marked for accuracy rather than understanding. A consistent gap between the two papers in school marks is the clearest diagnostic signal available to a parent, and it points at a cheap intervention.

faqs.question: What are the five criteria for the maths exploration and what are they worth?
faqs.answer: Presentation carries four marks, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three and use of mathematics six, giving twenty raw marks in total and twenty per cent of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level. Students typically concentrate entirely on the mathematics and lose marks across the other four criteria, which between them carry fourteen of the twenty. Notation and defined variables are marked. Reflection must run through the work rather than sit at the end. Knowing the allocation before drafting starts is worth more than any amount of later polishing.

faqs.question: What kind of exploration help stays inside the IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a boundary that should be written down first. A tutor may explain each criterion and its marks, discuss whether a proposed task carries enough mathematics for the course, teach the mathematics required, show what good notation and genuine reflection look like, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the topic, perform the mathematics that appears in the report, supply the reflection, or edit the work to completion. The qualification belongs to the student, and crossing that line puts the qualification at risk rather than the fee.

faqs.question: What should a Diploma maths tutor cost per hour in Dubai right now?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 ran roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200; AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270; and AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits including travel. BartyED is published at AED 650 at the premium end. None of those is an IB Gram price. We publish a free trial lesson and a consultation instead, because the course and the component change the answer.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation an easier course than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is a different course, not a lighter one, and students who move expecting relief are often surprised. Applications and Interpretation emphasises statistics, modelling and interpretation with a graphing calculator permitted throughout, and its papers ask candidates to choose a model, read output and justify a conclusion in context. A correct number with no interpretation scores a fraction of the marks available. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic method, calculus and proof, and sits Paper 1 without a calculator. Which is harder depends entirely on the student; which is right depends on the university route they intend.

faqs.question: Can my child change maths course or level after starting Year 12?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the deadline is set by the school rather than by the IB, which is why acting early matters more than anything else about it. There are four courses, so a change of emphasis is available without necessarily dropping a level: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level to Applications and Interpretation Higher Level keeps a Higher Level on the transcript. Two diagnostic sessions on unscaffolded problems usually settle whether the difficulty is the content or the course. If it is the course, the money saved by a timely change exceeds anything a rate negotiation can achieve.

faqs.question: Does my child need Analysis and Approaches Higher Level for engineering?
faqs.answer: Check the published entry requirements for each specific programme rather than assuming, because the assumption is what keeps students in a course that is not working for them. Quantitative degrees commonly list Analysis and Approaches, and some list a Higher Level requirement, but the detail varies by university, by country and by programme, and several routes accept Applications and Interpretation. Each university publishes its own requirements and those are the only reliable source. A tutor stating a requirement from memory is guessing, and in this market that guess has kept a lot of students in the wrong course.

faqs.question: How much maths tutoring does a Diploma student in Emirates Living usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which component is losing marks, which is the argument for buying a diagnostic first. A Year 12 student drifting on content typically needs one weekly hour through the year. A Year 13 student losing method and accuracy marks often needs four to six focused sessions and a stop date, not a term. Exploration support is usually three to five sessions spread across the drafting period. Paper 3 work is a short block of extended problems. Buying a package of hours before knowing which of those applies is how families here end up paying for the wrong thing competently delivered.

faqs.question: Why do mock examinations matter more than the final mocks suggest?
faqs.answer: In most schools they are the main evidence base for the predicted grade sent with university applications, which means they help determine which offers exist long before a final result does. That makes the term before the mocks the one in which tutoring can change an offer, and the term after them the one in which it can change a final grade. Those are different objectives with different price tags. Families who begin in the January of Year 13 are generally buying the second while believing they bought the first, which is the most common misallocation we see.

faqs.question: Can we sit timed papers at home instead of paying for the session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you should. Exam pace is built by sitting full papers under timed conditions, and that can happen at a kitchen table in The Meadows on a Saturday morning with a timer and a printed paper at no cost. The part worth paying for is the marking: proper marking against the published scheme, with losses categorised by cause, is what turns a score into a plan. A tutor who suggests this arrangement rather than selling you the sitting is giving you better value, and it is a reasonable thing to ask for directly.

faqs.question: Will you publish the IB exam dates for the next session?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth stating. The IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project, so no session or results date in this set is confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate dates that look plausible and are sometimes wrong, and planning a revision programme around a wrong date is worse than planning around none. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the session window, the internal deadlines and the school's predicted-grade deadline in one email, or confirm on ibo.org. UAE schools sit the May session; that much is safe to plan around.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working with Dubai families need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE operates under the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and covering registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listed with no fee and two working days. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are rumour. Asking about the permit is an ordinary question.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points requirement for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not one that can be responsibly published here. The July 2026 reporting that sets out the British and American track requirements states no IB points threshold, so any figure quoted elsewhere is unsourced as far as this project is concerned. On the British track the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. Verify any IB figure on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. Equivalency is a Ministry process and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: What if no Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than after, with the alternative named. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and Paper 3 preparation are the thinnest parts of this subject's supply anywhere, and in the weeks before the May session they thin further because demand across Dubai peaks simultaneously. Where no UAE-based tutor covers the course at the slot you need, the match may be an experienced Diploma maths specialist teaching from outside the UAE on the same live video format and the same Gulf Standard Time schedule. Disclosing a coverage limit up front is the point; concealing it until after payment is the market norm.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingHeading: Price the component, not the hour
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-meadows.closingBody: Find out which of the four Diploma maths courses your child sits, gather the most recent marked evidence, and work out which component the marks are leaving from before you agree any rate. Then tell us the course, the level and the earliest realistic start time from your part of The Meadows, and take the free 45-minute trial with the tutor who would teach the term. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is a short block, a level change or marking papers you sit at home, you will hear that first.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Mathematics to students in The Springs and the wider Emirates Living cluster. Each one specialises in either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation rather than claiming both, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: The cheapest maths tutoring is the kind that starts in the right course
paragraphs: Most cost conversations about Diploma mathematics start at the wrong end. A parent in The Springs asks what an hour costs, compares two quotes, and picks the cheaper one. Six months later the family has spent somewhere between AED 3,000 and AED 9,000 and the predicted grade has not moved. The money was not wasted because the rate was wrong. It was wasted because nobody established, in the first hour, which of four distinct courses the student is on and which component of the grade is actually failing.

IB Mathematics is four separate subjects wearing one name. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation each run at Standard and Higher Level, and they assess genuinely different things. A tutor who is strong on AA Higher Level proof by induction may be the wrong person for an AI Standard Level student struggling with regression and Voronoi diagrams. A Springs family that pays specialist rates for the wrong specialism gets a pleasant hour a week and no change in the mark.

The second thing that quietly decides cost is the shape of the grade. At Standard Level there are two papers weighted forty per cent each and an exploration worth twenty. At Higher Level there are three papers, weighted thirty, thirty and twenty, with the exploration again at twenty. That means a fifth of a Higher Level grade sits in a single sixty-minute paper that almost nobody prepares for properly, and another fifth sits in a document written at home with no timetabled teaching attached. Those two components are where tutoring hours have the clearest return, and they are the two most families buy last.

This page is written from cost outwards, with the figures attributed. Published Dubai market rates are set out with the provider that publishes each band, so a quote you receive from anyone can be judged against them. Where the money goes wrong in Emirates Living households is named specifically: the wrong course, the generalist maths tutor, the group class pitched at a different level, and the April start in the second year of the Diploma. None of those are rate problems.

What should also be clear from the start is how the teaching arrives. All UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. For a maths lesson this is close to an advantage rather than a compromise: a shared digital whiteboard keeps every worked solution in one place, which a paper exercise book at a kitchen table does not, and a student revising in March can scroll back to the derivation they were shown in October.

One more framing point before the figures. Everything below is written for a family that has not yet spent anything, which is the moment when a few questions are worth more than any amount of money. By the time a Springs household is eight lessons into the wrong arrangement, the sunk cost makes it harder to stop, and the second-year calendar makes it harder to switch. The order matters: establish the route, find the failing component, then compare rates.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: A Springs household buying maths support is usually at one of three points: approaching the Diploma, inside it, or about to be assessed by it. The money behaves differently at each point, so the stages are worth separating.

programmes.name: MYP 5 or Year 11 into the Diploma
programmes.description: The cheapest maths intervention available, and the one almost nobody buys. Six to ten lessons across the summer before DP1 close the algebraic-fluency gap that otherwise costs an entire first term. Students arriving from MYP criterion assessment or from IGCSE 0580 both need this, but for different reasons.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates Living feeds both IB and British campuses, so Springs students enter DP1 from two different places. An MYP 5 student has done investigations and criterion marking but may have thin procedural fluency. An IGCSE 0580 Extended student has strong procedure and no experience of an extended piece of independent mathematical writing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: The year where the route decision becomes irreversible and the exploration should start. Spending here is low-intensity and high-return: one weekly slot that keeps pace with the school, plus a short block in the summer term to choose and scope the exploration topic before it becomes urgent.
programmes.countryNote: DP1 is also when a Springs family discovers whether the school's set placement matches the student. Moving from Higher to Standard Level is usually possible early in DP1 and progressively harder after that, and it is a decision worth taking with a tutor's diagnostic rather than on a single test result.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Year 2
programmes.description: The expensive year, because demand spikes across Dubai and because families arrive late. Hours here go on examination technique, Paper 3 at Higher Level, and finishing the exploration properly. Content teaching is still possible but costs more per mark gained than the same teaching twelve months earlier.
programmes.countryNote: The exploration deadline set by a Dubai school usually sits well before the external deadline, because the school needs time to authenticate and mark internally. Ask for that internal date in September of DP2 and work backwards from it rather than from anything published by the IB.

programmes.name: After the Diploma
programmes.description: Where the route choice is finally priced. Engineering, physics and mathematics programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level; business, economics and social-science programmes more often accept Applications and Interpretation. The requirement belongs to the individual programme, not to the country.
programmes.countryNote: Check the named programme's own admissions page rather than a general statement about the UAE or the UK, because requirements differ between universities and between faculties inside one university. A student who needs AA and is sitting AI should find out in DP1, when a change is still practical.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics is five topic areas plus a toolkit, and the cost of help varies sharply between them. These are the areas Springs families most often ask about, with what each one actually rewards.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents and logarithms at both levels; binomial theorem, proof by induction, complex numbers and partial fractions at AA Higher Level. Weak algebraic fluency here shows up as lost marks in every other topic, which is why diagnostics almost always start with it.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Transformations, rational functions, inverse and composite functions. AA Higher Level adds a much heavier algebraic load. Students who can sketch a graph on a calculator but cannot reason about a function without one lose marks on the non-calculator paper.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations in AA; three-dimensional geometry, Voronoi diagrams and graph theory in AI. Vectors sit at Higher Level in both routes with different emphases. This is where mark loss is most often about unit and diagram discipline rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Core to AI at both levels and lighter in AA. Binomial and normal distributions, regression, correlation and hypothesis testing. AI Higher Level students need confident calculator work plus the ability to interpret what the output means in context, which is where most of the marks actually sit.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, with AA Higher Level extending into Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation and differential equations. The commonest expensive gap in DP2: a student who can differentiate but cannot choose a technique under time pressure.

subjects.name: The toolkit and mathematical inquiry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: The modelling and investigation strand that underpins the exploration. Rarely timetabled as its own lesson, which is exactly why it is worth tutoring hours. Learning to pose a question that can be answered mathematically is the skill the exploration criteria reward most.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: A twelve-to-twenty-page independent piece worth twenty per cent of the final grade in every route. Assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. A tutor may coach the process and give feedback; the mathematics and the writing must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Higher Level Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended response questions in sixty minutes, worth twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade. It rewards sustained reasoning across a structured investigation rather than recall. Most students meet their first full Paper 3 weeks before the examination, which is late.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: A graded expectation rather than a convenience. AI requires calculator fluency on every paper; AA requires it on Paper 2 only, which means AA students must be able to work without one on Paper 1. Technology marks are among the cheapest to recover.

subjects.name: Mathematical communication and notation
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Correct notation, defined variables, labelled diagrams and stated units. Worth a criterion of its own in the exploration and quietly worth marks in every paper. A student losing two or three marks a paper on notation is losing a grade boundary to something fixable in four lessons.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision that costs most to get wrong
paragraphs: A Springs family paying for maths support before checking which route their child is on is buying blind, and this is the commonest expensive error in the cluster. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistical and calculator-led. The content overlap is real but the emphasis is not, and a tutor who teaches one fluently can be mediocre in the other.

The route also prices itself differently. An AA Higher Level student typically needs more hours than an AI Standard Level student, because the algebraic load is heavier and the non-calculator paper removes the safety net. An AI Higher Level student needs fewer content hours but more time on interpretation: writing a sentence that says what a regression coefficient means in context is worth marks that fluent calculator work alone will not earn.

Where the decision becomes a financial one is the post-Diploma requirement. Engineering, physics and mathematics programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level; business, economics and many social-science programmes accept Applications and Interpretation. That requirement belongs to the individual programme, so it has to be read on that programme's own admissions page rather than inferred. A student who discovers in DP2 that they need AA while sitting AI has almost no good options left.

There is a diagnostic shortcut for a parent who is not sure which course their child is in. Look at a recent paper: if one of them was sat without a calculator, the student is on Analysis and Approaches. If every question assumed a graphic display calculator and several asked what a result means in a real context, it is Applications and Interpretation. The school will confirm it in a sentence, and the answer changes who you should be paying.

sections.heading: What Diploma maths support costs around Emirates Living, counted monthly
paragraphs: Start from the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually feels. Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month in the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages visible in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Converted to hours, the published bands look like this. Budget online tutoring, generally a university student working from a textbook, is advertised by EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 an hour and by Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors teaching online sit between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate showing 200 to 450 and beyond. Premium and examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 or more, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at 180 to 350.

The arithmetic a Springs parent should do is total cost per mark, not rate per hour. Twenty-four lessons at AED 180 with the wrong specialism costs AED 4,320 and moves nothing. Eight lessons at AED 300 aimed at Higher Level Paper 3 and the exploration costs AED 2,400 and addresses forty per cent of the grade. The second is both cheaper and more useful, and the only way to tell them apart in advance is a diagnostic.

These figures are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026, and are reproduced so a family can judge any quote. They are not IB Gram's price list. Our own conversation starts with a free trial lesson and an honest view of how many hours the diagnosis actually justifies.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit, and what an hour buys in each place
paragraphs: A Diploma maths grade is not one thing, so tutoring hours do not buy the same amount of grade everywhere. At Standard Level there are two papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty. At Higher Level there are three papers weighted thirty, thirty and twenty, with the exploration again at twenty. Paper durations differ too: ninety minutes each at Standard Level, two hours each for Higher Level Papers 1 and 2, and sixty minutes for Higher Level Paper 3.

Read that structure as a shopping list. Non-calculator technique affects forty per cent of an AA Standard Level grade through Paper 1 alone, and it is highly trainable. Technology fluency affects every paper in AI and only Paper 2 in AA. Extended reasoning across an unfamiliar structured investigation affects a fifth of a Higher Level grade and is the component with the thinnest classroom coverage anywhere.

The pattern that repeats across Emirates Living households is a student who is fine in class and loses marks in papers. That is almost never a content problem. It is technique selection, time allocation and notation, and it is diagnosed by marking a full paper properly rather than by covering more topics. A tutor who responds to a poor Paper 2 by re-teaching calculus has misread the problem and will bill for a term.

Weightings and durations should be confirmed against the current subject guide for your child's examination session, because the IB revises course structures periodically and this page does not publish IB dates it cannot verify.

sections.heading: The exploration: a fifth of the grade with no timetabled teacher
paragraphs: Every Diploma maths student writes an exploration, and it is worth twenty per cent of the final grade in all four routes. It runs to roughly twelve to twenty pages, is chosen by the student, and is written largely outside lessons. That combination makes it the single most reliable place for a Springs family to spend money, and the place most families spend it last.

The marks are allocated by criterion, and knowing the allocation changes how a student works. Presentation carries four marks and rewards a coherent, organised piece rather than a decorated one. Mathematical communication carries four and is where notation, defined variables and consistent symbols earn or lose. Personal engagement carries three and rewards genuine ownership of the question. Reflection carries three and is the criterion most students treat as a concluding paragraph when it should run throughout. Use of mathematics carries six and is the only one where the level and accuracy of the mathematics itself is judged.

Two patterns account for most low exploration marks in Dubai cohorts. The first is a topic chosen because it sounds interesting rather than because it contains answerable mathematics, which caps use of mathematics no matter how well the writing goes. The second is a draft produced in the last fortnight, which makes reflection impossible to evidence because there was no process to reflect on. Both are fixed by starting in DP1, and three sessions at that stage are worth more than ten in DP2.

The boundary here is not negotiable. A tutor may discuss topic choice, explain what each criterion rewards, and give written feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor must never write the exploration, supply mathematics for the student to copy, or edit the document to completion. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice exposure for the student, not a service.

sections.heading: Higher Level Paper 3 and the hours it genuinely needs
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit a third paper of sixty minutes carrying twenty per cent of the grade, built from two extended response questions. It is not a harder version of Paper 1. It is a structured investigation: a scenario is introduced, early parts establish a result, and later parts require the student to use that result in a way they were not shown. Recall contributes almost nothing.

Schools cover it unevenly for an understandable reason. Paper 3 cannot be taught topic by topic, because its content is drawn from the whole course and its difficulty is in the sustained reasoning. A department teaching a two-year syllabus to a deadline reaches it late, which means a great many Higher Level students in Dubai attempt their first complete Paper 3 within six weeks of the real one.

Four to six lessons change that materially, and they are the clearest value in the whole Higher Level budget. The work is specific: reading a long stem and extracting what is actually being asked, carrying notation forward consistently through a multi-part question, allocating minutes per part against the marks available, and recognising when an earlier result is being handed to you for later use. None of that is content revision, and content revision will not produce it.

The right time to start is the spring term of DP2, after the mocks have identified whether Paper 3 is a weakness, and before the final revision crush makes everything compete for the same evenings. A Springs family spending a fixed block on this rather than another term of general lessons typically spends less and gains more.

sections.heading: Three ways maths money is wasted in Emirates Living households
paragraphs: The first is the generalist. A tutor advertised as a maths tutor in Dubai may be excellent with IGCSE 0580 and genuinely unfamiliar with the structure of a Diploma exploration or with AI Higher Level graph theory. Parents discover this around lesson eight, by which point AED 1,500 to 2,500 has gone. The preventive question is specific: which route and level have you taught to examination, and what does criterion E reward? A vague answer is the answer.

The second is the group class pitched at the wrong level. Group tuition is cheaper per hour and can work well where a cohort shares the same gap. In practice a Dubai group advertised for IB maths often mixes AA and AI, Standard and Higher, and two different school sequences, which produces an hour of content that fits nobody precisely. For a student who is behind on one specific topic, a group class is the most expensive cheap option available.

The third is starting in April of DP2. By then the route, the set and the exploration are all fixed, the whole cohort in Dubai is competing for the same tutors, and the only honest offer is focused work on a handful of high-yield components. That can move a borderline grade. It cannot replace two years, and nobody should promise it will. A family that starts a single weekly slot in DP1 almost always spends less in total than one that buys an intensive rescue in the final term.

A fourth pattern is worth naming briefly: paying specialist rates for homework supervision. If what a household actually needs is somebody to make sure the work gets done at 17:00, that is a different and much cheaper product than a subject specialist, and conflating the two inflates the bill without improving the mark.

sections.heading: Verifying the tutor, and who is allowed to teach privately in the UAE
paragraphs: Before money changes hands there are two checks worth making, and neither takes long. The first is legal. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time and an application route through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

The second check is ethical and specific to schools. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication. The practical point stands in Dubai too: hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to create a problem for everyone.

Neither check says anything about teaching quality, which is why a third question matters more than both. Ask the tutor to describe, for your child's exact route and level, where students most often lose marks and what the first four lessons would do about it. A specialist answers in specifics within thirty seconds. Nobody can be accredited by the IB as a tutor, and any provider claiming board approval is making a claim worth questioning closely.
IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and does not present itself as holding one. What the platform does is match, disclose and then get out of the way of the teaching.

sections.heading: Starting maths support from The Springs, and what the first hour should produce
paragraphs: The first hour should end with a diagnosis written down, not with a package sold. Which route and level, which component of the grade is actually weak, and whether the cause is content, technique or timing. Those three causes need different lesson plans and different numbers of hours, and a provider who cannot tell you which one applies after sixty minutes with your child is not in a position to quote.

Practically, the sequence from a Springs household is short. Confirm the route and level from the school, including the set and any pending change. Name the school's internal exploration deadline if the student is in DP1 or DP2, because that date governs the whole plan. Pick the slot the week can actually hold, which for most of this community is 17:00 on a weekday or a Saturday morning. Then take the free trial lesson and read what the tutor writes afterwards.

Three limits, stated before payment rather than after. Teaching is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, because that service exists only in India. A narrow combination of route, level and hour cannot always be filled from the UAE-based pool, and when it cannot we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere at the same rate rather than filling the slot with the wrong person. And no tutor can guarantee a grade in any subject; a provider offering one is telling you something useful about themselves.

On the exploration, the line again: coaching on process, explanation of the criteria, and feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor must never write the exploration. That boundary is a feature of honest tutoring rather than a limitation of it, because the alternative puts the entire Diploma at risk over twenty per cent of one subject.
