process.title: Confirm the route and level
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard or Higher, plus the current set and whether a change is under discussion. This single line determines which specialist is the right one, and getting it wrong is the most expensive error available.

process.title: Name the weak component
process.description: Paper 1, Paper 2, Paper 3 or the exploration. A recent paper with marks on it, or the school's question-level analysis of a mock, turns a vague request into a four-lesson plan with a measurable endpoint.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: Sixty minutes working through real questions in the student's own route, after which the tutor writes down what they saw: content gaps, technique selection, timing or notation. That note is the basis of the quote, not the other way round.

process.title: Fix the slot and the total
process.description: A weekly slot the Springs week can genuinely hold, or a block with the number of lessons and the total cost agreed up front. Exploration coaching is scheduled against the school's internal deadline rather than the external one.

process.title: Review at four lessons
process.description: What moved, what did not, and whether the diagnosis was right. Families continue, change tutor, or stop. Stopping at four lessons because the problem turned out to be smaller than expected is a good outcome, not a failed sale.

whyPoints.title: Route-specific specialists, not maths tutors
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from AA or AI and Standard or Higher Level, because the two Higher Level courses need genuinely different people. A tutor who claims equal strength in both is describing a marketing position rather than a teaching history.

whyPoints.title: Every figure on this page is attributed
whyPoints.description: Each AED band names the provider or rate table that published it and the month it was read. Nothing is presented as IB Gram's price, and nothing is an estimate dressed as a fact, so any quote you receive can be measured against the same numbers.

whyPoints.title: The exploration is treated as a fifth of the grade
whyPoints.description: Criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own drafts, scheduled against the school's internal deadline. Coaching and feedback only; the mathematics and the writing stay the student's, which is what keeps the qualification safe.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 is planned, not discovered
whyPoints.description: Higher Level students get dedicated work on sustained reasoning and time allocation across two extended investigations, timed to the spring term of DP2 rather than to the fortnight before the paper.

whyPoints.title: Slots built for the Emirates Living clock
whyPoints.description: Scheduling starts from when the bus actually reaches your part of The Springs. A 17:00 weekday slot and a Saturday morning block are the two arrangements that survive a Dubai exam term intact.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits said out loud
whyPoints.description: When a specific route, level and hour cannot be filled from the UAE pool, we say so and offer a specialist elsewhere at the same rate. No competitor examined in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Our school offers both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation. Which costs less to support?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is usually the lighter commitment, because the algebraic load is smaller and a calculator is available throughout. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level typically needs the most hours: heavier algebra, proof by induction, complex numbers and a non-calculator Paper 1 with no safety net. Cost should still not drive the choice. If the programme your child wants specifies Analysis and Approaches, sitting the cheaper course is the most expensive decision in the whole plan. Read the named programme's admissions page before weighing tutoring hours.

faqs.question: How many hours of IB maths tutoring does a Springs student usually end up buying?
faqs.answer: It varies with where the weakness sits rather than with the student. A DP1 student keeping pace with one weekly slot across a school year is looking at roughly thirty lessons. A DP2 student buying a targeted block on Higher Level Paper 3 plus exploration feedback is looking at ten to fifteen. The families who spend most are those who start general lessons in the spring of DP2, because that buys the largest number of hours at the lowest return. A diagnostic in the first hour is what separates the two patterns.

faqs.question: Why does the exploration matter so much to what we spend?
faqs.answer: Because it is twenty per cent of the final grade, it is written largely outside lessons, and no teacher is timetabled to supervise it closely. That makes it the component where a small number of well-timed sessions changes the most. Three sessions in DP1 on scoping a question that can carry course-level mathematics are worth more than ten sessions in DP2 trying to rescue a topic that cannot. The marks are split across five criteria, and the one worth six marks depends almost entirely on a decision taken at the start.

faqs.question: Is a group IB maths class in Dubai better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Only when the group genuinely shares your child's gap. Group tuition is cheaper per hour, and for a cohort from one school all sitting the same route at the same level it can work well. The common Dubai reality is a group advertised for IB maths that mixes Analysis and Approaches with Applications and Interpretation, Standard with Higher, and two school sequences, producing an hour that fits nobody precisely. For a specific topic weakness that is the most expensive cheap option available. Ask what route and level the other students are on before booking.

faqs.question: What is Higher Level Paper 3 and should we pay for help with it?
faqs.answer: It is a sixty-minute paper of two extended response questions carrying twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade. It draws on the whole course and tests sustained reasoning through a structured investigation rather than recall, which is why it cannot be revised topic by topic. Many Dubai students attempt their first complete Paper 3 within six weeks of the real one. Four to six focused lessons on reading long stems, carrying notation through multi-part questions and allocating minutes against marks is usually the clearest value in a Higher Level budget.

faqs.question: My child is fine in class and loses marks in maths papers. What is that worth fixing?
faqs.answer: A great deal, and it is usually cheaper than it sounds. That pattern is almost never a content problem. It is technique selection under time pressure, minute allocation across a paper, and notation. Those are diagnosed by marking a complete paper properly rather than by covering more topics, and they respond to a short focused block rather than a term of lessons. A tutor whose answer to a poor Paper 2 is to re-teach calculus has misread the problem and will bill for months without touching the cause.

faqs.question: Can a tutor at AED 60 an hour teach Diploma maths properly?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a narrow job. The published budget band, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, generally buys a university student working from a textbook. That can be genuinely useful for consolidating Standard Level content a student half-understands. What it rarely buys is route-specific Higher Level teaching, exploration criterion knowledge or Paper 3 technique, because those require someone who has taught the course to examination. Pay the budget rate for the budget job and do not expect the specialist outcome from it.

faqs.question: Does an in-home maths tutor in Dubai teach better than an online one?
faqs.answer: The published rates suggest you are paying for the journey rather than the teaching. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350, while named online specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above. At the same price you are choosing between proximity and subject specialism. For maths specifically, a shared digital whiteboard that keeps every worked solution is more useful than a kitchen table. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should a Springs family start paying for maths help?
faqs.answer: The summer before DP1 is the cheapest useful moment, and almost nobody uses it. Six to ten lessons then close the algebraic-fluency gap that otherwise costs a whole first term, whether the student is arriving from MYP criterion assessment or from IGCSE 0580 Extended. The next best is early DP1, with one weekly slot keeping pace. The most expensive entry point is April of DP2, when the route and the exploration are fixed and the whole Dubai cohort is competing for the same tutors.

faqs.question: How is the maths exploration marked, criterion by criterion?
faqs.answer: Five criteria totalling twenty marks. Presentation carries four and rewards a coherent argument rather than decoration. Mathematical communication carries four, covering notation, defined variables and labelled graphs. Personal engagement carries three and rewards genuine ownership of the question. Reflection carries three and should run through the piece rather than sit in a final paragraph. Use of mathematics carries six and is the only criterion judging the mathematics itself, which is why the topic choice decides the ceiling. Confirm the current allocation against your child's subject guide.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write the maths exploration if my child is stuck?
faqs.answer: A tutor must never write any part of it. What is legitimate is discussing whether a topic can carry course-level mathematics, explaining what each criterion rewards, and giving written feedback on a draft the student has produced themselves. That is teaching. Providers in this market openly sell completed Internal Assessments, and buying one risks a malpractice finding against your child rather than a better grade. Ask any prospective tutor where they draw this line; a vague answer tells you what you need to know.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach maths and physics for the same Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it can reduce the total bill, because the mathematical technique in Higher Level physics overlaps heavily with Analysis and Approaches. Where it breaks down is when both subjects are at Higher Level and both are weak for different reasons, since the physics investigation and the maths exploration are separate pieces of assessed work with separate criteria. In a Springs household the practical arrangement is often two consecutive slots on one evening, which keeps the rest of the week free.

faqs.question: Do maths lessons keep running through Ramadan and the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the time moved rather than the plan. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the productive window shifts later, so a 17:00 slot typically becomes 20:30 or later for the month; families who arrange that in advance keep continuity instead of losing four weeks. The long summer, from late June or early July into early September, is the only interruption-free block in a two-year course and the best time for bridging work or for scoping an exploration. Lessons also continue while a family travels.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IB maths tutor in the first five minutes?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which route and level have you taught to examination? What does criterion E of the exploration reward, and how do students lose it? What does Higher Level Paper 3 ask for that Paper 1 does not? And given this marked paper, what would the first four lessons cover? A specialist answers all four in specifics within a couple of minutes. Anyone who answers in general terms about confidence and foundations is describing a sales position rather than a teaching history.

faqs.question: Will you put the IB examination dates on this page so I can plan backwards?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth stating. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Publishing a date we cannot verify across a large set of pages would eventually mislead somebody at the worst possible moment. UAE schools sit the May session; for the exact window, ask your school's IB coordinator or check ibo.org directly. The date that actually governs your plan is the school's internal exploration deadline, which the coordinator can give you today.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for our route, level and time slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than filling the slot. A narrow combination - Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, say, at a fixed half-hour on a Tuesday - cannot always be matched from the UAE-based pool. The options then are a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, a different hour with the right person, or an honest wait with an estimate. Putting an available but unsuitable tutor into a booked slot is how families end up paying specialist rates for the wrong specialism.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Diagnose first, then decide how many hours to buy
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-springs.closingBody: Before comparing rates, get three facts straight: which Mathematics route and level your child is on, which component of the grade is actually weak, and what the school's internal exploration deadline is. Then take the free trial lesson. Sixty minutes with a route-specific specialist and a recent marked paper produces a written diagnosis, and that diagnosis is what tells you whether you are buying thirty lessons or eight. Families who do this in that order usually spend less in total than those who start with a price comparison, and they can see what the money bought.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-sustainable-.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB mathematics to students across The Sustainable City, Mudon, Arabian Ranches and the wider Dubailand belt. Each is listed against the route and level they teach to examination, because Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and Higher Level Applications and Interpretation are not interchangeable teaching jobs.

intro.heading: The comparison families here are really making
paragraphs: Almost every mathematics enquiry from this part of Dubai arrives with a second community attached to it. A family in The Sustainable City is comparing its own school against one in Arabian Ranches. A family in Mudon has just moved from Motor City. Somebody in Remraam is weighing a place at a school in Dubai Investments Park against a longer run up the E311. Those comparisons are genuine and they matter for school choice. For mathematics tutoring, they resolve to the same answer, and it is worth explaining why rather than pretending each neighbourhood needs a different page.

The reason is supply. There are two IB mathematics routes, each at two levels, so four distinct courses. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a serious piece of mathematics with a third paper that is an extended investigative problem. The number of people in Dubai who teach that course to examination standard is modest, and they are not distributed evenly across villa communities. Whether you live inside The Sustainable City's car-free clusters or in a Ranches cul-de-sac fifteen minutes away, the local pool for that specific course is effectively the same: small.

What does differ between these communities is logistics, and the differences are real. A child at the school inside The Sustainable City is home far earlier than one commuting to Motor City or Al Barsha, which moves the first usable session time by as much as two hours. Tutors quoting for home visits price the Al Qudra Road run differently from the Ranches run. Those variations are set out in a table further down, because they change when a session happens even when they do not change who should teach it.

Mathematics also has a structural feature that reorders the whole tutoring question. The exploration — the student's own piece of mathematical writing — is 20% of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level in both routes, and it is marked against five criteria worth twenty marks in total. It is submitted months before any examination, to a school deadline. A family that only thinks about mathematics tutoring in the final term has already conceded a fifth of the grade without ever seeing a paper.

Delivery is stated plainly rather than buried: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an address in The Sustainable City, Mudon or Arabian Ranches. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard where working is written out by hand and seen as it happens. Home visits exist in our India operation only. For mathematics in particular the online format loses almost nothing, because the whole subject is the working on the page.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-sustainable-.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through the whole continuum, and the preparation that makes a Higher Level route possible happens years before the choice is made. These are the stages we teach and what each one decides.

programmes.name: Middle Years mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student can be numerically competent and still sit on a 4 because the investigation and communication criteria are not about getting an answer. Extended mathematics in the final MYP years is the realistic preparation for Higher Level work later.
programmes.countryNote: In a continuum school such as the one inside The Sustainable City, MYP mathematics grades feed directly into the Diploma route conversation. A student hoping to keep Higher Level Analysis and Approaches open needs algebraic fluency secured in MYP 4, because by the second term of MYP 5 the choice is being locked and there is no time left to change the evidence.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Algebra, functions, calculus, trigonometry, proof, and statistics, with the emphasis on analytic method. Standard Level sits two papers; Higher Level sits three, the third being an extended investigative problem that rewards a sustained written argument rather than a sequence of answers. The exploration carries 20% at both levels and is assessed partly on mathematical communication.
programmes.countryNote: This is the course Dubai families ask about most when a degree in engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science or quantitative economics is in view. Published requirements differ by university and change, so the only reliable method is to read the admissions pages of the specific institutions on the shortlist rather than relying on general advice, including ours.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Modelling, statistics, data interpretation and applied contexts, with technology assumed throughout. It is a different mathematics rather than an easier one: Higher Level contains substantial work on matrices, graph theory and complex modelling. The recurring failure is treating a calculator output as an answer rather than as a step that still requires interpretation and justification.
programmes.countryNote: Students in this belt who switch from Analysis and Approaches to Applications partway through DP1 usually do so for the right reason and too late. The switch is far easier in the first term than the second, because the exploration and the accumulated course content both have to be reset, and schools have their own deadlines for changing a registered course.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP into Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: The step into Diploma mathematics is the sharpest in the programme, particularly into Higher Level Analysis and Approaches from a Core or Foundation IGCSE tier. The gap is rarely conceptual; it is fluency. Students who have to think about rearranging an expression cannot simultaneously think about the calculus question that expression sits inside, and the papers assume both happen at once.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between communities in this belt often change schools and boards at the same time, which means a student may arrive in DP1 from a different mathematics sequence entirely. A short bridging block over the summer or in the first term closes that gap far more cheaply than remediation in the second year.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-sustainable-.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the subject on this page, so what follows is the detail by course and by the subjects that depend on it. The specific weakness matters more than the subject name when booking.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
subjects.description: Three papers, with Paper 3 an extended investigative problem. Proof, calculus and complex algebraic manipulation dominate. Marks are lost on incomplete justification in proof questions and on calculus applied without checking the domain. Paper 3 rewards students who have practised writing out a sustained argument.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
subjects.description: Two papers covering the same areas with less depth. The commonest pattern is a student who can execute a procedure but cannot select which procedure applies to an unfamiliar question. Practice on mixed, unlabelled question sets fixes that faster than more topic drills.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
subjects.description: Substantially more demanding than students expect, with matrices, graph theory and complex modelling. The technology-assumed design means the examiner wants interpretation, not output. Statistical tests need to be chosen and justified rather than performed and reported.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level
subjects.description: Weighted towards modelling, statistics and real-data work. Marks disappear in the sentences around the numbers: a correct regression with no comment on validity, or a prediction made outside the range of the data without noting the problem.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade and twenty marks across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics. The most common cause of a low mark is a topic too ambitious for the student to handle rigorously rather than a topic too simple.

subjects.name: Middle Years mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion-marked rather than graded on content alone. The investigating patterns criterion is where capable students lose ground, because describing a pattern is not the same as justifying a general rule. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the honest preparation for Higher Level later.

subjects.name: Physics, where the mathematics is the obstacle
subjects.description: A substantial share of lost physics marks are mathematical: rearranging before substituting, handling powers of ten, propagating uncertainty. Students whose physics improves after mathematics tutoring usually never had a physics problem at all.

subjects.name: Chemistry calculations
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and titration calculations carry sign conventions and unit conversions that punish approximate arithmetic. The fix is procedural discipline rather than more chemistry, which is why a mathematics tutor sometimes raises a chemistry grade.

subjects.name: Economics, quantitative components
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics includes quantitative questions that reward exactly the skills Analysis and Approaches builds: reading a function, calculating elasticity accurately, and interpreting what the number means in context rather than restating it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking and complexity reasoning depend on comfort with mathematical abstraction. Students who find recursion unintuitive often need the underlying mathematics rather than more code, and that is a diagnosable distinction rather than a guess.

sections.heading: The Sustainable City against the next community over, honestly set out
paragraphs: Here is the comparison without the marketing. For mathematics specifically, the thing that varies between these neighbourhoods is when a session can start and what a visiting tutor would charge to get there. The thing that does not vary is who should teach Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, because the pool of people who teach it to examination standard is small across the whole of Dubai and is not clustered in any one villa community. Reading the table below usually settles the question for a family that arrived expecting a different answer.

The timing column is where real differences live. A child attending the school inside The Sustainable City is home by mid-afternoon, so a 3.30pm start is available. A child commuting from Mudon or Remraam to a school in Motor City or Al Barsha is not realistically free until half past five, and by seven in the evening the quality of a calculus session drops sharply. That is a genuine difference between neighbourhoods and it should drive whether you book a weekday hour or a weekend block.

The supply column is where families expect a difference and find none. Arabian Ranches has a denser informal tutor network than this community does, and that network circulates recommendations for general support and primary-level help, which is where most demand sits. It does not reliably produce someone who has taught the Higher Level third paper. So the Ranches family and the Sustainable City family end up at the same conclusion from different starting points, which is the honest version of this comparison.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: decide it from the degree
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects a Dubai student's options, and it is routinely made on the wrong basis. Applications and Interpretation is not the easier course; it is a different mathematics, weighted towards modelling, statistics and technology use, and its Higher Level is genuinely demanding. Analysis and Approaches is weighted towards algebra, calculus and proof. Choosing between them by perceived difficulty tends to produce a student who dislikes the course they chose and performs below their capability in it.

The reliable method is to work backwards from the degree. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and quantitative economics commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Business, psychology, design, architecture and most social sciences generally accept either, and some actively prefer the statistical grounding Applications gives. Medicine and life sciences vary widely by country and institution. Because published requirements differ and are revised, the only safe approach is to read the admissions pages of the specific universities on the shortlist, early enough to act on what they say.

Where tutoring genuinely changes the outcome is before the choice is locked. A student whose algebraic fluency is shaky in MYP 5 or the first weeks of DP1 can be brought to a point where Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a real option rather than a gamble. Once the course is registered, the switch becomes a school administrative matter with its own deadline, and in the second term it usually means resetting the exploration as well. Earlier is cheaper here, as it is in most of the Diploma.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, on the dimensions that decide it
paragraphs: The Higher and Standard Level decision is separate from the route decision and is often taken too quickly. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches adds depth across algebra, calculus and proof, and adds a third paper which is an extended investigative problem rather than a longer version of the other two. That paper is the part students have practised least and the part that most clearly separates outcomes, because it rewards a sustained written argument rather than a series of discrete answers.

Teaching hours are the practical constraint. Higher Level courses carry more contact time at school, and a student taking three Higher Levels alongside the core is working to a genuinely full timetable. Adding two tutored hours a week on top of that is frequently counterproductive: the between-session work does not get done, and the student arrives at each session having forgotten the last. One well-used hour with real work between sessions beats two hours that displace the work.

The right-fit signals are observable by the end of the first term. A student suited to Higher Level enjoys the problem that does not resolve immediately and will sit with it. A student unsuited to it does the exercises accurately and stalls at anything unfamiliar. That distinction is visible in how they behave in front of an unseen question, which is exactly what a diagnostic session examines, and it is far better established in the first term of DP1 than in the second.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, and where they go
paragraphs: A fifth of an IB mathematics grade comes from the exploration, a piece of independent mathematical writing marked out of twenty across five criteria. Almost nothing in this market explains those criteria, which is strange, because knowing what each one rewards changes how a student chooses a topic. The single most common cause of a disappointing exploration mark in this community is a topic that was too ambitious for the mathematics the student could actually handle rigorously.

Criterion weighting should drive topic choice. The use of mathematics criterion carries the largest share of marks, and it rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and commensurate with the level of the course. A student who attempts something far beyond the syllabus and handles it loosely scores worse than a student who takes a modest topic and treats it rigorously. Personal engagement and reflection reward genuine ownership and genuine critique, which cannot be manufactured in the final week.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and we say it precisely. They may explain each criterion, test whether a topic is feasible, question whether a step is justified, point out that a conclusion does not follow, and comment on writing the student produced. They may not choose the topic, perform the mathematics, write or rewrite any part of the exploration, or supply a model to adapt. Operations in this market sell completed internal assessments; buying one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: Mathematics is unusually diagnosable. Unlike an essay subject, a lost mark in mathematics almost always has a single identifiable cause, and the causes repeat. In this community the pattern is consistent enough to be worth publishing: fluency failures in manipulation, method marks forfeited by not writing working down, calculator answers presented without interpretation, and domain or units ignored. None of those are conceptual gaps and all of them are correctable within a term.

The most expensive habit is answering without showing method. Both routes award method marks on multi-step questions, and a student who writes only a final answer forfeits every one of them when the answer is wrong. For a student under time pressure this feels efficient and is the opposite. Correcting it takes several weeks of enforcement rather than explanation, because it is a habit rather than a misunderstanding, which is precisely the kind of thing weekly sessions are good at.

The second most expensive is calculator dependence in Applications and Interpretation. The course assumes technology, which students read as permission to produce outputs. The examiner wants the output interpreted, justified and bounded: was the regression appropriate, is the prediction inside the range of the data, what does the gradient mean in the context given. That is a writing skill attached to a mathematical one, and it is where Applications candidates most often leave marks on the table. Three to six weeks of writing practice alongside the mathematics usually closes it, because the student already has the result and only needs to learn what the examiner wants said about it.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor costs here, and whether the neighbourhood changes it
paragraphs: The short answer is that the rate is a function of the tutor, not the postcode — with one exception, which is travel. Published Dubai market figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider advertising AED 650. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65.

In-home visiting rates are published at AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500. That is where the neighbourhood does matter: a tutor pricing an Al Qudra Road run and a tutor pricing a trip into Arabian Ranches are pricing different journeys, and both are pricing them into the hour. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits.

For Higher Level mathematics specifically, the tier that matters is the specialist one, because the thing being bought is judgement about the third paper and the exploration rather than knowledge of the content. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026; they are the market's numbers, not ours. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial, against the actual course and level.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a subject where the work is checkable
paragraphs: Mathematics has a particular honesty profile. A finished exploration written by somebody else is often detectable, because the mathematics in it does not match the mathematics the student demonstrates in class, and a supervisor who has taught that student for a year notices. Teachers also conduct the formal process around the exploration, including progress checks. So the practical risk of outsourced work in this subject is high as well as the ethical cost being unacceptable.

The boundary we work to is explicit. A tutor may teach content, explain each exploration criterion, test whether a topic is feasible at the level of the course, question whether a step is justified, point out an unsupported conclusion, and give feedback on writing the student produced. A tutor may not select the topic, carry out the mathematics, write or redraft any part of the submission, or supply a specimen to be adapted. The test is whether a line in the final piece exists because the tutor wrote it.

The same applies to materials. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright, and we reference them rather than hosting or distributing them. Sessions work from questions on screen and from the published criteria, with the school's own legitimate access as the source. A tutoring service offering an unlimited paper bank invites a reasonable question about provenance, and in some cases about material that has not been released. The school's own holdings are also the papers the student will be marked against, so they are the better source in practice as well as the correct one.

sections.heading: Scheduling mathematics around a Dubai week
paragraphs: Mathematics tolerates a weekly rhythm better than most subjects and tolerates lateness worse. Fluency work depends on frequency, so a shorter session twice a week often beats one long one; exploration work depends on thinking time between sessions, so a fortnightly pattern can be right. What does not work is a late-evening calculus session after a long school run, which is why the neighbourhood comparison earlier in this page matters practically rather than just descriptively.

The UAE calendar shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days, which is why weekend blocks suit Higher Level paper work in households where weekday evenings are taken by sport or by a long commute. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar; a mathematics session at that time is frequently better than any afternoon slot during that month.

We hold slots in Gulf Standard Time, move them after Iftar through Ramadan with the same tutor, and pause blocks during a school's own examination fortnight, when additional sessions produce fatigue rather than marks. We do not rotate students between tutors to fill a diary. In mathematics in particular, a tutor who knows which manipulation a student gets wrong under pressure is carrying information that takes weeks to rebuild with somebody new, and that information is most of what makes the fourth session more useful than the first.

process.title: Tell us the route, the level and the year
process.description: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the second Diploma year is a different engagement from Applications at Standard Level in the first. Those four words decide which tutors we approach. If the exploration is underway, say where it has reached, because that usually becomes the first priority.

process.title: Send a marked piece of work
process.description: A photograph of a recently marked paper or exploration draft is worth a long description, because mathematics errors are diagnosable from the page. We look for whether the losses are fluency, method, interpretation or genuine conceptual gaps, since those four need different kinds of session.

process.title: A free trial on an unseen question
process.description: Run by the tutor who would continue, using an unfamiliar question rather than a revision topic, because how a student behaves in front of something unseen is the whole diagnosis. It ends with the tutor naming the first thing they would fix and how long they expect it to take.

process.title: A plan with a measurable first target
process.description: You receive a short written plan naming the first specific target — showing method on every multi-step question, or narrowing the exploration topic to something feasible — with the sessions and between-session work to reach it. Vague plans cannot be checked; this one can.

process.title: Weekly sessions and a tracked error pattern
process.description: Each session ends with a note recording which error categories appeared: fluency, method, interpretation, domain or concept. Over a month the pattern either thins or it does not. If it does not, we change the approach or the tutor rather than quietly adding hours to the invoice.

whyPoints.title: Matched to one of four courses, not to maths
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level are four distinct teaching jobs. Online delivery means your child is matched to someone who teaches their specific course, which no villa community in Dubai can supply locally.

whyPoints.title: The exploration treated as 20% of the grade
whyPoints.description: Because it is. We work on the criteria by letter with the mark allocation named, and we start with topic feasibility, which is the decision that determines the use-of-mathematics mark months before anything is written.

whyPoints.title: Errors diagnosed by category
whyPoints.description: Mathematics losses are classifiable: fluency, method, interpretation, domain or concept. Naming the category is what makes the next four weeks efficient, and it is why a session note here lists causes rather than topics covered.

whyPoints.title: An explicit honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, test feasibility, question steps and critique the student's own writing. They do not choose the topic, perform the mathematics or write any part of the exploration, and we do not source completed coursework from anyone.

whyPoints.title: Comparisons made honestly
whyPoints.description: This page says plainly that the answer for mathematics is the same whether you live in this community or the next one, because local supply for Higher Level is thin everywhere in Dubai. A page that claimed a local advantage it does not have would be easier to write and less useful.

whyPoints.title: Figures with publishers attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names who published it and the month it was read. We publish no star ratings, satisfaction scores or improvement statistics, and claim no approval or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or any board.

faqs.question: Is it better to find a maths tutor inside The Sustainable City or in Arabian Ranches?
faqs.answer: For IB mathematics, neither, and the comparison is worth retiring. The number of people in Dubai who teach Higher Level Analysis and Approaches to examination standard is small and they are not concentrated in any villa community. Arabian Ranches has a denser informal network, but it circulates general and primary-level recommendations rather than Higher Level specialists. What genuinely differs between the two communities is when a session can start, because school runs differ. IB Gram delivers online one-to-one and sends no tutors to UAE addresses, so the match is made on course rather than location.

faqs.question: How much of the IB maths grade comes from the exploration?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Higher and Standard Level in both routes, marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest share at six marks. It is submitted to a school deadline months before any examination, which makes it the part of the grade most often discovered too late to influence. If you are deciding when mathematics tutoring is worth paying for, that weighting argues for the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: My daughter picked Applications because it sounded easier. Was that a mistake?
faqs.answer: Possibly, though not for the reason she expects. Applications is not easier; it is a different mathematics weighted towards modelling, statistics and technology use, and its Higher Level is demanding in its own right. The real risk is to options: engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and quantitative economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Check the published requirements of the specific universities on her shortlist. If a switch is needed, the first term is far easier than the second, because the exploration has to reset too.

faqs.question: What makes the Higher Level third paper different?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 in Analysis and Approaches is an extended investigative problem rather than a longer set of questions. It rewards a sustained written argument: establishing a result, generalising it, justifying each step and carrying structure across several pages. Most students have practised it least because it does not resemble the exercises they do in class, which makes it the clearest remaining source of marks in the final terms. It usually needs six to ten weeks of specific practice, separate from general paper work.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks when his answers are right?
faqs.answer: Most commonly because he writes only the final answer. Both routes award method marks across multi-step questions, so a student who shows no working forfeits all of them whenever the answer is wrong, and gains nothing when it is right. It feels efficient under time pressure and is the opposite. Correcting it takes two to four weeks of enforcement rather than explanation, because it is a habit. It is the single cheapest grade improvement available in IB mathematics and is why session notes here track causes rather than topics.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my child's exploration topic?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to should be declined. The tutor's legitimate role is to explain each criterion, test whether a proposed topic can be handled rigorously with the mathematics the student commands, question whether a step is justified, and comment on writing the student produced. Choosing the topic, performing the mathematics or writing any part of the piece crosses into academic misconduct, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the tutor. Supervisors who have taught a student for a year also tend to notice mathematics that is not theirs.

faqs.question: How early should a student start thinking about Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: In MYP 4 or Year 9, which sounds absurdly early and is not. The constraint on Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is algebraic fluency, and fluency is built by repetition over months rather than taught in a term. A student whose manipulation is secure by the end of MYP 5 has the Higher Level option genuinely open; one who is still thinking about rearranging expressions does not, regardless of ability, because the papers assume manipulation and reasoning happen simultaneously.

faqs.question: Does an online whiteboard really work for a maths session?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is the subject where it works best, because the whole subject is the working on the page and a shared whiteboard shows that working as it is produced. The tutor sees the line where a student hesitates, which is the diagnostic information that matters. Screen-shared questions, annotated step by step, replicate what happens on paper closely. The honest exception is younger children, roughly Year 5 and below, who often need an adult physically present for reasons that have nothing to do with mathematics.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths specialist charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider advertising AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. For Higher Level work the specialist tier is what matters, because the purchase is judgement about Paper 3 and the exploration. Those are market figures read in October 2026; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.question: Should we book one long session or two short ones for maths?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem. Fluency work depends on frequency, so two shorter sessions in a week beat one long one: manipulation improves through repetition spread across days. Exploration work depends on thinking time between sessions, so a fortnightly pattern can be correct. Higher Level paper practice needs an uninterrupted block, which in commuting households usually means a weekend. Naming the problem first is what makes that choice obvious, and it is the first thing a diagnostic session establishes.

faqs.question: My child switched schools mid-year and the maths sequence does not match. What now?
faqs.answer: A bridging block, which is one of the commonest requests in this belt because families move between these communities regularly. Different schools teach topics in different orders, so a mid-year arrival typically has two or three specific unmet topics rather than a general weakness, plus two or three already covered twice. A diagnostic session names which, and the gap usually closes within a term. It matters more than it sounds, because an unmet topic in the first Diploma year compounds into the second.

faqs.question: Do you provide IB maths past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. We reference them, cite the official source, and work from material your child's school has legitimate access to, with questions shown on screen during sessions and the published criteria used as written. Be cautious of any service advertising an unlimited paper bank, because it raises a fair question about where the material came from and occasionally about whether it has been released at all.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting maths tutoring in the final term?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the target has to be honest. In the final term the achievable gains are technique: method-mark discipline, time per mark, command-term reading, and for Higher Level students targeted work on the third paper. What is not achievable is covering substantial unmet content, and the exploration is already submitted. A tutor who promises a two-grade lift in that window is selling. We would rather state the realistic target before a booking than defend an unrealistic one afterwards.

faqs.question: Do you claim any IB accreditation for your maths tutors?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is not IB-accredited, is not an IB World School, holds no KHDA or ADEK approval, no Cambridge or Pearson partnership, and no UAE office. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, because that claim is widely made in this market and rarely supported. What we will tell you about any tutor is which course and level they teach, and how long they have taught it to examination.

faqs.question: How long until we can see whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: About four weeks for a fluency or method problem, because those produce visible changes in marked work quickly: the same question type stops failing in the same place. Conceptual gaps take longer, and exploration work is judged against criteria rather than marks until the school assesses it. Each session note records which error categories appeared, so the pattern is visible rather than anecdotal. We publish no improvement statistics, because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is not evidence.

Next is a free trial lesson on an unseen question with the tutor who would continue, then a short written plan with a measurable first target. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Sustainable City in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and the same tutor is available whichever community you live in.

intro.heading: In this community the first comparison is between qualifications
paragraphs: The Valley is a newer community on the road to Al Ain with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing, so students here travel outward in two broad directions and attend several different schools. Some of those schools run the IB Diploma; others run A Levels; a few offer both. The practical result is that a mathematics conversation in this community frequently starts earlier than it does elsewhere, with a choice between qualifications rather than between levels within one.

That makes this page a comparison page in a specific sense. It begins with IB mathematics against A Level Mathematics, because that is the decision a Valley family often faces when choosing a school or a post-16 route. Then it compares the two IB routes, Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation, which is the decision that follows. Only after that does it get to the things that are the same whichever answer a family reaches: the exploration, the marks and the cost.

The headline difference between the qualifications is coursework and breadth. IB mathematics carries an exploration worth 20% of the grade at both Higher and Standard Level, written independently and submitted to a school deadline months before any examination. A Level Mathematics is externally examined with no coursework component. A student who writes well and plans badly is better served by one; a student who performs under timed conditions and resists independent writing is better served by the other.

What does not differ is the nature of the local supply problem. The number of people in Dubai who teach Higher Level Analysis and Approaches to examination standard is modest, and they are not distributed by villa community. In a neighbourhood with no school inside it and no school-gate network, a proximity search for that specific skill returns almost nothing, which is why the match has to be made on the course taught rather than on the map.

Delivery is online and stated plainly rather than implied: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard on which working appears as it is written. Household visits exist in our India operation only. For mathematics the format loses almost nothing, because the subject is the working on the page and the diagnostic information is the line where a student hesitates. The format also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which in a household where the school run has already taken an hour from the day is the difference between a session a student can use and one they merely attend.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through the whole continuum here, and in a community whose children attend several schools the preparation that keeps options open matters more than the label on the course. These are the stages we teach.

programmes.name: Middle Years mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed on four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Capable students lose most ground on investigating patterns, because describing a pattern is not the same as justifying a general rule, and on communicating, where notation and structure are marked rather than the answer.
programmes.countryNote: Valley students reach the Middle Years at several different schools, so the point at which extended and standard mathematics pathways separate varies between neighbours. A family hoping to keep a Higher Level route open should ask its own school when that split happens rather than assuming the street shares a timetable.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Algebra, functions, calculus, trigonometry, proof and statistics, with the emphasis on analytic method. Standard Level sits two papers; Higher Level sits three, the third an extended investigative problem rewarding a sustained written argument. The exploration carries 20% at both levels and is assessed partly on mathematical communication.
programmes.countryNote: This is the course Dubai families ask about when engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science or quantitative economics is in view. Published university requirements differ and are revised, so read the admissions pages of the specific institutions on the shortlist rather than relying on general advice, including ours.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Modelling, statistics, data interpretation and applied contexts with technology assumed throughout. It is a different mathematics rather than an easier one, and Higher Level contains substantial work on matrices, graph theory and complex modelling. The recurring failure is treating a calculator output as the answer rather than as a step requiring justification.
programmes.countryNote: Students in this belt who switch from Analysis and Approaches to Applications partway through the first Diploma year usually do so for sound reasons and too late. The switch is far easier in the first term than the second, because the exploration and the accumulated content both have to reset and schools set their own deadlines for changing a registered course.

programmes.name: A Level Mathematics as the alternative
programmes.description: Externally examined with no coursework component, narrower in breadth and deeper in the pure mathematics it covers, usually taken alongside two or three other A Levels rather than within a six-subject framework. Students who perform well under timed conditions and dislike independent extended writing often do better here than in the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools reachable from The Valley offer A Levels, and a few offer both routes, which means this is a live choice for families here rather than a theoretical one. The decision should be made on how the student works rather than on which qualification sounds more demanding, because both are accepted widely by universities.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the subject here, so what follows is the detail by course and by the subjects that depend on it. The specific weakness matters more than the course name when booking.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
subjects.description: Three papers, with Paper 3 an extended investigative problem. Proof, calculus and complex manipulation dominate, and marks are lost on incomplete justification in proof questions and on calculus applied without checking the domain. Paper 3 rewards students who have practised sustaining an argument across pages.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
subjects.description: Two papers covering the same areas with less depth. The commonest profile is a student who can execute a procedure but cannot select which procedure an unfamiliar question needs, which mixed unlabelled question sets fix faster than further topic drills.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
subjects.description: More demanding than students expect, with matrices, graph theory and complex modelling. The technology-assumed design means the examiner wants interpretation rather than output, and statistical tests must be chosen and justified rather than simply performed and reported.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level
subjects.description: Weighted towards modelling, statistics and real-data work. Marks disappear in the sentences around the numbers: a correct regression with no comment on validity, or a prediction made beyond the range of the data with no acknowledgement of the problem.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade and twenty marks across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest cause of a low mark is a topic too ambitious to be handled rigorously rather than one too simple.

subjects.name: Middle Years mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion-marked rather than graded on content alone, with investigating patterns the criterion capable students most often neglect. Extended mathematics in the final Middle Years years is the honest preparation for Higher Level work afterwards, whichever qualification follows.

subjects.name: Physics, where the mathematics is the obstacle
subjects.description: A substantial share of lost physics marks are mathematical: rearranging before substituting, handling powers of ten, propagating uncertainty. Students whose physics improves after mathematics tutoring generally never had a physics problem in the first place.

subjects.name: Chemistry calculations
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and titration work carry sign conventions and unit conversions that punish approximate arithmetic. The fix is procedural discipline rather than more chemistry, which is why a mathematics tutor sometimes raises a chemistry grade.

subjects.name: Economics, quantitative components
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics includes quantitative questions rewarding exactly the skills Analysis and Approaches builds: reading a function, calculating accurately, and interpreting what the number means in context rather than restating it in words.

subjects.name: A Level Mathematics and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: For students on the alternative route, the demands differ: no coursework, more pure mathematics, and examination technique under timing carrying the whole grade. Students moving between routes mid-stream need a bridging block rather than general support.

sections.heading: IB mathematics against A Level Mathematics, for a family choosing
paragraphs: This comparison matters more in The Valley than in a community built around a single continuum school, because students here travel to schools offering both routes and the choice is genuinely open. Both qualifications are widely accepted by universities, so the decision should be made on how the student works rather than on which sounds harder. The differences that actually affect a student's two years are coursework, breadth, and how much of the grade rests on performance in a single week.

IB mathematics carries an exploration worth 20% of the grade at both levels, written independently over months and submitted to a school deadline well before the examinations. A Level Mathematics has no coursework component: the grade is decided entirely by externally examined papers. That is the single biggest practical difference. A student who writes and plans well banks a fifth of their grade early; a student who struggles with self-managed writing carries that weakness into a fifth of the result.

Breadth is the second difference. The Diploma requires six subjects plus the core, so mathematics sits inside a wide programme with competing deadlines. A Levels usually mean three or four subjects studied more deeply. Neither is better in the abstract, and the honest advice is to read the student rather than the qualification. The table sets out the dimensions that decide it, including the signals that are visible by the end of a first term in either route, which is when a change is still practical.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: Once a family has settled on the Diploma, this is the decision that follows and it is routinely taken for the wrong reason. Applications and Interpretation is not the easy option; it is a different mathematics, weighted towards modelling, statistics and technology use, with a Higher Level that is genuinely demanding. Analysis and Approaches is weighted towards algebra, calculus and proof. Choosing by perceived difficulty tends to produce a student who dislikes their own course and performs below their capability inside it.

What a week of homework actually feels like is a better guide than any syllabus summary. In Analysis and Approaches the work is largely manipulation and proof: a problem resolves or it does not, and the satisfaction is in exactness. In Applications the work is modelling and interpretation: a result has to be judged, bounded and explained in words. Students usually have a clear preference once the distinction is put to them this way, and that preference predicts performance better than prior attainment does.

The constraint is university requirements, which should be read rather than assumed. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and quantitative economics commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Business, psychology, design and most social sciences generally accept either, and some prefer the statistical grounding Applications gives. Published requirements differ by institution and change, so check the admissions pages of the specific universities on the shortlist early enough to act on what they say.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria
paragraphs: A fifth of an IB mathematics grade comes from the exploration, an independent piece of mathematical writing marked out of twenty across five criteria. Almost nothing in this market explains those criteria, which is strange, because knowing what each one rewards is what should drive the choice of topic. The commonest cause of a disappointing mark is a topic too ambitious for the mathematics the student can handle rigorously rather than a topic that was too modest.

Criterion weighting should therefore drive topic choice. The use of mathematics criterion carries the largest share of the marks, and it rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and commensurate with the level of the course. A student who reaches far beyond the syllabus and handles it loosely scores below a student who takes a modest topic and treats it rigorously. Personal engagement and reflection reward genuine ownership and genuine critique, neither of which can be manufactured in the final week before submission.

The boundary on what a tutor may do is strict and we state it rather than leaving it vague. A tutor may explain each criterion, test whether a topic is feasible, question whether a step is justified, point out that a conclusion does not follow, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not choose the topic, perform the mathematics, write or rewrite any part of the exploration, or supply a model to adapt. Operations in this market sell completed internal assessments; buying one is academic misconduct and the candidate carries the consequence.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and the hours it costs
paragraphs: The level decision sits beneath the route decision and is often taken too quickly. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches adds depth across algebra, calculus and proof and adds a third paper which is an extended investigative problem rather than a longer version of the other two. That paper is the part students have practised least and the part that most clearly separates outcomes, because it rewards a sustained argument rather than a series of discrete answers.

Teaching hours are the practical constraint, and in a commuting community they are tighter than elsewhere. Higher Level courses carry more contact time at school, and a student taking three Higher Levels plus the core already has a full timetable before a long school run is added. Adding two tutored hours a week on top of that is frequently counterproductive: the between-session work does not get done and the student arrives each week having forgotten the last session.

The right-fit signals are observable by the end of the first term. A student suited to Higher Level will sit with a problem that does not resolve immediately. A student unsuited to it executes taught procedures accurately and stalls at anything unfamiliar. That difference shows up in how they behave in front of an unseen question, which is exactly what a diagnostic session examines, and it is far better established in the first Diploma year than in the second, when a change of level is administratively harder and the accumulated content works against it.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks are lost, and how long each takes to fix
paragraphs: Mathematics is unusually diagnosable, because a lost mark almost always has one identifiable cause and the causes repeat. Across both routes the pattern is consistent: manipulation that is slow rather than wrong, method marks forfeited by writing only an answer, calculator results presented without interpretation, and domain or validity ignored. None of those are conceptual gaps, and all of them are correctable within a term if they are named rather than described as weakness in maths.

The most expensive habit is answering without showing method. Both routes award method marks on multi-step questions, and a student who writes only a final answer forfeits every one of them whenever the answer is wrong. Under time pressure this feels efficient and is the opposite. Correcting it takes several weeks of enforcement rather than explanation, because it is a habit, which is precisely the kind of thing a weekly slot across a term is good at and a crash course is not.

The second most expensive, in Applications and Interpretation, is calculator dependence. The course assumes technology, which students read as permission to produce outputs. The examiner wants the output interpreted, justified and bounded: was the model appropriate, is the prediction inside the range of the data, what does the gradient mean here. That is a writing skill attached to a mathematical one, and it takes three to six weeks of practice alongside the mathematics rather than instead of it, because the student already has the result and only needs to learn what the examiner wants said about it.

sections.heading: What two years of mathematics support actually costs
paragraphs: Families usually ask about an hourly rate and then plan in terms they never total up. Published Dubai figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200, and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and one premium provider advertising AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and budget online tutoring AED 33 to AED 65.

The useful exercise is to cost the whole Diploma rather than the hour, because mathematics is a two-year commitment and the sensible plan is uneven across it. A term of weekly sessions in the first year to secure fluency, a short exploration block, and a technique block before the final papers is a very different total from two years of continuous weekly tutoring, and in most cases it produces more. The uneven plan also matches where the marks actually move.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, with monthly packages advertised at AED 799 for eight online sessions. All of these figures belong to the companies and rate guides that published them and were read in October 2026. sections.heading: Timing a mathematics session when the school run is long
paragraphs: Mathematics tolerates a weekly rhythm well and tolerates fatigue badly, which makes session timing a real variable in a community with no school inside it. A Valley student is realistically home around a quarter past five, and manipulation accuracy drops noticeably after seven in the evening. A plan that puts a calculus session at eight o'clock is teaching a tired student to make errors they would not make at four, and then reviewing those errors as if they were real.

The structure that works here splits the work by its timing needs. Fluency drilling benefits from frequency rather than length, so two short weekday sessions beat one long one where the household can manage it. Exploration work and Paper 3 practice need uninterrupted blocks, which in this community means the weekend. A student doing one weekday fluency slot and one weekend block is running a better programme than one doing two tired weekday hours.

The UAE calendar then shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar, where a mathematics session is frequently better than any afternoon slot in that month. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time, move after Iftar with the same tutor, and can pause during a school's own examination fortnight when adding sessions produces fatigue rather than marks. We keep the same tutor across a term rather than rotating students to fill a diary, because knowing which manipulation a particular student rushes under pressure is most of what makes a later session efficient.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Mathematics has a particular honesty profile, because an exploration written by somebody else is often detectable: the mathematics in it does not match the mathematics the student demonstrates in class, and a teacher who has taught them for a year notices. Schools also run a formal process around the exploration including progress checks. So outsourced work in this subject carries a high practical risk as well as being unacceptable in principle, and the trade exists locally at a published price.

So the boundary is drawn as a single question, and everything else is derived from it: does any line in the finished exploration exist because the tutor wrote it? If the answer is yes anywhere, the piece is not your child's. Reading that test backwards produces the prohibitions, and they are the shorter list. A tutor may not select the topic, may not carry out the mathematics, may not write or redraft any part of the submission, and may not supply a specimen to be adapted. Everything else stays available, and it is where the twenty marks are actually earned: teaching the content, explaining each exploration criterion in turn, testing whether a topic is feasible at the level of the course, questioning whether a step is justified, pointing out an unsupported conclusion, and giving feedback on writing the student has already produced. A tutor working inside those limits can still move a grade. A tutor working outside them has put the whole diploma at risk for the sake of a few marks.

On materials and claims: IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright, so we reference them and work from what the school legitimately holds. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners without evidenced current status. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry or IB approval, accreditation or partnership and no UAE office, and an individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.
