faqs.question: Should our son do IB mathematics or A Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Decide it on how he works rather than on which sounds more demanding, because both are widely accepted by universities. The biggest practical difference is coursework: IB mathematics carries an exploration worth 20% of the grade, written independently and submitted months before the examinations, while A Level Mathematics has no coursework and is decided entirely by examined papers. A student who plans and writes well banks a fifth of the grade early; a student who performs best under timed conditions may prefer the A Level. Breadth is the second difference, six subjects against three or four.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier IB maths route?
faqs.answer: No, it is a different mathematics. It is weighted towards modelling, statistics, data interpretation and technology use, and its Higher Level contains substantial work on matrices, graph theory and complex modelling. Analysis and Approaches is weighted towards algebra, calculus and proof. Choosing by perceived difficulty tends to produce a student who dislikes their course and underperforms in it. A better guide is what a week of homework feels like: exactness and proof in one, judgement and interpretation in the other.

faqs.question: What share of the final maths grade is decided before the exams?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Higher and Standard Level in both routes, marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying six marks. It is submitted to a school deadline months before any examination, which makes it the part of the grade families most often discover too late to influence. If you are deciding when mathematics tutoring is worth paying for, that weighting argues for the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: Why does the commute matter for a maths session specifically?
faqs.answer: Because manipulation accuracy falls off with fatigue in a way that conceptual discussion does not. There is no school inside The Valley at the time of writing, so a secondary student is realistically home around a quarter past five, and a calculus session at eight in the evening produces errors the same student would not make at four. Reviewing those errors wastes the hour twice. The structure that works is a weekday evening slot for fluency and a weekend block for exploration and Paper 3 work.

faqs.question: What makes Paper 3 different in Higher Level Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is an extended investigative problem rather than a longer set of questions. It rewards sustaining a written argument across pages: establishing a result, generalising it, justifying each step and holding structure throughout. Most students have practised it least, because it does not resemble the exercises they do in class, which makes it the clearest remaining source of marks in the final terms. It typically needs six to ten weeks of specific practice, separate from general paper work, and it suits a weekend block.

faqs.question: My daughter keeps getting answers right and losing marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly that she writes only the final answer. Both IB mathematics routes award method marks across multi-step questions, so showing no working forfeits all of them whenever the final answer is wrong and gains nothing when it is right. Under time pressure it feels efficient and is the opposite. Correcting it takes two to four weeks of enforcement rather than explanation, because it is a habit. It is the cheapest grade improvement available in the subject and the one weekly sessions handle best.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose or write part of the exploration?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor offering to should be declined. The legitimate role is to explain each criterion, test whether a proposed topic can be handled rigorously with the mathematics the student commands, question whether a step is justified, and comment on writing the student produced. Choosing the topic, performing the mathematics or writing any part of it crosses into academic misconduct, and the consequence falls on the candidate. Teachers who have taught a student for a year also tend to notice mathematics that is not theirs.

faqs.question: How should we spread tutoring across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Unevenly, because that is where the marks move. A term of weekly fluency work in the first year secures the manipulation the papers assume; a short block scoping and reviewing the exploration protects a fifth of the grade; a technique block before the mocks and again before the final papers is where most of the second year's gains sit. That plan usually produces more than two years of continuous weekly tutoring and costs considerably less. A crash course in the final term is the weakest use of the same money.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths specialist cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IB from AED 200, and IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included. Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour is AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Those are market figures read in October 2026; we quote after a free trial for the actual route and level.

faqs.question: Does an online whiteboard work for mathematics?
faqs.answer: It is the subject where it works best, because the whole discipline is the working on the page and a shared whiteboard shows that working as it is produced. The tutor sees the line where the student hesitates, which is the diagnostic information that matters most. Screen-shared questions annotated step by step reproduce what happens on paper closely. The honest exception is younger children, roughly Year 5 and below, who often need an adult physically present for reasons unconnected to mathematics.

faqs.question: Our son wants to switch from Analysis and Approaches to Applications. Is that wise?
faqs.answer: It depends on the reason and heavily on the timing. If the reason is a genuine mismatch of thinking style, it is sensible; if it is the assumption that Applications is easier, it usually is not. Timing matters more: a switch in the first term is manageable, while a switch in the second means resetting the exploration as well as the accumulated content, and schools set their own deadlines for changing a registered course. Ask the school what its deadline is before deciding anything.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level maths worth taking if it is not required?
faqs.answer: Only if the student will sit with a problem that does not resolve immediately, because that is what the course and particularly Paper 3 assess. Higher Level carries more school contact time, which in a commuting household leaves less room for anything added, and a student taking three Higher Levels plus the core is already at capacity. If a target degree does not require it, Standard Level taken well and a stronger profile elsewhere is often the better outcome than Higher Level taken grimly.

faqs.question: We moved here mid-year and the maths sequence does not match. What now?
faqs.answer: A bridging block, which is one of the commonest requests in this community because families move in from across Dubai and from abroad. Schools teach topics in different orders, so a mid-year arrival typically has two or three genuinely unmet topics and two or three covered twice rather than a general weakness. A diagnostic session names which, and the gap usually closes within a term. Doing it in the first Diploma year is far cheaper than discovering it in the second.

faqs.question: After how many sessions should a change show up in marked work?
faqs.answer: About three to four weeks for a method or habit problem, because the change appears directly in the next marked paper. Fluency problems take four to eight weeks, since they improve through repetition rather than instruction. Conceptual gaps take one to three weeks per topic, and exploration work is judged against criteria rather than marks until the school assesses it. Session notes record which error categories appeared, so the trend is visible in the record rather than in impressions.

faqs.question: What will you actually tell us about a tutor's credentials?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is not IB-accredited, is not an IB World School, holds no KHDA or ADEK approval, no Cambridge or Pearson partnership, and no UAE office. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, because that claim is widely made in this market and rarely supported. What we will tell you about any tutor is which route and level they teach and how long they have taught it to examination.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near The Views who actually teaches this syllabus?
paragraphs: Taken literally, the answer is probably no, and a page that pretended otherwise would be useless to you. The Views is a cluster of towers in Emirates Living beside the golf course. Within a ten-minute drive there are good mathematics teachers, there are university students who were strong at A Level, and there are tuition centres running group classes. What there is unlikely to be, in that radius, free at 17:15 on a Tuesday, is somebody whose main teaching subject is IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, who has taught Paper 3 to a cohort, and who can tell you which of the five exploration criteria your child's draft is losing marks against.

That is not a Dubai problem. It is an arithmetic problem. IB mathematics is two separate courses at two levels, which is four distinct teaching jobs. Roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment sits on an IB programme at all, and of those students only a fraction take Higher Level mathematics. Narrow further to the ones taking Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation, and the pool of local specialists who teach that course as their day job is genuinely small. Filtering by distance on top of that leaves whoever remains, which is not a selection method.

So IB Gram drops the distance filter and keeps the two that matter: the route and the level. Your child is matched with a tutor who teaches that specific course, and the lesson arrives over live video, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week. Nobody drives to a Views tower; in-home visiting is a service we run in India only. For mathematics in particular that is an improvement rather than a compromise, because most of the work is shared-screen work: a graph plotted and replotted, a mark scheme opened beside a past-paper question, an exploration draft annotated line by line and saved for the following week.

The rest of this page is written to let you test any tutor, ours or anybody else's. It sets out the difference between the two routes and what each one implies for university applications. It gives the full assessment structure with the weightings and the paper durations. It names where marks are actually lost at each level, what Paper 3 asks for, and how the exploration is marked criterion by criterion with the mark allocation. It gives you a short list of questions that separate somebody who knows this syllabus from somebody who knows mathematics, and it publishes what the Dubai market charges by the month rather than by the hour, with sources.

What it does not do is quote an exam date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been verified at source. UAE schools sit the May session; for the dates your child is working to, the school's IB coordinator is the only reliable authority. We also publish no grade guarantee, no invented statistic, and no claim of approval from the IB, KHDA or the Ministry of Education, because IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds none of those.

If you want to shortcut the reading: the first lesson is free, one per family, about thirty minutes, with no charge and no card details taken. Bring your child's last marked mathematics assessment to it. A tutor who can look at that script and name the pattern, rather than the topic, is the one worth booking.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Four mathematics courses sit behind the single phrase IB maths, and a Views family needs to know which one is on their child's timetable before anything else is discussed. programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
programmes.description: The proof-and-calculus route taken at depth. Assessment is Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, each two hours and each worth 30% of the grade, plus Paper 3 at one hour and 20%, plus the exploration at 20%. Content runs from proof by induction and complex numbers through to differential equations and Maclaurin series.
programmes.countryNote: This is the course Views students heading for engineering, mathematics, physics or quantitative economics are usually advised into, and the one where tutoring demand from Emirates Living is heaviest. It is also where families most often discover in the second term of DP1 that an Extended IGCSE grade 7 was not the preparation they assumed it was.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
programmes.description: The same analytical flavour at a reduced scope. Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, each ninety minutes and each 40% of the grade, plus the exploration at 20%. There is no Paper 3. Calculus, functions and trigonometry carry most of the content and most of the lost marks.
programmes.countryNote: A sensible destination for a Views student who wants an analytical course without six Higher Level commitments, and the usual landing place for students who start AA Higher Level and move down during DP1. The move is routine and is better made in November than in April.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
programmes.description: Modelling, statistics and technology led, with a graphic display calculator assumed on every paper. Paper 1 and Paper 2 are two hours each at 30%, Paper 3 is one hour at 20%, and the exploration is 20%. The statistics content at Higher Level is substantial, including hypothesis testing, regression and Markov chains.
programmes.countryNote: Chosen by students heading towards business, geography, design or the life sciences at university. Views families who selected it believing it to be the easier route are regularly surprised by the Higher Level statistics, which is the single commonest reason for a mid-DP1 tutoring enquiry in this course.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level
programmes.description: The most widely taken of the four. Two ninety-minute papers at 40% each, both with a calculator, plus the exploration at 20%. Content centres on modelling with functions, descriptive statistics and probability, with an emphasis on interpreting a result in context rather than deriving it.
programmes.countryNote: Taken by a large share of Diploma students at the Emirates Living and Al Barsha schools. The marks here are mostly lost to interpretation rather than computation: a correct regression equation followed by a conclusion that does not reference the context earns a fraction of the available credit.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on a Diploma timetable of six, and the requests from The Views rarely arrive alone. These are the courses and components most often tutored alongside or instead of mathematics for students in this community.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof route. Higher Level marks are lost in induction proofs, complex-number manipulation, implicit differentiation and in the written justification that turns a correct answer into a complete one. Standard Level marks go mostly in calculus and in the non-calculator paper's algebra.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route. Lost marks cluster in the interpretation sentence rather than the calculation: a hypothesis test completed correctly and then concluded without reference to the significance level, or a regression used to extrapolate well outside the data.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing marked against five criteria out of twenty marks. Students lose most on personal engagement and reflection, because they choose a topic they do not care about and then describe what they did instead of evaluating it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The commonest companion request. A student struggling with Higher Level physics and taking Applications and Interpretation Standard Level mathematics is usually struggling with the mathematics, not the physics, and the fix belongs in the mathematics session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the lost marks. The quantitative strands overlap with mathematics enough that the same student often needs both, which is why Views households frequently book two subjects with two specialists rather than one generalist.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and the three internal assessment commentaries decide the grade. Higher Level adds quantitative content that a student on Applications and Interpretation handles comfortably and one on neither mathematics route finds unexpectedly hard.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Shares an audience with Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Students who can code often lose marks on the theory paper's precise vocabulary around data structures and complexity, which is a writing problem rather than a programming one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application rather than tool recall. The quantitative sections, break-even and investment appraisal among them, are where a student without either mathematics route at Higher Level tends to concede marks quietly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge students most often choose and least often handle well, because they argue that mathematics is certain rather than examining how mathematical knowledge is justified. A mathematics tutor can help more here than most families expect.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in mathematics
subjects.description: Chosen by a small number of Higher Level students each year and frequently regretted. The research question is the whole difficulty: too broad and it becomes a textbook summary, too narrow and there is nothing to analyse. Process coaching on the question itself is the useful intervention.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that decides who can teach your child
paragraphs: Before any conversation about tutors, a Views parent needs to know which of the two courses is on the timetable, because they are not variants of one subject. They share five topic headings and almost nothing else about how they feel to study. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and analytical route: proof, calculus developed formally, functions manipulated by hand. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout and an emphasis on what a result means rather than how it was derived.

The practical consequence shows up in the first paper. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which means algebraic fluency is being assessed directly and a student who has leaned on technology since Year 9 is exposed immediately. Every Applications and Interpretation paper assumes a calculator, so the exposure is different: a student who can operate the device but cannot say what the output means loses the interpretation marks, which carry more weight than most candidates believe.

University expectations are the other half of the decision, and they are more specific than school guidance sometimes suggests. Engineering, mathematics, physics and the more quantitative economics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and some overseas departments state it explicitly. Business, geography, psychology, design and most life-science routes accept either, and a strong Applications and Interpretation grade is worth more than a weak Analysis and Approaches one. Families in The Views aiming at UAE universities should check the specific programme's published requirement rather than assume, because requirements differ between institutions and change.

The reason this matters for tutoring is simple. A tutor who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level can usually cover Applications and Interpretation Standard Level. The reverse is not true, and neither is the assumption that a good A Level mathematics teacher can teach either course well without having taught it. The exploration alone is a different assessment from anything in the A Level system.

sections.heading: The assessment structure, paper by paper, with the weightings
paragraphs: Most families know their child's mathematics grade and almost none can say how it is composed. That gap is worth closing before buying any tutoring, because the component a student is losing marks in determines what kind of help is useful. A student weak in the non-calculator paper and a student weak in the exploration need different tutors on different schedules.

At Standard Level, both routes sit two papers of ninety minutes, each worth 40% of the grade, with the exploration making up the remaining 20%. At Higher Level, both routes sit two papers of two hours at 30% each, a third paper of one hour at 20%, and the exploration at 20%. The arithmetic matters: at Higher Level the exploration and Paper 3 together are 40% of the grade, and they are the two components schools have least time to prepare properly.

The weighting also tells you where a late intervention can and cannot help. In February of DP2 there is no realistic way to rebuild a weak algebraic foundation, but Paper 3 technique is genuinely learnable in six sessions because the format is unfamiliar rather than difficult, and the exploration is already submitted. In the first term of DP1 the priority is reversed: the foundation is still fixable and Paper 3 is a year away.

One more thing the table shows. Both papers at Standard Level are worth the same, so a student who is strong with a calculator and weak without one is conceding up to 40% of the grade in Analysis and Approaches. Diagnosing that split is a ten-minute job with two past papers, and it is the first thing a competent tutor will do.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, topic by topic
paragraphs: Reports tell you a grade. They rarely tell you which category of error produced it, and the categories are far more useful than the topics. Across the Diploma mathematics students we see from Emirates Living, lost marks fall into four recognisable patterns, and a tutor who cannot name which one your child has is guessing.

The first is method-mark forfeiture. A student reaches the right answer by a route the examiner cannot follow, or jumps three lines of algebra, and loses the marks allocated to the working rather than the result. This is the most common pattern and the fastest to fix, because it is a habit rather than a gap. Two or three sessions of writing solutions out properly, marked against a real mark scheme, usually converts it.

The second is the unjustified conclusion, and it dominates Applications and Interpretation. A hypothesis test is carried out correctly, the p-value is computed, and then the conclusion is written without reference to the significance level or to the context of the question. The mathematics was right and the marks are gone. The same pattern appears in regression questions where a student extrapolates far outside the data without comment.

The third is foundation erosion, and it is the only one that genuinely needs time. A DP1 student who cannot confidently manipulate indices, solve a quadratic without a calculator or handle a trigonometric identity will struggle through calculus regardless of how well calculus is taught, because every question hides algebra inside it. The fourth is simply unfamiliarity with Paper 3 at Higher Level, where students who perform well on Papers 1 and 2 stall because they have never practised sustaining one problem across twenty-five minutes.

sections.heading: Paper 3 at Higher Level: one hour, two problems, twenty per cent
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the component Views parents have most often never heard of, and it carries a fifth of the Higher Level grade. It runs for one hour, contains two extended problem-solving questions, and is sat with a graphic display calculator in both routes. Unlike Papers 1 and 2 it does not sample across the syllabus in short questions. It takes one or two contexts and builds a long, scaffolded investigation through them, where part (f) depends on having got part (c) right and understood why.

That structure is what makes it hard for able students. A candidate used to twelve independent questions can afford to lose one. A candidate facing two long chains cannot afford to break early, and the commonest failure mode is not an inability to do the mathematics but a decision to stop. Students reach a part they cannot see through, spend six minutes staring at it, and arrive at the second question with twenty minutes left.

The good news is that this is the most trainable component in the whole course, precisely because the difficulty is structural rather than mathematical. A student who has worked through six or eight genuine Paper 3 questions under timing learns the moves: read the whole question before starting, accept a given result and continue if a part will not yield, watch for the moment the paper hands you a general case after two specific ones. None of that is content. All of it is worth marks.

It is also the component schools have the least time for. A Higher Level teacher with a syllabus to finish and an exploration cohort to supervise will prioritise Papers 1 and 2, which is a reasonable allocation of scarce time. It is the clearest single reason a Views family might buy mathematics tutoring in DP2 even when the school is strong and the grades are respectable.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion, with the marks
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is 20% of the grade, it is written during DP1, and it is the component where a Views student is most likely to lose marks they could easily have kept. It is marked out of twenty against five criteria lettered A to E, and almost no family has seen the mark allocation. Seeing it changes how students write.

Criterion E, the use of mathematics, carries six marks and is the one students assume is the whole task. It is not even a third of it. Criterion A on presentation and criterion B on mathematical communication carry four marks each, which together outweigh the mathematics. Criterion C on personal engagement and criterion D on reflection carry three marks each. That means seven of twenty marks are awarded for caring about the topic and for thinking critically about what the mathematics showed, and those are exactly the marks a capable student discards by choosing a topic they are indifferent to and then describing their method instead of evaluating it.

The failure patterns are consistent. A student picks a topic from a list of suggested explorations, so there is nothing personal to engage with. The mathematics is either below course level, which caps criterion E, or copied in at a level the student cannot explain, which caps criterion B. The reflection section is written in the last hour as a paragraph saying the exploration was interesting and could have used more data. And the presentation wanders, because no structure was planned before writing began.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and worth stating plainly. The criteria can be taught, because they are published. A research question can be narrowed in conversation. A method can be demonstrated on entirely different data so the technique transfers. A draft the student has written can be read and told which criterion is underserved and why. What a tutor must not do is write any part of it, rewrite a passage into their own prose, or supply the data or the conclusion. The school's supervisor runs the process and signs it off; a tutor who tries to take that over is making your child's position worse.

sections.heading: The calculator is half the subject, and nobody teaches it
paragraphs: A graphic display calculator is required equipment in IB mathematics, and in Applications and Interpretation it is assumed on every paper. Schools issue them, teach the basics in a lesson or two, and then move on. The result is a cohort of students who can find a numerical solution but cannot use the device to check an algebraic one, who do not know how to read a regression output properly, and who have never set up a graph window deliberately.

The marks lost to this are invisible on a report. A student who plots a function with the default window and concludes there is one root where there are three has made a calculator error that looks like a mathematics error. A student who computes a correct standard deviation but reports the population version where the sample version was wanted has made a menu error. A student who cannot store a value and recall it loses two minutes per question, which across a two-hour paper is a question and a half.

This is one of the places where an online session is plainly better than a tutor at a dining table. A calculator emulator on a shared screen lets a tutor show every keystroke, with the student following on their own device, and lets the student record the sequence for later. Across a table, both people are looking at a small screen upside down and one of them is guessing what the other pressed.

The practical upshot for a Views family is that a few sessions of deliberate calculator work early in DP1 is some of the cheapest grade protection available in this course. It is not glamorous, no school report will ever name it, and it is worth more than an extra month of calculus for most Applications and Interpretation students.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that separate a mathematician from a specialist
paragraphs: You do not need to know IB mathematics to find out whether somebody else does. You need four or five questions with answers specific enough that a general mathematics teacher cannot bluff them. Ask these in the free first lesson, of us or of anybody else you are considering, and listen for whether the answer is precise or approximate.

The first is simply which route and level they teach most. A specialist answers in the syllabus's own words, naming Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation and the level, and usually volunteers which one they prefer and why. A generalist answers with IB maths, which tells you they have not had to distinguish them in practice.

The rest of the questions are in the table below, with the shape of a knowledgeable answer and the shape of an unconvincing one. None of them is a trick. They are the facts a person who has taught the course for a year knows without thinking, and the facts somebody who has read about it cannot produce under mild pressure. A tutor who says they will check and come back on the exploration mark allocation is being honest, which is better than a confident wrong number, but it also tells you where they are in their experience of the course.

One addition worth making to any such conversation: ask what they would want to see before the second session. The answer you want involves your child's own work, a marked paper or a draft. An answer that involves their own diagnostic test is not wrong, but it suggests the teaching will follow their material rather than your child's school.

sections.heading: What a mathematics specialist costs around Emirates Living, by the month
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a Diploma decision. Mathematics support in this course is not a one-off purchase; it is a weekly commitment running anywhere from three months to two years, and the number a Views family actually needs to plan against is monthly. Reading the market that way changes which options look sensible.

Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for one weekly hour put a budget arrangement at AED 240 to AED 600 a month, a mid-market one at AED 600 to AED 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more. Advertised monthly packages in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is eight teaching hours and eight separate journeys by somebody's car.

Convert that into the two realistic Diploma patterns and the planning becomes concrete. One weekly hour across a full DP1 year at the mid-market band is roughly AED 6,000 to AED 12,000 over nine months. A two-term intensive in DP2, at two hours a week in the specialist band, lands in a similar place while buying twice the weekly contact for half the duration. Which is better depends entirely on whether your child's problem is foundation erosion, which needs the long version, or technique, which responds to the short one.

Underneath those figures sit the hourly bands for reference: online university-student tutors from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour at Tutopiya and EdFlik, qualified online subject tutors from AED 150 at Unitors with IB from AED 200, named specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above with TutorChase quoted at AED 270, in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel, and premium examiner-led tutors quoted at AED 650 by BartyED. Every one of those is that provider's own published rate as read in October 2026, not ours. IB Gram publishes no fixed price list on these pages; your quote follows the free first lesson, because route, level and slot all change it.

sections.heading: Starting from The Views, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Tell us four things: the school, the route and level, the component where marks are going, and the evenings that are genuinely free. If you do not know the route, the school knows and a timetable or a report will usually say. If you do not know where the marks are going, that is fine; it is the first thing the free lesson establishes, and it is more often technique than topic.

Bring a marked script. A past paper with an examiner's or teacher's marks on it is worth more than any description of the problem, because it shows whether the marks went to method, to interpretation, to foundation or to time. An exploration draft is equally useful if the exploration is the live issue. A tutor who reads that in the first half-hour and names the pattern has earned the booking; one who talks around it has not.

After that the arrangement is plain. Same tutor, same evening, written notes after each session, and a cadence that rises before mocks and the exploration deadline and falls afterwards. If the pairing is wrong, say so after the second lesson and we will change the tutor rather than defend the match. Mathematics tutoring in particular depends on a student being willing to show what they cannot do, and that only happens if they like the person.

The limits, said once and clearly. No tutor travels to a UAE address; home visiting is an India-only service. No examination date appears on this page, because the IB's site cannot be checked automatically and your school's IB coordinator is the only source worth trusting for your child's session. No grade is guaranteed. No part of the exploration is written for your child. And when no Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist is free in your slot, you are told the realistic date rather than offered a general mathematics tutor who will spend a term discovering the difference.

faqs.question: Is there really nobody near The Views who teaches IB maths properly?
faqs.answer: There are good mathematics teachers in Emirates Living. What is scarce within a short drive is somebody whose main subject is a specific IB route at a specific level, free in the one evening slot your family has. IB mathematics is two courses at two levels, which is four separate teaching jobs, and only a fraction of Dubai's private-school students take any of them. Dropping the distance requirement and keeping the route and level requirement is what makes a genuine specialist reachable at all, and it is why lessons run online.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, or look at a timetable or report, which will name the course in full as Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, with Higher or Standard Level. The distinction is not cosmetic. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-based with a non-calculator Paper 1 at both levels; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with a calculator assumed on every paper. A tutor who is not told which one will teach the wrong preparation competently.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route do UAE universities expect?
faqs.answer: It depends on the programme rather than the country. Engineering, mathematics, physics and the more quantitative economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and some departments say so explicitly. Business, geography, psychology, design and most life-science routes accept either. Requirements differ between institutions and are revised, so check the specific programme's published entry requirements rather than relying on a tutoring page. A strong Applications and Interpretation grade is generally worth more than a weak Analysis and Approaches one.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why has nobody mentioned it?
faqs.answer: It is the third examination at Higher Level only: one hour, two extended problem-solving questions, worth 20% of the grade, sat with a calculator in both routes. It is rarely mentioned because schools with a syllabus to finish and explorations to supervise prioritise Papers 1 and 2, which is a defensible use of limited time. It is also the most trainable component in the course, because students fail it by stopping when stuck rather than by not knowing the mathematics. Six to eight practised papers change that.

faqs.question: How is the mathematical exploration actually marked?
faqs.answer: Out of twenty marks against five criteria. Criterion A for presentation and criterion B for mathematical communication carry four marks each. Criterion C for personal engagement and criterion D for reflection carry three each. Criterion E for use of mathematics carries six. So seven of the twenty marks are awarded for genuine interest in the topic and for critical reflection on the result, which is exactly where able students throw marks away by picking a topic from a suggestion list and describing their method instead of evaluating it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the exploration without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the published criteria, help narrow a research question from unanswerable to workable, demonstrate a technique on completely different data, and read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is underserved. A tutor must not write or rewrite any part of it, or supply the data or the conclusion. Your school's supervisor owns the process and the sign-off. The test a school applies is whether the work is recognisably your child's, in their own voice.

faqs.question: My child is strong on Paper 2 and weak on Paper 1. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly calculator dependence, and it is a specific and fixable diagnosis rather than a general weakness. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels and is worth 40% of the grade at Standard Level and 30% at Higher. A student who has leaned on technology since Year 9 can manipulate expressions on a screen and not on paper. The remedy is unglamorous: timed non-calculator algebra, marked against a real mark scheme, usually across six to eight sessions.

faqs.question: My child switched from MYP maths into DP1 and is drowning. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is one of the commonest enquiries from this community. Middle Years Programme mathematics is assessed against criteria and rewards investigation and communication; Diploma papers reward speed, algebraic fluency and precise notation under timing. A student can be genuinely able and still arrive without the drilled algebra the first calculus unit assumes. The work needed is mostly technique rather than content, and it is best done in the first term of DP1 rather than discovered in the second, when calculus is already hiding the algebra.

faqs.question: Is an Extended IGCSE grade 7 enough preparation for AA Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Often not, and this is where Views families get caught. A Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 Extended grade 7 shows competence across an IGCSE syllabus, but Analysis and Approaches Higher Level assumes fluency rather than competence, and it moves into proof and formal calculus quickly. The shortfall surfaces in the first proof and calculus unit of DP1, not in September. Bridging work over the summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the single most effective intervention available, and it is cheaper than repairing the gap in February.

faqs.question: How much should we budget monthly for IB maths support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' published figures as read in October 2026, not ours. We publish no fixed price list, because a Higher Level Paper 3 block and a Standard Level weekly hour are not the same product.

faqs.question: Does the graphic display calculator need teaching separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and almost nobody does it. Schools issue the device, cover the basics in a lesson or two, and move on. Students then lose marks that look like mathematics errors but are menu errors: a default graph window that hides two roots, a population standard deviation reported where the sample version was wanted, no stored values so two minutes go per question. A few deliberate sessions with an emulator on a shared screen, where every keystroke is visible, is some of the cheapest grade protection in this course.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A specialist in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level frequently teaches Physics too, and where a student's physics problem is actually a mathematics problem, which is common for a Higher Level physics student on Applications and Interpretation Standard Level, one tutor is better than two. Where both subjects have independent problems, two specialists in two shorter slots usually outperforms one person covering both, because the depth matters more than the convenience.

faqs.question: We are in DP2 with four months left. Is maths tutoring still worth it?
faqs.answer: It depends on the diagnosis, and the honest answer differs by component. Foundation erosion cannot be repaired in four months, and anybody promising otherwise is selling. Technique can: method-mark discipline, timing, the interpretation sentence, and Paper 3 format work are all learnable in six to ten sessions because the obstacle is habit rather than knowledge. The exploration is already submitted, so it is off the table. Bring the mock script and the plan will follow what it shows rather than a generic revision schedule.

faqs.question: Why will this page not tell me when the IB maths exams are?
faqs.answer: Because we could not confirm the dates at source. The IB's own website returns an error to automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been verified, and secondary sites publish windows that occasionally disagree. UAE schools sit the May session, and that much is safe. For the dates your child is actually working to, including registration deadlines and the school's internal exploration checkpoints, the IB coordinator at the school is the only authority worth relying on.

faqs.question: What if no AA Higher Level specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a realistic date. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the 17:00 to 18:00 window is one of the tightest combinations we handle, because every Emirates Living family wants the same hour. The alternative to saying so is placing a general mathematics tutor in a Higher Level slot, which costs a term before anyone admits the mismatch. Usually the fix is an adjacent evening or a weekend block. Occasionally it is a wait of a week, and the decision is yours.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IB Mathematics for Tilal Al Ghaf and the Dubailand communities around it. Each teaches a named course at a named level, because Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation Standard Level are different jobs with different papers.

intro.heading: Five topics, two or three papers, one diagnosis
paragraphs: Mathematics is the Diploma subject where a parent can get a genuinely precise answer about what is wrong. Both IB mathematics courses are organised into five topic areas — number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus — and every examination question belongs to one of them and appears on a particular paper. So a marked paper does not have to produce the vague verdict that a student is weak at maths. It can produce a sentence like: most of the lost marks were in functions and calculus, concentrated on the non-calculator paper, and most of those were method rather than answer.

That sentence is what a first session should deliver, and it is what the rest of a plan should be built on. A student losing marks in statistics on the calculator paper has a different problem from one losing them in algebra on the non-calculator paper, and the sessions that fix each look nothing alike. The first is usually about interpretation and writing a conclusion in context. The second is usually about hand execution that has quietly decayed over two years of graphing-display use.

There are four courses, not one, and the first thing any tutor should establish is which. Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. They share the five topic areas and then diverge sharply in what they do within them, in which papers they set and in whether a calculator is permitted. A tutor advertising for 'IB maths' is advertising for all four and specialising in none.

Tilal Al Ghaf makes one part of this easier than most of the Dubailand belt. The community has a school inside its boundary and DAMAC Hills and Dubai Sports City have their own provision next door, so pupils are frequently home before four. For mathematics that matters more than for most subjects, because the thing a Higher Level student most needs and least often gets is a clear two hours in which to sit a full paper while still alert. An early slot makes that possible without using up a weekend.

The exploration deserves naming in the introduction because it is a fifth of the grade in all four courses and is marked out of twenty across five criteria. It is also the component that most rewards starting early, since the decisive factor is whether the chosen topic allows mathematics at or slightly beyond the course level. A student who picks a safe question in the second year cannot reach the upper bands for use of mathematics however neatly the work is presented.

IB Gram delivers mathematics tuition to Tilal Al Ghaf as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics the format costs almost nothing, because a session is worked problems on a shared screen with the student's own working visible line by line, and it widens the shortlist to everyone who teaches your child's exact course.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through every IB programme and the diagnosis changes at each stage. These are the four points at which Tilal Al Ghaf families ask for help.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria each out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where most pupils score worst, because it rewards generalising and justifying rather than calculating, and no amount of arithmetic practice improves it.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai MYP5 mathematics is where the Diploma course decision is effectively made, often on criterion grades the family never read closely. If your child is heading for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, the criterion to watch is investigating patterns rather than knowing and understanding.

programmes.name: IGCSE into Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: Most pupils in this part of Dubailand reach the Diploma from IGCSE rather than the Middle Years Programme, because local provision is predominantly British curriculum. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are the best preparation for Analysis and Approaches, since they introduce calculus and logarithms before the Diploma does.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended or Higher tier is effectively a prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at either level. A pupil entered for Core or Foundation who intends to take the Diploma mathematics route has a content gap rather than a confidence problem, and it should be addressed before Year 12 begins.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four courses across two subjects and two levels, all carrying a 20% exploration. Standard Level sets two papers; Higher Level adds a third. Higher Level extends the five topic areas in depth rather than appending new ones, which is why it cannot be prepared by learning the Standard Level course and adding material at the end.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session. No IB exam or results dates appear on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date a parent acts on is worse than none. Confirm every one with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: Mathematics as a university prerequisite
programmes.description: Engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics courses frequently specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Requirements are published by each institution and vary by course and by year, so they should be read on the university's own course page rather than inferred from a school's general advice.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE university application the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements apply alongside the university's own. The British-track figures are published and sourced; no IB points threshold should be relied on unless read on the Ministry's own channel. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the five syllabus topic areas with the sub-topics Tilal Al Ghaf families most often ask about, plus the components that sit outside them. Marks are lost in nameable places, and this is the list.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging, indices, surds and logarithmic laws. The strongest single predictor of a Diploma mathematics grade, because every later topic is carried by it. A student who hesitates over rearranging loses marks in physics and chemistry too.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: sequences and binomial
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums to infinity, and binomial expansion. Reliable early-paper marks and a reliable source of lost ones, usually through off-by-one errors in the index or forgetting the condition for convergence.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations, and the behaviour of rational and exponential functions. Transformation questions are lost by students who apply the shifts in the wrong order, which is a procedural fix rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry: identities and equations
subjects.levels: All four, substantially extended in AA HL
subjects.description: The unit circle, identities, equations in a given interval and compound angle formulae at Higher Level. The dominant error is solving and reporting only the principal value, losing the remaining solutions in the interval. Exact values without a calculator are examinable in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry: vectors
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, lines and planes, intersections and distances. Students handle the algebra and lose marks on interpretation: whether two lines are skew, or what the angle between a line and a plane means geometrically. Sketching is not required and reliably raises marks.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: All four, heavily weighted in AI
subjects.description: Distributions, conditional probability, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing. In Applications and Interpretation the marks sit in interpretation: correct calculator output with no statement of what it means in context earns very little. Conditional probability is the standard trap in both courses.

subjects.name: Calculus: differentiation
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, then optimisation and related rates. Students who learn the rules without the reasoning fail on applied questions, where the difficulty is setting up the expression rather than differentiating it. Implicit differentiation at Higher Level is a common collapse point.

subjects.name: Calculus: integration
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Techniques, areas, volumes of revolution and, at Higher Level, substitution and integration by parts. The error pattern is mechanical: limits substituted in the wrong order, constants dropped, or a definite integral given a constant it should not carry.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction and proof by induction. The content least like anything in IGCSE, so students arrive with no technique at all. Induction is a format teachable in two sessions and then reliable for the rest of the course.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity. Marks go to argument conventions and to not sketching the Argand diagram, which usually makes the question obvious. Self-contained, so it rewards focused tutoring unusually well.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: A 12 to 20 page individual piece of mathematics marked out of 20 across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Topic choice decides most of the outcome, because use of mathematics is the largest criterion and rewards work at or beyond course level.

subjects.name: Graphing calculator technique
subjects.levels: All four, examined in Papers 2 and 3
subjects.description: Solving numerically, finding intersections, statistical functions, and knowing when a displayed answer still needs supporting working. Students lose marks both by not using the device where it is allowed and by using it without showing the method that earns the credit.

sections.heading: The five topics mapped to the papers
paragraphs: Both IB mathematics courses organise their content into five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation use the same five headings and then weight and treat them very differently, which is the single most useful thing a parent can understand about the choice between them.

In Analysis and Approaches the weight sits in algebra, functions and calculus, with trigonometric identities extended substantially at Higher Level and complex numbers added there. In Applications and Interpretation the weight sits in statistics and probability and in modelling, with calculus present but treated more lightly and more numerically. A student strong at manipulation and weak at interpretation is in the wrong course if they are in Applications; a student who reasons well about data and struggles to rearrange is in the wrong course if they are in Analysis and Approaches.

The mapping to papers is what makes a diagnosis precise. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which means the topics that depend on hand execution — algebraic manipulation, exact trigonometric values, differentiation and integration by hand — concentrate their marks there. Paper 2 permits the device, which shifts the emphasis towards setting up problems correctly and interpreting output. At Higher Level, Paper 3 sets a small number of extended questions requiring sustained reasoning across connected parts.

So a marked paper can tell you something genuinely actionable. Not 'weak at maths' but, for example: losses concentrated in functions and calculus on the non-calculator paper, predominantly method marks rather than final answers. That diagnosis points to a non-calculator block and enforced working, which is four to six weeks of work. A different pattern — losses in statistics on the calculator paper, with correct numbers and no interpretation — points somewhere else entirely and takes two or three sessions.

sections.heading: Paper 1 without a calculator: what is actually examinable by hand
paragraphs: In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, and it is the single most common reason a capable Dubai student underperforms. The problem is not that the mathematics is harder. It is that two years of working with a graphing display erodes hand fluency silently, and the student does not discover it until a mock, by which point there is less time to rebuild it.

What is examinable by hand is a finite and learnable list, which is why this block responds so well to focused work. Exact trigonometric values at the standard angles. Surd manipulation and rationalising. Index laws and fractional and negative indices. Logarithmic laws, including change of base. Completing the square and the quadratic formula applied cleanly. Differentiation by rule, including chain, product and quotient. Standard integrals and definite integration with limits substituted in the right order. Sketching from an equation rather than plotting from a table.

The diagnostic is uncomfortable and quick: take the calculator off the desk and set twenty minutes of questions from that list. A student who is fine will be visibly fine. A student who is not will stall on the second or third item, and the stalling is almost always in the same places — exact values and logarithmic manipulation. Neither is conceptually difficult; both have simply not been practised by hand since Year 11.

Rebuilding takes four to six sessions plus set work, and it is among the highest-yield blocks available in Diploma mathematics, because the marks are spread across the whole of a paper rather than concentrated in one topic. A student who recovers hand fluency does not gain marks in one area; they stop leaking them everywhere on a paper that carries a substantial share of the grade.

sections.heading: Mathematical command terms, which are not the same as other subjects'
paragraphs: Every IB subject has command terms, but mathematics has a set of its own that behave differently and cost marks specifically. They are instructions about method as well as about output, and a student who treats them as synonyms for 'answer the question' loses marks while producing correct mathematics.

'Show that' means the answer is given and the marks are entirely in the working; a student who writes the stated result and nothing else scores zero on a question they could do. 'Hence' means you must use the previous part, and a student who starts again from first principles and reaches the right answer can still lose the marks. 'Hence or otherwise' releases that constraint, and knowing the difference between the two is worth marks every paper. 'Deduce' means draw a conclusion from what is already established rather than recompute. 'Verify' means substitute and confirm, not solve.

'Write down' is the one students over-answer. It signals that no working is expected and the answer should come from a result already available, so a student who produces half a page has spent three minutes earning one mark and will not finish the paper. 'Find' and 'determine' both expect working. 'Prove' requires a complete logical argument, and in proof by induction the structure itself carries marks: base case, inductive assumption, inductive step, conclusion.

This is teachable in two or three sessions and it is almost never taught explicitly, because it looks like exam-technique trivia rather than mathematics. It is not trivia. In a paper where several questions carry a 'show that' or a 'hence', a student who misreads the instruction is discarding marks on questions whose mathematics they have fully understood, and no amount of further content teaching recovers them.

sections.heading: Higher Level Paper 3, and why short questions do not prepare for it
paragraphs: At Higher Level both courses set a third paper carrying a fifth of the grade, and it is the component students prepare least. It consists of a small number of extended questions, each built in connected parts that develop an unfamiliar context, and it runs for an hour. Confirm the current structure and weighting with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides.

The reason ordinary revision does not prepare a student for it is structural. Papers 1 and 2 reward recognising a question type and executing a known method. Paper 3 rewards holding an argument together across eight or ten parts in which each answer feeds the next, usually in a setting the student has never seen. A student who is excellent at short questions can be genuinely lost here, and the loss is not about knowledge.

What works is practising whole questions, slowly at first and then under timing, with explicit attention to the structure. Part (a) is almost always accessible and establishes something the rest will use. The middle parts generalise. The later parts ask for a conclusion or a proof that depends on everything before it. Students who abandon the question after a difficult middle part lose the later marks, many of which were reachable from the earlier results alone. Teaching a student to move on and return is worth marks in itself.

Paper 3 is also where the early slot this community allows is most valuable. An hour of sustained unfamiliar reasoning is not something a student does well at seven in the evening after a full day and other homework, and a paper attempted then produces a misleadingly poor result that knocks confidence for no useful reason. In Tilal Al Ghaf, where pupils are often home before four, a weekday Paper 3 session is actually feasible.

sections.heading: The graphing calculator: where it earns marks and where it loses them
paragraphs: On the calculator papers the device is not optional decoration; it is examined. Students lose marks in two opposite directions and both are worth naming, because the fixes are different and neither is about mathematics.

The first loss is under-use. A question that permits a calculator and asks for a root, an intersection, a definite integral or a statistical measure is expecting the device to be used, and a student labouring through it by hand is spending four minutes on a two-minute question. That pattern shows up as an unfinished paper rather than as wrong answers, which is why it is so often misdiagnosed as a content problem.

The second loss is over-reliance without method. A displayed answer with no supporting working forfeits the method marks, because mark schemes credit the steps. In statistics this is the dominant loss: a student produces a correct regression equation or test statistic and writes nothing about what it means in the context of the question, and the interpretation is where the marks were. In Applications and Interpretation that single habit can account for a large share of a paper's deficit.

There is a third issue specific to Dubai classrooms, which is model familiarity. Students sometimes arrive mid-course having used a different calculator model at a previous school, and a device the student cannot operate fluently under pressure is worse than no device. That is a two-session fix and it is worth checking in a first diagnostic, because it masquerades as weakness in whichever topic the question happened to be about.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine for mathematics specifically
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where past-paper work is most often done badly, because doing questions feels productive and the useful part happens afterwards. A routine that works has four elements and most students use one.

First, separate the papers. Work non-calculator questions without the device, properly, with it out of the room. Students who keep it nearby use it, and the practice becomes worthless for the paper it was meant to prepare. Second, time the work. Twenty-five minutes against a clock teaches more about pacing than ninety minutes of untimed questions, and pacing is where a large share of marks go on a two-hour paper.

Third, mark against the published scheme rather than against whether the answer looks right. This is the element that changes results, because it shows where credit actually sits: a method line, a stated conclusion, a unit, an exact rather than decimal form. Students who learn to read a mark scheme start writing for the marker, and in mathematics that shift alone is frequently worth a grade. Fourth, tag every lost mark with a topic and a type — functions and method, statistics and interpretation, calculus and arithmetic slip — and keep the tally across several papers.

The tally is the point of the whole exercise. After three or four marked papers a pattern appears that no single paper shows, and it is usually narrower than the student believed. A tally that says two-thirds of losses are method marks in algebra across both papers is a four-week plan. A tally spread evenly across five topics and both papers means the issue is pacing rather than content, which is a different and cheaper fix. Without the tally, revision defaults to whichever topic feels worst, which is rarely the one costing the most.

sections.heading: What mathematics tutoring costs, by what you are buying
paragraphs: Mathematics is the one Diploma subject where the work can be costed before it is bought, because the diagnosis names a block of known length. So read the published bands as a price per block rather than per hour. At the bottom, EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 make a two-session calculator-technique block a sum that barely registers against a Tilal Al Ghaf household's monthly outgoings. In the middle, Unitors publishes from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, and Bestimate's Dubai table puts IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 - at which point a six-session non-calculator restoration block becomes a figure a parent will reasonably want a reason for, and the marked papers are that reason. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to AED 350 on the same table. The monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support describe open-ended arrangements, which is the shape of spending this page argues against. Every figure comes from a competitor's own published page, read in October 2026.

In mathematics the useful way to read those numbers is by block rather than by month, because the diagnosis points to blocks of known length. A non-calculator restoration block is four to six sessions. A command-term block is two to three. A calculator-technique block is two. Exploration coaching is six to eight across a term. Whole-topic repair in calculus or algebra is a holiday block of four or five sessions a week. Each of those has a price you can calculate from the band, and each targets a different and identifiable share of the grade.

That framing also shows where the money should not go. Open-ended weekly tutoring with no named target is the most expensive thing in this market, because it continues indefinitely and addresses whatever came up that week. A family paying the specialist band for general weekly maths support, without a tally of where marks are going, is buying attention rather than diagnosis. The tally costs one session and redirects everything after it.

IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page, because the right figure depends on which of the four courses, which level, and which block the evidence calls for. The market band above lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free. Ask the tutor in it to name the five exploration criteria with their marks and to explain the difference between 'hence' and 'hence or otherwise'; a genuine specialist answers both without pausing.

sections.heading: The exploration, honesty and the permit position
paragraphs: The exploration is worth a fifth of the grade in all four courses and is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics is the largest single criterion and rewards work at or slightly beyond the course level, which is why a safe topic cannot reach the top bands however neatly it is presented. Confirm the current criteria with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides.

That weighting also explains the honesty boundary in practical terms. Personal engagement and reflection reward thinking the student actually did, and an exploration written by someone else reads precisely as such. There are providers in this region selling completed internal assessments at published prices; submitting one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student. The marks it would have gained are exactly the ones it destroys.

What a tutor legitimately does is test viability, teach any mathematics the chosen question requires including content beyond the course, explain each criterion and its descriptors, and give feedback on the student's own drafts. What a tutor does not do is write any part of it, supply the mathematics as a finished solution to be transcribed, choose the topic, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. Where a draft is not working, the tutor names the problem and the student rewrites.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so distrust quoted amounts. We also do not distribute IB papers, mark schemes or boundary tables, and IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education.
