dubai/ib-may-session-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: The May session sits at the end of a two-year programme, and where a student is in that programme changes what preparation means. These are the three stages Dubai families are usually buying for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: Content is being taught for the first time and the Internal Assessments are beginning. Useful work here is keeping taught topics alive and getting the Extended Essay question narrowed, not revision. A student who reaches the second year with a settled Extended Essay question has bought themselves ten weeks of the final year.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run internal examinations towards the end of the first year, and those are the first realistic measurement of where a student stands. A marked paper at that point, rather than a report comment, is what makes the second-year plan specific instead of general.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: Thirty weeks containing six Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, mock examinations, predicted grades, university applications and then the written papers. The scarce resource is weeks, not willingness, and the only way through is a schedule built backwards from the internal deadlines rather than forwards from September.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai candidates sitting the May session are usually applying to universities across several systems at once, with the main UCAS deadline in January, United States deadlines through the winter, and UAE university applications on their own timetable. Those dates collide with the internal deadline period, which is the real reason the second year feels impossible.

programmes.name: Retake and November candidates
programmes.description: A candidate retaking subjects sits a later session with a different shape: no new teaching, a narrow set of components, and a results date that arrives after many university deadlines have passed. Preparation is almost entirely paper technique, because the content was taught and the loss was usually in the paper rather than in the knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: For a Dubai family, the practical consequence of a retake is a gap year decision taken on incomplete information. Working out which subjects are realistically movable, and by how many marks, before committing to a retake entry is the part worth paying for.

dubai/ib-may-session-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: In the final year the question is never which subjects to study but which to give the scarce hours to. Each entry below names what is most recoverable in that subject late in the year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Late gains come from non-calculator fluency and from written method on multi-step questions. Higher Level Paper 3 is short, often under-practised, and rewards setting out an approach, which makes two marked attempts at it unusually productive in the final ten weeks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The recoverable marks sit in interpreting output in context and stating assumptions, both of which are writing skills rather than mathematics. Students who are fluent with technology and weak on commentary can move several marks a paper in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions reward precise reading rather than recall and are the fastest component to improve late. Extended responses need the mark scheme's accepted terminology, which is learned by marking rather than by reading.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation method marks and organic mechanism detail are the recurring losses, and both are habits. A student who writes steps and includes conditions and reagents recovers marks across every paper without learning new content.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and the explicit statement of the principle being used are where scripts bleed. Late in the year this is the highest-return work available, because the physics is usually known and the marks are being discarded on presentation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy with labels and a stated direction of change earns marks independently of the prose, and evaluation at the end of extended responses is the most common omission. Both are trainable inside four marked questions.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source questions are structural and improve quickly once origin, purpose and content drive value and limitations. Essays need a line of argument sustained across paragraphs, which is harder to fix late and should be started in the first year.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis and the comparative essay both reward writing to the clock. Comparing two of the student's own timed attempts a fortnight apart shows structural improvement in a way that reading model answers does not.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three of the forty-five points, and both are internally deadlined long before the written papers. In the final year they are the components most often left late and the ones where late work costs the most, because they compete directly with revision weeks.

dubai/ib-may-session-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: In the final year the location question is simply when a session can happen, because a candidate carrying six subjects plus the core has very little uncommitted time. These notes cover the realistic slots across the city.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Large Diploma cohorts and heavy co-curricular calendars, so weekday sessions often start after 19:30. Holding a fixed weekly slot matters more here than finding an ideal one, because a moving slot is the main reason final-year plans collapse.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Short commutes allow a 16:30 start, which is the one part of the city where an after-school paper rehearsal is realistic on a weekday. Worth using for timed components rather than for discussion sessions.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Households often have a Diploma candidate and an IGCSE sibling sitting examinations in overlapping windows. One household calendar with both sets of internal deadlines on it prevents the collisions that produce missed submissions.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long eastern commutes make weekday evening sessions short and tired. Families here get more from a longer weekend block for paper work and a brief midweek check-in than from two full weekday sessions.

regions.name: Downtown, Business Bay and Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Central apartments close to two continuum IB schools, with quiet space at a premium during the mock period. Splitting a timed paper into two halves, logged as such, beats a sitting interrupted in the middle.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University-belt families with strong Higher Level maths and science cohorts. Demand concentrates on Paper 3 work and on Internal Assessment evaluation sections, both short and both commonly left until after the mocks.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Big final-year cohorts with mock timetables clustered in the same weeks, which means tutoring capacity in this part of the city is scarcest exactly when families decide they need it. Booking before the mock window is the only real advantage available.

schoolClusters.city: Central and eastern Dubai Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: A mix of continuum IB schools and schools where the Diploma runs alongside other curricula. Students here more often arrive in the first Diploma year from IGCSE, which makes the Internal Assessment calendar unfamiliar rather than merely demanding.

sections.heading: What the May session means for a Dubai candidate
paragraphs: The May session is the northern-hemisphere examination series, and it is the one almost every Dubai IB school enters its candidates for. The practical meaning is that the second year of the Diploma ends in written papers in the late spring, with the Dubai school year finishing shortly afterwards. A candidate in the May session is therefore sitting examinations while the school term is still running, which is not how families who remember a long study leave expect it to feel.

No examination date, upload deadline or results date for the IB appears on this page. That is deliberate and worth explaining, because every competitor either omits the calendar entirely or publishes dates with no source. The IB's own site blocks automated verification, so nothing here could be checked at the time of writing, and a date a parent acts on must come from somewhere verifiable. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed dates for your child's session, including the internal deadlines, which are the ones that actually bind.

What can be said without a date is the order, and the order is what families get wrong. Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay are submitted internally and uploaded by the school well before the papers. Predicted grades are produced before most university deadlines. Mocks sit between the two. Written papers come last. A plan that treats the papers as the first milestone will arrive at the Internal Assessment deadlines unprepared, and those marks are already banked by the time revision starts.

The second thing worth stating is that the May session is not the only session. A November series exists, and for a candidate who is genuinely not ready, entering later is a real option with real costs, chiefly that results arrive after many university decisions. Knowing that early changes the conversation from panic to arithmetic, which is the right way to make it.

sections.heading: Thirty weeks, counted backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Backwards planning is the single most useful thing a final-year family can do, and nobody in this market publishes it. Start from the written papers and work back in blocks rather than dates, because blocks stay true year after year while dates do not. Each block has a different job, and the mistake is treating all thirty weeks as revision weeks when only the last ten really are.

In the first block, roughly weeks thirty to twenty-one before the papers, the work is coursework and content. Internal Assessment drafts in several subjects, the Extended Essay moving from question to draft, Theory of Knowledge beginning. Revision in this block is low-value because the syllabus is incomplete, but keeping earlier topics alive with short marked question sets prevents the decay that shows up as a bad mock.

In the middle block, weeks twenty to eleven, the internal deadlines close and the mocks arrive. This is the busiest and most decisive stretch of the Diploma, and it is also when Ramadan currently falls, shifting routines for several weeks. The marks submitted in this block are final, so time spent here on a draft is worth more per hour than time spent later on revision, which is counter-intuitive and consistently ignored.

In the final block, weeks ten to one, nothing but the papers remains. This is where whole-paper rehearsal, error logs and habit change belong, and where a tutor can honestly say what is reachable. The table sets the blocks out with the evidence each should leave behind, so you can check at any point in the year whether the plan is actually running.

sections.heading: The internal deadlines nobody warns you about
paragraphs: Families plan for examinations and are blindsided by internal deadlines, which is the structural feature of the Diploma that most distinguishes it from an examination-only qualification. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment with a school deadline. The Extended Essay has a sequence of supervisor meetings, a reflection requirement and a submission date. Theory of Knowledge has an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. All of these are marked work that contributes to the final result and all of them close before the papers.

The consequence of missing one is not a late penalty in the ordinary sense. Work the school cannot upload by its own deadline creates a problem that the school then has to manage, and the student's result can be affected in ways that are entirely avoidable with a calendar. Schools are generally very clear about these dates; the gap is that nobody assembles them into one list the family can see, so each arrives as a surprise.

Building that list is a half-hour job and the highest-value half hour in the final year. Ask the coordinator for every internal deadline across all six subjects plus the core, write them on one calendar with the mock window and the university deadlines, and look at where they cluster. The clustering is the problem: three Internal Assessment deadlines and a university application in the same fortnight is a workload issue that can only be solved by starting earlier.

sections.heading: What a Dubai mock result actually tells you
paragraphs: Mock season in Dubai schools usually falls in the middle block of the final year, and the results produce more family arguments than any other single event in the Diploma. The reason is that everybody treats the mock grade as a forecast when it is a measurement taken before the examination-specific work has happened. A mock sat two-thirds of the way through the syllabus, in a hall, by a tired student in the middle of the internal deadline period, is not a prediction of a result two months later.

What a mock does give you, if the scripts come back, is the best diagnosis available all year. The useful questions are not what grade but where the marks went. How many were lost in the final third of each paper, which indicates endurance rather than knowledge. How many were lost on command terms. How many on method not shown. How many on topics taught in the first year and never revisited. Those four numbers point at four different plans.

Most families never see the scripts, and asking for them is reasonable and usually granted. A mock script with the marks mapped by cause is worth more than any amount of discussion of the grade. Where the school cannot release scripts, a tutor can replicate the diagnosis with one comparable paper sat under the same conditions, which is a slower route to the same information.

The other thing a mock does is set the predicted grade conversation in motion, which has consequences for university offers. A student who understands that the mock is a diagnosis can use the weeks after it to change the inputs. A student who treats it as a verdict loses two weeks to demoralisation in the most expensive part of the year, which is the real cost of reading the number wrongly.
bullets: Ask for the scripts, not just the grades
Map lost marks by cause: content, command term, method, time

sections.heading: The weekly evidence record, and how to read it
paragraphs: A parent who does not teach chemistry can still tell whether final-year preparation is working, provided the right things are being produced. The test is simple: at the end of each week, does something exist that was not there at the start, and can you look at it. A marked question set with a score. A raw mark on a timed component, with the date and the paper reference. An Internal Assessment draft with comments naming criterion letters. A topic list with two items crossed off.

Weeks that produce nothing are not necessarily wasted, but they should be rare and explained. A session spent narrowing an Extended Essay question produces a sentence rather than a score, which is legitimate and should be written down as such. A session spent talking generally about revision technique produces nothing and should not recur. The record is what makes that distinction visible rather than contested.

Over six weeks the record becomes a trend, and the trend is the only honest measure of progress available before results. Three raw marks on comparable papers in the same subject, sat under the same conditions, show movement or they do not. An error log with cleared items shows habits changing. A topic list that is the same length as it was a month ago shows that hours are being spent without being converted.

The table gives the weekly artefact for each type of session, so you can ask for the right thing rather than for a progress report. Progress reports are easy to write and hard to check; marked work is the opposite.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the Dubai term calendar across the revision window
paragraphs: Ramadan currently falls across the February-and-March part of the UAE academic year and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which places it inside the middle block of the final Diploma year for the current cycle. School hours are shortened, the structure of the day changes, and in many households the rhythm of eating and sleeping changes with it. None of that is a reason to pause preparation and all of it is a reason to plan the preparation differently.

The practical adjustments are straightforward. Sessions move later, after Iftar, for families who are fasting, and the fixed slot is worth re-establishing for the month rather than negotiated weekly. Timed papers, which need two hours of alertness, are better placed on weekend mornings during this period than on weekday evenings. Content-heavy sessions move earlier in the window and lighter review work later.

Eid holidays then remove several days entirely, and they tend to land close to a mock window or an internal deadline. A family that looks at the term calendar in the first block can see that collision coming and move a draft forward by a fortnight. A family that looks in the week before cannot. This is the clearest example on this page of planning that costs nothing and saves a great deal.

The final consideration is that the Dubai school year typically ends only weeks after the written papers, so the long decompression other systems offer does not exist here. Students sit papers while term is running, with lessons and school commitments continuing around them. Planning the last two weeks as a closing-down period rather than a cramming period matters more in this city than in a system with extended study leave.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, university offers, and what the May session decides
paragraphs: Predicted grades are produced by the school and used by universities, and they are generated from evidence the school holds: classwork, internal assessments and mock results. They are not a negotiation, but they are not a mystery either, and a student who understands which evidence feeds them can act on it in the weeks that matter. Asking the coordinator what evidence informs the prediction, and when it is finalised, is a reasonable question that very few families ask in time.

The application calendar then collides with the internal deadline period. The main UCAS deadline falls in January each year, with the current date published on UCAS's own site. United States applications run through the winter. UAE university applications and any Ministry of Education equivalency work run on their own timetables. All of this happens while Internal Assessments are closing, which is why the second year feels less like a course and more like a logistics exercise.

What the May session itself decides is whether conditional offers are met, and that is where the arithmetic of the final ten weeks becomes concrete. A conditional offer names points or specific subject grades, so the preparation plan should be weighted towards the subjects the offer actually depends on. A student spending equal hours across six subjects when the offer rests on two Higher Level grades is allocating by anxiety rather than by consequence.

Equivalency is worth a separate sentence because it is widely misunderstood. Recognition of a foreign secondary certificate in the UAE is handled by the Ministry of Education through its own process, which IB Gram does not perform and no tutoring service should present as something it can secure. For the British track the published requirements are specific; no IB points threshold is quoted here, because none has been verified from an official Ministry source for this page.

sections.heading: What six weeks can and cannot move
paragraphs: Families arrive at six weeks out more often than at any other point, and they deserve a straight answer. Six weeks can change habits, and habits are worth real marks: writing method, matching command terms, putting units on answers, adding the evaluation sentence, pacing a paper so the final third is not abandoned. Across six subjects those changes are visible on a marked script within three papers, and they do not require any new content.

Six weeks can also fix one or two specific components. A Higher Level Paper 3, a data-based question type, a source paper structure, a diagram convention in economics. These are narrow and high-density, which is exactly what a short window suits, and a tutor who proposes two components rather than two syllabuses is giving you the better plan.

What six weeks cannot do is teach a year of missing content, raise every subject at once, or recover a mark already banked on a submitted Internal Assessment. Anyone who implies otherwise is selling hope. The honest version names what will be covered, what will not, and what the realistic effect is, and leaves the family to decide whether that is worth the fee.

This page carries no success rate, average point score or satisfaction figure, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method. No tutor can promise a Diploma score or a specific subject grade. What can be promised is that the work produces artefacts you can read: marked scripts with raw marks and dates, comments tied to criterion letters, a topic list that shortens and an error log that narrows. That is the whole offer, and it is checkable week by week.

process.title: Build the single deadline calendar
process.description: Ask the Diploma coordinator for every internal deadline across all six subjects plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, then put them on one calendar with the mock window and university dates. The clustering is the information. This takes half an hour and is the highest-value half hour of the final year.

process.title: Measure once, with a marked paper
process.description: One timed paper in each of the two weakest subjects, marked to the published scheme, with every lost mark classified as content, command term, method or time. That classification is what makes a plan specific. Mock scripts work for this too, if the school will release them, which is usually worth asking.

process.title: A free trial lesson on the real artefact
process.description: The trial is a real session with the tutor who would continue, no card details taken beforehand, spent on the student's marked script or Internal Assessment draft. It ends with a written note: what is recoverable, in what order, over how many sessions, with an end date you can hold.

process.title: Weekly artefacts, monthly comparison
process.description: Every week produces something you can look at. Every month, the first and latest raw marks on comparable papers sit side by side and the topic list is counted. If the marks have not moved and the list has not shortened, the method changes rather than the hours increasing.

process.title: Close the plan rather than extend it
process.description: In the last fortnight nothing new starts. The error log is reviewed, the habits are rehearsed, the timetable is checked against the school's own copy, and sleep is protected. A tutor proposing new content in the final two weeks is adding load at the point where load is the problem.

whyPoints.title: Deadlines before papers
whyPoints.description: The plan starts from the school's internal deadline list, because Internal Assessment and core marks are banked before revision begins. Sessions placed against those dates change a submitted mark; the same hours spent later change a feeling about readiness.

whyPoints.title: Dates we cannot verify are not published
whyPoints.description: No IB examination, upload or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be checked automatically for it. Your coordinator holds the confirmed dates. A page that invents them is the kind of page a family acts on and then regrets.

whyPoints.title: Mocks read as diagnosis
whyPoints.description: A mock grade is a measurement taken before the examination-specific work has happened, not a forecast. The scripts, with lost marks mapped by cause, are worth more than the grade, and asking the school for them is reasonable and usually granted.

whyPoints.title: The record is the product
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts with raw marks and dates, comments tied to criterion letters, a shortening topic list, a narrowing error log. All of it readable by a parent who does not teach the subject, which is the point of keeping it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the last six weeks
whyPoints.description: Habits and one or two components can move in six weeks. A year of missing content, six subjects at once, and a submitted Internal Assessment mark cannot. Saying which situation you are in costs us a sale and saves you a term of false expectation.

faqs.question: What is the May session, and will my child's Dubai school sit it?
faqs.answer: The May session is the northern-hemisphere IB examination series, and it is the one almost every Dubai IB school enters its candidates for. In practice it means the written papers fall in the late spring, with the Dubai school year ending only weeks afterwards, so candidates sit examinations while term is still running. A November series also exists and is used mainly for retakes and by schools on a different academic calendar. Your Diploma coordinator can confirm which session your child is entered for and the exact dates.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the exact IB examination dates for the session?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB's own site for this page, and a date a family acts on has to come from somewhere checkable. The IB blocks automated access, so any date reproduced here would be second-hand. That matters more than it sounds: a wrong deadline published on a tutoring site is exactly the kind of thing a parent plans a term around. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed examination, upload and internal deadlines for your child's session, and those internal dates are the ones that actually bind.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the papers should serious preparation start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families expect, but not as revision. The final year runs about thirty teaching weeks, and the first ten belong to Internal Assessment drafts and the Extended Essay, because those marks are banked before any revision happens. Weeks twenty to eleven cover the internal deadlines and the mocks. Only the last ten are genuinely revision weeks. So the honest answer is that preparation starts at the beginning of the final year and changes character three times, and a plan that treats all thirty weeks as revision will miss the parts it could have changed.

faqs.question: What should I be able to see after four weeks of paid preparation?
faqs.answer: Something readable without knowing the subject. Three or four marked artefacts with dates: a timed component with a raw mark and paper reference, a question set with a score, or an Internal Assessment draft with comments naming criterion letters. A topic list with items crossed off rather than rewritten. An error log with a narrowing pattern. If four weeks have produced only progress conversations, ask what artefact the next four weeks will produce, because that question changes how the sessions are run.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss one of the school's internal coursework deadlines?
faqs.answer: It is not a late penalty in the ordinary sense. Work the school cannot upload by its own deadline becomes a problem the school has to manage, and the student's result can be affected in ways that were entirely avoidable. Schools publish these dates clearly; the gap is that nobody assembles them into one family-visible list, so each arrives as a surprise. Ask the coordinator for every internal deadline across all six subjects plus the core, put them on one calendar, and look at where they cluster.

faqs.question: What does a Dubai mock result actually predict?
faqs.answer: Less than families think, and it diagnoses more than they use. A mock is sat partway through the syllabus, in the middle of the internal deadline period, by a tired student, so the grade is a measurement rather than a forecast. The scripts are the valuable part. Map the lost marks by cause, count separately how many were lost in the final third of each paper, and you have four different numbers pointing at four different plans. Ask the school to release the scripts; the request is reasonable and usually granted.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect revision before the May papers?
faqs.answer: Ramadan currently falls across the February-and-March part of the academic year, inside the busiest block of the final year, and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year. School hours shorten and household routines change for several weeks. The practical adjustments are to move sessions after Iftar and keep the slot fixed for the month, to put timed papers on weekend mornings rather than weekday evenings, and to front-load content-heavy work. Eid holidays then remove several days, often close to a mock window, which is worth seeing on a calendar months ahead.

faqs.question: Can a predicted grade still change before university offers are confirmed?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades are produced by the school from the evidence it holds, which includes classwork, internal assessments and mock performance, and they are finalised at a point the coordinator can tell you. They are not a negotiation, but they are not arbitrary either, so a student who knows which evidence feeds the prediction and when it closes can act in the weeks that matter. Ask the coordinator what informs the prediction and when it is submitted. Very few families ask early enough for the answer to be useful.

faqs.question: Is six weeks enough to move a grade before the written papers?
faqs.answer: Six weeks can reliably change habits, and habits carry real marks: writing method, matching command terms, units and significant figures, the evaluation sentence at the end of an extended response, pacing so the final third of a paper is not abandoned. It can also fix one or two narrow components such as a Higher Level Paper 3 or a source paper structure. It cannot teach a year of missing content, lift six subjects at once, or recover a mark already banked on a submitted Internal Assessment. A plan that says which of those applies is the useful one.

faqs.question: Should my child revise all six subjects equally in the final term?
faqs.answer: No, and allocating evenly is the most common planning error in the final term. Weight the hours by two things: where marks are most recoverable, which a marked paper tells you, and what a conditional university offer actually depends on. A student whose offer rests on two Higher Level grades should not be spending equal time on six subjects. The uncomfortable version of this is that a subject with whole topics missing may be the wrong place to spend the last six weeks, even though it feels like the most urgent.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Dubai Hills or Emirates Hills during the exam term?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and every session is delivered online over live video. In the final year that has a practical benefit beyond cost. A candidate carrying six subjects and a co-curricular calendar can take a 19:30 or 20:00 session without anybody adding a drive to the evening, and the fixed slot is far more likely to survive a busy term, which matters more than any single session does.

faqs.question: What does final-year Diploma preparation cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from around AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialist work, with a premium named tier reaching AED 650 at BartyED and TutorChase quoting AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above in a specialist exam year. Those are the providers' own figures. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson, stating session length and whether marking is included.

faqs.question: My child may need retakes as well as the May session. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the arithmetic rather than the method. A later session means no new teaching, a narrow set of components and a results date that arrives after many university decisions, so the first question is which subjects are realistically movable and by how many marks. That is answerable from marked scripts rather than from feelings. Deciding before entries close, with the numbers in front of you, is far better than deciding in the week after results, and it is the part of the process worth paying for.

faqs.question: How do we build a week-by-week record without it becoming a chore?
faqs.answer: Keep it to one page and four columns: date, what was produced, the raw mark if there was one, and what changed on the topic list or the error log. A session that produced a sentence rather than a score is recorded as that, which is legitimate for an Extended Essay session. The record takes two minutes a week and does one job: it makes the difference between a productive week and a busy one visible rather than contested, which is what most final-year arguments are really about.

faqs.question: What happens to Theory of Knowledge and CAS in the final term?
faqs.answer: Both should already be finished, and when they are not they become the most expensive items on the calendar, because they compete directly with revision weeks. The Theory of Knowledge essay carries core points and has a school deadline set against the IB's upload window. CAS is a completion requirement with reflections, and an incomplete record turns into an administrative problem during examination weeks. Ask the coordinator in the first block of the year what remains outstanding on both, which is the moment when finishing them is still cheap.

dubai/ib-may-session-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start with one calendar and one marked paper
dubai/ib-may-session-exam-preparation.closingBody: Two things change a final Diploma year, and neither of them is more hours. Ask the coordinator for every internal deadline across the six subjects and the core, put them on one calendar with the mock window and the university dates, and look at the clustering. Then have your child sit one timed paper in each of the two weakest subjects and have the lost marks classified by cause. Book the free trial lesson and spend it on those artefacts. By the end you should have a written plan with an end date, and from then on you can check it week by week by looking at what exists rather than by asking how it is going.

dubai/ib-mock-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Diploma mock preparation across the six subject groups, plus the core. Each works from marked scripts and official command terms, and every session runs live, one-to-one, at a Dubai-friendly hour.

intro.heading: What a Dubai IB mock actually measures
paragraphs: A mock exam is the only moment before May when a Diploma student sits a full paper under timed conditions and has it marked by someone applying IB criteria. Dubai schools treat that information seriously. Most run Diploma mocks in a window that opens in late November and closes in early February, usually with DP2 cohorts sitting two or three papers per subject across a fortnight. The marks feed directly into the predicted grades a coordinator submits, and those predictions are what a university admissions office reads months before any real result exists.

That makes the mock a high-stakes administrative event and a low-stakes learning event at the same time. The grade itself changes nothing on the final transcript. The pattern inside the paper changes everything about what the next five months should contain. A student who scored 4 in Biology HL may have lost almost all of those marks on command terms, not content: answering 'explain' questions as if they said 'describe', or writing three correct sentences where the mark scheme wanted a causal chain. Another student in the same class with the same 4 may know the content badly in two topics and well everywhere else. Those two students need entirely different work, and a summary grade cannot tell them apart.

IB mock exam preparation in Dubai therefore starts with the script, not the syllabus. We ask for the marked paper, the mark scheme the school used, and the subject report if the teacher wrote one. From there a tutor builds a map of where the marks actually went: by paper, by question type, by topic, by command term. That map is usually surprising. Students who describe themselves as weak at Mathematics often turn out to be losing most of their marks to method-mark presentation and calculator use rather than to the mathematics itself.

Dubai adds its own timing pressures. The mock window overlaps with the internal deadlines for Internal Assessments in most subjects, with the Extended Essay final submission in many schools, and often with family travel over the winter break. A revision plan written as if the student had free evenings for eight weeks will be abandoned by week two. Ours is written against the actual school calendar: which weeks are already full, when the IA draft is due, where a 90-minute session fits between a 3:30pm finish and dinner.

The second thing Dubai adds is distance from the usual tutoring pool. A family in Dubai Hills looking for a Chemistry HL specialist who can mark Paper 3 to criteria has a far smaller local market than a family in London. Because every session here runs over live video, the constraint disappears: the match is made on subject and level, not on who can reach your community by 5pm. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and the online format is what makes a genuine subject specialist reachable from any Dubai community.

dubai/ib-mock-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Mock exams exist at all three IB stages, but they mean different things at each. Below is what a mock measures in each programme and how that changes the work in a Dubai context.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma mock is the serious one. DP2 students sit full-length papers under exam conditions, marked against published criteria, across six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge. Results drive the predicted grades submitted to universities and often decide whether a school recommends a level change from HL to SL while that is still administratively possible.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are concentrated in a relatively small set of schools, which means subject sizes can be tiny: a Physics HL class of nine is common. A student who is third from bottom in that class may still be sitting at a grade 5 globally, and the reverse happens too. Comparing a mock mark against published criteria rather than against eight classmates is the single most useful correction a tutor makes at this stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment is criterion-referenced rather than paper-based, so an MYP mock is usually a criterion-aligned task rather than a past paper. Students are marked A to D on strands specific to each subject group, and the levels do not convert to IB grades in any simple way, which is the source of most parental confusion at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, skipping IGCSE altogether. For those families the Year 11 mock is the first timed-paper experience the student has ever had, and the gap is usually exam stamina and written structure rather than subject knowledge. Work in Dubai MYP5 mocks tends to focus hardest on the shift from criterion tasks to a clock.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There are no mocks in the PYP. Assessment is continuous, portfolio-based, and reported against transdisciplinary learning rather than subject marks. Where families seek support at this stage it is usually for the transition into MYP, for English as an additional language, or for the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the PYP.
programmes.countryNote: PYP parents in Dubai often meet the word 'mock' for the first time when an older sibling reaches DP2 and the house changes shape for six weeks. Understanding early that the Diploma mock is a diagnostic rather than a sentence makes the later years calmer, and it is worth knowing which secondary school a Dubai primary feeds before Year 6 ends.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines DP courses with a career-related study and four core components. Students sitting DP subjects within a CP frame sit the same mock papers as DP candidates for those subjects, but carry a different overall workload and a reflective project instead of the full six-subject spread.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by only a handful of UAE schools, so CP students in Dubai frequently find that generic IB revision material does not match their timetable. Mock preparation for a CP candidate is narrower and more intense: usually two or three DP subjects at once, with the career-related study deadlines sitting awkwardly across the same weeks.

dubai/ib-mock-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Mock marks leak in subject-specific ways. The list below names the component where Dubai students most often lose marks in a mock and what a session does about it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Mock losses here are rarely conceptual. They cluster in method presentation, premature rounding, and the non-calculator paper, where students who can solve a problem on a graphic display calculator cannot show the algebra. Sessions rebuild working-out habits against mark schemes so method marks survive a wrong final answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The AI mock punishes weak modelling language and statistical interpretation rather than algebra. Students write the right test and then fail to state a conclusion in context. Work focuses on the sentence after the calculation, which is where a surprising share of the marks sits.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 2 extended response is the usual casualty: energetics and equilibrium answers that state a correct fact without the mechanism the mark scheme wants. HL mocks also expose gaps in organic reaction pathways. Sessions work through marked responses line by line against criteria rather than re-teaching whole topics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do the damage. 'Outline', 'explain', 'distinguish' and 'suggest' each want a different shape of answer, and Dubai mock scripts regularly show full content knowledge scoring half marks because the shape was wrong. Data-based questions on Paper 2 are the second recurring weak point.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mock papers expose unit and significant-figure discipline, and the habit of starting a mechanics question with the wrong equation from the data booklet. HL candidates lose most in fields and induction. Sessions drill the booklet itself: which relationship applies, and how to show the substitution.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the mark. An unlabelled axis or a shifted curve without an explanation turns a good argument into a mid-band answer. Evaluation in Paper 1 part (b) is the other gap: students describe both sides without reaching a judgement supported by the diagram.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis is where mock marks go missing, usually because the student summarises the text rather than analysing how its features create meaning. Sessions practise unseen extracts under time, then compare the response against the published assessment criteria strand by strand.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case-study paper rewards tool application, not tool recall. Mock scripts routinely include a correct Ansoff matrix with no link back to the stimulus firm. Work focuses on using the case material as evidence and on the HL extension topics that appear late in DP2.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Mock answers lose marks on study detail: aim, method, findings and conclusion, with the link back to the question made explicit. Students often know ten studies loosely and none precisely. Sessions build a smaller, firmer bank of studies that can carry multiple question types.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Where a school mocks TOK it is normally an essay against a prescribed title. Marks go on claims without counterclaims, and on examples drawn from nowhere in particular. Support is feedback on the student's own reasoning and structure, never drafting on their behalf.

dubai/ib-mock-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Mock windows and school-run timings differ by community, and both decide when a session can realistically happen. Below is what the mock weeks look like in some of the Dubai areas families contact us from.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: A young community with a heavy DP2 population across nearby IB and British schools. Mock fortnights here often collide with winter travel, so families tend to front-load sessions into late November.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Feeds several established Diploma cohorts. Pick-up times are late enough that a 6pm Gulf-time session usually works better than a 4:30pm one during mock weeks.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mostly British-curriculum schools with IB Diploma at a handful. Mock preparation requests here frequently come from IGCSE-trained students meeting IB command terms for the first time.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Villa community with long school runs. Mock-period sessions tend to be booked in 90-minute blocks twice a week rather than shorter daily slots, because the travel pattern makes short evening slots impractical.

regions.name: Downtown and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living and shorter commutes, so earlier weekday sessions are feasible. Many students here attend schools outside the district, which means mock windows vary household to household.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Dense school cluster with IB Diploma running alongside British provision. Mock timetables at adjacent schools can differ by three weeks, so a shared revision plan between friends rarely fits both.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Largely Indian and British curriculum, with IB families travelling further to school. Mock-season demand peaks in January here, later than in the Marina and Hills communities.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: High-rise families with short commutes and compressed evenings. Mock preparation is often needed at speed, with four or five weeks' notice rather than a term's planning.

schoolClusters.city: IB Diploma schools in central and new Dubai
schoolClusters.note: These schools run full Diploma cohorts and mark mocks against IB criteria, which is what makes a marked script from them worth working from. Mock windows differ between them by several weeks, so always check your own school's published dates rather than a friend's.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma provision in established Dubai schools
schoolClusters.note: Several long-standing Dubai schools run the Diploma alongside or instead of A Level, and their mock papers are often set by departments with a decade of IB marking behind them. Students from these cohorts usually arrive with detailed subject reports attached to the mock result.

modes.title: Script review block
modes.description: Two to four sessions on a single marked mock paper. The tutor works through the script against the mark scheme, identifies where the marks went, and hands back a written list of the specific habits costing marks. Suited to a student whose grade was acceptable but whose teacher flagged a pattern.

modes.description: Weekly sessions in one or two subjects running from the mock result through to the final weeks before the May session. sections.heading: The Dubai IB mock calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Mock preparation is a scheduling problem before it is a teaching problem. The Diploma runs two sessions a year, May and November, and almost every Dubai school sits the May session. Working backwards from May, the mock sits roughly four to five months out, which is close to the last point at which a structural change, such as moving a subject from HL to SL, is still realistic.

The table below is a planning skeleton, not a set of official dates. IB session and results dates are published by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring site, including this one. What does not move year to year is the order of events and the gaps between them, and that order is what makes a revision plan either feasible or fictional.

Read the right-hand column as the actual instruction. If your child is in the mock window and has not yet handed in a Mathematics IA draft, the revision plan for January is already wrong, because the IA will take the hours the plan assumed. Families who map these two calendars against each other in November almost always find two weeks they did not know were already full, and finding them in November is far cheaper than finding them in March.

One more piece of sequencing is worth noting in advance. The window in which a level change from HL to SL can still be processed closes earlier than most families expect, and it is tied to the school's own administrative deadlines rather than to the exam itself. If the mock has raised that question, raise it with the coordinator in the same week the script comes back, not after the next report cycle. Waiting costs the option rather than the grade, and the option is sometimes the better outcome for a student carrying three HLs that no longer fit.

sections.heading: Reading a mock script instead of a mock grade
paragraphs: A mock grade compresses a great deal of information into one digit, and most of what a tutor needs is in the part that got compressed away. The first thing we do with a returned script is rebuild the mark distribution: how many marks were available per question, how many were earned, and what kind of question each one was. Patterns appear quickly once the marks are laid out that way.

Four patterns account for most Dubai mock underperformance. The first is command-term mismatch, where the content is known and the answer shape is wrong. The second is timing collapse, visible as strong early answers and blank or one-line later ones, which is a pacing problem rather than a knowledge problem and is fixed by practice under a clock. The third is topic-local ignorance, where one or two syllabus areas are genuinely unlearned while everything else is sound. The fourth is presentation loss, especially in Mathematics and Physics, where correct thinking earns no method marks because it was never written down.

Each of those four needs a different intervention, and that is precisely why a general revision course struggles with mock follow-up. A student with timing collapse gains nothing from more content teaching, and a student with two unlearned topics gains nothing from more timed papers. Separating them takes one careful session with the script in front of both tutor and student, which is also the session in which most students stop believing the grade means they are bad at the subject.

The script is also the honest record of what the student can do unaided. Homework and coursework are produced with notes, time and help. A mock answer is not. For a parent deciding whether to spend on tutoring at all, a marked mock is better evidence than any report comment, because it shows the gap between supported performance and unsupported performance in a single document.

sections.heading: What mock preparation costs in Dubai, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Prices in this market are easy to find and hard to compare, because providers quote different things: an hour, a 90-minute session, a monthly package, or a block. The figures below are published market rates from the Dubai tutoring market as read in October 2026, not IB Gram's own price list. We publish them because three of the six highest-ranking pages for Dubai IB tutoring queries show no price at all, and two of the remaining three quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family pays in.

Mock season is also the point in the year when rates move most. Demand for Diploma specialists concentrates into the same eight weeks across the whole emirate, which is why a family starting a search in mid-January finds both less availability and firmer pricing than one starting in October. The same effect is visible again in March and April before the May session.

Three things move a quoted number more than anything else. Level is the first: HL work in a science or Mathematics commands more than SL across every provider band. Format is the second, and the travel premium on an in-home visit is substantial, as the table shows. Specificity is the third and least obvious: a tutor who can mark Chemistry Paper 3 to criteria sits in a narrower market than one who can teach general secondary science, and narrowness is what parents are actually paying for during mock follow-up.

For IB Gram's own position: we publish no fixed rate card on these pages, because the right figure depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain. The free trial lesson exists so a family can judge the match before any money is discussed, and the rate for the specific subject and level is confirmed in that conversation.

sections.heading: Online mock coaching against an in-home tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: The honest comparison matters here because mock preparation is unusually sensitive to tutor specificity. A generalist can help a student revise. Only a subject specialist can tell a parent that the four marks lost on question 7(b) went because the answer gave a correlation where the mark scheme wanted a mechanism. The question is therefore not whether in-home tuition works, but what a Dubai family gives up in exchange for the convenience.

In-home tutoring in Dubai is a real and substantial market. Published rates run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages quoted around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Part of that premium is teaching and part is travel: a tutor crossing from Mirdif to Arabian Ranches at 5pm on a weekday is spending an hour in a car that the family is paying for in one form or another. The deeper constraint is the catchment. A family is choosing from the specialists willing to drive to them, which in a niche like Physics HL Paper 3 may be nobody at all.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE session runs one-to-one over live video, which is also what the other forty-eight country pages on this site state. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature: it is what allows a Dubai Hills family to work with a Chemistry HL specialist who marks to criteria instead of with whoever covers their community. Screen sharing suits mock review particularly well, because tutor and student look at the same scanned script and the same mark scheme at the same time, and the annotated version is saved rather than left on a kitchen table.

Where in-home genuinely wins is with younger children who need physical presence to stay on task, and with households where screen time is already contested. For a DP2 student six weeks out from predicted grades, the trade runs the other way, and the table below sets out why.

sections.heading: Mocks, predicted grades and what universities actually see
paragraphs: Predicted grades are the practical reason mock season carries weight. A Diploma candidate applying to universities does so before any real IB result exists, so the application carries a predicted grade for each subject, submitted by the school. Mocks are the most substantial piece of evidence a coordinator has when deciding what to predict, which is why a bad mock can echo for a year.

What a parent can usefully do is narrow. The prediction belongs to the school and is made on the school's professional judgement; no tutoring provider influences it and any that implies otherwise should be treated with suspicion. What a student can influence is the evidence available at the moment the prediction is made. A piece of strong, recent, criteria-marked work handed in two weeks after a weak mock is genuinely relevant information, and several Dubai schools will look at it.

The sequencing therefore matters more than the intensity. Support that arrives three days after a mock result and produces a marked improvement on the next assessed piece is worth more, at this specific moment, than the same number of hours spread thinly across February and March. After predictions are submitted the calculus flips entirely: from that point the only thing that matters is the May paper itself, and the work should widen from targeted repair to full past-paper rotation.

One further Dubai-specific point. Students applying to UAE institutions, or seeking Ministry of Education equivalency for a degree here, face a separate documentary process from the admissions process itself. That is administrative rather than academic, it is handled by the Ministry and the relevant authority, and no tutoring service performs or guarantees it. Ask the school's university counsellor early, because the paperwork timeline is long and independent of exam results.

sections.heading: Academic honesty during mock and IA season
paragraphs: Mock season in Dubai overlaps with Internal Assessment deadlines in most subjects, which puts families in front of a choice that some providers in this market answer badly. The IB's academic-honesty rules are unambiguous: assessed work must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain the criteria, ask questions about reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite, or edit the work into shape.

This matters commercially because at least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells finished Internal Assessments outright, at prices around AED 3,750. Buying one exposes the student to a malpractice finding, which can mean the loss of the entire Diploma, not just the subject. No grade is worth that, and no price makes the risk sensible. We state the boundary on every page in this set because the boundary is itself a reason to choose differently.

In practice the line is easy to hold once it is named. A productive IA session sounds like questions: what is your research question actually asking, why did you choose that method, what does this graph show that your conclusion does not mention. An unproductive one sounds like dictation. Parents can audit this themselves by asking the student to explain their own IA argument without notes a week after the session. If they cannot, the work was not theirs.

The same rule applies to past papers and mark schemes. We reference official IB, Cambridge and Pearson material and link to the publishers rather than redistributing documents, because reproducing syllabus documents, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, an exam-security one. Your school's subject teacher is the correct route to the school's own mock papers.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own draft

sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai school calendar and Ramadan scheduling
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's school is public. It is worth reading the subject-level commentary rather than only the headline band, because inspection reports often name specific departments and that is directly relevant to where a mock result came from.

KHDA also sets requirements that shape the week around mock preparation. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met. For a DP2 student in mock season those lessons are fixed timetable, so revision hours have to come from elsewhere. Families consistently underestimate this when planning.

The academic calendar adds two further constraints. The winter break falls inside or immediately beside the mock window at most schools, which means either a fortnight of lost momentum or a fortnight of concentrated work, depending on the plan made in November. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a shifted household rhythm; sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, and students often prefer it, because evening focus during Ramadan is frequently better than late-afternoon focus.

On regulation of tutors themselves: private tuition in the UAE is permit-based. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry endorsement and claims none.

sections.heading: Getting started after a mock result, honestly
paragraphs: The useful first message is short and specific: the subject, the level, the mock grade, the target, and how many weeks remain. With that we can say whether a specialist in that exact combination is available, and if not, we say so rather than offering an approximate match. Diploma HL sciences and Mathematics AA HL are the two areas where availability tightens most during Dubai mock season, because every school's mock window overlaps.

The marked script is the second thing to send, and it changes the first session completely. Without it, a trial lesson becomes a general conversation about the subject. With it, the tutor arrives having already mapped where the marks went and can spend the hour on the pattern rather than on discovery. Schools in Dubai generally return mocks within two to three weeks of sitting, and asking the subject teacher for the mark scheme alongside the script is a normal request.

The trial lesson is free and carries no condition beyond scheduling it. Its purpose is narrow: can this tutor explain this subject to this student, and does the student want to come back. Mock preparation collapses quickly if the student is not willing, which is why we would rather a family walk away after a trial than commit to six weeks on a poor match. If the fit is wrong we will say so first.

After that the shape depends on how much time is left. Six weeks or more out from a mock, weekly sessions with marked work in between is the usual pattern. Two or three weeks out, a narrower intensive on the published mock scope makes more sense. After mocks, the work is diagnostic repair first and then full timed-paper rotation towards the May session. All of it runs in Gulf Standard Time, so sessions sit in the evening a Dubai family actually has rather than in a time zone that suits the tutor.

faqs.question: When do Dubai IB schools actually sit Diploma mock exams?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai schools sit Diploma mocks in a window running from late November to early February, with DP2 cohorts taking two or three papers per subject across a fortnight. The exact dates are set school by school and can differ by three weeks between neighbouring schools, so confirm with your own IB coordinator rather than with other parents. Marked scripts usually come back within two to three weeks, and predicted grades follow soon after. If you are planning a revision block, build it around your school's published window and its Internal Assessment deadlines together, because the two almost always overlap.

faqs.question: Does a bad IB mock grade mean my child will get a bad final grade?
faqs.answer: No. The mock grade changes nothing on the final transcript, and the gap between a mock and a May result can be large in either direction. What the mock does is produce evidence, and the evidence is in the script rather than the grade. A 4 caused by command-term errors and a 4 caused by two unlearned topics need completely different work, and only the paper shows which you have. The mock grade does matter indirectly, because it informs the predicted grades a school submits to universities, which is why acting quickly on the script is worth more than worrying about the digit.

faqs.question: How many sessions does mock preparation usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of the four common problems the script shows. A pacing or presentation problem is often largely fixed in two to four sessions of timed practice with marked feedback, because the student already knows the content. Two genuinely unlearned syllabus topics take longer, typically six to eight sessions in that subject. A student who needs both, in two subjects, is looking at a weekly commitment through to the May session. We would rather give you that estimate after seeing the marked paper than guess beforehand, and the estimate is revised at week three against new marked work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with an Internal Assessment during mock season?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundary the IB sets. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, question the research question, discuss whether a method answers it, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, or edit it into shape, and anyone offering to is putting the whole Diploma at risk of a malpractice finding. One provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750; that is not a service, it is an exposure. A good test is whether your child can explain their own argument without notes a week later.

faqs.question: What does IB mock preparation cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where travel is inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Monthly packages in the market sit around AED 799 online for eight sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for in-home blocks. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. Our own rate depends on subject, level and weeks remaining, and is confirmed after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Dubai for mock revision?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. The honest case for that is not convenience, it is the tutor pool. An in-home arrangement limits you to specialists willing to drive to your community, which for something as narrow as Chemistry HL Paper 3 marking may be nobody. Online, the match is made on subject and level. Mock review also works unusually well on a shared screen, because tutor and student annotate the same scanned script together and the marked-up version is saved rather than left behind.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do Dubai families most often need mock help with?
faqs.answer: Demand concentrates in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at both levels, the HL sciences, and Economics. Mathematics requests usually come from method-mark and non-calculator-paper losses rather than from conceptual gaps. Science requests cluster around Paper 2 extended responses, where a correct fact scores half the marks because the mark scheme wanted a mechanism. Economics requests are nearly always about diagram accuracy and evaluation. English A requests rise sharply in January, when students who scored well on coursework discover that Paper 1 unseen analysis is a different skill entirely from the one they had practised.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the mock is three weeks away?
faqs.answer: Three weeks is enough to change a mock result, provided the work narrows. At that distance there is no value in a broad syllabus refresh; the useful plan is the school's published mock scope, full-length timed papers on the specific papers being sat, and marked feedback between sessions. Three to five sessions across those weeks is the usual shape, often across two subjects. What three weeks cannot fix is a wide content gap built over a year, and we will tell you that rather than sell you hours against it. In that case the better target is the May session itself.

faqs.question: How do predicted grades relate to the mock result?
faqs.answer: Predicted grades are submitted by the school because university applications happen before any real IB result exists. Mocks are usually the strongest evidence a coordinator holds when deciding what to predict, which is why a weak mock has consequences beyond the mark itself. No tutoring provider influences a prediction, and one that implies it can should be treated carefully. What a student can influence is the evidence on the table when the prediction is made, so strong criteria-marked work produced in the fortnight after a weak mock is genuinely relevant and several Dubai schools will consider it.

faqs.question: Will mock revision sessions still run through Ramadan and the winter break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families prefer it. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a different household rhythm, and students frequently focus better in a post-Iftar evening slot than in a late afternoon one. Because every session is scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and delivered over live video, moving a recurring slot later in the evening for several weeks is straightforward. The same flexibility covers the winter break, when families travel: sessions can continue from wherever the student is, or pause and resume, as long as the plan is adjusted deliberately rather than by drift.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's subject teacher after a mock?
faqs.answer: Four questions cover most of it. Which paper lost the most marks, and was it content or technique? Were there questions left blank, and was that time or knowledge? Which syllabus topics in this paper are still weak? And is the mock scope the same as the final paper's scope, or narrower? Also ask for the mark scheme alongside the script, which is a normal request and makes any outside support far more precise. Teachers in Dubai schools generally answer these readily, and the answers are worth more than a report comment written for a wider audience.

faqs.question: Does KHDA regulate private tutors in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not individually. KHDA oversees private schools in Dubai and inspects them annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and it issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. Individual private tutors are covered separately by the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and does not describe itself as KHDA approved, because that phrase means something specific that we do not hold.

faqs.question: How is mock preparation different from ordinary subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ordinary tutoring works forwards through a syllabus. Mock preparation works backwards from a specific marked paper, which makes it narrower and usually shorter. The input is the script, the mark scheme and the teacher's comments; the output is a list of the particular habits costing marks, and practice aimed at those. It also has a deadline that cannot move, so content that will not be assessed gets cut from the plan deliberately. After the mock the work widens again into full past-paper rotation towards the May session, which is a different exercise with a different rhythm.

faqs.question: Can we work on two subjects at once before a mock?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in the pre-mock weeks it is common, because mocks arrive in a cluster rather than one at a time. The practical limit is the student's week rather than our availability: two 90-minute sessions plus the timed practice between them is roughly the ceiling for a DP2 student who also has school, an Internal Assessment in progress and the mandatory UAE subjects on the timetable. Beyond that, nothing gets done properly. If three subjects genuinely need work, we would usually sequence them rather than run them in parallel and tell you which to start with.

faqs.question: What if nobody covers my child's HL subject during the mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: We say so. Availability in Diploma HL sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL tightens sharply during the Dubai mock window, because every school's mock period overlaps and demand concentrates into the same weeks. When the exact specialist is not free, we will tell you the realistic wait rather than offer a near match and hope. In some cases a tutor from outside the UAE covers the subject at the same online format and Gulf-time scheduling, and we name that openly, because concealing where a tutor is based is one of the trust failures common on competing pages.

dubai/ib-mock-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start from the paper your child has already sat
dubai/ib-mock-exam-preparation.closingBody: A mock result is information, and most of it is still sitting in the script rather than in the grade. Send the subject, the level, the mark and the weeks remaining, and we will tell you whether a specialist in that exact combination is free. Share the marked paper and the mark scheme, and the first session starts from where the marks actually went instead of from a general conversation about the subject. The trial lesson is free and carries no condition. Everything runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, so the session sits in the evening your household has.

dubai/ib-myp-arabic-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Arabic and measure it. Each one runs the same opening diagnostic, logs a timed reading check, and bands written work against the phase descriptors so a family can see movement without being able to read the script themselves.

intro.heading: You do not need to read Arabic to tell whether Arabic tutoring is working
paragraphs: This is the particular difficulty of paying for Arabic in Dubai. In maths a parent can look at a page and see whether the answers are right. In Arabic the page is unreadable to most of the people paying for it, which leaves a family relying entirely on a tutor's cheerful assurance and a report card that arrives months later. The result is that Arabic support gets renewed on faith and cancelled on frustration, often without either decision being informed.

The way out is to insist on measurements that do not require you to understand the language. Reading speed on the same passage, once with short vowels printed and once without, is a number. The count of letters confused in initial, medial and final position is a number. Words per minute on unseen vowelled text is a number. Two recordings of the same speaking prompt a fortnight apart is a comparison any parent can hear. None of it depends on knowing a word of Arabic.

Those measurements also happen to be diagnostic rather than decorative. A Dubai student who reads fluently with harakat and collapses without them does not need more vocabulary; they need a decoding block. A student whose medial letter forms are weak is guessing from context, which works until the text gets harder. A student using one verb pattern in every sentence has a range problem, not an effort problem. The right next step falls out of the measurement instead of being guessed at.

The home-tutor question deserves a plain answer. People do drive across Dubai to teach Arabic in villas, the market charges between AED 180 and 500 an hour for it according to Bestimate's 2026 rate table and independent listings, and monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits are widely advertised. IB Gram does not do it: in-home teaching is offered only in India. Dubai lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

For Arabic script work specifically, that is less of a compromise than it sounds and in one respect it is an improvement. A tutor writing on a shared screen shows stroke order the right way up, rather than upside down across a dining table. Written work photographed and annotated comes back inside two days rather than at the next visit. And the timed checks get logged in a file rather than remembered, which is the whole point of measuring anything. The rest of this page is the detail behind those claims: what the opening diagnostic tests and why each task is there, the sequence that unvowelled reading follows and roughly how long each stage takes, what the in-home alternative in Dubai actually costs and contains, and the four documents a family should be holding by the end of a term. It also says, in plain terms, what the stopping condition is, because a provider who cannot name one is selling a subscription rather than a solution.
