sections.heading: Premium pricing, examiner claims and what a high rate should buy
paragraphs: At the top of the Dubai market, AED 500 to AED 650 an hour is published, and it is usually justified on one of three grounds: examiner experience, a track record of high scores, or scarcity of the subject and level. Only the third is straightforwardly verifiable, and it is also the least often stated. The first two deserve direct questions before a parent pays four times the qualified band.

On examiner claims, the position we take is deliberately conservative. We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners, because current examiner status for an individual is not something we can evidence, and because examiner status must never be used to imply access to marking schemes, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. If a provider's price rests on that claim, ask what they will show you and what exactly it entitles your child to. A reasonable answer describes familiarity with mark schemes. An unreasonable one hints at inside knowledge.

On track records, ask for the method rather than the headline. A claim of a particular average score needs the number of students, the years covered and how students were counted to mean anything, and most published versions in this market supply none of the three. No provider, at any price, can promise a grade in a programme whose boundaries the school applies. What a high rate can legitimately buy is a genuinely scarce specialism at a genuinely scarce hour, and in MYP chemistry the honest version of that is a tutor who has marked criterion C work in this subject at this year group. That is a question with a checkable answer.
bullets: Scarcity is the only one of the three premium justifications that is easily verified
We do not claim examiner status, and no examiner claim implies marking access
Any score claim needs the number of students, the years and the method
Ask instead which criterion strands the tutor has marked, and at what year group

sections.heading: The last AED 1,000 before a chemistry assessment: where it actually returns
paragraphs: Budgets often run out in the final weeks, which is exactly when the temptation to buy a large block is strongest. At the published qualified band, AED 1,000 buys between three and six hours. Spent well, that is enough to move specific marks. Spent as general revision it buys company for an evening, and the student would have revised anyway.

The first hour should be diagnostic, working through a past chemistry paper or the last marked task while the tutor counts error types rather than correcting each one. The second and third should address whichever quantitative error dominates, almost always mole conversion or titre averaging, because those recur across every paper. If criterion C work is part of the assessment, one hour on processing and the conclusion structure is worth more than three hours of content revision. Keep the final hour for a timed paper reviewed immediately afterwards.

What not to buy with the last AED 1,000: new content in the final fortnight, which competes with consolidation and usually loses; a two-hour in-home visit, where a substantial share of the fee is travel; or a group revision class covering topics the student already has. And if the assessment is an on-screen MYP 5 sitting, insist that the timed practice happens on screen rather than on paper, because the interface costs marks that content revision cannot recover. Confirm the format with the MYP coordinator first; we publish no IB dates on these pages, since the IB's own site cannot be verified automatically.
bullets: Hour one: diagnose by counting error types on a past paper or marked task
Hours two and three: the dominant quantitative error, usually moles or titres
One hour on criterion C processing if the assessment includes it
Final hour: a timed paper, reviewed immediately, on screen if the sitting is on screen

process.title: Send the last marked chemistry task
process.description: A photograph of the last marked chemistry task, with the rubric or strand marks if the school publishes them, is worth more than any description of how the term has gone. We read it before the first session so the hour opens on the actual error pattern. It also lets you judge, cheaply, whether we read it at all.

process.title: Free trial lesson, with the condition written down
process.description: One forty-five-minute online session at no charge. No card details are taken and there is nothing to cancel afterwards. The tutor teaches from the task you sent and finishes with a written note naming the error types and what a fixed-length block would target. You keep the note whether or not you book.

process.title: Settle the six billing terms in writing
process.description: Unit of charge, minimum booking, cancellation notice, what happens to prepaid sessions, whether the figure includes tax, and the trial condition. We will answer all six in writing before you pay anything, and we would encourage you to ask every provider you are comparing the same six questions.

process.title: Choose a scenario, not a subscription
process.description: Pick the lean, middle or intensive shape from the budget table and write down the hours and the review points. A plan with a known total is easier to sustain than an open-ended monthly commitment, and it makes the half-term decision about evidence rather than about inertia.

process.title: Review each half term against marked work
process.description: At half term we compare the error tally with the baseline and recommend continuing, reducing to fortnightly or stopping. Reducing is the most common recommendation after a successful quantitative block, and it halves the monthly figure. A tutor who never recommends fewer hours is not reading their own evidence.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: A plan with a known total
whyPoints.description: The budget table sets out three two-year shapes with hours, totals and assumptions visible, so the commitment is legible before it starts. Reactive buying in the final term costs a comparable amount and arrives when availability is worst and rates sit at the top of the published band.

whyPoints.title: We will recommend fewer hours
whyPoints.description: Where the error tally is dominated by mole conversion and titre averaging, the useful purchase is a fixed block of four to six sessions, not a year of weekly chemistry. We say so, and after a successful block we usually recommend halving to fortnightly maintenance rather than continuing weekly.

whyPoints.title: No examiner claims and no score claims
whyPoints.description: We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners, because individual examiner status is not something we can evidence, and it must never be used to imply access to marking or boundaries. We publish no statistic without the number of students, the dates and the method behind it, which rules out most of what this market advertises.

whyPoints.title: Online by design, with the travel premium removed
whyPoints.description: Published Dubai in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with the drive inside the fee. Teaching over live video removes that and the geographic shortlist behind it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home teaching is a service we provide only in India.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP chemistry tutor in Dubai cost per session?
faqs.answer: At the qualified online tier in this market, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a sixty-minute session, based on published rates read in October 2026. Below that, marketplace tiers advertise from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, and above it premium named tutors publish up to AED 650. In-home visits run about AED 180 to AED 500 with travel inside the fee. For MYP 4 and 5 chemistry specifically, expect the qualified band rather than the entry tier, because the quantitative work needs a tutor who handles it fluently.

faqs.question: Why do chemistry tutors in Dubai quote more than biology tutors?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. A biology tutor needs secure content knowledge and good command-term discipline. A chemistry tutor needs both plus fluent quantitative handling, because a large share of MYP 4 and 5 chemistry marks sit behind mole arithmetic, concentration and titre processing. The pool is thinner in Dubai specifically, where IB programmes account for 7 per cent of private school enrolment and most chemistry tutors have taught Cambridge 0620 or CBSE chemistry far more often than they have marked a criterion C titration table.

faqs.question: What should a two-year MYP 4 and 5 chemistry plan cost in total?
faqs.answer: At published Dubai qualified rates of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, a lean plan of about thirty hours comes to roughly AED 4,500 to AED 9,000 across two years. A middle plan of about sixty hours runs AED 9,000 to AED 18,000, and an intensive plan of ninety hours runs higher. Reactive buying, two emergency blocks late in each year, often lands in the same range as the middle plan while delivering fewer useful hours, because availability at that point is poor and rates sit at the top of the band.

faqs.question: Is a tutor charging AED 650 an hour worth four times the standard rate?
faqs.answer: Only if what you are buying is genuinely scarce and the claim behind the price is evidenced. Premium rates in this market usually rest on examiner experience or a score record. Ask what evidence is offered for each. Current examiner status for an individual is hard to verify, and it should never imply access to mark schemes or grade boundaries. Any score claim needs the number of students, the years and the counting method. A better question is which criterion strands the tutor has marked, at which year group, because that has a checkable answer.

faqs.question: What hidden charges turn an hourly chemistry rate into a larger monthly bill?
faqs.answer: Six terms account for nearly all of it. Whether the price is per hour or per session, and what a session actually lasts. Whether a minimum booking applies, which is often two hours for in-home visits because of travel. What notice cancels without charge and whether a missed session is banked. What happens to prepaid sessions if you stop or the tutor becomes unavailable. Whether the figure quoted includes any tax, confirmed in writing. And what condition is attached to a free trial. Settle all six before paying anything.

faqs.question: Are group chemistry classes in Dubai good value at a lower rate per head?
faqs.answer: For shared content, yes. Group rates at MYP 4 and 5 run roughly AED 70 to AED 130 an hour per student, and tuition centres advertise monthly packages from about AED 799. That is good value for first teaching of the mole, balanced-equation arithmetic, command-term work and pre-test revision, provided every student is in the same MYP year. It is poor value the moment the work becomes one student's own criterion plan, one student's titration data or one student's marked script, none of which can be worked on in a group.

faqs.question: Should we prepay a block of chemistry sessions to get a discount?
faqs.answer: Only with the exit terms written down. A twenty-hour discount is attractive in September and awkward in February when the student no longer needs twenty hours, or when the tutor becomes unavailable. Before prepaying, establish whether unused sessions expire, whether credit transfers to a different tutor or a different subject, and what happens if you stop entirely. Our own preference is no prepayment, because a plan should be able to shorten when the marked work says the problem is fixed, and a prepaid block quietly discourages exactly that.

faqs.question: We have about AED 1,000 left before the chemistry assessment. How should we spend it?
faqs.answer: At the qualified band that is three to six hours, which is enough if it is targeted. Hour one diagnoses, working a past paper while the tutor counts error types. Hours two and three address the dominant quantitative error, usually mole conversion or titre averaging, because those recur on every paper. If criterion C forms part of the assessment, spend one hour on processing and conclusion structure. Keep the last hour for a timed paper reviewed immediately. Avoid new content in the final fortnight and avoid paying for travel.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper chemistry tutor in Dubai mean a less qualified one?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, but the cheapest tiers are explicitly priced for university students and generalists, and MYP 4 and 5 chemistry is where that shows. The budget band of AED 33 to AED 65 an hour is adequate for integrated sciences in MYP 1 to 3 and thin for quantitative chemistry two years later. The better test than price is two questions: which MYP chemistry criterion strands have you marked, and will you work from our school's task sheet and rubric. A confident, specific answer to both matters more than the number.

faqs.question: How do we compare an agency, a marketplace and a freelance chemistry tutor on cost?
faqs.answer: Compare what the rate contains rather than the rate. A marketplace rate excludes vetting. An agency rate includes coordination you may never use. A freelance in-home rate includes a car and usually a two-hour minimum. A tuition centre package includes a venue and a group. Then compare three things that decide real cost: what a mismatch costs you, whether a trial exists and on what condition, and what happens to money already paid if you stop. Those determine the bill far more than the headline figure does.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start chemistry support in MYP 4 or to wait for MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Starting in MYP 4 is almost always cheaper overall, for two reasons. The quantitative foundation, moles, reacting masses and concentration, only needs fixing once, and fixing it early means two years of chemistry built on it rather than one. And availability in MYP 5 concentrates into the same few weeks across every Dubai cohort, so the affordable slots vanish first and what remains sits at the top of the published band. Waiting usually means paying more per hour for more hours at a worse time.

faqs.question: Do tuition centres in Dubai work out cheaper than one-to-one chemistry tutoring?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, with advertised monthly packages from about AED 799 against AED 150 to AED 300 an hour individually. Whether it is cheaper per unit of progress depends on the match between the class and the student's actual gap. A centre class covering rates of reaction is worth little to a student whose problem is converting grams to moles. Ask what the class will cover week by week, how many students are in it and what year they are in, then compare that against the error pattern in your child's own marked work.

faqs.question: What does fixing the mole arithmetic cost compared with general chemistry revision?
faqs.answer: A fixed block of four to six sessions, so roughly AED 600 to AED 1,800 at published qualified rates, against an open-ended weekly arrangement that can run to several times that across a year. The block is better value for most students because the arithmetic is the single dependency behind reacting masses, concentration, titration processing and rate calculations. General revision spreads the same money across topics the student may already understand, which is why we ask for a marked task first and often recommend the shorter option.

faqs.question: Can we cut the cost by having fewer, longer chemistry sessions?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is the main reason in-home arrangements feel poor value. Attention in a chemistry session falls off sharply after about an hour, especially on quantitative work in the evening after a long Dubai school commute. Two forty-five-minute sessions a fortnight generally produce more than one two-hour session a month at the same cost. The exception is a timed past paper followed immediately by review, which genuinely needs a longer block and is worth scheduling at a weekend rather than on a school evening.

dubai/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.closingHeading: Decide the hours first, then ask the price
dubai/ib-myp-chemistry-tutor.closingBody: The reason chemistry tutoring in Dubai feels unpredictable is that families agree a rate before deciding what they are buying. Reverse the order. Send the last marked chemistry task, let the trial lesson produce an error tally, choose the lean, middle or intensive shape with its hours written down, and settle the six billing terms before paying anything. A plan with a known total and a half-term review point costs less and survives longer than an open monthly commitment. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India.

dubai/ib-myp-design-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below has taught the MYP design cycle and marked against its strands. Sessions are run in the student's own software and around the student's own school workshop access, because those two constraints decide what is realistically achievable before a deadline.

intro.heading: The thing a home visit cannot bring with it
paragraphs: There is a specific reason this search exists. MYP Design is the one MYP subject that appears to need equipment, so when a project goes wrong parents reasonably assume the fix is someone physically present, helping to make the thing. Then the quote comes back at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is what the Dubai market charges for an in-home visit, and the hour turns out to be a conversation at the dining table because the laser cutter is at school and the 3D printer has a queue.

Look at where the marks actually are and the problem reframes itself. A project is scored on four criteria of eight marks each. Criterion A is inquiring and analysing. Criterion B is developing ideas. Criterion C is creating the solution. Criterion D is evaluating. Only Criterion C touches the making, and three of its four strands — the logical plan, following that plan, and justifying changes to the design and plan — are written evidence about the making rather than the making itself. Something like twenty-four of the thirty-two marks live in documents.

That is good news for a family with a deadline and no workshop. Documents can be fixed at home, at speed, in the right order, and they are where almost every lost mark in this subject sits. The specification that was written after the build. The research that was collected rather than prioritised. The product analysis that became a gallery of photographs. The testing section that asks a friend whether she likes it. Each of those is a named strand with marks attached, and none of them needs a machine.

The practical constraint that does need managing is school workshop access, and it is a scheduling problem rather than a tutoring one. Dubai schools with laser cutters and 3D printers run them on booking systems, often with a technician present only on certain days, and print failures are common enough that a single slot is not a plan. A tutor who knows this asks for the booking date in session one and works the paperwork backwards from it, which is the opposite of what students do unprompted.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing in both directions. For this subject that is not a concession. The assessed artefacts are CAD files, dimensioned drawings, photographs and a written journal, all of which sit better on a shared screen than on a table two people are leaning over. The rest of this page covers where the marks are, what materials cost in Dubai and where to buy them, and what to fix first when time is short.

dubai/ib-myp-design-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The three IB programmes handle designing and making very differently, and a Dubai family moving through them hits a different practical constraint at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Making happens inside units of inquiry with no criteria attached, which means the equipment question barely matters and the documentation question matters a lot. A child who keeps a photograph of what failed and one line about why has the habit that MYP 4 students are still being taught at fourteen. Cardboard, tape and a phone camera are sufficient tooling.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP provision ranges from a dedicated maker space with a technician to a shelf of recycled materials, and open evenings rarely make the difference clear. Ask to see the room rather than the brochure, and ask who supervises it, because an unstaffed maker space is a cupboard.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · Years 7-11, labelled MYP 1 to MYP 5
programmes.description: Five years of the full design cycle with sixteen assessed strands. The equipment question becomes real in MYP 4 and 5, when projects get ambitious and workshop time becomes scarce. The paperwork question becomes decisive at the same point, because strand expectations sharpen while students' documentation habits usually do not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools book workshop and machine time centrally, and technician availability often defines the project calendar more than the teacher's scheme of work does. Families who ask for the booking date in week one plan a project; families who do not discover in week six that the slot is after the deadline.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Design Technology sits in Group 4 with examination papers and an internal assessment; Computer Science and Visual Arts are the other common destinations. Equipment matters more here, which is exactly why not every school offers Design Technology, and why the question to ask in MYP 4 is whether last year's group actually ran.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai student who wants DP Design Technology and whose school cannot timetable it has two realistic answers: a different Group 4 subject, or a school move at the end of MYP 5. Neither is a crisis, and both need deciding a year earlier than families typically raise it.

dubai/ib-myp-design-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: What Dubai families actually ask for inside MYP Design, described by the constraint each one runs into rather than by syllabus heading.

subjects.name: MYP Design documentation repair
subjects.description: The most requested work and the most productive. Reading an existing folder against the sixteen strands, naming the ones with no evidence, and closing them in order of marks per hour. Needs no equipment and routinely recovers more marks than any amount of additional making time.

subjects.name: Testable specifications
subjects.description: Turning adjectives into measurable statements with units, counts or rating scales. The document sits in Criterion B and supplies everything Criterion D measures against, so one session here pays twice. Entirely a desk exercise, which makes it ideal for a home week with no workshop access.

subjects.name: Criterion D testing design
subjects.description: Writing tests before the prototype exists, so they measure the specification rather than flatter the result. Needs a ruler, a scale, a kitchen weight and three willing users, all of which exist in a Dubai apartment. The thinnest section in most folders and the cheapest to improve.

subjects.name: CAD modelling in the student's own software
subjects.description: Fusion, Tinkercad, SketchUp, Onshape and similar, worked on screen-share both ways. The tutor watches the modelling rather than the render, which is where unconstrained sketches and fragile timelines show up. Also covers exporting properly dimensioned drawings for the planning strand.

subjects.name: Cardboard and low-fidelity modelling
subjects.description: An underrated route to the chosen-design strand when no machines are available. A dimensioned card model, photographed from three angles with measurements marked, evidences the presented-design strand as well as a print does. Materials cost under AED 30 at any Dubai stationer.

subjects.name: Material sourcing and costing
subjects.description: Where in Dubai to buy acrylic, plywood, fixings, fabric and electronics, what the lead times are, and how to produce the itemised dated costing that a cost specification line needs. Students usually guess the prices; a real receipt is better evidence and takes one afternoon.

subjects.name: Digital design and interface prototyping
subjects.description: For schools running the digital strand. The strand expectations are identical, with one trap: screenshots are not planning drawings, and the planning strand asks for accuracy and dimensions that an interface mock-up does not supply unless the student adds them deliberately.

subjects.name: MYP Design to Personal Project crossover
subjects.description: Many Dubai MYP 5 students choose a making project, then apply Design criteria to it and lose marks in both. A tutor separates the two frameworks, questions the goal and gives feedback on what the student has written. The student writes every word of the report and the journal themselves.

subjects.name: DP Design Technology preparation
subjects.description: Closing the written-analysis gap before DP1 rather than during it. The MYP habits that transfer are specification writing and justified iteration; the step up is the volume of reasoning expected per decision and the technical depth behind each material choice.

subjects.name: DP Computer Science preparation
subjects.description: The natural route out of a digital-led MYP Design course. Programming is new content and worth starting before DP1 begins, while the solution-development documentation will feel familiar to any student who wrote a genuine specification rather than a retrospective one.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or the school workshop: what each one can actually give you
paragraphs: The honest comparison for a making subject is not online against in-home. It is online against in-home against the school workshop, because the three supply different things and only one of them has machines. Families who understand that stop paying a travel premium for a conversation that could have happened on a screen, and start treating workshop access as the scarce resource it is.

An in-home tutor in Dubai costs AED 180 to 500 an hour on market rates read in October 2026, with travel inside the rate. What arrives is a person, a laptop and whatever they can carry. For Criterion A, B and D work that is identical to what an online session delivers, minus forty to fifty minutes of term-time driving each way that you are paying for. For Criterion C making, it is still not a workshop: no laser cutter, no 3D printer, no technician and no dust extraction.

The school workshop is where the equipment is, and it runs on a booking system that students treat as a formality and should treat as the project's spine. Technician days, machine queues and print failures are the real constraints. A single booked slot is not a plan, because the first print of anything structural has a decent chance of failing, and a student with no slack has to redesign under time pressure and then justify the change honestly in Criterion C.

So the sensible division of labour is this: the school supplies machines and supervision, the student supplies iteration time and a journal, and a tutor supplies the sequence and the marking standard. The table sets out what each channel delivers against the four criteria. The pattern it shows is that for twenty-four of the thirty-two marks, physical presence buys nothing at all.

sections.heading: Where the thirty-two marks actually sit, and what each one costs in hours
paragraphs: Treat a Design project as a mark budget and the decisions get much easier, particularly under deadline. There are thirty-two marks, four criteria of eight, split across sixteen strands. Each strand needs evidence in the folder. Working out which strands are empty and how long each takes to fill is a twenty-minute job for someone who knows the criteria, and it is the single most useful thing to do before deciding what to work on.

The pattern across the Dubai folders we read is consistent. Criterion C is usually the healthiest, because students enjoy making and because the school structures that part. Criterion A loses marks on prioritised research and product analysis. Criterion B loses them on the range of ideas and on planning drawings that are sketches rather than dimensioned drawings. Criterion D is frequently close to empty. The eight marks in Criterion D and the four or so recoverable in Criterion A are therefore where an hour of work pays best.

The table below is a triage tool rather than a syllabus. It lists interventions in rough order of marks recovered per hour of work, with the strand each serves and an honest estimate of how long it takes. Use it when the deadline is close: starting at the top and working down is almost always a better use of a fortnight than remaking a prototype that already evidences the making strand adequately.

Two caveats. Nothing here is a route to marks the work does not deserve: a testing method written honestly can only report what the test showed, and a specification tightened in week ten has to be labelled as a revision in the journal rather than backdated. And no tutor can promise a grade, in this subject or any other. What a triage session can do is make sure the marks the project has already earned are visible to the person marking it.

sections.heading: Buying materials in Dubai: where, what it costs and how long it takes
paragraphs: Nobody writes about this and every MYP Design family needs it. A cost line in a specification requires an itemised, dated costing from real prices, and a project plan requires lead times that are true. Students guess both, which produces a costing that reads as invented and a schedule that collapses the first time something has to be ordered.

Dubai is unusually well supplied if you know where to look. Dragon Mart in International City is where most student project material is actually bought: fixings, small electronics, hand tools, adhesives and sheet material at the lowest prices in the city, with the trade-off that quality varies and you need to see the item. Al Quoz holds the acrylic and timber suppliers and several cutting bureaux, which matters when a school machine queue is full. Nasser Hardware in Bur Dubai and the Deira hardware souks sell in small quantities and will happily sell four screws. Satwa is the place for fabric, foam and trimmings. Online, Amazon.ae and noon cover electronics and specialist components with two to four days of delivery, which has to go into the plan.

The figures in the table are indicative retail ranges observed in Dubai and should be treated as a budgeting aid rather than a quotation; prices move and a project costing must use the student's own dated receipts. That distinction is worth teaching, because a costing built from real receipts is strong evidence for the cost specification line, and one built from estimates is not evidence at all.

The sourcing trip itself is worth documenting. Photographs of the material, the price label and the receipt, dated, go into the process journal and evidence the costing. Students who do this once stop guessing prices in later projects, and it also tends to shrink their ambitions to something buildable, which helps the planning strand more than any amount of advice does.

sections.heading: Making a project work without a workshop at home
paragraphs: A fair number of Dubai MYP students live in apartments where cutting and sanding are not realistic, and their school machine access is a handful of booked hours. This is a solvable problem, because the strands do not require a finished manufactured object; they require evidence of a designed solution, a plan followed, technical skill demonstrated and changes justified.

The chosen-design strand asks for the chosen design to be presented. A dimensioned card or foamboard model, photographed from three angles with measurements marked, presents a design perfectly well, and costs under AED 30 at any stationer. The planning-drawing strand asks for accuracy and detail, which a CAD export supplies better than a hand sketch does; the student does not need to own a printer to produce a properly dimensioned drawing. The technical-skills strand can be evidenced in CAD technique, in careful hand modelling, or in digital prototyping, depending on what the school's course emphasises.

Where a genuinely functional prototype is required, the sequence is to finalise the design digitally, print or cut one part commercially or during the school slot, and spend the home weeks on testing and documentation. That ordering also happens to be the ordering the criteria reward, because it forces the specification and the testing design to be complete before anything is made. Students who are forced into it by circumstance frequently score better than those with unlimited machine access.

One honest limit: a student whose school runs a workshop-heavy course and who skips the making entirely will lose marks in the technical-skills strand, and no amount of documentation substitutes. The right response to that is a conversation with the Design teacher about access rather than a purchase. Dubai schools are generally accommodating about this if asked in week two, and unhelpful if asked in week seven, which is a scheduling lesson rather than a policy one.

sections.heading: Planning backwards from the workshop booking
paragraphs: Every Dubai MYP Design project has one immovable date in it, and it is rarely the submission deadline. It is the day the machine or the workshop is available. Everything upstream of that date has to be finished before it, and everything downstream depends on whether what came off the machine worked. Students plan forwards from today and hit the booking unprepared; the fix is to put the booking date in the middle of a timeline and fill in both directions.

Upstream, the work is Criterion A and B in full plus the testing design from Criterion D: justified need, prioritised research, product analysis, brief, testable specification, a genuine range of ideas, the chosen design presented, dimensioned drawings, a sequenced plan, and tests written against each specification line. That is most of the project, and it is all desk work. Students are routinely shocked that the build is near the end rather than the middle.

Downstream, allow for failure. Prints warp, cuts come out oversized, joints do not fit, and a component ordered online arrives on the wrong day. One slot is a hope rather than a plan, so the sensible approach is to book early in the window rather than late and to treat the second attempt as expected. Each failure is also a Criterion C justified-change entry if it is photographed and explained on the day, which converts a setback into marks.

There is a Dubai-specific wrinkle worth planning around: the calendar. School days shorten during Ramadan, technician availability changes, and the weeks either side of a long holiday are poor bets for machine access. A student with a spring deadline should be looking at the workshop calendar in the winter term. Ask for the school's internal assessment calendar at the first parents' evening; most Dubai IB schools publish one, and it is the document that makes a backwards plan possible.

sections.heading: Marking a folder honestly: what a tutor writes and what a parent can check
paragraphs: A Design folder is marked by looking for evidence of sixteen strands. A tutor's feedback should therefore be a strand-by-strand statement rather than a general impression, and a parent can check that without understanding design at all. Ask for the list: which strands are evidenced, which are thin, which are empty. If the feedback does not take that form, it cannot be compared with the school's marking, which is the only test of whether the tutoring is pointed at the right thing.

The second thing a parent can check is the dating. Journal entries should be made on the day the work happened, and a folder full of entries written in one sitting the week before submission reads exactly like what it is. A tutor who is doing this properly will be pushing for same-day entries and will refuse to help reconstruct a timeline that did not happen. That refusal is a good sign rather than an inconvenience.

The third is the boundary around whose work it is. A tutor can explain what a strand asks for, challenge an untestable specification line, teach a CAD technique and mark a draft. A tutor does not generate the ideas, draw the drawings, write journal entries or produce the report. We set this out in writing before the first session, because under IB academic-honesty rules the consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than on the tutor, and because parts of this market are considerably less careful about it.

What that leaves is a short, checkable list for any Dubai family assessing any provider, including us. Does the feedback name strands? Are entries dated on the day? Is the line about authorship stated in writing? And is there a point at which the arrangement ends rather than rolling on? Four questions, all answerable before you pay anyone anything.
bullets: Feedback should name strands, not give impressions
Journal entries dated on the day they happened, not reconstructed
Authorship boundary stated in writing before the first session
A defined end point rather than an open-ended arrangement

sections.heading: Fitting Design sessions into a Dubai week, including Ramadan
paragraphs: The usable weekday window in Dubai is narrow. Buses from the Al Barsha, Jumeirah and Dubailand school clusters deliver students home between four and a quarter to five, and the far communities later than that. Design sessions for Dubai students sit mostly between half past five and half past seven Gulf Standard Time, with Saturday mornings taking the overflow. A project block of six to eight sessions therefore spans two months of term, which is why the booking date matters so much.

Ramadan reorganises everything upstream and downstream of the workshop. School days shorten, technician hours change, late afternoons are a poor time for concentration, and families plan around iftar. Two slots work: early afternoon, newly free because school finished earlier, and after iftar. For Design the early-afternoon slot is often better than it is for language subjects, because CAD and documentation work tolerate a quieter kind of attention than speaking practice does.

Material ordering also needs Ramadan thinking. Delivery times stretch, supplier hours shift, and the Al Quoz and Dragon Mart trips that are a casual Saturday errand in November become a planned expedition. A student with a spring submission should have materials bought before the month starts rather than during it, which is the sort of detail nobody mentions until it has already cost a week.

The one durable advantage of the online format here is that a session survives disruption. Family travel, a changed bus time, a school trip, a shifted iftar hour: all of these are a calendar edit rather than a renegotiated commute, because nobody is driving anywhere. Over a two-month project block that resilience is worth more than it sounds, since the sessions that get cancelled in an in-home arrangement are usually the ones closest to the deadline.

process.title: Send the folder, the brief and the booking date
process.description: Three things: the school's project brief with its criteria sheet, whatever is in the process journal so far, and the date the workshop or machine is booked for. The third is the one families forget and the one that shapes the plan, because everything upstream of it has to be finished before it.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a strand map
process.description: Sixty minutes, no payment, spent reading the folder against the sixteen strands. The output is written: strands evidenced, strands thin, strands empty, and the order to close them in given the time left. A fair number of Dubai families act on that map alone and come back for the next project.

process.title: Agree the plan backwards from the fixed date
process.description: The workshop booking goes in the middle of a timeline, with Criterion A, B and the Criterion D testing design upstream of it and testing, evaluation and documentation downstream. One failed attempt is assumed rather than hoped against, because that is what actually happens with prints and cuts.

process.title: Work in the student's own files, and document on the day
process.description: Sessions run with the student's CAD model, drawings and journal on a shared screen. Entries are made the day the work happens, tagged to a strand. The tutor will not help reconstruct a timeline retrospectively, which occasionally disappoints and is the right answer under IB academic-honesty rules.

process.title: Finish with a checklist, not a subscription
process.description: The last session of a block hands over a one-page strand checklist the student runs alone on the next project. Most Dubai families book Design support once per key stage rather than weekly for years. That is the intended outcome, and we would rather say so than pretend otherwise.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what presence buys
whyPoints.description: Roughly twenty-four of the thirty-two marks sit in documents, and a visitor at the dining table cannot bring a laser cutter. We say that plainly rather than selling a travel premium for work that is identical on a screen. The scarce resource in this subject is school workshop access, not a tutor's postcode.

whyPoints.title: Marks-per-hour triage when time is short
whyPoints.description: A folder two weeks from submission gets read against the sixteen strands and worked in order of marks recoverable per hour, which usually means testing methods and specification before any remaking. Published on this page as a table, so you can run the same triage without us.

whyPoints.title: Dubai material sourcing, with lead times
whyPoints.description: Where to buy acrylic, timber, fixings, fabric and components in this city, indicative AED ranges and realistic delivery times, so a costing is built from dated receipts rather than guesses and a plan does not assume same-day material that takes four days.

whyPoints.title: Planned backwards from the workshop booking
whyPoints.description: The immovable date in a Design project is the machine slot, not the deadline. Sessions are planned around it, with one failed print or cut assumed. Each failure photographed and explained on the day becomes a justified-change entry, which converts a setback into Criterion C marks.

whyPoints.title: Strand-level feedback a parent can check
whyPoints.description: Feedback names which of the sixteen strands an entry evidences and which are still empty, in the same framework the school assesses against. That makes the two sets of comments comparable, which no amount of general encouragement does.

whyPoints.title: A stated authorship line and a defined end
whyPoints.description: The tutor teaches, questions and marks; the student writes the journal, draws the drawings and builds the solution. Blocks end on a date rather than rolling on. Both are in writing before the first session, because an IB academic-honesty finding follows the student.

faqs.question: Can a home tutor in Dubai actually help with a making project?
faqs.answer: With most of it, yes, and not with the part families imagine. A visitor brings a laptop and whatever they can carry, not a laser cutter, a 3D printer or a technician. Since roughly twenty-four of the thirty-two marks in an MYP Design project sit in written evidence rather than in the object, that is less of a limitation than it sounds. The work that moves the grade is the specification, the research prioritisation, the product analysis and the testing design, and all of it is desk work that runs equally well on a screen.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home design tutor in Dubai cost so much more per hour?
faqs.answer: Travel. Dubai in-home rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for an online subject specialist, and the difference is forty to fifty minutes of term-time driving each way sitting inside the rate. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. The second cost is invisible: an in-home tutor is drawn from whoever will make that drive, so for a minority subject like Design you are choosing by geography before expertise.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai students buy materials for an MYP Design project?
faqs.answer: Dragon Mart in International City for fixings, small electronics, tools and cheap sheet material. Al Quoz for acrylic, timber and commercial cutting. Nasser Hardware in Bur Dubai and the Deira hardware souks for small quantities, where nobody minds selling four screws. Satwa for fabric, foam and trimmings. Amazon.ae and noon for specialist components, with two to four days of delivery that has to go into the plan. Photograph the material, the price label and the receipt; that is the evidence a cost specification line needs.

faqs.question: What should an MYP Design project cost in materials?
faqs.answer: Most school projects are achievable well under AED 200 in materials, and a card-modelling route under AED 30. Indicative Dubai retail ranges in October 2026: acrylic sheet AED 20 to 80 a piece, plywood or MDF offcuts AED 15 to 60, a PLA filament spool AED 60 to 150, fixings AED 5 to 40 an item, microcontrollers and sensors AED 40 to 200. Treat these as budgeting aids rather than quotations, and build the actual costing from dated receipts, because estimates are not evidence.

faqs.question: The school 3D printer has a three-week queue. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Three. Book earlier in the window next time and assume one failed attempt, because the first print of anything structural often fails. Use a commercial bureau in Al Quoz or at Dragon Mart for a single part, typically tens of dirhams with one to three days of lead time and the requirement that your file is correct. Or evidence the chosen-design strand with a dimensioned card model instead, which the criteria accept. The queue is a planning problem, so raise it with the Design teacher in week two rather than week seven.

faqs.question: Can my child complete a Design project at home with no workshop at all?
faqs.answer: Largely, with one honest limit. The chosen-design strand can be evidenced by a dimensioned card or foamboard model photographed from three angles. The planning-drawing strand is better served by a CAD export than by a hand sketch, and no printer is needed to produce one. Testing and evaluation need a ruler, a kitchen scale and three willing users. The limit is the technical-skills strand on a workshop-heavy course, where skipping making entirely costs marks that documentation cannot replace.

faqs.question: Which CAD software should my child use, and does it have to be the school's?
faqs.answer: Use whatever the school teaches, because the planning-drawing strand is marked on the output rather than the tool and because a student fighting unfamiliar software wastes session time. Dubai schools commonly run Fusion, Tinkercad, SketchUp or Onshape, most of which have free education access. Tell us which one before matching a tutor; a workshop specialist and a digital-prototyping specialist are not interchangeable, and the mismatch wastes a term without anyone doing anything wrong.

faqs.question: Our deadline is two weeks away. How many marks are still reachable?
faqs.answer: Usually more than families expect, because the emptiest strands are also the fastest to fill. Testing methods written against each specification line put up to eight marks in play over two or three hours. Making the specification measurable takes an hour or two and makes the whole evaluation section possible. A product analysis of four real products under five headings is one session. Remaking the prototype at two weeks out is almost never the right call. Send the folder; a strand map takes about twenty minutes and tells you what is realistically reachable.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to see the physical prototype?
faqs.answer: Photographs are enough, and in some ways better. What gets assessed in the folder is photographic and written evidence, so reviewing what an assessor will actually see is more useful than handling the object. Three angles, a ruler or a known object in frame for scale, and good light. Where a joint or a mechanism is in question, a short video of it working or failing is more informative than any still, and it doubles as evidence for the justified-changes strand.

faqs.question: What should we photograph for the journal if the making happens at school?
faqs.answer: Everything, on the day, including the failures. A photograph of the machine set-up, the part as it came off, the problem, and three sentences on what changed and why, completes the justify-changes strand in about five minutes. Students delete photographs of warped prints and broken joints because they look like mistakes; those photographs are the evidence. If the school restricts phones in the workshop, ask the teacher at the start of the project rather than discovering the restriction mid-build.

faqs.question: Will a tutor talk to my child's Design teacher about the project?
faqs.answer: We do not contact schools directly, and we would be cautious of any provider that offers to. What a tutor does is prepare your child to ask the right questions: what the booking window is, whether phones are allowed in the workshop, which strands the teacher thinks are weakest, and what the internal deadline actually is. Those conversations are more productive coming from the student, and they are also part of what the programme is trying to teach at this age.

faqs.question: How do Design sessions work during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School days shorten and technician hours change, so both sessions and workshop access need replanning. Two slots work: early afternoon, newly free because school finished earlier, and after iftar. For Design the early-afternoon slot often suits better than it does for language subjects, because CAD and documentation tolerate a quieter kind of attention. Order materials before the month starts rather than during it; delivery times stretch and the Al Quoz or Dragon Mart run becomes a planned trip rather than a Saturday errand.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same class share one Design session?
faqs.answer: Only if they are genuinely on the same project at the same stage, which siblings sometimes are and classmates rarely are. The bigger problem is academic honesty: two students who develop ideas together in a tutored session and then submit individual folders create a collusion question neither of them needs. A shared session for teaching a CAD technique is fine. A shared session for developing specifications is not, and we would decline it rather than create the problem.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram keep my child's CAD files, photographs or project work?
faqs.answer: We ask for what is needed to mark the work and no more, we tell you what is collected and why, and we delete it on request. A privacy link sits on every page. Lead forms for tutoring involve personal data about a minor, which the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection covers, so we do not ask for a child's school record, grades and photograph without stating the purpose. Keep your own copies of files and recordings; the folder is your child's.

faqs.question: Is this really the same service as a home tutor, or a cheaper substitute?
faqs.answer: It is a different delivery of the same teaching, and for this subject it is the stronger one. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What an online session adds is a wider tutor pool, since the match is made on knowing the MYP design cycle rather than on living nearby, plus screen sharing on the student's own files, which is how the assessed artefacts are actually examined.

dubai/ib-myp-design-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the strand map and the booking date
dubai/ib-myp-design-home-tutor.closingBody: Two pieces of information decide what to do with an MYP Design project: which of the sixteen strands currently have no evidence attached, and when the workshop or machine is booked. The first takes a specialist about twenty minutes to establish and is what the free trial lesson produces, in writing. The second is the fixed point everything else is planned around. Neither requires anyone to drive anywhere, and both are more useful than an extra hour of making. Send the school's brief, the criteria sheet, whatever is in the process journal and the booking date, and we will match a Design specialist for the trial lesson.

dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here have taught the MYP design cycle rather than generic product design or graphics. That means they mark against strands, ask for the process journal before the prototype, and know that Criterion D is where most Dubai MYP projects quietly lose their grade.

intro.heading: Why a good-looking project still scores a five
paragraphs: MYP Design confuses parents more than any other subject group, and the reason is visible on the kitchen table. The student has built something. It works. It looks competent. The grade comes back as a five, and nobody can explain why. The explanation is that MYP Design does not assess the object. It assesses the design cycle around the object, across four criteria of eight marks each, and within those four criteria sit sixteen separate strands that each have to be evidenced somewhere in the student's own folder.

The four criteria are Inquiring and analysing, Developing ideas, Creating the solution, and Evaluating. Only the third of those is about making anything. The first demands a justified need, prioritised primary and secondary research, an analysis of existing products and a design brief. The second demands a design specification, a range of feasible ideas, a presented chosen design and accurate planning drawings. The fourth demands detailed and relevant testing methods, an explanation of how the solution could be improved, and an account of its impact on the client or target audience. Three of the four criteria are documents.

Which produces the characteristic Dubai MYP Design pattern: strong Criterion C, weak Criterion A, and Criterion D almost empty. Students who enjoy the subject rush to the build, because the build is the fun part and the laser cutter is booked for Thursday. The specification gets written retrospectively to match what was made, the testing section becomes 'I asked my friend and she liked it', and twelve marks out of thirty-two vanish before the project is even assessed. No amount of extra workshop time recovers them.

A tutor's job in this subject is therefore mostly editorial and sequential. Get the research done before the ideas. Get the specification written before the drawings. Get the testing methods designed before the prototype exists, because a testing method invented after the fact is a description rather than a method. The work is unglamorous and it is worth roughly half the available marks, and almost nobody does it in the right order without being made to.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video with screen sharing. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Design this turns out to be the natural medium rather than a compromise: the artefacts that get marked are digital files, photographs and a written journal, and all of them live on a screen. A tutor can open a student's Fusion or Tinkercad model, annotate a planning drawing, and mark a specification line by line, which is harder to do leaning over a desk than it is with the file open between you.

dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.programmesIntro: Design appears in different forms across the three IB programmes, and the habits built in one carry into the next. The MYP version is the one where the cycle itself gets assessed explicitly.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No Design subject and no criteria, but the design cycle appears inside transdisciplinary units as inquiry, making and reflection. The habit worth building here is documentation: a child who photographs a failed attempt and writes one line about why it failed is already doing in Year 5 what MYP 4 students struggle with at fourteen.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools vary enormously in workshop and maker provision, from fully equipped design labs to a cupboard of cardboard. It is worth asking at a Year 6 open evening what the MYP 1 Design room actually contains, because the answer shapes which design strand the school can run for the next five years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · Years 7-11, labelled MYP 1 to MYP 5
programmes.description: Design is one of the eight subject groups and runs the full five years. The four criteria stay constant from MYP 1 to MYP 5; the strand expectations sharpen. By MYP 4 and 5 the student is expected to justify a need, prioritise research, write a testable specification, plan with accurate drawings, and design testing methods that measure the specification rather than ask for opinions.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools split roughly between a product-design emphasis, with workshops, laser cutters and 3D printers, and a digital-design emphasis built around CAD, app prototyping and graphics. Both are legitimate. Families transferring between Dubai schools mid-MYP sometimes move between the two, which is a bigger adjustment than the timetable suggests.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Design Technology sits in Group 4 alongside the sciences, with an internal assessment and examination papers. Computer Science and Visual Arts are the other common destinations for an MYP Design student. The MYP habits that transfer are specification writing, justified iteration and testing design; the habit that does not transfer is leaving documentation until the end.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai IB school offers DP Design Technology, because it needs workshop space, technician time and enough candidates to timetable. Families planning that route should ask in MYP 4 rather than MYP 5, and have a second Group 4 option in mind in case the group does not fill.

dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP Design is one subject with several faces depending on what a school is equipped to teach. These are the strands and adjacent courses Dubai families ask us about.

subjects.name: MYP Design: the full design cycle
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Sessions run the cycle in order rather than in the order the student finds interesting, because a specification written after a prototype cannot generate valid testing methods and the two criteria that depend on it both collapse.

subjects.name: MYP Design: digital design strand
subjects.description: App and interface prototyping, graphics, web and digital product work. Marks are lost here on the same strands as product design, with one addition: students present screenshots instead of planning drawings, and the planning-drawing strand asks for accuracy and detail that a screenshot does not supply.

subjects.name: MYP Design: product design strand
subjects.description: Physical products, often with laser cutting, 3D printing and workshop time. The constraint is scheduling: workshop access forces a build date, and students then reverse-engineer the paperwork to fit it. Sessions here are mostly about getting Criterion A and B finished before the machine is booked.

subjects.name: CAD and 3D modelling for MYP Design
subjects.description: Fusion, Tinkercad, SketchUp, Onshape and similar. A screen-shared session is the natural format for this: the tutor watches the student model rather than the finished render, which is where technique problems are visible. Dimensioned drawings exported from the model also satisfy the planning-drawing strand properly.

subjects.name: The MYP Design specification
subjects.description: The single highest-leverage document in the subject. A specification written as measurable, testable statements feeds Criterion B directly and makes Criterion D almost automatic. A specification written as adjectives feeds nothing. Two sessions on this usually move more marks than ten on the build.

subjects.name: The process journal
subjects.description: Not a diary. It is the evidence base from which the four criteria are assessed, and strands that are not evidenced in it effectively did not happen. Sessions cover what to record, when, and in what form, including photographing failed iterations, which students delete and should keep.

subjects.name: Criterion D testing methods
subjects.description: The thinnest section in most Dubai MYP Design folders. A testing method states what is measured, how, against which specification point, and with whom. 'I asked my friend' is not one. Designing tests before the prototype exists is the whole trick, and it takes about two sessions to learn.

subjects.name: DP Design Technology
subjects.description: Group 4 at Diploma level, with examination papers and an internal assessment. The MYP strands that transfer most directly are specification writing and justified iteration. The jump is in the technical depth and in the volume of written analysis expected per decision.

subjects.name: DP Computer Science
subjects.description: A common destination for MYP students who favoured the digital design strand. Programming is new content, but the solution-development documentation will feel familiar to anyone who wrote a real MYP specification rather than a retrospective one.

subjects.name: DP Visual Arts
subjects.description: The other route out of MYP Design for students whose strength is the making and the visual thinking rather than the engineering. The process portfolio rewards exactly the documentation habits MYP Design is trying to build, which makes the transition smoother than the change of subject name suggests.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Design students frequently choose a making project, which is sensible and carries a trap: the Personal Project criteria are not the Design criteria. A tutor questions the goal, discusses sources and gives feedback on what has been produced. The student writes every word of the report and the process journal themselves.

dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities we take MYP Design requests from
dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.regionsIntro: Design requests cluster around the schools with real workshop and CAD provision, which in Dubai means the southern and eastern school belts and the newer Dubailand communities. The detail below is about what actually constrains a weekly session.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Well-provisioned design labs in several of the schools serving this community, which raises the technical level of requests. Students arrive with CAD files rather than questions about what CAD is, and sessions tend to start at the planning-drawing strand rather than at the brief.

regions.name: Dubai International Academic City and Al Warqa
regions.note: Long bus routes and a late arrival home, so weekday sessions start at six or later. A high share of MYP 5 requests here come three weeks before a portfolio deadline, which is late but recoverable if the testing methods are tackled first.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Newer schools with newer equipment and, in several cases, teachers also new to the MYP criteria. Parents here ask unusually precise questions about strand wording, which is a good sign. Sessions commonly focus on Criterion A research prioritisation.

regions.name: Motor City and Victory Heights
regions.note: Compact, villa-heavy and well served by schools within a short drive, so in-home supply exists here. The limiting factor is subject rather than distance: a general art or IT tutor is easy to find locally and is not the same thing as a Design specialist.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Established villa communities with a long-running IB presence. Requests skew to MYP 4 and 5 students planning a DP route, so sessions often cover whether Design Technology, Computer Science or Visual Arts is the right destination.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Sustainability runs through the school culture here, which shows up in design briefs about waste, water and energy. That helps Criterion A, because the justified need writes itself, and hurts Criterion D unless the student learns to measure an environmental claim rather than assert it.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Khail Heights

sections.heading: The four criteria and their sixteen strands: what each one actually asks for
paragraphs: Everything in MYP Design hangs off sixteen strands. They are published, they are specific, and a project is assessed by looking for evidence of each one in the student's folder. The reason a capable student scores five rather than seven is almost never that the work was bad; it is that four or five strands have nothing pointing at them. A tutor's first task on any project is to read the folder with the strand list beside it and name the gaps.

Criterion A, Inquiring and analysing, wants the need for a solution explained and justified, research identified and prioritised into primary and secondary, an analysis of a group of similar existing products, and a design brief. The strand students skip is the product analysis, because it feels like homework and it is where the specification's content is supposed to come from. Criterion B, Developing ideas, wants a design specification, a range of feasible ideas, the chosen design presented, and accurate detailed planning drawings. The strand students skip is the range: three variations on one idea is not a range.

Criterion C, Creating the solution, wants a logical plan, demonstrated technical skills, a solution made by following that plan, and a full justification of any changes made to the chosen design or the plan. That last strand is the one students lose for free. Changes happen in every project; the marks are for explaining them, and a photographed note in the journal on the day takes two minutes. Criterion D, Evaluating, wants detailed and relevant testing methods, an explanation of how the solution could be improved, and an explanation of the solution's impact on the client or target audience.

Read the table against your child's folder rather than against your memory of the project. The diagnostic value is in the gaps column: a folder with nothing under 'prioritised research' and nothing under 'testing methods' is a predictable five whatever the prototype looks like, and both gaps can be closed in a fortnight if they are found before submission rather than after.

sections.heading: Criterion A: the project is decided before any making starts
paragraphs: If a project is going to score a seven, it is already on course by the end of Criterion A, and if it is going to score a four, that is usually decided there too. The criterion asks for four things in sequence: a justified need, prioritised research, an analysis of existing products, and a design brief. Done properly this takes two to three weeks of a school project and produces the raw material for everything after it. Done badly it takes an evening and leaves the student designing in a vacuum.

The justification strand is where Dubai students are often strongest, because the context is genuinely interesting: water use in a villa community, shade in a school courtyard, waste from a canteen, accessibility in a tower lobby. What follows is weaker. Research gets collected rather than prioritised, which is the actual verb in the strand. Prioritising means stating which findings will shape the design and why, and discarding the rest visibly. A folder with eleven pages of pasted search results and no prioritisation scores lower than one with three pages and a ranking.

The product analysis strand is the one to insist on. Analysing a group of similar existing products means examining several real products against consistent headings — materials, manufacture, cost, user, failure points — and drawing conclusions that become specification lines. Students treat it as a gallery of photographs. A tutor's intervention here is simple and unpopular: pick four real products, build a comparison table with five headings, write one conclusion per heading. It takes a session and it unblocks Criterion B.

The design brief then becomes a summary rather than an invention. Students who write the brief first and the research afterwards produce briefs that cannot be justified from their own evidence, and assessors notice. The sequence is not pedantry; each strand supplies the input for the next, which is why working out of order costs marks in two criteria at once rather than one.
bullets: Justify the need from evidence, not from enthusiasm
Prioritise research: state what will shape the design and discard the rest visibly
Analyse four real products against five consistent headings
Write the design brief last, as a summary of the three strands before it
Two to three weeks of a school project, not an evening

sections.heading: The design specification: one document, two criteria, half the marks
paragraphs: The specification is the hinge of the whole project. It sits in Criterion B, and it is also what Criterion D's testing methods must test against. Write it as measurable statements and the evaluation almost designs itself. Write it as adjectives — attractive, durable, user-friendly, sustainable — and Criterion D has nothing to measure, which is precisely why so many Dubai MYP Design folders have a thin evaluation section attached to a competent build.

The repair is mechanical. Every specification line gets a quantity, a unit or a verifiable condition, and a test. 'Must be durable' becomes 'must withstand 50 open-and-close cycles without the hinge loosening, tested by cycling and photographing the joint at 0, 25 and 50'. 'Must be attractive to Year 7 students' becomes 'at least seven of ten Year 7 users rate the appearance 4 or 5 on a five-point scale, tested by a structured questionnaire with the scale shown'. Neither is elegant prose. Both are worth marks in two criteria.

There is a Dubai-specific version of this worth flagging. Sustainability briefs are popular here, encouraged by school culture and by the city's own sustainability programming, and they generate the hardest specification lines to make testable. 'Reduces plastic waste' is unmeasurable in a school project. 'Replaces at least two single-use items per user per week, verified by a seven-day user log' is measurable, modest and honest. Students resist shrinking the claim; the mark scheme rewards it.

The table below is the format we use in sessions. Students fill it in before any planning drawing exists, and the right-hand column becomes the Criterion D section verbatim. It also catches the specification line that cannot be tested at all, which is a line worth deleting before an assessor finds it.

sections.heading: Criterion C: why the best-made project in the class can still lose marks
paragraphs: Criterion C is the one students think the subject is about, and it is still only a quarter of the marks. It contains four strands: construct a logical plan, demonstrate technical skills, follow the plan to create the solution, and fully justify changes made to the chosen design and the plan. Three of those four are documentation about the making rather than the making itself.

The logical plan strand wants a sequence with time estimates and resources, produced before work starts. A Gantt-style table is enough; students who write it retrospectively produce something suspiciously tidy that does not match the dated photographs in the journal, which is worse than a messy honest plan. In Dubai schools where workshop or laser-cutter access is booked in advance, the plan has real teeth, because the booking date is a hard constraint everything else has to fit around.

The justification strand is the cheapest marks in the subject and the most commonly abandoned. Every project changes: a material is unavailable, a joint fails, a 3D print warps, a dimension was wrong. The marks are not for avoiding the change, they are for explaining what changed, why, and what effect it had on the specification. A photograph plus three sentences in the journal on the day it happens is the whole requirement. Reconstructed from memory six weeks later, it reads like fiction and is marked accordingly.

Technical skill itself does get assessed, and this is where online sessions earn their place. Watching a student model in CAD rather than looking at the finished render shows where technique is weak: a sketch that is not fully constrained, a timeline full of unnecessary features, a model that cannot be edited without collapsing. Those are fixable in two sessions and invisible in a final image, which is why screen sharing in both directions is the format we use for this part of the work.

sections.heading: Criterion D: designing testing methods before the prototype exists
paragraphs: Criterion D is the thinnest section in most of the Dubai MYP Design folders we read, and it is the easiest eight marks on the page to improve. It asks for three things: detailed and relevant testing methods, an explanation of how the solution could be improved, and an explanation of its impact on the client or target audience. 'Relevant' means relevant to the specification, which is why a weak specification guarantees a weak evaluation.

The core discipline is to design the tests before the solution exists. If the specification says the product must hold 2 kg without deformation, the test is written in week two: load with 2 kg for ten minutes, measure deflection before and after with a ruler, photograph both. Writing that in week two takes five minutes. Writing it in week ten, after the prototype is built, invites the student to invent a test the product will pass, which assessors recognise and which also destroys the point of the exercise.

The improvement strand is not an apology. Students write 'if I had more time I would have made it neater', which scores nothing. It wants a specific change traced to a specific test result: the hinge developed 2 mm of play after 40 cycles, so a nylon bushing or a larger-diameter pin would be the next iteration, at an estimated additional cost of AED 8. That is an engineering statement, and it is what the strand is asking for in plain terms.

The impact strand asks about the client or target audience, and Dubai students have an advantage here if they use it. A real target user is available: a sibling, a classmate, a teacher, a facilities manager, a neighbour in the same tower. Three structured responses from real users beat a paragraph of speculation about an imagined market. Collect them with a printed scale, tabulate the answers, and the strand is evidenced rather than asserted.
bullets: Write every test in week two, against a specification line
Measure something: a unit, a count, a rating scale
Trace each improvement to a named test result
Use real target users, three of them, with a structured instrument
A test invented after the build is a description, not a method

sections.heading: The process journal, week by week, and what each entry is evidencing
paragraphs: The process journal is the folder from which all four criteria are assessed. Strands not evidenced in it effectively did not happen, however well the project went. Students treat it as a diary to be written up at the end, which produces a document that is simultaneously long and empty: lots of reflection on feelings, no dated evidence of prioritised research or justified changes.

What makes a journal work is that entries are made on the day, in whatever form is fastest, and tagged to a strand. A photograph of four products on a shelf with five headings written beside it is a Criterion A entry. A dated screenshot of a CAD sketch with the constraint error visible is a Criterion C entry. A phone photo of a failed joint with three sentences about what changed is the justified-changes strand, complete. None of this takes more than five minutes, and all of it is unrecoverable later.

The table maps a typical eight-week Dubai school project onto journal entries. It is deliberately a schedule of evidence rather than a schedule of work, because the work usually happens and the evidence usually does not. A parent can use it as a checklist without knowing anything about design: ask which week the project is in, and ask to see the entry that week was supposed to produce.

One thing worth telling students explicitly: keep the failures. Students delete the photograph of the warped print and the broken joint because it looks like a mistake. Those photographs are the evidence for the justified-changes strand and often for the testing strand too. A folder with no failures in it is either a project where nothing was learned or a folder where the learning was not recorded, and both are marked the same way.
