sections.heading: Digital or product design: what your Dubai school is equipped to teach
paragraphs: MYP Design gives schools latitude, and Dubai schools use it differently depending on what their building contains. Some run a workshop-led product design course with laser cutters, 3D printers and technician support. Others run a digital-led course built on CAD, interface prototyping and graphics. A few manage both across the five years. None of these is better, but they are different courses, and a family transferring between Dubai schools mid-MYP can find the subject almost unrecognisable.

This matters for two practical reasons. The first is tutoring fit: a tutor who knows workshop processes is not interchangeable with one who knows interface prototyping, and matching a student to the wrong one wastes a term. We ask what software and what machines the school actually uses before matching, because the answer changes the tutor rather than the price. The second is the DP route. A digital-led MYP Design background points naturally at Computer Science; a workshop-led one points at Design Technology, where it exists.

Dubai's private sector is expanding fast enough that this is a live question rather than a settled one. KHDA reported that the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four following a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up 6%. New campuses often arrive with strong equipment and staff new to MYP criteria, which is a specific combination: technical capability high, strand literacy still settling.

The practical advice for a Dubai parent choosing or changing schools with Design in mind is to ask three questions at the open evening. Which design strand does the school run through MYP 4 and 5? What software and machines do students actually use, as opposed to own? And does the school offer DP Design Technology, and did the group run last year? The third question is the one that gets the most informative answer.

sections.heading: Where MYP Design leads at Diploma level, and what to settle in MYP 4
paragraphs: MYP Design does not lock a student into anything, but the MYP 4 and 5 experience shapes which Diploma options feel possible. Three destinations come up repeatedly for Dubai students: Design Technology in Group 4, Computer Science in the same group, and Visual Arts in Group 6. A fourth, quieter route is to drop design entirely and carry the documentation habits into a science internal assessment, where they transfer better than students expect.

Design Technology is the direct continuation and the one with the most practical constraints attached. It needs workshop space, technician time and enough candidates to timetable, which is why not every Dubai IB school runs it. Ask in MYP 4 whether the school expects to offer it, and ask whether last year's group ran. A group that did not fill is not a group, and discovering that in the spring of MYP 5 leaves no room to plan a Group 4 alternative.

Computer Science suits the student who enjoyed the digital strand and the systematic parts of the cycle. The programming is genuinely new content and the pace in DP1 is brisk, but the solution-development documentation rewards anyone who wrote a real specification in MYP rather than a retrospective one. Visual Arts suits the student whose strength was the making and the visual reasoning; its process portfolio is close in spirit to a well-kept MYP process journal.

The table sets out what each route assumes and what to close during MYP 5. One general point applies to all of them: the single most transferable thing MYP Design teaches is writing a testable statement and then testing it. That skill shows up in a DP science internal assessment, in a Design Technology project and in an extended essay methodology, which is a reasonable argument for taking the unglamorous strands seriously even if the student never studies design again.

process.title: Send the project brief and the folder as it stands
process.description: The school's project brief, the assessment criteria the teacher issued, and whatever the student has in the process journal so far, even if it is three photographs. A tutor can read that against the sixteen strands in twenty minutes and name the gaps, which is a better starting point than a conversation about how the project is going.

process.title: A free trial lesson spent on the strand map
process.description: Sixty minutes with a Design specialist, no payment. The output is a written strand map: which of the sixteen are evidenced, which are thin, which are missing, and in what order to close them given the deadline. Families frequently act on that map themselves and come back for the next project.

process.title: Fix the sequence before adding any work
process.description: If the specification is unwritten and the build is already underway, the first sessions go backwards: product analysis, prioritised research, a testable specification, then the testing methods. It feels like going the wrong way. It is the only order in which the remaining marks are reachable.

process.title: Work in the student's own files
process.description: Sessions run with the student's CAD model, drawings and journal on a shared screen, in their own software rather than a demonstration version. The tutor watches the modelling rather than the render, which is where technique problems show, and annotates drawings live so the corrected version is the one the student keeps.

process.title: Hand back a checklist the student can run alone
process.description: The last session of a project block produces a one-page strand checklist the student uses on the next project without us. Most Dubai families book a Design block once per key stage rather than weekly for years, and that is the intended outcome rather than a lost sale.

whyPoints.title: Marking by strand, not by impression
whyPoints.description: Feedback names which of the sixteen strands an entry evidences and which are still empty. That is the same framework the school assesses against, so the two documents can be compared. An impression of a project tells a parent nothing they could not see on the kitchen table.

whyPoints.title: The sequence enforced, not suggested
whyPoints.description: Research before ideas, specification before drawings, testing methods before prototype. Students resist this order because the build is the interesting part, and almost every lost mark in MYP Design comes from working the other way round. Enforcing it is most of what a Design tutor is for.

whyPoints.title: Screen sharing suits this subject
whyPoints.description: The assessed artefacts are files, drawings and photographs, and all of them live on a screen. A tutor can watch a student construct a CAD sketch and spot an unconstrained profile, which is invisible in a finished render and hard to see leaning over a desk.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the software and machines your school uses
whyPoints.description: We ask which CAD package and which workshop equipment the school actually runs before matching a tutor, because a workshop specialist and an interface-prototyping specialist are not interchangeable. The answer changes the tutor rather than the rate.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on whose work it is
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions, teaches technique and gives feedback on what the student has produced. The student writes the journal and the report and builds the solution. For the MYP Personal Project in particular we put that boundary in writing, because an academic-honesty finding under IB rules follows the student.

whyPoints.title: Sourced facts, including the inconvenient ones
whyPoints.description: School-sector figures here come from KHDA and Dubai Media Office releases and are dated. We do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages, because they could not be verified from the IB directly, and an unsourced date on a deadline page is worse than no date.

faqs.question: What does MYP Design actually get marked on if not the finished product?
faqs.answer: Four criteria of eight marks each, containing sixteen strands in total. Criterion A is inquiring and analysing, Criterion B is developing ideas, Criterion C is creating the solution, and Criterion D is evaluating. Only Criterion C involves making anything, and three of its four strands are documentation about the making rather than the making itself. The practical consequence is that a well-built product with a thin specification and two lines of testing sits around a five, and no extra workshop time recovers those marks.

faqs.question: My child's project works and looks good but the Design grade is a five. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because four or five strands have no evidence pointing at them. The common pattern in Dubai folders is strong Criterion C, weak Criterion A and an almost empty Criterion D: the product analysis was skipped, the research was collected rather than prioritised, the specification was written after the build, and the testing section asks friends for opinions. Each of those is a named strand with marks attached. Read the folder against the strand list and the missing eight to twelve marks are usually visible in twenty minutes.

faqs.question: What belongs in an MYP Design process journal, and how often?
faqs.answer: Entries made on the day, in the fastest usable form, each tagged to a strand. A photograph of four real products with five comparison headings written beside it is a Criterion A entry. A dated screenshot of a CAD sketch is a Criterion C entry. A phone photo of a failed joint plus three sentences about what changed completes the justified-changes strand. None takes more than five minutes, and none is recoverable later. Tell your child to keep the failures: deleted photographs of warped prints are deleted marks.

faqs.question: How detailed does an MYP Design specification need to be?
faqs.answer: Detailed enough that every line can be tested. Give each line a quantity, a unit or a verifiable condition, and a test. 'Must be durable' becomes 'must withstand 50 open-and-close cycles with no hinge loosening, measured in millimetres of play at 0, 25 and 50 cycles'. This is the highest-leverage document in the subject because it sits in Criterion B and also supplies everything Criterion D measures against. A specification made of adjectives guarantees a thin evaluation however good the prototype is.

faqs.question: What counts as a testing method in Criterion D?
faqs.answer: A method states what is measured, how, against which specification line, and with whom. Load 2 kg for ten minutes and measure deflection before and after. Cycle a hinge 50 times and record play in millimetres. Give ten target users a printed five-point scale and tabulate the ratings. 'I asked my friend and she liked it' is an opinion, not a method. The discipline that makes this work is writing the tests in week two, before the solution exists, so the test measures the specification rather than flattering the prototype.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach CAD properly over video?
faqs.answer: It is the better format for it. With screen sharing in both directions the tutor watches the student construct the model rather than looking at the finished render, which is where technique problems live: unconstrained sketches, a timeline cluttered with unnecessary features, a model that collapses when a dimension changes. None of that is visible in an exported image. Sessions also cover exporting properly dimensioned drawings from the model, which satisfies the planning-drawing strand and which many students do not realise their software can do.

faqs.question: Is MYP Design assessed by an examination or a portfolio?
faqs.answer: Where a Dubai school registers MYP 5 students for IB MYP eAssessment, Design is a portfolio subject, externally moderated against the same four criteria used throughout the programme. The two-hour on-screen examinations sit in Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Mathematics, Sciences and interdisciplinary learning. Many Dubai IB continuum schools do not register for eAssessment at all and move students straight into the Diploma. Ask your MYP coordinator which route applies, and confirm all deadlines with the school and the IB's own published guidance.

faqs.question: Does my child's school teaching only digital design limit their options?
faqs.answer: It shapes them rather than limiting them. A digital-led MYP Design course built on CAD, interface prototyping and graphics points naturally at DP Computer Science and sits comfortably alongside Visual Arts. A workshop-led course points at Design Technology where the school offers it. The sixteen strands are identical either way, so the transferable skills are the same. The practical thing to check is whether your school runs DP Design Technology at all, and whether last year's group actually filled.

faqs.question: Where should we start if the project deadline is three weeks away?
faqs.answer: With Criterion D and the specification, in that order, which surprises most families. Testing methods and a testable specification can be written in two sessions and are usually the emptiest strands in the folder. Product analysis can be completed in one session with four real products and five headings. Reworking the build at three weeks out is almost never the right call. Send the folder first: a strand map takes a tutor twenty minutes and tells you which gaps are still reachable in the time available.

faqs.question: How many sessions does one MYP Design project usually need?
faqs.answer: Six to eight across a full project if you start at the brief, which maps roughly one session per stage of the cycle with the making weeks lighter. Two to four if the folder is nearly finished and the weak criterion is already identified. Most Dubai families book a project block once rather than weekly sessions for years, because the output is a reusable sequence the student runs alone next time. That is the intended result rather than a lost opportunity.

faqs.question: What does MYP Design tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read across Dubai providers in October 2026 run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, with in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the rate. Those are other providers' published figures rather than ours. Design is a smaller tutor pool than maths or sciences, so it sits in the specialist band more often. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson, when the scope of the project is actually known.

faqs.question: How does a tutor help with a design project without crossing an academic honesty line?
faqs.answer: By teaching, questioning and giving feedback on work that already exists. A tutor can explain what the planning-drawing strand asks for, challenge a specification line that cannot be tested, teach a CAD technique, and mark a draft against the criteria. A tutor does not generate ideas the student then submits as their own, draw the drawings, or write journal entries. We put that boundary in writing before the first session, because an IB academic-honesty finding attaches to the student rather than to the tutor.

faqs.question: Will the tutor know which design software my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: We ask before matching, because it decides the match. Dubai schools run a range including Fusion, Tinkercad, SketchUp, Onshape and various interface-prototyping tools, alongside workshop equipment from laser cutters to 3D printers. A workshop specialist and a digital-prototyping specialist are not interchangeable, and putting a student with the wrong one wastes a term without anybody doing anything wrong. Tell us the software, the machines and the project brief, and the match follows from that.

faqs.question: Is in-home design tutoring available anywhere in Dubai through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For Design the online format is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because every artefact that gets assessed is a file, a drawing or a photograph. Having the student's own model open between tutor and student beats sitting beside a laptop and looking at the same screen from an angle.

faqs.question: Can one tutor support both MYP Design and the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a sensible pairing because many MYP 5 students choose a making project. The warning is that the Personal Project criteria are not the Design criteria, and treating one as a continuation of the other costs marks in both. A tutor questions the goal, discusses sources, helps plan a realistic timeline and gives feedback on what the student has produced. The student writes every word of the report and the process journal themselves, and that line is set out before the first session.

dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.closingHeading: Send the folder, get the strand map
dubai/ib-myp-design-tutor.closingBody: The fastest useful thing anyone can do with an MYP Design project is read the folder against the sixteen strands and find out which of them have no evidence attached. That takes a specialist about twenty minutes and it is what the free trial lesson produces: a written strand map showing what is evidenced, what is thin, what is missing, and the order to close the gaps in given the deadline. Plenty of Dubai families act on that map themselves and return for the next project. Send the school's brief, the criteria sheet and whatever is in the process journal so far, and we will match a Design specialist for the trial.

intro.heading: An examination that generates its own evidence, if anyone bothers to collect it
paragraphs: Most tutoring is hard to audit. A parent pays for hours, the child reports that the sessions are useful, and the first independent measurement arrives on a school report months later. On-screen examinations are different, and the difference is worth exploiting. Every response your child types in a practice session is a document. It can be marked against the published criterion descriptors, timed task by task, filed, and set beside the response they wrote six weeks earlier. Progress on this component is measurable in a way almost no other tutoring is.

That is the whole basis of this page. An IB MYP eAssessment home tutor in Dubai is usually chosen on a recommendation and reviewed on atmosphere, and both are weak instruments when something measurable is available. The measurable version is a small stack of marked scripts with dates on them. If the criterion comments in week eight are about different problems from the ones in week one, the teaching is working. If they are about the same problems, it is not, and you can know that in a month rather than in May.

There is a Dubai-specific reason to insist on this. The emirate had 227 private schools across 17 curricula in 2024-25, per the Dubai Media Office, and families here routinely change school systems mid-education. An MYP report that reports criterion numbers out of eight, with no percentage anywhere, gives a parent who grew up with a national board curriculum almost nothing to act on. A marked script with a comment naming which descriptor was not met is legible to anybody, including a parent who has never read the subject guide.

The second Dubai reason is cost discipline. Published specialist tutoring rates in this market run from AED 200 to AED 450 and above per hour, according to Bestimate's Dubai survey, with named premium tutors advertised at AED 650 by BartyED. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. At that level, a family spending eight weeks on the wrong problem is spending real money. A marked baseline script costs one session and usually reveals that the actual problem is timing or command-term shape rather than subject knowledge, which changes what the remaining seven sessions should contain.

What follows is the mechanics of that evidence trail: what a marked script contains, how a timing analysis reads, what three measured mocks across a block actually show, how criterion movement looks week by week, and what the evidence cannot tell you. There is also an honest answer to the search term itself. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we operate only in India. For on-screen preparation that turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise, and the section below explains why rather than asserting it.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Measurable evidence becomes available at different points in the programme, and before MYP 4 there is very little of it. These are the stages we cover for Dubai families, framed by what can actually be measured at each.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 9
programmes.description: No external assessment and no on-screen paper, so the only evidence is the school's own criterion marking. That is still worth reading closely, because a student consistently weaker on one criterion letter across three subject groups has a transferable problem rather than three subject problems.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is the year the route decision gets made, since many schools move the cohort to International GCSE at Year 10. A parent asking for strand-level comments on one piece of marked work in each subject gets more diagnostic value here than from any paid assessment.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 10
programmes.description: The first year a timed criterion response is realistic, and therefore the first year a baseline script is worth taking. Mathematics splits into standard and extended routes here, and moderated portfolio material starts accumulating in the subject groups that will be submitted rather than examined.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the full programme generally begin on-screen familiarisation in Year 10 on school devices. Ask which device and platform the live session uses, because a baseline taken on a different keyboard is slightly optimistic.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 11, and the session
programmes.description: On-screen papers in May, moderated portfolios submitted earlier, and the personal project in the same winter term. This is the year the evidence trail matters most and is hardest to maintain, because the student's available hours are fully committed from November onwards.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Dubai sequencing problem is that portfolio and project deadlines cluster in the winter, leaving January to April as the clear run for on-screen work. A baseline script taken in January is the single most useful purchase of the year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: Written papers, internal assessments in every subject, and the Extended Essay. Criterion reading and command-term habits transfer directly from on-screen work. Handwriting stamina does not, and after two years of typing it is a genuine and measurable gap.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students moving into DP1 after eAssessment usually benefit from one timed handwritten paper over the summer, purely as a measurement. Most discover their hand fails before their argument does, which is easier to fix in August than in a November mock.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Evidence looks different in each subject group, because the criteria ask for different things. These are the areas Dubai families most often bring us, described by what a marked script actually shows in each.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The script shows whether analysis arrived at all. Weak responses spend 300 words introducing the extract and reach the first analytical sentence on the final line. The measurable improvement is the word position at which the first genuine claim appears, which tends to move forward sharply once it is pointed out.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: The script shows the ratio of description to evaluation. Counting sentences that judge a source against sentences that summarise one is crude and startlingly effective; students who start at one in ten usually reach one in three within four marked attempts.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: The script shows whether reasoning is stated or implied. Candidates write a correct conclusion without the intervening step, and the descriptor rewards the step. Marked attempts make the missing link visible, and the fix is a habit rather than content.

subjects.name: Mathematics, standard route
subjects.description: The script shows where method marks were available and not claimed. Students who work in their heads and write only the answer lose credit that was theirs, and the measurement is simply how many lines of working appear per question across successive attempts.

subjects.name: Mathematics, extended route
subjects.description: The script shows whether the student can sustain a multi-step problem under time. Extended questions reward persistence, and the common pattern is an abandoned second half. A timing analysis across three mocks shows whether abandonment is a knowledge problem or a clock problem.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: The script shows integration or its absence immediately, because an unintegrated response has a visible seam where one discipline stops and the other starts. This is the most diagnosable error in the entire set and the one most often left unexamined.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: No script exists, because the assessment is coursework marked by the school. The measurable evidence we can generate is parallel: a recorded spoken response in week one against one in week eight, which parents can judge without speaking the language.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: We work on a parallel brief rather than the submitted portfolio, so the evidence is an evaluation written on that separate brief, marked against the descriptor. Improvement there is what the student then applies to their own work, alone.

subjects.name: Arts and Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Documentation is the measurable variable. We can count dated process entries and check whether each records a decision rather than an activity, using the student's own separate practice log rather than anything that will be submitted.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, per KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines, and assessed outside the MYP subject-group structure. They consume timetable hours in the same term as on-screen preparation, which is a scheduling fact rather than an assessment one.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Running a two-hour mock at home, community by community
dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The evidence trail depends on your child being able to sit a timed two-hour response without interruption, which in Dubai is a housing and household question more than anything else. These notes cover what that looks like in different communities.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Villas with a spare room make a two-hour mock straightforward, and weekend mornings are usually clear of activities. The practical obstacle here is maids' day and family visits on Fridays, so Saturday mornings tend to hold better across an eight-week block.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Jumeirah Village Triangle
regions.note: Apartment living with thin walls, so noise rather than space is the constraint. Families here often run the mock early on a weekend morning. Headphones matter because audio stimulus is part of several papers and a shared room makes that genuinely harder.

regions.name: The Springs, The Meadows and Jumeirah Park
regions.note: Established communities with heavy after-school activity schedules through the week. A two-hour mock almost never fits a weekday evening here, so the realistic pattern is weekly short sessions plus a weekend mock at the three agreed measurement points.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Sporting commitments dominate weekends for many families, which pushes mocks to Friday mornings. If your child trains competitively, say so when scheduling, because a mock taken after a tournament measures fatigue rather than preparation.

regions.name: Town Square, Mudon and Dubailand
regions.note: Newer family communities with younger siblings in most households, which is the main threat to an uninterrupted two hours. Families here have more success with a mock split across two sixty-minute halves, which loses some timing realism but produces usable scripts.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Dense apartment living with reliable connectivity. The common issue is a shared study space with an older sibling in Diploma years. Agreeing who gets the quiet room on which morning is a small piece of household logistics that decides whether the evidence exists.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Remraam
regions.note: Quiet by design and generally good for timed work, with longer travel to central Dubai that makes online delivery the only sensible option for a weekday session. Mocks fit well on weekday afternoons during school holidays, which is when we schedule the mid-point reading.

regions.name: International City, Warsan and Al Nahda
regions.note: Often multi-child households in compact flats, where two uninterrupted hours is a real ask. The honest answer is that a shorter timed task done properly beats a two-hour mock done with interruptions, and the criterion evidence from a 40-minute response is still usable.

sections.heading: What a home tutor would bring to on-screen preparation, and what we do instead
paragraphs: The search term is reasonable and the underlying wish is sensible: a parent wants someone in the room who can see whether the child is actually working. Visiting tutors operate across Dubai and the published market rate is known. Bestimate's Dubai survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 per hour, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions circulate widely in this emirate. Those are other providers' figures with their reading date, not IB Gram prices.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Visiting tutors are a service we operate only in India, and we would rather publish that than take a booking and explain afterwards. For this particular component the online format is not a concession. An on-screen examination is sat on a keyboard in a browser, so a session conducted on a keyboard in a browser is a closer rehearsal than any version at a kitchen table with a notebook. The student types into a timed document and the tutor watches the response appear in real time, which is exactly the thing that cannot be observed in a printed-paper tutorial.

Remote invigilation also solves the problem parents actually have. A visiting tutor who sits beside a student for two hours is expensive and, by their presence, changes the conditions. A tutor present on video and muted provides the same honesty about conditions at a fraction of the cost, and leaves a marked script afterwards rather than a verbal summary at the door. The table below sets the comparison out without pretending the in-home option has no advantages, because for a fifteen-year-old who will not start without an adult present, it has one.

sections.heading: The marked script: the only evidence on this component that means anything
paragraphs: A marked script is a response with comments attached to specific sentences, each naming the criterion descriptor the sentence does or does not satisfy. It is not a percentage. The paper is criterion-referenced, so a percentage is a translation that loses the information a parent needs: not how much was wrong, but which descriptor was never addressed. A comment reading that the second paragraph describes the source accurately and never judges its reliability tells a family what to do next. Sixty-two per cent does not.

The script should also carry a comparison. Our session notes put the current criterion marks beside the previous ones for the same task type, which is how movement becomes visible across weeks rather than being asserted. Four attempts is usually enough to see a pattern: either the comments change subject, which means problems are being closed, or they repeat, which means the sessions are addressing something other than the real constraint.

There is a discipline to this that providers resist, because marking honestly is slower than teaching enthusiastically and sometimes produces an awkward conversation. A script that has not improved in four attempts is a fact that has to be reported. Our practice is to report it with a diagnosis: the student is not doing the between-session work, the instruction was too broad to act on, or the real gap is subject understanding that eight weeks will not supply. All three are useful to a Dubai family paying specialist hourly rates, and all three are more useful than another cheerful session.

sections.heading: Three measured mocks, and what counts as movement between them
paragraphs: An eight-week block carries three full mocks rather than one. The baseline is taken in week one, before any teaching, which parents sometimes object to and which is the most valuable session in the block. Teaching before measuring means never knowing what the teaching changed. The mid-point mock falls around week four or five, and the pre-session mock in the final fortnight, close enough to the real thing to be a rehearsal and far enough out that a bad result can still be acted on.

Each mock yields three readings. Criterion marks per task, which show whether the answer shape has changed. A timing breakdown, which shows where the two hours went. And a completion count, which is simply how many tasks were actually finished. The third is the crudest and often the most informative, because an incomplete paper caps the achievable marks regardless of quality, and candidates who finish nothing in week one frequently finish everything by week five with no change in their subject knowledge at all.

What counts as movement is worth agreeing in advance so that nobody is arguing about it in week six. Honest targets from a typical starting point: completion rising from most tasks unfinished to all tasks attempted, the first analytical sentence arriving in the opening third of a response rather than at the end, and the description-to-judgement ratio shifting measurably. We do not set a target criterion mark, because the mock is marked by a tutor rather than by the IB and treating a tutor's mark as a prediction is exactly the overselling this market is full of.

sections.heading: Timing analysis: where the two hours actually went
paragraphs: Timing is the most commonly decisive variable and the one least often measured, because it is invisible in a grade. The analysis is simple to produce and immediately legible: note the minutes spent on each task against the minutes the task's weight deserves, then look at the gap. The pattern across Dubai candidates in their first mock is remarkably consistent. Half or more of the two hours goes on the first extended task, and the final task receives under ten minutes or nothing at all.

There are three usual causes and they need different fixes. A student who over-invests in the first task because they are perfectionist responds to a hard rule: a visible clock and a stop point agreed before starting. A student who is slow because of navigation between the stimulus and the answer field responds to platform practice, which is mostly a matter of repetition on the real interface. And a student who is slow because they type at the speed of someone who writes by hand responds only to typing practice, which happens outside sessions and takes about six weeks.

The second pattern worth naming is the opposite failure, which is rarer and more frustrating. Some candidates finish in seventy minutes and sit for the remaining fifty, having written short, correct, under-evidenced answers. The timing analysis shows this instantly and the fix is not more speed but the opposite: a required minimum on each task, with the student instructed to use the time rather than to escape the room. Both patterns are mechanical, both are visible in one mock, and neither is diagnosable from a grade.

sections.heading: Criterion movement over eight weeks, week by week
paragraphs: The log below is composite rather than one student, and it is deliberately unflattering in places because real blocks have flat weeks. The useful reading is the right-hand column: what the marked script shows afterwards, which is the only part a parent can verify. Weeks three and six are the ones families query, because in both cases the session felt productive and the script barely moved.

The pattern is worth knowing in advance. Mechanical problems close quickly: completion, timing split, bullet-point answers, transcription of the stimulus. Judgement problems close slowly, because they depend on the student having something to judge with, and that is subject understanding accumulated across two years. So the first half of a block tends to produce dramatic-looking gains in completion and structure, and the second half produces smaller, slower gains in the quality of evaluation. A family expecting the second half to look like the first will conclude the tutoring has stalled when it has simply reached the harder problem.

What would genuinely indicate a stall is comments repeating unchanged across four marked scripts. If the same descriptor is named in week one, three, five and seven, the sessions are not addressing the real constraint and more of them will not help. At that point the honest options are a different tutor, a narrower focus on one subject group rather than two, or an acceptance that the limiting factor is subject understanding and that the money is better spent on next year.

sections.heading: What the evidence cannot tell you, and the providers who pretend otherwise
paragraphs: No marked mock predicts a grade. The script is marked by a tutor, not by the IB, against descriptors applied without the standardisation an official marking process carries, on a task that is not the live paper. Treating a tutor's criterion mark as a forecast is the single most common overselling in this market, and it is also unnecessary: the useful claim is about the work, not the result. This descriptor was never addressed in January and is addressed consistently in April. That is checkable and it is enough.

The evidence also cannot tell you about the moderated portfolio subjects, because we never see that work. For those subject groups the only honest measurement is parallel: an evaluation written on a different brief, a recorded spoken response compared across weeks. Those are real measurements of a real skill, and they are not measurements of the portfolio. Any provider offering to assess a portfolio they are also helping to produce is describing a conflict rather than a service.

Two further limits belong on the page. The evidence says nothing about whether the school's own mock conditions match the live session, which is a question for the coordinator. And it says nothing about the certificate arithmetic, which depends on thresholds the IB sets and revises; confirm those with your school rather than any tutoring site. We publish no predicted grades, no success rates, no student statistics and no borrowed credentials. Every AED figure on this page belongs to another provider and carries its reading date.

sections.heading: Integrity, invigilation and the question that filters this market
paragraphs: Evidence-led preparation has an integrity benefit that is worth stating. A marked script produced under observed conditions is unambiguously the student's own work, which is more than can be said for an unsupervised practice response emailed in at midnight. For on-screen subjects that means the whole evidence trail is clean by construction. For the moderated portfolio subjects, the boundary is harder and we draw it in the only place that holds: we do not look at submitted work.

This region gives that boundary real weight. Services in the Gulf advertise finished Internal Assessments at fixed prices, with one identified during our research selling completed work at AED 3,750. Buying assessed work is a malpractice matter under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the seller. Dubai families do not need a lecture about this. They need a filter, and one question does most of the work: ask whether the provider will work on the portfolio your child will submit. The right answer is no, followed by an explanation of what they do instead.

The related regulatory fact is worth having straight because it comes up in sales conversations. Private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. A parent can reasonably ask any tutor whether they hold the permit.

sections.heading: Stopping on the evidence, and the regulator context behind it all
paragraphs: Blocks should end. The evidence makes that judgement easy: when completion is consistent, the timing split is even, the comments have moved on from week one's problems and the remaining gap is subject understanding rather than technique, the block has done what a block can do. Continuing past that point buys reassurance at specialist hourly rates, and in Dubai those rates start at AED 200 per hour for IB support according to Unitors' own published figures and rise from there.

There is one short extension worth taking. Students continuing into the Diploma benefit from a summer measurement rather than a summer course: one timed handwritten paper, marked, purely to see whether the hand gives out before the argument does. After two years of typing it usually does, and discovering that in August is far cheaper than discovering it in a November DP1 mock. Two sessions covers it.

For completeness, the regulator picture that sits behind all of this. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, per the UAE government's own information service; Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. Naming a regulator is context; implying it endorses a tutoring platform would be a misrepresentation.

process.title: Check the entry pattern before anything else
process.description: Ask the school whether it registers candidates for eAssessment, whether that is for the certificate or individual results, and which subject groups your child is entered in. Many Dubai schools move the cohort to International GCSE at Year 10, in which case the evidence worth collecting is entirely different.

process.title: Free 45-minute first lesson that produces a script
process.description: No card details, no obligation. For an on-screen subject the lesson includes a short timed response marked aloud against the criterion descriptors, so the diagnosis comes from your child's own writing rather than from a conversation about confidence in tests.

process.title: Take the baseline mock before any teaching
process.description: Week one, full conditions, remotely invigilated. Parents sometimes want to teach first. Measuring first is what makes everything afterwards legible: completion count, timing split, answer shape and criterion marks per task, all dated and filed for comparison.

process.title: Agree what movement means
process.description: Before the block starts we write down what would count as progress: all tasks attempted, the timing split within a stated range, judgement arriving in the opening third. We do not set a target criterion mark, because a tutor's mark is not a prediction and treating it as one is dishonest.

process.title: Marked script and one instruction every week
process.description: After each session the script, the criterion comments, the comparison with the previous attempt and a single narrow instruction arrive the same evening. Parents who read nothing else should read the instruction, because next week's script shows whether it was acted on.

process.title: Review at the mid-point mock, and be willing to stop
process.description: If comments have repeated unchanged across four scripts, we say so and name the likely reason rather than selling more hours. When the technique problems are closed we end the block, and offer only the two-session summer handwriting measurement for students heading into DP1.

whyPoints.title: Criterion comments instead of percentages
whyPoints.description: The paper is criterion-referenced, so a percentage throws away the information a parent needs. Our marking names the descriptor a sentence failed to satisfy, which tells a family what to do this week. Sixty-two per cent tells them nothing except how to feel about it.

whyPoints.title: Baseline first, teaching second
whyPoints.description: A measurement taken before any teaching is the only way to know what the teaching changed. It is the session families most often want to skip and the one that makes the next seven legible, because every later script is compared against it on the same task type.

whyPoints.title: Timing measured, not guessed
whyPoints.description: Most first mocks put half the two hours into the first task and under ten minutes into the last. That is invisible in a grade and obvious in a breakdown. It is also mechanical, which means it closes in one or two sessions rather than over a term.

whyPoints.title: Remote invigilation at a fraction of the cost
whyPoints.description: A tutor present on video and muted gives honest conditions without anyone travelling, and leaves a marked script rather than a verbal summary. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 per hour, per Bestimate's survey, which is a lot to pay for the same observation.

whyPoints.title: We report flat weeks as flat
whyPoints.description: A script that has not moved in four attempts is a fact, and we send it with a diagnosis rather than an encouragement. The three real causes are no work between sessions, an instruction too broad to act on, or a subject-understanding gap a block cannot close. All three are useful to know.

whyPoints.title: No predicted grades and no borrowed authority
whyPoints.description: A tutor's criterion mark is not a forecast. No regulator or examination board endorses IB Gram and we claim none. Every AED figure here belongs to another provider with its reading date, and UAE schools sit the session in May, which is as specific as we will be about IB dates.

faqs.question: We cannot manage two uninterrupted hours at home - can we still get a baseline?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better than skipping the measurement. A properly conducted forty-minute timed task produces usable criterion evidence and a partial timing reading, which is most of the diagnostic value. What it will not show is stamina or end-of-paper collapse, so we would try to find one full two-hour slot during a school holiday for the mid-point reading. In compact flats with younger siblings, which is common in areas like International City and Al Nahda, a shorter task done honestly beats a long one done with interruptions.

faqs.question: What does a marked on-screen script actually look like when it comes back?
faqs.answer: The response with comments attached to specific sentences, each naming the criterion descriptor that sentence does or does not satisfy. Alongside it, a timing breakdown by task, a completion count, and the criterion marks from the previous attempt on the same task type for comparison. There is no percentage, deliberately. Finally one instruction, narrow enough that next week's script shows whether it was followed: not improve your evaluation, but put your first judgement in the opening third of every answer.

faqs.question: The school gave a percentage for the mock - why will you not give me one?
faqs.answer: Because the examination is criterion-referenced and a percentage is a translation that discards the useful part. Two students on the same percentage can have completely different problems: one wrote well and finished half the paper, the other finished everything in the wrong answer shape. The remedies are opposite. Schools report percentages because parents expect them and because reporting systems demand a number, and the criterion comments usually exist underneath. Ask the subject teacher for those rather than for the number.

faqs.question: What does a normal timing split across the two hours look like?
faqs.answer: Roughly proportional to the weight of each task, which in practice means no single task consuming more than about a third of the time unless it is explicitly the long one. The pattern in a typical first mock is nothing like that: half or more on task one and under ten minutes on the last. Our analysis lists minutes spent against minutes deserved, task by task. Families find it the single most legible document in the whole block, because it needs no knowledge of the subject to read.

faqs.question: My son's criterion marks rose but the school's report grade did not - which should I believe?
faqs.answer: Believe the school's grade as a grade and ours as a measurement of technique. A tutor's criterion mark is not standardised, not on the live paper and not a prediction, and we do not offer it as one. What our scripts can honestly show is that a descriptor never addressed in January is addressed consistently in April. School grades also lag, because a report written in March draws on work from February. If the scripts are improving and the grade is flat two reports running, that is worth raising with the subject teacher.

faqs.question: How many mocks is too many for one subject?
faqs.answer: Three in an eight-week block is our pattern, plus whatever the school runs. Beyond four or five the returns fall away sharply, because a mock measures rather than teaches, and the time is better spent on short timed tasks aimed at one descriptor. The exception is a candidate whose problem is stamina or collapse in the final twenty minutes, where full-length rehearsal is the treatment rather than the measurement. Families buying weekly two-hour mocks are usually paying for diagnosis they already have.

faqs.question: Do you mark the script or does my child self-assess it?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order reversed. The student marks their own response against the descriptors first, aloud, while the tutor asks which words in the paragraph satisfy the descriptor. Then the tutor marks it and the two are compared. The gap between the two marks is itself diagnostic: a student who consistently over-rates their own work has not internalised the standard, and that is the thing to fix before anything else. The written script that reaches the parent carries the tutor's marking.

faqs.question: If you will not look at my daughter's design portfolio, what evidence is there at all?
faqs.answer: Parallel evidence, which is real but separate. If the gap is evaluating against a specification, we take a completely different brief, read the criterion descriptor, and she writes an evaluation on that. It gets marked. Four weeks later she writes another on a third brief and the two are compared. The skill is measurably improving even though her submitted portfolio has never been in the room. She then applies the skill to her own work alone, which is the only version that survives external moderation.

faqs.question: Could a visiting tutor in Dubai invigilate a mock better than someone on video?
faqs.answer: Marginally, and for one type of student decisively: the fifteen-year-old who will not begin unless an adult is physically present. That is a genuine advantage and worth paying for if it describes your child. For everyone else, a tutor present on video and muted gives the same honesty about conditions, leaves a marked script rather than a doorstep summary, and costs a fraction of the AED 180 to 350 per hour that Bestimate's Dubai survey reports for in-home sessions. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: What should I ask for after four sessions, before paying for more?
faqs.answer: Four things, all cheap for an honest provider to supply. The four marked scripts in date order. The criterion comments on each, so you can see whether they address the same problem four times or different problems. The timing breakdowns, which should be converging on an even split. And the instruction set at the end of each session, with whether it was acted on. If the comments repeat unchanged across all four, more sessions of the same kind will not help and a competent provider will say so first.

faqs.question: How do you measure typing speed, and what counts as fast enough?
faqs.answer: We time a short response in the first session and count words produced rather than keystrokes, because thinking pauses are part of the real task. Fast enough means the student finishes every task in a full mock without visibly truncating an argument. The fix, where needed, is fifteen minutes of daily practice outside sessions across about six weeks, which moves most fifteen-year-olds from hunting for keys to adequate fluency. It is a constraint worth knowing about in January rather than meeting in May.

faqs.question: Is one marked mock really worth more than four hours of revision?
faqs.answer: For a student whose subject work is reasonable, almost always. Front-loaded timing, bullet-point answers, transcribed stimulus, and the interdisciplinary seam are invisible without a script and obvious with one, and each is a habit that closes in one or two sessions. Four hours of revision aimed at the wrong constraint changes nothing and costs more. At published Dubai specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 per hour, per Bestimate's survey, the arithmetic is not close.

faqs.question: The pre-session mock went badly three weeks out - what do we do now?
faqs.answer: Read the timing breakdown before concluding anything, because a bad mock three weeks out is often a tired mock. If the collapse is in the final twenty minutes, retest when rested before changing the plan. If completion and answer shape have genuinely regressed, narrow hard: one subject group, one descriptor, short timed tasks only, no new content. Three weeks is enough to recover a mechanical problem and not enough to build subject understanding, so spending it on content revision is the wrong choice.

faqs.question: Do you send the evidence to my child's school?
faqs.answer: Not unless you choose to. The documents are yours: marked scripts, criterion comments, timing breakdowns, session notes. Some Dubai families take a timing analysis to a subject teacher and find it genuinely welcomed, because teachers rarely have time to produce one per student. We do not contact the school ourselves, because the school owns the assessment relationship and a tutor inserting themselves into it helps nobody, least of all the student.

faqs.question: What does the free first lesson leave us with if we do not continue?
faqs.answer: A marked timed response and a written diagnosis you keep: the descriptor most often missed, the timing pattern visible in that response, and the single change most likely to move the result. No card details are taken and nothing follows automatically. A reasonable number of Dubai families take that document, work on it with their child and the subject teacher, and never book a paid session. We would rather be useful once than sell a block that was not needed.

faqs.question: Our school moved to International GCSE at Year 10 - is any of this relevant?
faqs.answer: The evidence discipline is, the format is not. For Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE the equivalent trail is marked past papers against the published mark scheme, with the syllabus code on the front and a question-by-question mark breakdown. That is easier to build than an on-screen trail because the material exists publicly. What transfers directly is the habit: measure before teaching, mark against the published standard rather than an impression, and compare dated attempts on the same question type.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-home-tutor.closingHeading: Measure first, then decide what to buy
dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up providers for your child's on-screen papers, ask each one what arrives after a session and whether they will take a baseline before teaching anything. The answers separate them quickly. Our free 45-minute first lesson produces a marked timed response and a written diagnosis, taken with no card details and no obligation, and plenty of Dubai families act on that document alone. Lessons run one-to-one on live video across the UAE, timed to Gulf Standard Time, on the keyboard your child will sit the real paper on.

intro.heading: Why the price of this particular preparation behaves differently
paragraphs: The MYP eAssessment is not a set of subject exams with a syllabus to finish. It is an externally assessed route to the IB MYP Certificate, built from on-screen examinations, teacher-assessed ePortfolios, the Personal Project and the service-as-action requirement. The on-screen examinations run for two hours and are task-based: a student is given unfamiliar stimulus material and asked to do something with it, applying conceptual understanding and the Approaches to Learning skills rather than reciting content. That single fact changes what tutoring is worth and therefore what it should cost.

Content cramming is poor value here. A tutor working at AED 250 an hour on memorised definitions is being paid to prepare a student for the wrong exam. The same money spent on handling unseen stimulus, reading command terms accurately, structuring a response under a clock and practising the on-screen interface converts into marks. Families who understand the distinction tend to buy fewer hours and get more out of them, which is the honest version of value in this market.

Dubai prices follow the shape of the wider tutoring market rather than anything MYP-specific. Published figures run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialist work, with a premium named tier reaching AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits of two hours. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider that published it, not to IB Gram.

What moves the number in this emirate specifically is worth naming, because it is not the emirate's cost of living. It is the component, the proximity of the examination window, whether the tutor marks work between sessions, whether the subject group is thinly covered, and whether you are paying for travel. The last of those is the largest single swing, which is why the in-home line in every published rate table sits above the online line by a wide margin.

Delivery here is online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service, and for an assessment sat on a computer that is more than a convenience. A student practising an on-screen examination wants to practise on a screen, with the tutor watching how they move through tasks, which is closer to the real thing than a kitchen table with a printed paper on it.

The rest of this page is organised the way a parent actually decides. First what the assessment is and which components your child may be registered for, because that governs everything. Then the market priced by the month rather than by the hour, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. Then the five things that genuinely move a Dubai quote, the difference between buying examination technique and buying portfolio support, where marks go on a two-hour task-based paper, and a cost-in-context table setting a term of preparation beside the emirate's school fee position.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.programmesIntro: Pricing a term of preparation sensibly means knowing which stage your child is at and what the next one demands, because the cost of catching up later is almost always higher than the cost of preparing now.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years 1 to 4
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed internally against four criteria marked zero to eight. No external component, so families often buy no tutoring at all during these years. The risk is that criterion-based writing and command-term accuracy are never drilled, and both arrive as a bill in year five.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools admit heavily into the MYP from British and Indian curricula at Years 7 and 9, and a student who arrives in Year 10 has had one year of criterion marking rather than four. That is the single most common reason a Dubai family finds themselves buying a concentrated and expensive block in year five.

programmes.name: MYP year five and the eAssessment
programmes.description: The externally assessed year. On-screen examinations in groups such as language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics and interdisciplinary learning; ePortfolios in language acquisition, arts, physical and health education and design; plus the Personal Project and service as action. Grades run one to seven per result.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai MYP school enters students for the certificate, and some enter for selected components only. Ask the coordinator which components your child is registered for before buying anything, because paying for preparation in a component the school is not entering is the most expensive mistake available here.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades one to seven per subject and up to three core points, to a forty-five point maximum. The Diploma rewards precisely the skills an on-screen examination tests, which is why year five preparation has value beyond the certificate.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is the destination for most MYP students who stay in the IB, and specialist Diploma tutoring is the most expensive tier in the published market at AED 200 to 450 and above. Money spent on examination technique in year five reduces the hours needed at a higher rate two years later.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.subjectsIntro: Price varies by component rather than by difficulty, so the grid below is organised by what each subject group is actually assessed with and the kind of session that earns its fee there.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A two-hour task-based paper built on unseen texts. Preparation that pays is timed response structure and precise handling of the command terms; preparation that does not is reading more set texts, since the stimulus is unfamiliar by design.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Integrated rather than split into history and geography, which unsettles students taught in separate blocks. Source handling, data interpretation and argument structure are the chargeable skills. Content revision has the lowest return of any component.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics in one task-based paper, often with data to interpret and a method to critique. Sessions are worth their rate when spent on reading graphs under time pressure and writing conclusions that reference the evidence given.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Standard and extended routes differ in content and in expected depth. The marks move on interpreting an unfamiliar context into mathematics and showing method on screen, which is a different discipline from the paper-based working students are used to.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: The component nobody prepares for and the one most likely to need paid help, because it is not owned by a single teacher. Students are asked to integrate two disciplines on unfamiliar stimulus. Two or three focused sessions usually cover it.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed by the teacher against criteria and moderated externally, with phases rather than year groups. Tutoring here is process work on drafting and on oral task preparation, and a tutor may never produce any part of the submitted portfolio.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Visual art, music, drama and film, assessed on process and reflection as much as outcome. The cost-effective session is a criterion audit of what the student has already made, rather than a weekly hour across a whole year.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Planning, performance and reflection components documented over time. Families rarely budget for this and often need one or two sessions on the written reflection, which is where the criteria concentrate and where marks are commonly left behind.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiry, development, creation and evaluation, documented as a cycle. Design students usually need help only on the evaluation criterion, which makes it one of the cheapest components to support properly.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.regionsIntro: Location changes the price of tutoring in Dubai mainly through travel, which is why the in-home line in every published rate table sits well above the online one. The notes below are about scheduling and supply rather than about any area paying a premium.

regions.note: Villa communities feeding full-continuum IB schools. In-home quotes here tend towards the upper end of the published AED 180 to 500 band because of distance between gates, not because of the subject.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: A long commute from the main school cluster, so a 16:00 session is unrealistic and evening in-home slots carry the heaviest travel cost. The eastern suburbs are where the online price advantage is widest.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown
regions.note: Central apartments with short school runs and tight study space. Two shorter sessions often work better than one long block here, and on an hourly rate that changes the monthly figure.

sections.heading: What the eAssessment is, and why it changes the value of an hour
paragraphs: The MYP eAssessment is the external route to the IB MYP Certificate at the end of year five. It is built from on-screen examinations in subject groups such as language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics and interdisciplinary learning; from ePortfolios in language acquisition, arts, physical and health education and design; from the Personal Project, which is externally moderated; and from the service-as-action requirement. Results are reported as grades from one to seven.

Two features of the on-screen examinations change what a tutoring hour is worth. The first is that they are two hours long and task-based: the student meets unfamiliar stimulus material and is asked to apply conceptual understanding and Approaches to Learning skills to it. The second is that they are sat on a computer, with the interface, the typing and the on-screen navigation forming part of the experience. Neither rewards memorised content, and a tutor selling content revision for this component is selling the wrong product at the right price.

That is also why the honest answer to how many hours a family needs is often lower than they expect. A student with secure subject knowledge and no examination technique can improve substantially in a short technique-led block, and a tutor who says so is giving up revenue. Any provider quoting a year-long plan before looking at a piece of the student's work is quoting the plan rather than the problem.

One warning on certificate requirements. The number of components a student must sit, and the points total the certificate requires, are set by the IB and applied by your school, and no figure for either is published on this page because none has been verified from an official source for it. Ask your MYP coordinator for the current requirements in writing. A page that invents a threshold for you is a page you cannot check.

sections.heading: What MYP eAssessment preparation costs in Dubai, by the month
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutors quote and monthly totals are how families actually decide, so this section runs on monthly figures. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 at mid tier, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those three bands cover most of what a Dubai family will be quoted for this preparation.

Packages in the market price differently again. An online package advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions works out below the mid-tier hourly equivalent, which usually means shorter sessions, no marking between them, or a less specialised tutor. An in-home monthly package of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits prices travel into every visit. Neither is wrong; both need reading against what the hour contains.

The underlying hourly bands are worth stating once so the monthly figures can be checked. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for an IB specialist. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's premium named tier reaches AED 650. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, with independent tutors quoted up to AED 500.

IB Gram does not appear in that table, and deliberately so. Our own rate is quoted after the free trial lesson, with the session length and whether marking is included stated in writing. Publishing a headline figure without those two details is how the market ends up with quotes that look comparable and are not.

sections.heading: What actually moves the number in this emirate
paragraphs: Travel is the largest single driver and the easiest to remove. Every published Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one above online one-to-one, and the gap is travel time rather than teaching quality. For a family in Mirdif or Dubai Hills, where the drive from the school cluster is long, that premium is at its widest. Removing it does not reduce the teaching; it reduces the mileage, and the saved budget buys either more hours or a more specialised tutor.

The component matters next. An ePortfolio evaluation criterion is a two-session job. A set of on-screen examinations with no technique in place is a term. Pricing those identically is how families end up on a year plan for a problem that needed a fortnight, so insist on a diagnosis from a real piece of work before agreeing a length.

Proximity to the examination window raises prices through scarcity rather than through any published increase: the tutors who know the component are booked, and what is left is whoever is free. Booking the block before the window opens is the one decision that reliably lowers the price a family pays, and it costs nothing to make early.

Two smaller drivers are worth checking in any quote. Whether the tutor marks work between sessions, because that time is real and a rate excluding it is not comparable with one including it. And whether the subject group is thinly covered, since a scarce combination such as integrated sciences at extended level with an interdisciplinary component attracts a specialist rate. The table sets out each driver with what a parent can actually do about it.

sections.heading: On-screen examinations and ePortfolios are two different purchases
paragraphs: Treating these as one product is the main reason families overpay. An on-screen examination is externally set and externally marked, sat under timing in a fixed window, and prepared for through repeated practice on unfamiliar material. An ePortfolio is assessed by the student's own teacher against criteria and then moderated externally by the IB, built over months from the student's own work.

The tutoring that helps differs accordingly, and so does the honest limit on it. For an on-screen examination a tutor can set tasks, mark them, drill command terms and rehearse the interface, with no boundary problem at all. For an ePortfolio the tutor is working alongside a teacher-assessed submission, which means explaining criteria, questioning a plan and commenting on a draft, and never producing any part of the portfolio. A provider offering to prepare portfolio material for submission is offering malpractice.

That difference shows up in the cost. Examination technique is sold by the hour and benefits from repetition, so it is the component that justifies a weekly commitment. Portfolio work is diagnostic and episodic: a criterion audit, a conversation about evidence, a draft read. Most families need two or three portfolio sessions in total and are quoted for twelve.

sections.heading: Where marks go on a two-hour on-screen examination
paragraphs: The first loss is misreading the task. Task-based papers use command wording precisely, and a student who identifies when asked to evaluate, or who describes when asked to justify, has written a competent answer to a question nobody set. This is trainable in a handful of sessions and it is the highest-return work available for the money, because the content knowledge is usually already there.

The second loss is time. Two hours across a task-based paper means the final task is routinely rushed or abandoned, and the final task is often the one carrying the most conceptual weight. Students who have never sat a full paper under timing do not discover this until the day. Three full rehearsals, marked and reviewed, change the distribution of marks across the paper more than any amount of topic revision.

The third loss is the stimulus itself. Unfamiliar material is the design of the assessment rather than an accident, and a student who expects to recognise the content freezes when they do not. The habit to build is mechanical: read the stimulus for what kind of thing it is, note what it allows you to claim, then answer the task using it. Practised on five different stimulus sets, that habit holds on the sixth.

The fourth loss is the screen. Typing speed, moving between tasks, keeping working visible for a mathematics response, and resisting the urge to write long where short is wanted are all specific to an on-screen format. Printed past papers do not train any of them, which is one practical argument for preparing online rather than at a table with a pen.

sections.heading: The ePortfolio boundary, and why it protects your money as well as your child
paragraphs: An ePortfolio is assessed by the student's own teacher against published criteria and then moderated externally by the IB. The work in it must be the student's. A tutor may explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, question whether a piece of evidence actually shows what the student claims, and comment on a draft by naming the criterion and the band. A tutor may not write, rewrite, produce or polish material for submission.

This is a financial point as well as an ethical one. A provider willing to produce portfolio content is charging for work that, if detected, costs the student the qualification rather than costing the provider anything. One site competing for UAE coursework searches advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed fee. A family buying that is paying for a risk transfer that runs entirely in the wrong direction.

Stated plainly, the boundary also makes the sessions cheaper. Explaining a criterion and auditing evidence takes two or three sessions. Shadow-writing a portfolio takes many more and produces a student who still cannot read a descriptor, which is the skill the Diploma will demand two years later at a specialist hourly rate.

Written comments left in the student's own document are the practical form this takes. They are evidence of honest support if the school asks, they can be shown to the teacher assessing the work, and they survive the session in a way a verbal conversation does not. That is worth asking for in any quote, whoever you buy from.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai school fees and what a term actually represents
paragraphs: A tutoring quote means little without something to measure it against, and Dubai gives a useful anchor. The KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. A family that budgeted for a fee rise and did not get one has, in effect, found the cost of a term of preparation.

The scale of the sector explains why the tutoring market is as varied as it is. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK programmes at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent.

Those figures carry two implications for a parent pricing this preparation. IB families are a minority of a very large market, so general tutoring supply is deep and IB-specific supply is thin, which is why the specialist band sits where it does. And three new IB schools entering the market increases demand for MYP-trained tutors before it increases the supply of them, which argues for booking early rather than waiting.
