sections.heading: Buying this honestly, including what happens when we cannot help
paragraphs: The sequence that keeps the cost down is unglamorous. Confirm with the school which components your child is registered for and when the window falls. Send one piece of the student's own work in the heaviest component. Take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue. Ask for a diagnosis and a proposed number of sessions with an end date, in writing. Then decide. Any step skipped tends to be paid for in extra hours later.

A diagnosis should name a component, a specific weakness and a number. Command-term accuracy in integrated sciences, four sessions, with a rehearsal paper at session two and session four is a plan you can hold somebody to. General support for MYP in the run-up to eAssessment is not a plan and cannot be priced sensibly, because nothing in it can be judged complete.

Some combinations are thinly covered at any given moment. Integrated sciences at extended level, less common language acquisition phases, and the interdisciplinary component are the usual gaps. Where no specialist is free, the honest options are a named date when one is, an adjacent component a current tutor can teach well, or being told plainly that we cannot help with this one. Taking a booking for a component nobody on the platform teaches properly costs a family the term that mattered.

Every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider or source that published it, and none of them is an IB Gram price. No success rate, average grade or satisfaction figure appears anywhere on this page, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method. And no tutor can promise a grade on an externally marked on-screen examination, whatever the rate.

process.title: Confirm the registration before you spend anything
process.description: Ask the MYP coordinator which components your child is entered for, whether the school is seeking the certificate, and when the examination window falls. Dubai schools enter different mixes. Paying for preparation in a component the school is not entering is the most expensive error available in this market, and one email prevents it.

process.title: Send one piece of real work
process.description: A past task, a timed attempt, a portfolio draft, anything the student produced themselves. A tutor reading one real piece can name the weakness and estimate the hours. A tutor quoting without seeing any work is quoting a plan rather than a problem, and that plan is always longer than the problem.

process.title: A free trial lesson, then a written diagnosis
process.description: The trial is a real session with the tutor who would continue, with no card details taken beforehand. It ends with a short written note: the component, the specific weakness, the proposed number of sessions and an end date. You keep that note and can compare it with any other quote you hold.

process.title: Marked tasks, recorded marks, honest stopping point
process.description: Each session sets a task that is marked and returned rather than discussed. Raw marks are recorded so improvement is visible and so the block can be cut short when the problem is solved. A provider who never proposes stopping is being paid for attendance rather than for progress.

whyPoints.title: Priced by component, not by calendar
whyPoints.description: A portfolio evaluation criterion is a two-session job and a set of on-screen examinations with no technique is a term. Quoting both as a year plan is how families overspend here, so the diagnosis names a component and a number of sessions with an end date.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, none of them ours
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page belong to EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED, each named beside its figure. IB Gram quotes its own rate after the trial, with session length and marking stated, because a bare hourly number cannot be compared.

whyPoints.title: Online because the assessment is on a screen
whyPoints.description: An on-screen examination rewards practice on a screen: navigation, typing, keeping method visible, resisting long answers where short ones score. Printed past papers train none of that. No home visits are offered anywhere in the UAE, and for this component that is an advantage rather than a limitation.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on portfolio work
whyPoints.description: A tutor will explain criteria, question evidence and comment on drafts, and will write no part of an ePortfolio or a Personal Project. Stating that before you book protects the student's qualification, and it also keeps the number of sessions honest.

whyPoints.title: No invented certificate thresholds
whyPoints.description: No points total or component count for the MYP certificate is published here, because none was verified from an official source for this page. Your coordinator can give you the current requirements in writing, which is better than a figure on a tutoring site that nobody can check.

faqs.question: Is the MYP eAssessment compulsory for my child at a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: No. The eAssessment is the optional external route to the IB MYP Certificate, and Dubai schools make different choices about it. Some enter students for the full set of components, some for a selection, and some do not enter at all while still teaching the MYP. Your coordinator can confirm what your child is registered for and when the examination window falls. Ask before buying any preparation, because paying for a component the school is not entering is the single most expensive mistake available in this market.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an on-screen examination and an ePortfolio?
faqs.answer: An on-screen examination is set and marked externally by the IB, sat on a computer under timing in a fixed window, and built on unfamiliar stimulus material rather than recall. An ePortfolio is a collection of the student's own work assessed by their teacher against criteria and then moderated externally. The preparation differs completely: examinations reward repeated timed practice, while portfolios need a criterion audit and draft comments. So does the cost, because the first justifies a weekly commitment and the second usually takes two or three sessions.

faqs.question: What does a term of this preparation cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 at mid tier, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits. Those are the providers' own published figures. Ask any quote whether marking between sessions is included, because that is where comparable-looking rates diverge.

faqs.question: Why is an on-screen examination harder to revise for than an IGCSE paper?
faqs.answer: Because there is less to memorise and more to do. The paper is task-based, runs two hours, and hands the student unfamiliar stimulus material they are expected to work with rather than recognise. A student who has revised content thoroughly can still score poorly by misreading a command term, running out of time on the final task, or freezing because the material is unfamiliar. The preparation that works is repeated timed practice on different stimulus sets, marked and reworked, which is a different purchase from topic revision.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the ePortfolio my child's own teacher is assessing?
faqs.answer: Within a clear limit, yes. A tutor can explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, question whether a piece of evidence shows what the student claims it shows, and comment on a draft by naming the criterion and the band it currently sits in. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or produce any portfolio material. The work is assessed by the teacher and moderated by the IB, and submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice, with the consequence falling on the student rather than on whoever was paid.

faqs.question: How many components does the IB MYP Certificate require?
faqs.answer: The IB sets the number of required results and the points threshold, and your school applies them. No figure for either is published on this page, because none was verified from an official source for it, and an unsourced threshold on a tutoring site is exactly the sort of number families act on and should not. Ask your MYP coordinator for the current requirements in writing. Knowing the threshold matters for budgeting: it tells you which components carry weight and therefore where preparation money is worth spending.

faqs.question: Does the eAssessment matter if my child is staying for the IB Diploma anyway?
faqs.answer: The certificate itself may matter less if the student continues in the same school, but the skills transfer directly. On-screen examinations test conceptual application, unfamiliar stimulus handling and timed structure, which is what Diploma papers test at a higher level. Specialist Diploma tutoring is the most expensive published tier in Dubai at AED 200 to 450 and above, so technique built in year five reduces the hours needed later at a higher rate. Ask the school how it uses eAssessment results in Diploma course counselling, because practice varies.

faqs.question: Is this preparation cheaper than IGCSE tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Per hour, no. Published rates do not distinguish by programme in a meaningful way, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 an hour. Per plan, it is often cheaper, because the useful work is technique rather than syllabus coverage and therefore shorter. An IGCSE year plan typically runs weekly across two terms; an on-screen examination block is ten to twelve weeks and a portfolio audit is two or three sessions. The total is what matters, and it is worth asking for both figures.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to our apartment in Business Bay or Downtown for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For this preparation the online format is the better match rather than a compromise. The on-screen examination is sat on a computer, so practising on one is practising the real thing, and the tutor can watch how the student navigates tasks and manages time. It also removes the travel premium that sits between the published online and in-home rate bands.

faqs.question: Does starting earlier reduce what we spend overall?
faqs.answer: Usually, for two reasons that have nothing to do with discounts. Scarcity near the examination window means the tutors who know the components are booked and what remains is whoever is free, often at a specialist rate. And a student who has been shown criterion-based writing in Year 9 or 10 needs a shorter block in year five than one meeting it for the first time. The practical advice is to book the block before the window opens and to keep it short and specific rather than long and general.

faqs.question: Does the interdisciplinary on-screen examination need its own sessions?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is the component families most reliably forget to budget for. It is not owned by a single subject teacher, so nobody at school is revising it in the way a science teacher revises science. Students are asked to integrate two disciplines on unfamiliar stimulus, which is a technique rather than a body of content. Two or three sessions on how to make an integrated claim and support it from both disciplines covers most of what is needed, which makes it one of the cheapest components to fix properly.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees going up, and how does tutoring compare with a fee rise?
faqs.answer: The KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a family that had budgeted for an increase, that is roughly the cost of a term of mid-tier weekly tutoring at AED 600 to 1,200 a month. It is a useful way to size the decision, though a component block of three to five sessions is a far smaller commitment.

faqs.question: How does service as action fit into the certificate requirements?
faqs.answer: It is a requirement recorded and confirmed by the school rather than an assessed component, so no tutoring is needed for it and nobody should sell you any. The only practical point is that the record has to exist and be complete, and students who leave it until the final term create an administrative problem in the middle of their examination preparation. Check with the coordinator that your child's record is up to date early in year five, which costs nothing and removes one avoidable distraction from the examination window.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers the subject group we need?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. Integrated sciences at extended level, less common language acquisition phases and the interdisciplinary component are the combinations most often thin at a given moment. The honest options are a named date when a specialist is free, a start on an adjacent component that a current tutor teaches well, or being told plainly that we cannot help with this one. Accepting a booking for a component nobody teaches properly costs a family the weeks that mattered, which is worse than an inconvenient answer.

faqs.question: Does the quoted rate include marking between sessions or only the live hour?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, because the answer differs across the market and it is the line item that makes two similar-looking rates incomparable. Setting a task, marking it against criteria and writing usable comments takes real time outside the lesson, and a rate that excludes it either does not include the marking or absorbs it invisibly. For this preparation the marked task is the product, since improvement on an on-screen examination comes from reworking marked attempts rather than from discussion. IB Gram states the inclusion when it quotes.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.closingHeading: Price the component, not the calendar
dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.closingBody: Before you compare quotes, do two things that cost nothing. Ask your MYP coordinator which components your child is registered for and when the window falls, then send one piece of the student's own work in the heaviest of them. With those in hand a tutor can name the weakness and a number of sessions with an end date, which is a quote you can judge. Take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would continue, ask whether marking between sessions is included, and keep the block short and specific. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider that published it, so you can check all of it yourself.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below prepare MYP 5 candidates for on-screen examinations and ePortfolio moderation. Each works from the published criterion descriptors and the command terms, because an on-screen paper rewards a different answer shape from the extended essays most Dubai students have been writing all year.

intro.heading: An examination your child sits on a keyboard, against material they have never seen
paragraphs: MYP eAssessment is the optional external assessment at the end of the Middle Years Programme, and it is the least understood examination in Dubai. Parents who sat O Levels, IGCSEs or a national board curriculum have a mental model of an examination hall, a printed paper and a pen. An MYP on-screen examination is two hours at a computer, where the questions arrive bundled with stimulus material the candidate opens for the first time in the room: a short film, an audio clip, a data set, a photograph, a text extract. There is no syllabus content list to revise in the conventional sense. The candidate is marked on what they do with the material in front of them.

That is the first thing an IB MYP eAssessment tutor in Dubai has to fix, and it is a thinking problem rather than a content problem. A student who has spent five years writing coursework to a deadline, with time to redraft and a teacher to ask, now has 120 minutes, no redrafting and no help. The criteria have not changed; each subject group is still marked on four criteria from 0 to 8. What has changed is that every criterion has to be hit inside a timed response, from cold, in writing the candidate types rather than hands over.

The second thing to establish is whether your child's school uses eAssessment at all, because in Dubai many do not. The emirate had 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes a minority of the roll according to the Dubai Media Office. Plenty of schools run the Middle Years Programme to Year 9 and then switch their cohort to Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for Years 10 and 11, in which case there is no eAssessment and no MYP certificate. Others run the full five years and register candidates for the May session. Both are legitimate and the difference changes everything about what preparation means.

Where a school does register candidates, the assessment splits two ways. Some subject groups are examined on screen: language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and the interdisciplinary examination that most candidates also sit. Others are submitted as an ePortfolio of the student's own work, marked by the school's teachers and moderated externally by the IB: language acquisition, arts, design, and physical and health education. Those two routes need completely different preparation, and families regularly buy the wrong one because nobody explained the split.

The rest of this page is the detail: the subject-group split, what the two hours actually look like, the errors that cost Dubai candidates marks, the certificate arithmetic, the May session counted backwards from a Dubai school year, and the honest boundary on ePortfolio support, which is coursework and therefore the student's own. Lessons are delivered one-to-one on live video across the UAE. Every IB figure here should be confirmed against your school's current documentation, because the programme's procedures are revised and your MYP coordinator holds the live version.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.programmesIntro: eAssessment sits at one end of a five-year programme and in front of a two-year one. These are the stages IB Gram covers for Dubai families, with what each contributes to an on-screen result.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 10
programmes.description: The year the examination skills either get built or do not. Subject teachers are already marking against four criteria, mathematics has split into standard and extended routes, and ePortfolio material for the moderated subject groups often starts being generated here. A student who has never answered a criterion question under time pressure by the end of Year 10 will meet that experience for the first time in a mock.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools running the full programme usually start formal on-screen practice in Year 10, often on the school's own devices. Ask which platform and which device the school will use in the live session, because practising on a different keyboard layout is a small but real disadvantage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Year 11
programmes.description: Examination year. On-screen papers in the May session, ePortfolios locked and submitted earlier, and the personal project running alongside both. The workload shape is unusual: the ePortfolio deadlines and the project deadline often land in the same winter term, leaving the spring free for on-screen practice.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Dubai problem in MYP 5 is sequencing. Families who treat the project, the ePortfolios and the on-screen papers as one undifferentiated mass of work tend to under-prepare the on-screen component, because it is the only one with no deadline until the session itself.

programmes.name: MYP eAssessment and the certificate
programmes.description: Externally validated results across required subject groups, combining on-screen examinations and externally moderated ePortfolios, plus the personal project and service as action. The IB sets a points total and a minimum grade for the certificate; confirm the current figures with your school's coordinator rather than with any tutoring site.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai school that registers candidates will handle entries, the platform and the room. What families control is preparation and the device practice. What nobody controls is the stimulus material, which is the point of the format.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with examinations at the end of two years, internal assessment in every subject, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Diploma papers are still largely handwritten, so the on-screen habit is not directly transferable; the criterion-reading and command-term habits very much are.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students moving from eAssessment into DP1 arrive with a genuine advantage in reading command terms and an occasional disadvantage in handwriting stamina. Three hours of written papers after two years of typing is worth practising before the first Diploma mock.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.subjectsIntro: Which route a subject takes decides what preparation means. These are the subject groups we support for Dubai MYP 5 candidates, with the assessment form each one takes and where the difficulty sits.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: An unseen text or multimedia extract, analysed against the subject group's four criteria inside the time limit. The difficulty is structural: candidates who have written long coursework essays over weeks produce rambling openings and run out of time before the analysis that carries the marks.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Source-based tasks using stimulus material the candidate has not seen, requiring evaluation rather than recall. Dubai candidates lose marks here by summarising the sources accurately and never evaluating them, which satisfies no criterion fully.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Data interpretation, experimental design and scientific reasoning against provided material. Knowledge is tested in application, not recall, so revision that consists of memorising definitions is close to useless and candidates discover that in the room.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Problems set in context, with the extended route carrying additional content and more demanding reasoning. The route decision is made in Year 10 at most Dubai schools and matters for later Diploma mathematics, so it deserves a proper conversation rather than a default.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: The examination most candidates find strangest: material drawn from two disciplines, requiring an integrated response that explicitly uses both. Marks are lost by answering as though it were two separate subject questions placed side by side.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Built from the student's own work across the course, including listening, reading, speaking and writing in the target language at the appropriate phase. French, Spanish and Arabic as an additional language are the common Dubai combinations. Preparation means course performance, not examination technique.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle evidenced through the student's own project work: investigation, development of ideas, creating the solution, evaluation. Weak portfolios are nearly always weak on the evaluation stage, where candidates describe what they made instead of testing it against their own specification.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Visual art, music or drama evidenced through process as well as outcome. The recurring gap is documentation: a strong final piece with no record of the decisions that produced it cannot be marked for the criteria that ask about process.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Planning for performance, applying skills, reflecting and improving, evidenced across the course. Candidates who train seriously outside school often under-record, submitting achievement without the planning and reflection the criteria actually mark.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, per KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines, and sitting outside the MYP subject-group structure. They occupy timetable hours in the same year as eAssessment preparation, which families planning session times need to count.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities and the questions to ask your school about eAssessment
dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.regionsIntro: Whether a Dubai school registers candidates for eAssessment, switches to International GCSE at Year 10, or runs the programme without external validation varies school by school rather than area by area. These are the questions worth asking in each part of the emirate, and what tends to come up locally.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Al Barsha South
regions.note: A dense cluster of IB continuum provision, so families here are more likely to find a school that runs the full five years. Ask whether candidates are registered for the certificate or only for individual subject results, since schools make that choice separately.

regions.name: Mirdif and Uptown
regions.note: Continuum provision alongside strong British-curriculum alternatives, which makes the Year 10 route conversation live for many families. Ask what proportion of the current Year 11 sat on-screen papers, and whether the school runs a full mock session on the real platform.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Device and connectivity questions are easiest to answer here, where school IT provision is generally strong. The useful question is which device model the live session uses, because keyboard and screen size differences are small disadvantages worth removing in advance.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park and Green Community
regions.note: Longer travel for some families, which matters for a session timetable in the spring term. Ask whether after-school revision sessions are offered on site, since those plus one weekly online slot is usually enough preparation for a single on-screen subject.

regions.name: Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed provision with many families moving between systems mid-programme. If your child joined the Middle Years Programme in Year 9 or 10, ask specifically whether they have enough course material banked for the moderated ePortfolio subject groups.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Strong continuum intake with heavy extracurricular schedules. The question to ask is when the ePortfolio submission deadlines fall, because they frequently collide with the personal project deadline and with sporting commitments in the same winter weeks.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JLT and Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: High rates of mid-year arrival and departure. A candidate joining in MYP 5 may not be registrable for the certificate at all, depending on how much course evidence exists, so this is a question to ask before enrolment rather than after.

regions.name: Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Muhaisnah
regions.note: Dense school provision across several curricula, so sibling comparison is common and unhelpful: one child on an International GCSE track and one on eAssessment are preparing for genuinely different things. Ask for each child's own assessment calendar in writing.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai IB continuum schools
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in these communities are more often at schools running all five Middle Years years, which means on-screen practice and ePortfolio moderation are familiar to the staff and the calendar is established. Our work there tends to be subject-specific technique rather than explaining the format from scratch.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and southern Dubai
schoolClusters.note: A wider mix, including schools that move students into International GCSE at Year 10. Students we support from these areas sometimes need the route question answered first, because preparation for an on-screen criterion paper and preparation for a Cambridge written paper are not interchangeable.

sections.heading: What eAssessment is, and whether your Dubai school uses it at all
paragraphs: MYP eAssessment is the external validation available at the end of the Middle Years Programme. Candidates sit on-screen examinations in some subject groups and submit externally moderated ePortfolios in others, and together with the personal project and service as action those results can lead to the IB MYP certificate. It is optional for schools. The IB does not require a school running the programme to register anybody, which is why two Dubai families whose children are both described as doing the MYP can be in completely different situations.

So the first question is not how to prepare. It is whether there is anything to prepare for. Ask your child's MYP coordinator three things in writing: does the school register candidates for eAssessment, is it for the full certificate or for individual subject results, and which subject groups will your child be entered in. The answers determine whether your child faces two-hour on-screen papers in May, a set of moderated portfolios, both, or neither. Families who buy tutoring before asking those questions regularly buy preparation for the wrong format.

The common Dubai pattern worth knowing is the Year 10 switch. A number of schools here run the Middle Years Programme for Years 7 to 9 and then move the cohort onto Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for Years 10 and 11, taking the view that externally examined subject certificates travel better in this market. In those schools there is no eAssessment, no MYP certificate, and the relevant preparation is Cambridge or Edexcel syllabus work with its own entry deadlines. Neither route is better in the abstract. They are different, and knowing which one your child is on is free.
bullets: eAssessment is optional for schools; many Dubai schools do not use it
Ask whether registration is for the certificate or individual subject results
Ask which subject groups your child will be entered in
A Year 10 switch to International GCSE means a different calendar entirely
Registration and entries are handled by the school, not the family

sections.heading: The subject-group split: on-screen examination or externally moderated ePortfolio
paragraphs: The split is the single most useful thing a parent can learn about this component, because it determines what preparation even means. On-screen examination subjects are assessed in a timed sitting against unseen material, so technique, timing and command-term reading are the levers. ePortfolio subjects are assessed on work produced across the course and marked by the school's own teachers before external moderation, so there is no examination technique to teach and the lever is course performance across months.

Candidates typically sit a combination. A common shape is on-screen papers in language and literature, individuals and societies, mathematics and sciences, plus the interdisciplinary examination, with ePortfolios in language acquisition and whichever of arts, design or physical and health education the student takes. Your school will confirm the exact pattern, and it varies with the options the student has chosen in Year 10.

What families get wrong is buying weekly subject tutoring for an ePortfolio subject in the spring term. By then the portfolio is largely built and often already submitted, and the marks are a function of work done months earlier. The useful intervention for a moderated subject happens in Year 10 and the first half of Year 11, on documentation and evaluation habits. In the spring of MYP 5, the money belongs in on-screen technique, where six weeks genuinely changes a result. The reverse mistake is rarer but costlier: a family who assumes everything is coursework, does nothing about the on-screen papers all year, and discovers in the mock that their child has never written a criterion answer against a clock. If you take one thing from this section, take the entry pattern, in writing, with the route for each subject group named beside it.

sections.heading: Inside the two hours: what an on-screen examination is actually like
paragraphs: The candidate sits at a school computer with a secure examination application open. The paper arrives with its stimulus material embedded: short video, audio, images, data tables, text extracts. Some of it is interactive. The candidate reads, watches or listens, then types responses into fields on the same screen. There is no calculator hunting, no paper to shuffle and no one to ask. Two hours, and the clock is visible.

Three features of that environment catch students out. The first is navigation. Moving between stimulus and answer field consumes time that a printed paper does not, and candidates who have not practised on the platform lose minutes they never notice losing. The second is typing. A student who types at the speed of a fifteen-year-old who mostly writes by hand will produce a shorter answer than their thinking deserves, and no criterion gives credit for intention. The third is the temptation to copy. Stimulus text is right there, selectable, and transcribing it feels like answering. It is not; it satisfies no descriptor.

There is also a positive consequence worth telling students about, because it changes their attitude to revision. Since the material is provided, the examination cannot test recall of a content list. A candidate who has internalised the criteria and the command terms, and who can read a source quickly and critically, is well placed even on a topic they have not studied closely. That is genuinely different from the examinations their parents sat, and students who understand it stop wasting the spring term memorising.
bullets: Stimulus material is embedded, unseen, and sometimes interactive

sections.heading: Where Dubai candidates lose marks on an on-screen paper
paragraphs: The errors are consistent enough to list, and most of them are fixable in six weeks because they are habits rather than gaps in knowledge. The largest single loss is summarising instead of evaluating. A candidate reads three sources, describes each accurately and never says which is more reliable or what the combination suggests. Every criterion descriptor at the upper bands asks for judgement, and the answer contains none.

The second loss is command-term blindness. Analyse, evaluate, explain, describe, justify and compare each require a different answer shape, and the marks follow the shape rather than the content. A student who explains beautifully when asked to evaluate has written a good answer to a question that was not set. We isolate this deliberately: ten minutes a session, one command term, the same stimulus answered two different ways so the student feels the difference rather than being told about it.

The third and fourth are structural. Candidates spend thirty minutes on a long opening response and leave nine minutes for the last two tasks, which are often worth as much. And they answer the interdisciplinary paper as two separate subject answers placed one after the other, when the criteria explicitly ask for integration. Both show up immediately on a marked mock and neither is visible without one, which is why we would rather a family paid for one properly marked mock than for four hours of general revision. A fifth error deserves naming because it is invisible to students: answering in bullet points. Fragments read as efficient on a screen and satisfy almost no descriptor above the lower bands, since the criteria ask for reasoning that a list cannot carry.

sections.heading: The certificate arithmetic, and what happens if a result falls short
paragraphs: The MYP certificate is awarded on a combination of results rather than on a single examination. Candidates need validated results across the required subject groups, including the interdisciplinary examination, together with the personal project and satisfactory completion of service as action. The IB sets both a minimum total across those results and a minimum grade below which a result does not count towards the award. Confirm the current figures with your child's coordinator; they are published in the programme's assessment procedures and they are revised, so a number from a tutoring site is not authoritative.

What matters practically is that the structure rewards breadth. A candidate cannot compensate for a failing result in one required area with an exceptional result elsewhere beyond the points arithmetic, because the minimum-grade condition applies to each required result separately. For Dubai families used to thinking in best-five or best-eight terms from other systems, that is the counterintuitive part: the weakest required result can be the one that decides the award.

If a result falls short, the consequence is narrower than parents fear. The student still receives subject results, the school still reports grades on the transcript, and progression into the Diploma Programme at a Dubai school is a school admissions decision rather than an IB entitlement. The certificate is a useful external validation and a good thing to hold; it is not a gatekeeper for the Diploma, and no reputable school treats it as one. Any provider implying your child's future depends on it is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: The May session counted backwards through a Dubai school year
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the session in May, at the end of MYP 5. We do not publish an IB examination or results date on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date. Your school's coordinator has the live timetable and the internal deadlines, and those internal deadlines are the ones that govern your family's calendar anyway.

Counted backwards from a May session in a Dubai school year, the shape is predictable even without dates. School registration happens in the autumn term and is the school's responsibility, not the family's, though it is worth confirming it has happened. ePortfolio material needs to be substantially complete before the winter break, because the submission and internal marking window follows. The personal project report deadline commonly lands between December and February. That leaves roughly the January-to-April stretch for on-screen technique, which is the only part of the preparation that responds well to a short intensive effort.

Two Dubai-specific collisions belong in the calendar in September. School mock examinations frequently sit in the same winter window as the project and portfolio deadlines. And Ramadan shortens school days and reshapes family evenings for part of the spring term, which in some years overlaps the last clear stretch of on-screen practice. Sessions can move to post-Iftar timings, and plenty of our Dubai families prefer that, but the planning has to be deliberate rather than discovered in week two.

sections.heading: ePortfolio integrity: why we teach on a different example
paragraphs: ePortfolios are coursework. They are produced by the student across the course, marked by the school's own teachers and then moderated externally. That makes outside help a genuine integrity question rather than a theoretical one, and it deserves a clear answer rather than a reassuring one. Our position is that we do not work on the material a student will submit. We teach the skill on a parallel example, and the student applies it to their own work alone.

In practice that is less restrictive than it sounds and better teaching than the alternative. If a design student cannot evaluate against a specification, we take a different brief entirely, read the criterion descriptor, and work through an evaluation on that. The student then goes back to their own portfolio and does it themselves, which is also the only version that survives moderation and the only version that teaches anything durable. A tutor who improves a submitted portfolio directly has improved one portfolio and taught nothing.

This matters more in this region than it should. Services in the Gulf advertise finished Internal Assessments at fixed prices, with one found during our research selling completed work at AED 3,750. Buying assessed work is a malpractice matter and the consequence lands on the candidate rather than the seller. The filter for a family is a single question: ask a provider whether they will work on your child's submitted portfolio. An honest answer is no, with an explanation of what they will do instead.

sections.heading: eAssessment or International GCSE: the Year 10 fork in a Dubai school
paragraphs: Dubai families often face a genuine choice at the end of Year 9, either because the school offers both routes or because moving school is on the table. It is worth making deliberately rather than by default, and the honest answer is that the right route depends on what happens after Year 11 rather than on which assessment sounds more rigorous.

A student continuing into the IB Diploma at the same school generally benefits from staying in the programme: the criterion habits, the command terms and the integrated thinking transfer directly, and the on-screen format is not a disadvantage for anything that follows. A student likely to move to a British-curriculum school, to A Levels, or to a country where subject certificates at sixteen are expected, often benefits from International GCSE, because Cambridge and Pearson subject certificates are widely recognised and the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency rules are written in their terms.

That last point is concrete rather than speculative. The published British-track equivalency requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No verified IB points threshold exists that we are willing to publish, so check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority before planning around any figure. Tutoring is not required for equivalency and no provider should tell you it is.

sections.heading: How these sessions run, what they cost in this market, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one on live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. For on-screen preparation specifically, the online format has an unusual advantage: the student works on their own keyboard, in their own browser, typing into a timed document while the tutor watches the response appear. That is closer to the real examination than any in-person session at a kitchen table with a notebook.

On price, the published Dubai market as we read it in October 2026: EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 per hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270 per hour for specialist IB support. Bestimate's Dubai survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year help at AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Those are other providers' published figures with their reading date, not IB Gram prices. We publish structure and a free first lesson rather than a fixed hourly rate, because the right tutor for an interdisciplinary paper and the right tutor for extended mathematics are different people.

What we will not claim: no regulator or examination board endorses us. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, per the UAE government's own information service, and that is a fact about KHDA rather than a credential of ours. We hold no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We publish no predicted grades and no success statistics. Private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so we quote none.

process.title: Confirm what your child is actually entered for
process.description: Before anything else, get three answers from the school in writing: does it register candidates, is it for the certificate or individual results, and which subject groups. We will ask for those in the first conversation because preparation for an on-screen paper and preparation for a moderated portfolio have almost nothing in common.

process.title: Free 45-minute first lesson
process.description: One lesson at no cost with no card details taken. For an on-screen subject it includes a short timed response, marked aloud against the criterion descriptors, so the diagnosis comes from the student's own writing rather than from a conversation about how they feel in tests.

process.title: Diagnose from a marked mock, not a worry
process.description: Where there is time, we would rather a family paid for one properly marked two-hour mock than four hours of general revision. Front-loaded timing, command-term blindness and the interdisciplinary error are invisible without a script and obvious with one.

process.title: Match on the subject group and the paper
process.description: Delivery is online for every UAE family, so matching is about who has taught this subject group at this level rather than who lives nearby. The interdisciplinary paper in particular needs someone comfortable across two disciplines, which is a smaller pool than any single Dubai community contains.

process.title: Timed practice every session, marked together
process.description: Twenty to thirty minutes of each hour is spent answering under conditions on the student's own keyboard, and the rest marking it against the descriptors. Students who only write untimed answers get better at writing untimed answers, which is not what May asks for.

process.title: Stop at the session, or bridge into DP1
process.description: Preparation ends when the session does. There is no rolling commitment and no automatic renewal. For students continuing into the Diploma we offer a short bridge block in the summer, including handwriting stamina, which catches out candidates who have typed for two years.

whyPoints.title: We ask what your child is entered for first
whyPoints.description: Many Dubai schools do not use eAssessment at all, and others register for individual results rather than the certificate. Practice on their own keyboard, marked against descriptors, is the only thing that reliably changes that.

faqs.question: What exactly is an on-screen examination, and how is it different from a paper my child writes by hand?
faqs.answer: It is two hours at a computer in a secure examination application, with the stimulus material embedded in the paper: short video, audio, images, data tables, text extracts, some of it interactive. The candidate reads or watches, then types responses into fields on the same screen. The practical differences are navigation, which quietly consumes minutes, and typing speed, which limits how much of their thinking a candidate can actually get down. There is no content list to memorise, because the material is provided and the marks are for what the candidate does with it.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's Dubai school even registers candidates for eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Ask the MYP coordinator three things in one email: does the school register candidates, is it for the full certificate or individual subject results, and which subject groups will my child be entered in. eAssessment is optional for schools and a substantial number of Dubai schools do not use it, moving students onto Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for Years 10 and 11 instead. Until those answers exist, nobody can tell you what preparation is useful, and a tutoring provider who starts selling before asking should be treated carefully.

faqs.question: Which subjects are examined on screen and which are submitted as a portfolio?
faqs.answer: Broadly, language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics and the interdisciplinary paper are examined on screen, while language acquisition, arts, design and physical and health education are submitted as ePortfolios marked by the school and moderated externally by the IB. Your child's exact entry pattern depends on the options chosen in Year 10, so confirm it with the coordinator. The split matters because on-screen subjects respond to six weeks of timed technique, whereas portfolio subjects are decided by work done months earlier.

faqs.question: My son's mock on-screen paper came back much lower than his coursework grades - why?
faqs.answer: Almost always timing and judgement rather than knowledge. Coursework rewards a student who can produce careful work over weeks with redrafting; an on-screen paper rewards someone who can reach a defensible judgement about unseen material in a fixed number of minutes. The three errors that produce exactly this gap are summarising sources instead of evaluating them, spending thirty minutes on the first task, and answering a command term with the wrong answer shape. All three are visible in a marked script and all three are habits, which means they respond quickly.

faqs.question: Is there any point revising content for an examination where the material is provided?
faqs.answer: Much less than families assume, and this is the single most liberating thing to tell a stressed MYP 5 student. Because stimulus material is supplied, the paper cannot test recall of a content list. What it tests is the ability to read a source critically, apply subject thinking to it, and write to the shape the command term demands. Time spent memorising definitions in the spring term is largely wasted; time spent producing timed responses and marking them against the criterion descriptors is not.

faqs.question: How much does a typing problem really matter in a two-hour paper?
faqs.answer: More than parents expect and less than students fear. No criterion gives credit for an argument that was in the candidate's head when the clock stopped, so a slow typist writes a shorter answer than their thinking deserves. The fix is outside sessions and cheap: fifteen minutes of daily typing practice across six weeks moves most fifteen-year-olds from hunting for keys to adequate fluency. We check it in the first session by timing a short response, because it is a constraint worth knowing about in January rather than discovering in May.

faqs.question: What is the interdisciplinary paper, and why do candidates find it the hardest?
faqs.answer: It presents material drawn from two disciplines and asks for a response that genuinely integrates both. Candidates lose marks by writing two separate subject answers and placing them back to back, which reads like diligence and satisfies no integration descriptor. It is also the paper schools have the least practice material for, so it tends to be under-prepared relative to its weight in the certificate arithmetic. Two or three sessions on integration technique is usually all it takes, and the gain is disproportionate to the time.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my daughter's design ePortfolio before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: We will not, and we would be cautious about anyone who offers to. The portfolio is coursework: the student's own work, marked by the school's teachers and then moderated externally by the IB. What we do instead is teach the skill on a parallel example. If the gap is evaluating against a specification, we take a completely different brief, read the criterion descriptor and work an evaluation through on that, and your daughter then applies it to her own portfolio alone. That version survives moderation and actually teaches something durable.

faqs.question: When does the session happen, and can you tell me the results date?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the session in May, at the end of MYP 5. We deliberately do not publish a specific examination or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date at all. Your school's MYP coordinator holds the live timetable and the internal deadlines, and the internal deadlines are what actually govern your family's calendar: portfolio submission, the project report, and the school's own mock schedule.

faqs.question: What does the MYP certificate require, and is my child's Diploma place at risk without it?
faqs.answer: The certificate needs validated results across the required subject groups including the interdisciplinary paper, plus the personal project and satisfactory completion of service as action, with both a minimum total and a minimum grade per required result set by the IB. Confirm the current figures with your coordinator rather than any tutoring site. A shortfall is less serious than families fear: subject results still stand, the school still reports grades, and entry to the Diploma at a Dubai school is a school admissions decision, not an IB entitlement.

faqs.question: My child joined the programme in Year 10 - can they still be entered?
faqs.answer: It depends on how much course evidence exists, and it is a question for the school rather than for us. On-screen subjects are less affected, because the paper assesses what the candidate can do with unseen material rather than a record of coursework. The moderated portfolio subjects are the constraint: a student who arrived in Year 10 may not have enough course work banked in language acquisition or arts for a portfolio to be submitted. Ask the coordinator before enrolment if the certificate matters to your family.

faqs.question: How many weeks of preparation does one on-screen subject actually need?
faqs.answer: For a student who already performs reasonably in the subject, six to eight weekly sessions with timed practice in each is usually enough to fix the habits that cost marks. Front-loaded timing goes in one session plus a mock. Command-term shape takes two. Evaluation rather than summary takes three or four. Beyond that the returns fall away quickly, because the remaining variable is subject understanding built across two years rather than anything a spring block can supply. Spreading a small budget across four subjects is the common mistake.

faqs.question: Do Ramadan timings disrupt the last stretch of preparation before May?
faqs.answer: They change it rather than disrupt it. School days shorten, family evenings shift, and in some years the period overlaps the clearest run of on-screen practice before the session. The workable pattern in Dubai is to move sessions to post-Iftar slots, which many of our families prefer anyway because the student is more alert, and to plan it in September rather than negotiating it in week two. Independent typing and timing practice is easier to sustain through a shortened day than new teaching is.

faqs.question: Should my child stay in the programme for Years 10 and 11 or move to International GCSE?
faqs.answer: It depends on what happens after sixteen rather than on which assessment is harder. A student continuing into the IB Diploma at the same Dubai school usually gains from staying: criteria, command terms and integrated thinking carry straight over. A student likely to move to a British-curriculum school, to A Levels, or to a country expecting subject certificates at sixteen often gains from International GCSE, partly because UAE Ministry of Education equivalency rules for the British track are written in GCSE and A Level terms.

faqs.question: How does this preparation differ from the IGCSE tutoring my older child had?
faqs.answer: Substantially. International GCSE preparation is syllabus-led: a published specification with a code, a bank of past papers, mark schemes and predictable question types. On-screen MYP preparation has none of that, because the paper is criterion-referenced against material nobody has seen. So there is nothing to work through in the conventional sense. Sessions are built from the criterion descriptors, the command terms and timed responses to varied stimulus, and progress is judged on marked scripts rather than on past-paper percentages.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor with the right subject-group experience is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than putting a generalist in the slot and letting you discover the mismatch. The interdisciplinary paper and extended mathematics are the two areas where the pool is smallest, and for those it sometimes means a short wait or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time. Because every lesson for UAE families is one-to-one live video, availability is a question of subject match and timetable rather than driving distance from your community.

dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one email to the coordinator
dubai/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.closingBody: Before you buy anything, ask your child's MYP coordinator whether the school registers candidates, whether it is for the certificate or individual results, and which subject groups your child is entered in. Those three answers decide what preparation means. Then take the free 45-minute first lesson: for an on-screen subject it includes a short timed response marked aloud against the criterion descriptors, so the diagnosis comes from your child's own writing. No card details are taken. Lessons run one-to-one on live video across the UAE, timed to Gulf Standard Time, on the keyboard your child will actually use.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-home-t.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach extended content in the order it has to be learned: index laws and factorisation before algebraic fractions, right-angled work before the sine and cosine rules, and generalisation before justification. Each checks the prerequisite before teaching the topic you asked for.

intro.heading: Extended failures are almost never about ability
paragraphs: A Dubai parent with an able child in an extended set and a report that says 4 is looking at one of three things, and none of them is a ceiling on what the child can do. The first is sequencing: a topic was taught on top of a prerequisite that had never been secured, so the new work had nowhere to attach. The second is pace: the extended scheme makes one pass over most topics, so an absence turns into a permanent hole rather than a temporary lag. The third is criterion B, where the extended route's harder patterns demand a justification the student has never been shown how to write.

Each of those has a different fix and they are easy to tell apart from marked work. Sequencing failures look like confident method with wrong manipulation: the student knows what to do with an algebraic fraction and cannot factorise the denominator. Pace failures are topic-shaped: everything fine except one unit, and the unit coincides with a fortnight away. Criterion B failures are structural: patterns found, rules written, nothing justified, and the mark stuck at 4 or 5 however good the algebra is.

What the extended route actually adds is a defined list rather than a general difficulty. Harder factorisation, including non-unit coefficients and completing the square. Algebraic fractions. Function notation and the transformations of graphs. Non-right-angled trigonometry, with the sine and cosine rules and work in three dimensions. More demanding generalisation, including quadratic and non-linear patterns and reasoning that edges towards proof. Those five groups are where a Dubai extended-set student needs teaching, and everything else on the course is shared with the standard route.

Now the search term. Families type home tutor because that is how one-to-one help is described, and the market answer is worth giving straight: visiting tutors in this city publish hourly figures of roughly AED 180 to AED 350 according to the Bestimate rate survey, with individual listings to AED 500. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student writing on a shared whiteboard.

On an extended brief that delivery choice has a concrete advantage beyond the obvious. The thing that separates a useful extended session from a wasted one is whether the tutor checks the prerequisite before teaching the requested topic, and that habit belongs to people who have taught the sequence many times. In a city where a visiting tutor is selected from whoever can reach your community before the evening closes, the selection is made on geography. Video makes it on experience, which on this route is the whole game.

The page that follows is therefore about the mathematics and the order of it. The extended additions, topic by topic. The dependency chain, written out so you can diagnose at home. Where extended students lose marks standard students do not. Criterion B at extended depth. Three-dimensional trigonometry and the diagram habit. The collision between the extended pace and the Personal Project year. What a session can fix, and what needs a conversation with the school instead.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-home-t.programmesIntro: Extended mathematics only makes sense in relation to what comes after it, because the whole point of the additional content is a later course. Here are the stages, with what each assumes.

programmes.name: Middle Years extended mathematics
programmes.ageRange: Ages 14-16 · MYP 4 and MYP 5 in most Dubai schools
programmes.description: The same four branches and the same four criteria as the standard route, plus additional algebra, function work and trigonometry, taught at a faster pace with a single pass over most topics. Assessment is unchanged: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each marked 0 to 8. The additional content is not harder to understand in isolation; it is harder to survive because it is sequenced tightly and never revisited.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set extended groups at different points and movement between routes varies by school rather than by programme rule. Ask the department three questions: when placement is reviewed, what evidence is used, and whether a student may move down mid-year without losing the criterion marks already banked.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, higher level
programmes.description: The course the extended route is built for. It assumes fluent algebraic manipulation, confident function work and comfort with formal reasoning, and it extends them into calculus, proof and series. Students who arrive with the five extended topic groups secure find the first term demanding rather than impossible. Students who arrive having passed extended assessments on partially understood algebra find the term brutal, because calculus exposes manipulation weaknesses immediately.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical test of readiness is not the extended grade but the criterion B mark alongside it. A student with a strong knowing-and-understanding mark and a weak investigating-patterns mark has been rewarded for computation, and higher-level Analysis and Approaches is where that profile stops working. Ask for an honest read before the Diploma choices are filed.

programmes.name: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling, statistics and technology course, which the standard route feeds and which an extended-route student can of course take. It rewards the criterion D skills the extended course also develops: model selection, interpretation in context and evaluation of validity. A student whose extended strength is modelling rather than algebra is often better served here, and the Middle Years criterion profile usually says which.
programmes.countryNote: Worth checking against target university courses while your child is in Year 10. Some UAE and overseas engineering and economics programmes specify a route or a level, and reading two published requirements takes ten minutes and settles two years of planning.

programmes.name: International GCSE additional mathematics
programmes.description: Where a Dubai school leaves the programme at Year 10, the closest equivalent of extended work is an additional mathematics qualification alongside the main one, examined by timed papers. An extended-route transfer student usually has the content and lacks the pace, so the retraining is about marks per minute, question triage and knowing when to leave a question rather than about new mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge examines International GCSE in June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, warning that the correct zone timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Get the zone timetable from your school's examinations officer.

dubai/ib-myp-extended-mathematics-home-t.subjectsIntro: Extended briefs should name the topic and, ideally, the prerequisite. These are the areas Dubai extended-set families bring, with what the content demands and the dependency underneath it.

subjects.name: Index laws and surd handling
subjects.description: Rarely the reason a parent calls and frequently the reason the called-about topic failed. Negative and fractional indices, and exact-form answers, sit under factorisation, function work and trigonometric manipulation. A student who computes indices on a calculator rather than reasoning about them will stall in algebraic fractions without either of you knowing why.

subjects.name: Harder factorisation
subjects.description: Non-unit coefficients, difference of two squares in disguise, grouping, and recognising when nothing factorises. The load-bearing topic of the whole extended route: algebraic fractions, quadratic solving and function behaviour all rest on it. Most apparent algebraic-fraction weakness is factorisation weakness wearing a different hat.

subjects.name: Completing the square and the discriminant
subjects.description: Turning points, maximum and minimum values, and the number of roots. Taught as a procedure in many schemes and assessed as a connection to graph behaviour, which is where marks are lost. The test of understanding is whether a student can read a discriminant and sketch without computing roots.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions
subjects.description: Simplifying, adding and subtracting with algebraic denominators, and solving equations containing them. Hard to self-teach because textbook examples are chosen to factorise neatly. Errors are nearly always in the factorisation or in cancelling across an addition, which is the single most common extended algebra mistake we see in Dubai marked work.

subjects.name: Function notation and transformations
subjects.description: Reading function notation, substituting into it, and translating, reflecting and stretching graphs. Procedural rules are easy to memorise and useless without a model of what the notation means. The diagnostic question is whether a student can predict the effect of an unfamiliar transformation in words before touching a calculator.

subjects.name: Sine and cosine rules
subjects.description: Non-right-angled triangles, the area formula with sine, and the ambiguous case. The judgement of which rule to use is the skill; the arithmetic is not. Students who were never fully secure in right-angled trigonometry struggle here for a reason that has nothing to do with the new content.

subjects.name: Three-dimensional trigonometry
subjects.description: Angles between lines and planes, diagonals of solids, and extracting a two-dimensional triangle from a three-dimensional picture. The whole topic turns on drawing the extracted triangle separately, labelled. Students who work on the original diagram lose marks they could have earned, and the habit is teachable in one session.

subjects.name: Quadratic and non-linear generalisation
subjects.description: Second differences, non-linear growth, and patterns where the rule is not immediately polynomial. The extended route's criterion B tasks are genuinely harder than the standard route's, so the justification step carries more weight and more marks, and it is the most common place an able extended student is capped.

subjects.name: Model selection and rejection
subjects.description: Extended modelling tasks often admit more than one defensible model, and the marks sit in explaining why one was chosen and another rejected. Students trained to produce an answer find this uncomfortable, because it requires committing to a judgement in writing and defending it.

subjects.name: Exact answers and rounding discipline
subjects.description: Working in exact form until the final step, then rounding appropriately for the context and saying so. Extended tasks penalise premature rounding more than standard ones because answers are chained through several steps. A short habit block fixes it and recovers marks across every topic simultaneously.

sections.heading: What the extended route adds, topic by topic
paragraphs: Extended mathematics is not a different subject and it does not carry a different grade scale. It is the same four branches, the same four criteria and the same conversion to a grade from 1 to 7. The additional content is a finite, nameable list, and knowing the list changes what a family buys, because it separates the topics that genuinely need a specialist from the ones shared with the standard route and available at the qualified band.

The five groups are harder factorisation including completing the square and the discriminant; algebraic fractions; function notation and graph transformations; non-right-angled trigonometry including three-dimensional work; and more demanding generalisation at criterion B. Everything else your child meets in an extended set is standard-route content taught faster. That distinction is useful in a first conversation with a prospective tutor, because a brief that names one of the five groups tests whether the tutor knows the sequence.

Each addition exists for a later purpose, and that purpose is worth knowing. Completing the square exists so that quadratic behaviour can be read rather than computed. Algebraic fractions exist so that rational functions are manageable at Diploma level. Function notation exists so that transformations and composition are available in calculus. The sine and cosine rules exist because real geometry is not right-angled. Students taught the reason remember the procedure; students taught only the procedure forget it over a summer.

sections.heading: The dependency chain: why the topic you asked about is not the problem
paragraphs: Extended mathematics is more tightly sequenced than anything else in the Middle Years framework, and that produces a diagnostic rule a parent can apply without a tutor. If a student is failing a topic while clearly knowing what the topic is for, the failure is almost always one level down. The student who cannot simplify an algebraic fraction usually knows exactly what to do and cannot factorise the denominator. The student who cannot handle a transformation usually knows the rule and cannot read the function notation it is written in.

The chain runs roughly like this. Index laws and surds sit under factorisation. Factorisation sits under algebraic fractions, under completing the square, and under solving quadratics. Function notation sits under transformations and under anything involving composition. Right-angled trigonometry sits under the sine and cosine rules, which sit under three-dimensional work. Arithmetic with negatives and fractions sits under all of it, which is why an able Year 10 student with a Year 7 fraction gap can look like a mystery.

You can test this at home in ten minutes with four questions: simplify an expression with a negative index; factorise a quadratic with a non-unit coefficient; evaluate a function at a given value using notation; and find a missing side in a right-angled triangle, giving an exact answer. A student who stumbles on any of those should not be having a session on algebraic fractions next week, and a tutor who teaches one anyway is being paid to build on sand.

This is also the reason extended sessions should be booked by topic with the prerequisite named rather than by the month. A block that begins with a prerequisite check is one or two sessions longer and several sessions cheaper overall. The table sets out the chain so you can look up what to test before you buy.

sections.heading: Where extended students lose marks that standard students do not
paragraphs: Three losses are specific to the extended route, and none of them is about knowing less. The first is at the top of criterion A. An extended task's final part is set in a genuinely unfamiliar context with harder content behind it, so the gap between the practised version and the assessed version is wider than on the standard route. Students who have only ever met the practised version leave it blank, and on the extended route that blank costs more because the upper bands are where extended students are expected to live.

The second is criterion B justification. Extended patterns are quadratic or non-linear, which means the general rule is harder to state and much harder to justify. A student can reach a correct quadratic rule, verify it on two further cases and still sit mid-band because no reason was offered for why the structure of the problem produces that rule. On the standard route the rule itself is often enough to reach a decent mark; on the extended route it is not.

The third is rounding and exact form. Extended answers are chained through more steps, so premature rounding propagates and the final answer is marked wrong despite correct reasoning throughout. Worse, the student cannot see the error, because every individual line looks right. This is the cheapest of the three to fix and the one most often ignored, since it reads as carelessness rather than as a habit nobody taught.

The table maps the four criteria at extended depth to the characteristic loss and the fix. Read it next to marked work rather than instead of it: the pattern in a teacher's comments will usually match one row, and that row is the plan.

sections.heading: Criterion B at extended depth: from second differences to a reason
paragraphs: Pattern work on the extended route starts where the standard route finishes. A constant second difference signals a quadratic rule, and building that rule is mechanical once a student has done it a dozen times. The extended difficulty sits in the two steps after it. Verification means testing the rule on cases outside the table, which requires generating terms from a rule rather than a rule from terms, and students who have only practised one direction cannot do it. Justification means explaining why the structure of the problem produces that rule, and almost nobody is taught how.

Justification at Middle Years level is not formal proof, and saying so relieves a great deal of anxiety. If the pattern counts the squares on the surface of a growing cube arrangement, the justification explains why each new layer contributes what it contributes, in words tied to the picture. If the pattern is the number of handshakes in a growing group, it explains why each new person adds the number already present. Three worked examples across different structures, with the student writing each one, is usually enough for a fourth to appear unaided.

Extended tasks also include patterns whose rule is not polynomial at all, and here the useful teaching is diagnostic: how to tell from the data whether to look for a constant difference, a constant second difference or a constant ratio. Students who only know the difference-table method try it on exponential growth, find no constant difference, and conclude the task is impossible. Ten minutes on the ratio test prevents an entire wasted investigation.

None of this is content the student is missing. It is method nobody showed them, which is why a bounded block beats a term of general support here. It is also the single highest-value purchase on the extended route, because criterion B carries the widest mark range in the subject and is where able extended students are most often capped at 5.
bullets: Generate terms from a rule as fluently as rules from terms, or verification is impossible
Justification is a reason tied to the structure, not a formal proof
