sections.heading: What the travel actually costs, line by line
paragraphs: The in-home premium is not a quality premium. It is a transport cost, and in Dubai between 16:00 and 19:00 it is a large one. A tutor travelling from the Jumeirah or Al Barsha tutor belt to Arabian Ranches, Town Square or Damac Hills at that hour is committing ninety minutes to two hours of unpaid driving around a sixty-minute lesson, and no rational pricing survives that without a premium.

That arithmetic drives three consequences a parent feels directly. The first is the rate itself, AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online. The second is minimum session length: many visiting tutors will not take a sixty-minute booking at all, which converts a modest weekly spend into a bigger one. The third is reliability, because a lesson that depends on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at 17:30 fails more often than one that depends on a wifi connection.

There is a fourth cost that never appears on an invoice: the size of the pool. A car-based model means your choice of tutor is limited to people willing to drive to your community at your preferred hour. For standard-route mathematics in Al Barsha that is a long list. For Arabic as a first language in Town Square, or Design in Remraam, it is a very short one, and a short list means accepting a generalist.

None of this makes in-home teaching worthless. For a nine-year-old, or a student who genuinely cannot hold attention on a screen, presence in the room is the service being bought and it is a reasonable thing to pay for. For a fourteen-year-old working on criterion C in Individuals and Societies, it is a premium for a car journey, and the table below is the comparison we would want to read before paying it.

sections.heading: The seven things that change the number in Dubai
paragraphs: Hourly rate is not one number. It moves with a short list of variables, and knowing which ones apply to your child lets you predict a quote before you ask for it. Several of these are specific to Dubai rather than general to tutoring.

The largest single variable is scarcity of the subject stream. Standard-route mathematics prices at the bottom of the qualified-tutor band because Dubai has many people who can teach it well. Arabic as a first language prices towards the specialist band because it does not. Design sits awkwardly in between, because plenty of people can teach design and few are comfortable teaching the design cycle as an assessment with four criteria attached.

The second largest is slot timing. Every family in Dubai wants 17:00 to 19:00 on a weekday, and that window is finite. Friday afternoon after the early school finish, weekend mornings and the 15:00 to 16:30 band for communities with short school runs are all less contested. A family willing to take an off-peak slot has more choice of tutor at the same rate, which in practice means a better match rather than a cheaper one.

The remaining variables are year group, route, assessment load, session length and term timing. Middle Years 4 and 5 prices above 1 to 3. A school that has switched to International GCSE changes what you are buying entirely. A Personal Project in progress adds a block rather than an hourly premium. Ninety minutes costs less per minute than sixty. And the weeks before a reporting cycle are when demand peaks, which is the worst moment to start looking and the most common one.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees and the 2026-27 freeze
paragraphs: A tuition figure means nothing without the budget it sits inside. Dubai school fees are the dominant line in any family's education spend, and in 2026 the authority did something unusual with them, which is useful context for anyone deciding whether to add weekly tutoring.

The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family whose fee bill was expected to rise, that is headroom that did not exist a year earlier, and in practice it is where a good deal of new tutoring spend has come from.

The market around it keeps growing. The authority reported seven new private schools for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, following six openings during 2025-26 and a 6% rise in enrolment. More supply tends to moderate fee pressure and to widen the continuum choice, which matters for families currently at a school that switches to International GCSE at sixteen.

The table below sets tutoring against the other things on an education invoice. The point of it is proportion: one weekly session at the qualified-subject band is a modest fraction of an annual fee bill, while three subjects twice a week at the specialist band is not, and families routinely drift from the first into the second without ever deciding to.

sections.heading: Monthly packages and the arithmetic nobody shows you
paragraphs: Packages look like discounts and frequently are not. The published online package in this market is AED 799 a month for eight sessions, which works out at just under AED 100 a session. The published in-home package is AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits, which is AED 400 to AED 450 a visit or AED 200 to AED 225 an hour. Both are inside their respective market bands, so neither is a bargain; they are a different billing shape.

What a package genuinely buys is commitment on both sides, and that has real value. A tutor with eight sessions booked plans a sequence rather than reacting week to week, and a family that has paid attends. What it also buys, less helpfully, is friction if the match turns out to be wrong, which is why the replacement policy matters more in a package than in pay-as-you-go.

The arithmetic that actually reduces spend is different. Fewer, longer sessions cost less in total than more, shorter ones at the same tier, because setup and marking time is spread further. One subject chosen by criterion profile costs a third of three subjects bought because a report card looked bad across the board. And a fortnightly block with a defined end point costs a fraction of an open-ended weekly arrangement that nobody ever cancels.

One honesty point on the word free. A free first lesson should mean a full lesson at no cost, with no card details required and no obligation to continue. If a trial is fifteen minutes, or requires payment details, or is really a sales call with a tutor present, the condition belongs on the same screen as the word. Ours is a full lesson, it ends with a written note on what the gap is, and nothing is charged if you stop there.

sections.heading: The permit question: why a legal tutor is not the cheapest tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the cheapest quotes in a Dubai community group often come from people who are not covered. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here, and anyone quoting one should be asked for their source.

The permit itself is not an obstacle. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The ministry's own service is listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fees stated and a two working day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

So the permit does not cost money, which means it does not explain a price difference. What it does signal is seriousness, and it carries a code of conduct. That code, together with the professional-ethics rules reported for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff, bars a teacher from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. We do not arrange for a child to be taught privately for a fee by a teacher at their own school, anywhere in the country.

Two further things no parent should pay for. A service that describes itself as approved, accredited or licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, because a Dubai educational services permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises and IB Gram does not hold one and does not claim one. And a service that offers to produce assessed work: one site visible in this market sells completed internal assessments, which under IB rules is malpractice with the consequence falling on the student.

sections.heading: Where Dubai families actually waste tutoring money
paragraphs: After a few hundred Dubai enquiries the waste is predictable, and almost none of it is about the hourly rate. The largest single loss is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A report card showing 4s across six subjects produces an instinct to hire three tutors, when the criterion profile usually shows one shared weakness, typically communication or application, which one tutor can address in one subject and the student then transfers.

The second loss is persisting with a match that is not working because there is no mechanism to change it. Six weeks at AED 220 an hour with the wrong tutor is AED 1,320 that bought nothing, and it happens because the parent feels the problem is their child rather than the pairing. Any provider should change the tutor on request after a bad fortnight; if yours will not, that is the thing to fix, not the rate.

The third is buying examination-year intensity for Middle Years work. There is no external examination in most years of this programme, so paying premium specialist rates for weekly teaching in Year 8 is spending Diploma money on a skill-building job. The corollary is that families underspend in the years where it would be cheap and overspend in the year where it is not.

The fourth is timing. Starting six weeks before a reporting cycle, when every tutor in the city is fully booked, means accepting whoever is free at whatever rate and in whatever slot. Starting in the first weeks of a term means choice. The same money buys a materially better tutor in September than it does in March, and that is the cheapest optimisation available to a Dubai parent.

sections.heading: How lessons are delivered, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and there is no UAE office or centre to visit. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one student with one tutor over live video, and that is stated here rather than discovered on a phone call, because a parent who searched for a visiting tutor deserves the answer before they spend time.

A lesson works like this. The student joins from a laptop or tablet, the tutor shares a whiteboard, and the student's own unit sheet, task instructions, marked work or draft sits on screen. Written work is photographed, uploaded, marked against the published criterion descriptors and returned annotated before the next session, which removes the week of feedback lag a visiting model has by design. For Design and the Arts the tutor works through the process folder, which is where most of the available criterion marks live.

The limits are stated too. A practical build, a laboratory procedure or a physical performance cannot be coached over video, although the written planning, documentation and reflection criteria attached to them can. Younger students need an adult within earshot for the first few weeks. A student who will not turn a camera on learns less than one who will, because a tutor who cannot see the working cannot correct it.

On claims: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, and we name those bodies only to explain what they do. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no student headcount, because none of them could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method attached. On whether a quoted price includes value added tax, ask us about our own figures and check the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance for the treatment of tuition fees rather than relying on a tutoring page for a tax position.

process.title: Say which subject and which year group, not just the grade
process.description: A quote depends on the subject stream, the year group and whether the school runs the programme to Year 11 or switches to International GCSE. Send the last report with its criterion marks and we can tell you which tier of tutor the work actually needs, which is often lower than a parent expects.

process.title: Take the free first lesson before paying anything
process.description: A full lesson at no cost, with no card details required and no obligation to continue. It ends with a short written note naming the criterion that is costing marks. If you stop there, nothing is charged. That is the condition stated on the same page as the word free, which is how it should be.

process.title: Buy a diagnosis before buying hours
process.description: The single biggest waste in Dubai tutoring is hiring three tutors because six grades looked low. A criterion profile usually names one shared weakness, and fixing it in one subject transfers to the others. One session of reading the evidence saves several weeks of unnecessary spend.

process.title: Choose the session shape deliberately
process.description: Ninety minutes once a week costs less in total than two sixty-minute sessions at the same tier and suits extended writing and project work better. Sixty minutes suits maintenance and younger students. A fortnightly block with a fixed session count suits the Personal Project and the bridge into the next course.

process.title: Change the tutor rather than persisting
process.description: If the pairing is not working after a fortnight, say so and we change it. Six weeks of lessons with the wrong tutor is the most expensive thing in this market and it is entirely avoidable. Progress is reviewed against criterion marks at the next reporting cycle, not against a vague sense of improvement.

whyPoints.title: No travel time in the price
whyPoints.description: The gap between the AED 180 to 500 in-home band and the AED 150 to 300 online band is mostly a car. We do not bill travel because no tutor travels, and that is the whole of the cost argument stated plainly rather than dressed up as a benefit.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, with the tier it applies to. Three of the six most visible sites serving Dubai publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, which is why a sourced table is worth more here than another contact form.

whyPoints.title: The tier is matched to the work, not to the invoice
whyPoints.description: Middle Years work usually needs a qualified subject tutor rather than an examiner-experienced specialist, because there is no external examination in most years of the programme. We say so even though the lower tier bills less, since the alternative is selling Diploma pricing for a skill-building job.

whyPoints.title: A free trial with the condition stated
whyPoints.description: A full first lesson, no card details, no obligation, and a written diagnosis at the end. If a trial anywhere requires payment details or lasts fifteen minutes, the condition belongs next to the word free. Ours is on the same screen as the offer.

whyPoints.title: The tutor can be changed on request
whyPoints.description: The largest avoidable loss in Dubai tutoring is weeks paid to a match that should have ended after a fortnight. Changing the tutor is a request, not a negotiation, and it costs nothing. A replacement policy is worth more than AED 40 an hour off the rate.

faqs.question: What does a visiting tutor in Dubai charge once the driving is in the price?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put an in-home one-to-one hourly visit at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages in this market run AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, which is AED 200 to 225 an hour. Against that, a qualified subject tutor working online publishes at AED 150 to AED 300. The gap is mostly transport, and in the 17:00 to 19:00 Dubai peak it is a large transport cost.

faqs.question: If you never visit homes, why does this page target the phrase at all?
faqs.answer: Because it is the phrase Dubai parents actually type, and because the price comparison is the most useful thing anyone can give them. Pretending the search does not exist would just mean a parent finds a page that quotes nothing. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one to one over live video. We would rather say that in the first paragraph, with the rate tables next to it, than let someone find out on a call.

faqs.question: For Middle Years work, is one ninety-minute lesson better value than two sixty-minute ones?
faqs.answer: On cost, yes, at the same tier, because fixed setup and marking time is spread further. On teaching, it depends on the job. Ninety minutes is the right unit for extended writing, a Design or Arts process folder, marking a full task together, or any week with a draft in progress. Two shorter sessions are the better buy during a catch-up block, when frequency matters more than depth. For a steady term with one criterion to move, one ninety-minute slot on a Friday afternoon usually wins on both counts.

faqs.question: Does the rate go up between Year 7 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, by roughly one tier. Years 7 to 9 sit comfortably in the AED 150 to 300 qualified-subject band, because there is no external assessment and the work is skill-building. Years 10 and 11 drift towards the AED 200 to 450 specialist band, because content deepens, mathematics splits into standard and extended routes, sciences may separate into three subjects and all four criteria are reported in every subject. The practical implication is to spend early and small rather than late and large, since the early criteria are what every later mark depends on.

faqs.question: How much of a Dubai tutoring invoice is really the drive?
faqs.answer: On a car-based model, a lot. A tutor travelling from the Jumeirah or Al Barsha belt to Arabian Ranches, Town Square or Damac Hills at 17:00 is committing ninety minutes to two hours of unpaid driving around one hour of teaching, and that is why many visiting tutors will not take a sixty-minute booking. The hidden cost is the tutor pool: your choice narrows to people willing to make that trip at that hour, which for a thin subject like Arabic as a first language means accepting a generalist.

faqs.question: Did the Dubai school fee freeze change what families spend on tuition?
faqs.answer: Anecdotally yes, and the dates line up. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For families who had budgeted for a rise, that is headroom that did not exist previously, and a good deal of new weekly tutoring spend appears to have come from it rather than from a change in academic need.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a Dubai tuition centre cheaper than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually, at roughly AED 60 to 150 a student depending on the centre. Per outcome, often not, and the reason is structural rather than about teaching quality. A class of six cannot be taught to one child's criterion profile, and criterion profiles are exactly what Middle Years marks depend on: a student losing marks on communication and a student losing marks on content need opposite lessons. A group class also means you travel to the centre, so the transport cost moves to you rather than disappearing.

faqs.question: Do Dubai tutoring rates rise before reporting deadlines?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens more than price does, which has the same practical effect. Demand peaks in the weeks right after reports go out, and that is precisely when most families start looking, so the choice narrows to whoever is still free at whatever hour is left. The same budget buys a materially better match in the first weeks of a term than in the fortnight after a report card. Starting early is the cheapest optimisation available to a Dubai parent and it costs nothing at all.

faqs.question: Does a quoted tutoring price in Dubai include value added tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly about their own figures, and check the Federal Tax Authority's published guidance for the treatment of tuition fees rather than relying on a tutoring page for a tax position. Competitor pages quote rates without ever stating whether tax is included, which makes two quotes hard to compare. For our own numbers we will tell you what is and is not included before you pay, and we do not publish a tax interpretation we cannot cite to the authority that sets it.

faqs.question: Who absorbs the cost if the tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: We change the tutor on request, and that is the single most valuable clause in any tutoring arrangement. The largest avoidable loss in this market is not a high hourly rate; it is six weeks at AED 220 an hour with a pairing that should have ended after a fortnight, which is AED 1,320 that bought nothing. Parents often persist because they assume the problem is their child rather than the pairing. Ask any provider you are considering what their replacement mechanism is before you buy a package.

faqs.question: Does a permitted tutor in Dubai charge more than an unpermitted one?
faqs.answer: The permit itself costs nothing, so it cannot explain a price difference. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, with no fees listed on the ministry's own service page and a two working day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, anyone quoting an amount should be asked for their source.

faqs.question: What does Personal Project support cost as a block rather than weekly?
faqs.answer: Twelve to sixteen sessions spread across the final year is the honest shape, concentrated at the planning and reflection stages rather than before submission. The project is marked against three criteria, each out of eight for a total of 24, and two of those three are about process evidence recorded as it happened. That evidence cannot be bought late at any price, which is why a fortnightly block from the start costs less in total than a panic block at the end and scores better.

faqs.question: Can we pay monthly rather than per session?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it is worth knowing that monthly packages in this market are a billing shape rather than a discount. The published online package is AED 799 for eight sessions, just under AED 100 each, which sits inside the normal band; the in-home equivalent at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits works out at AED 200 to 225 an hour. What a package genuinely buys is commitment on both sides, which has real value. What it also buys is friction if the match is wrong, so take the free first lesson first.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to lift one grade on a Middle Years report?
faqs.answer: Find the lowest criterion mark, read its descriptor, and buy teaching for that one thing. Four criteria at eight marks each gives a total out of 32, which converts to the 1 to 7 grade, and the bands are uneven. Moving a single 4 to a 6 often moves the grade; raising three criteria by one mark each costs three times the teaching and frequently does not. One session spent reading the evidence is worth more than a month of general revision bought at any rate.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Dubai Year 10 student realistically need?
faqs.answer: One session a week in one subject, for most students, which at the qualified-subject band works out at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's 2026 figures. Two subjects at once is justified when the criterion profiles are genuinely different; three almost never is, because a flat low profile across six subjects usually means one shared weakness in communication or application. Families who buy three subjects in Year 10 are typically buying reassurance, and it is the most expensive form of it available.

faqs.question: Does living in Town Square rather than Al Barsha change what we pay?
faqs.answer: Not with us, because no tutor travels and there is no distance component in the price. In a car-based model it changes things considerably: the southern communities are furthest from the established tutor belt, in-home quotes there sit at the top of the AED 180 to 500 band, and minimum session lengths of ninety or 120 minutes are common to make the trip viable. The bigger effect is choice rather than cost, since the pool willing to drive to Town Square at 17:30 is short.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-h.tutorsIntro: Tutors below cover the Individuals and Societies group by discipline rather than as one subject, across MYP Years 1 to 5. Each states which strands they teach, from historical source evaluation to geographical data handling and introductory economics, and all sessions run over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: A subject group, not a subject
paragraphs: The first thing to establish about MYP Individuals and Societies is that nobody teaches it. Schools teach history, geography, economics, business management, civics and global politics, and report them under one subject-group heading. A Dubai parent looking at a report that says Individuals and Societies: 4 is looking at a mark that may have been earned mostly in a geography unit about urbanisation, with a history unit on migration contributing a different set of criterion judgements entirely. Asking for a tutor for the subject group, without naming the discipline, is how families end up with a capable tutor who is wrong for the task in front of them.

The second thing is that the group is assessed on four criteria rather than on content coverage. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, criterion B is investigating, criterion C is communicating, and criterion D is thinking critically. Each is marked out of eight against published strands. That has a counter-intuitive consequence: a student can know a great deal of history and score poorly, because three of the four criteria reward skills rather than recall. The skills are specific and teachable, and they are almost never taught explicitly in a crowded Dubai timetable.

The third thing is the research question. Every MYP investigation begins with one, the student writes it, and criterion B rewards not only the question but an explanation of why it is relevant. A question like how did oil change the UAE cannot be answered in two thousand words with sources a fourteen-year-old can reach. A question about the effect of a named policy on a named indicator in a named decade can. The distance between those two sentences is several marks, and it is the single highest-value thing a tutor can teach in this subject group.

Now the practical question in the search phrase. Home tutoring in Dubai is a real and substantial market: published rates for an in-home one-to-one hour run from roughly AED 180 to 500, visits are commonly sold as two-hour sittings because the travel has to be recovered, and families in villa communities routinely lose part of a 17:00 booking to traffic nobody can predict. Those are genuine trade-offs, not sales points, and they are what parents are weighing when they type the phrase.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai, in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own documents shared on screen. For Individuals and Societies the argument for that is unusually strong, because the subject group is really five subjects. A family in Mirdif needs a tutor who can mark a source evaluation or an economics diagram, and the probability that such a person lives within a twenty-minute drive is low. Selecting by discipline rather than by distance is what makes the hour useful.

The sections below go through each discipline, the research question, source work, the command terms that shape a humanities answer, and how the mandatory UAE subjects required in every Dubai private school relate to the MYP course. Where a rule comes from a regulator, the regulator is named.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-h.programmesIntro: Humanities looks different at each stage of the continuum, and the disciplines separate out gradually. Knowing where your child sits in that sequence explains why the work suddenly feels harder in a particular year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Social studies content is embedded in transdisciplinary themes such as where we are in place and time and how we organise ourselves. Children investigate communities, settlements, migration and governance without meeting the discipline names. The research habits built here, asking a question, finding information, saying where it came from, are the direct ancestors of MYP criterion B.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP cohorts often arrive in the MYP having done genuinely ambitious inquiry work and having never written a formal research question. That is a format gap rather than a skills gap, and it closes in a few weeks once someone shows them what a question narrow enough to answer actually looks like.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies runs through all five years as a subject group, with units drawn from history, geography, economics, business and civics, framed by key concepts such as time, place and space, systems, and global interactions. Four criteria, each out of eight. By Years 4 and 5 the disciplines are usually distinguishable in the unit titles even where the report still shows one grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ in how early they separate the disciplines. Some run integrated humanities to the end of Year 5; others introduce distinct history and geography courses from Year 4 and add economics or business as an option. Which model your child's school uses determines whether you need one tutor or two, and the MYP coordinator will tell you in an email.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The group splits fully into named subjects: History, Geography, Economics, Business Management, Global Politics, Psychology, Digital Society and Environmental Systems and Societies among them. Each has its own paper structure and its own internally assessed component, and each assumes the independent research and source-evaluation skills the MYP was building.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma humanities teachers report the same recurring gap in Year 12: students who can describe and cannot adjudicate. The MYP students who arrive ready are the ones whose criterion D marks were already strong, because criterion D is where weighing perspectives and evaluating sources by origin and purpose is actually assessed.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A career-related study alongside a smaller set of Diploma courses, with a reflective project at its centre. For a humanities student the reflective project is recognisably the MYP investigation grown up: an extended independent inquiry with an ethical dimension, researched, documented and defended by the student.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools offer the CP, so families should confirm availability and the course list with the school rather than from any tutoring provider. Where it is offered, students with strong MYP criterion B habits tend to handle the reflective project with much less supervision than their peers.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-h.subjectsIntro: These are the disciplines and skill areas that appear on a Dubai MYP student's Individuals and Societies tasks. Naming the one your child is actually struggling in is the difference between a useful tutor and a pleasant hour.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Built around causation, consequence, change, continuity and significance. Tasks ask students to explain why something happened and to judge how far a source can be trusted. The commonest mark loss is treating a source as information rather than as something produced by someone for a reason.

subjects.name: Geography: human and physical
subjects.description: Place, space, scale, process and sustainability, usually with data attached. Students meet population pyramids, climate graphs, land-use maps and fieldwork results. Marks go missing on describing a pattern where the task asked for an explanation of the process producing it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Scarcity, choice, markets, trade and development, introduced with diagrams. A drawn and labelled diagram earns little on its own; the marks come from the written explanation of what shifted and why. Students who treat the diagram as the answer consistently underscore on criterion A.

subjects.name: Business management
subjects.description: Stakeholders, functions of a business, basic finance and marketing, mostly through case studies. A first response usually describes the company. A marked redraft applies a concept to it and reaches a judgement, which is where criterion D credit begins.

subjects.name: Civics, governance and global politics
subjects.description: Power, rights, representation and international relations. These units produce the clearest criterion D evidence because they require genuinely competing perspectives, and they expose a student's habit of writing one-sided arguments faster than any other topic.

subjects.name: Research and investigation skills
subjects.description: Writing a focused research question and explaining its relevance, building an action plan with dates and methods, recording information so it can be retrieved, and evaluating the process honestly. The most transferable skill set in the group and the least often taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Source evaluation
subjects.description: Judging a document by origin, purpose, value and limitation rather than by content. One taught shift, from what the source says to who made it and why, typically moves a criterion D mark by two points and transfers to every subsequent unit.

subjects.name: Academic referencing and documentation
subjects.description: Criterion C explicitly requires sources documented using a recognised convention. Students lose these marks to inconsistency rather than ignorance: three citation styles in one bibliography, or in-text references that do not match the list at the end.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies
subjects.levels: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: A separate, separately reported subject required by KHDA alongside the licensed curriculum, with its own content set by the Ministry of Education. It is not MYP Individuals and Societies, and its materials may not be substituted or added to without prior MoE permission.

subjects.name: Moral, Social and Cultural studies
subjects.levels: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools
subjects.description: Also required by KHDA and taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students. Families regularly confuse its reported marks with Individuals and Societies criterion marks, which is worth sorting out before any tutoring is arranged.

sections.heading: The home-tutoring question, answered straight
paragraphs: A parent searching for a home tutor in Dubai is asking a reasonable question and deserves a direct answer rather than a redirect. In-home tutoring here is a well-established market. Published rates put an in-home one-to-one hour at roughly AED 180 to 500, with a Dubai rate survey clustering most of it at AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors advertising up to AED 500. Monthly in-home packages commonly appear as four two-hour visits. Visits are sold long because the travel is fixed, and in a villa community the drive at 16:30 is not predictable.

There are things an in-home visit genuinely does well. A younger child who will not settle at a screen settles with an adult in the room. A household with no quiet corner gets one by appointment. A tutor who sees a child's desk, their folder and their timetable learns things a video call does not show. None of that is marketing; it is why the market exists and why some families are right to choose it.

For MYP Individuals and Societies the balance tips the other way, and the reason is arithmetic rather than preference. This is a subject group containing at least five disciplines. A student mid-way through a history source enquiry needs someone who can mark provenance analysis. Three months later, in an economics unit, they need someone who can explain why a diagram without a written shift explanation earns almost nothing. The chance that both people live within a short drive of any one Dubai community is small, and the chance that the same person is both is smaller.

So the position here is explicit. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the student's own drafts shared on screen and sessions set in Gulf Standard Time. What a Dubai family gains is the discipline match. What they give up is a person in the room, which for a twelve to sixteen-year-old redrafting a research question is a smaller loss than the in-home market implies.

sections.heading: What is actually inside the subject group
paragraphs: Individuals and Societies draws on history, geography, economics, business management, civics and global politics, and in some schools on sociology, anthropology, philosophy or psychology as well. Units are framed by key concepts, among them time, place and space, systems, change, global interactions and identity, with related concepts specific to each discipline. The result is a course where the content changes shape every term while the assessment criteria stay fixed, which is why students who rely on content revision alone perform unevenly.

Each discipline fails in its own way, and the failures are predictable enough to name. In history, students treat a source as a container of facts rather than as something produced by a person with a purpose, so criterion D stays in the middle of the range however much they know. In geography, they describe a pattern when the task asked them to explain the process generating it, which loses criterion A marks that look like understanding marks. In economics, they draw and label a diagram and stop, when the mark is for the written account of what shifted and why.

In business management, first attempts describe the company rather than applying a concept to it. In civics and politics, students write a case rather than a discussion, which caps criterion D however articulate the case is. Those five patterns cover the large majority of marked humanities work that Dubai families send through, and each has a short, specific fix that transfers to the rest of the course once it is taught.

The practical implication for choosing support is that the discipline of the current unit matters more than the subject-group heading on the report. Before arranging anything, find out what the unit is: the statement of inquiry and the task brief are usually in the student's folder or the school's online platform, and either names the discipline immediately. A tutor who begins by asking for those two documents is a tutor who understands what they are being asked to teach.

sections.heading: The research question: the sentence that carries the marks
paragraphs: Criterion B opens with formulating a clear and focused research question and explaining its relevance. Most MYP students write a topic and call it a question, and almost all of the eventual criterion B loss follows from that one decision. A topic has no answer, so there is nothing to plan towards, no way to choose sources rationally, and no honest evaluation to write at the end. The investigation becomes a report about a subject rather than an answer to a question, and criterion D suffers too, because there is nothing to adjudicate.

A question that works does three things. It names something specific, it names a way of measuring or judging it, and it is bounded in time or place so that the evidence available to a school student is actually sufficient. In history, that usually means one event, one group and one decade. In geography, one location and one indicator. In economics, one market or one policy and one measurable outcome. The test is whether the student can say, in a sentence, what evidence would change their answer. If they cannot, the question is still a topic.

The relevance explanation is a separate strand and a separate mark, and it is the one students skip entirely. It is not a statement that the topic is interesting. It is an argument about why the question is worth answering: what it tells us that we did not know, which debate it sits inside, who the answer matters to. Two or three sentences of genuine justification, written once and taught as a structure, carries into every subsequent investigation the student does.

A tutor's job here is interrogation, not supply. Reasonable moves: ask what exactly the student means by a vague noun, ask how they would know, ask what their answer would be if the evidence pointed the other way, show them a worked example on a question they are not using. Unreasonable moves: hand them a question, or rewrite theirs. Under IB academic honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work, and a question written by a tutor contaminates everything built on it.

sections.heading: Source work: origin, purpose, value, limitation
paragraphs: Criterion D asks students to analyse and evaluate a range of sources or data in terms of origin and purpose, recognising value and limitations. Four words, and they are the whole of what separates a middling humanities student from a strong one in the MYP. The usual first attempt summarises what the source says and then asserts that it is reliable or biased. Neither summary nor assertion earns the strand, because neither is an evaluation.

Origin is who produced the document, when, and in what circumstances. Purpose is why: to persuade, to record, to sell, to justify, to inform a particular audience. Value follows from those two and must be stated as a consequence: because this was written by a participant shortly afterwards, it gives direct access to how the decision was understood at the time. Limitation follows the same way: because the author was defending their own conduct, the account of the alternatives considered is likely to be incomplete.

Written like that, the evaluation does work. The word because is the hinge, and teaching students to require it of themselves is the single most efficient intervention available in this subject group. It takes two or three sessions and it moves criterion D by a mark or two across every unit that follows, which is why it is worth doing early rather than in the weeks before a Year 5 deadline.

Data sources need the same treatment, and students find this harder because a graph looks neutral. Who collected these figures, how, over what period, with what definitions, and who commissioned the collection. A development indicator reported by a government and the same indicator estimated by an external body are different sources with different limitations, and a student who can say why is doing exactly what criterion D asks. Practise on unfamiliar documents rather than ones the class has already discussed, because the strand is about transfer.
bullets: Summary is not evaluation, and reliable or biased is an assertion not an argument

sections.heading: UAE Social Studies, Moral Education and the MYP course: three separate things
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies alongside whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, and this is where families most often become confused about what their child is actually being graded on. These mandatory subjects are set by the Ministry of Education, required by KHDA, reported separately, and are not part of the MYP Individuals and Societies course. A low Social Studies mark and a low Individuals and Societies criterion mark are different problems with different answers.

The requirements are specific and public. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines state that schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter for anyone arranging support. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. And the guidelines state that the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. That is a real constraint on tutoring: legitimate support for UAE Social Studies works from the school's own materials and on study skills, not from substituted content.

There is also a federal baseline worth knowing. UAE government guidance states that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA regulates private education in Dubai; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry. IB Gram holds no approval from any of them and claims none.

sections.heading: Command terms and the shape of a humanities answer
paragraphs: MYP tasks are written with command terms, and in Individuals and Societies the terms do more work than in any other subject group, because the content rarely tells a student what structure to use. Identify, outline, describe, explain, analyse, compare, discuss, evaluate, justify and to what extent all appear, and each demands a different shape. A student who writes the same essay for discuss and for explain will be marked down on one of them without ever being told why.

The crucial boundary in this subject group is between explain and discuss. Explain wants causes and mechanisms, organised and supported: why the migration happened, why the price changed, why the policy produced that outcome. Discuss wants a balanced review in which more than one position is considered and the student reaches a judgement. A beautifully argued one-sided answer to a discuss question is capped, and the student usually believes they wrote a strong response, because they did write a strong response to a different question.

Evaluate and to what extent sit higher still. Both require a judgement and both require the limitations of the evidence to be acknowledged. To what extent in particular invites a graded answer, largely or only in part, rather than a yes or a no, and students who commit to an absolute position lose the strand even when their reasoning is sound. Compare and contrast have their own trap: a paragraph about one case followed by a paragraph about the other is not a comparison, because nothing is held side by side.

The teaching here is mechanical and quick. Take a question the student has already answered, identify the command term, write the shape the term requires as a short plan, and have them re-answer it from the plan. Twenty minutes, one question, and the structure sticks because they can see the difference between their own two versions. Repeated across three or four terms it is worth more marks than any amount of additional content.

sections.heading: From the MYP into Diploma humanities
paragraphs: At the end of MYP Year 5 the subject group splits into named Diploma courses, and the choice is consequential in a way MYP unit selection never is. History, Geography, Economics, Business Management, Global Politics, Psychology and Digital Society all draw on the same four MYP criteria in different proportions. A student whose criterion D marks were strong and whose criterion A marks were ordinary is usually better suited to History or Global Politics, where argument carries the paper. A student with the reverse profile often does better in Geography or Business Management, where structured content and applied method count for more.

What the Diploma assumes, in all of them, is the criterion B skill set: a student who can frame a question, plan an investigation, record sources and evaluate their own process. Every Diploma humanities subject has an internally assessed component that is, in effect, a longer and stricter MYP investigation. The students who struggle in Year 12 are rarely the ones with content gaps; they are the ones who have never independently framed a question and are being asked to do it for marks that count externally.

There is a second thing worth saying plainly, because this market frequently implies otherwise. No tutoring arrangement can promise a university place, and no particular humanities subject guarantees an admission outcome. Entry requirements differ by country, by institution and by programme, and the only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific university. Students in the UAE whose qualifications need Ministry of Education equivalency should check the requirements on the Ministry's own channels rather than relying on any provider's summary.

The useful work in MYP Year 5 therefore has a clear shape. Close the criterion B and D gaps while the stakes are still internal. Write two investigations properly, start to finish, including the evaluation of the process. Get fluent with the command-term distinctions, because Diploma papers apply them far more strictly. A student who arrives in Year 12 able to frame a question and weigh a source has bought themselves two much easier years, whichever subject they choose.
bullets: Diploma humanities subjects weight the same four MYP skills differently

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in an MYP investigation
paragraphs: This subject group is assessed largely through work produced outside the classroom, which makes the academic-honesty boundary more than a formality. IB rules require the work to be the student's own. A tutoring arrangement that crosses that line does not help a Dubai student; it puts their MYP record at risk and leaves them without the skill the task was designed to build. It is worth stating in detail, because the UAE search results for IB support include providers openly selling finished coursework.

Legitimate help is substantial. Teaching the content of a unit. Explaining what a criterion strand means in plain words. Marking a draft and identifying exactly where it falls short. Modelling source evaluation on a document the student is not using. Asking the questions that make a student notice their own missing counter-argument. Teaching a referencing convention and checking a bibliography for completeness and internal consistency. Coaching the planning and reflection behind a Personal Project. All of that leaves authorship untouched.

Illegitimate help is equally clear. Supplying the research question. Choosing and reading the sources on the student's behalf. Providing sentences or paragraphs to be inserted. Restructuring a draft so thoroughly that the voice changes. Writing the evaluation of the process. None of these should ever be offered, and a provider who offers them is selling a risk rather than a service. The test a parent can apply without reading the subject guide is the same one that works everywhere: ask your child to explain any paragraph and why it is there.

Materials follow the same logic. Official IB, Cambridge and Pearson documents are copyright and should reach a student through their school or the board's own site, not through a tutor's file share. For UAE Social Studies the constraint is tighter still, since KHDA's guidelines state that different or additional content requires prior permission from the Ministry of Education. Sessions built on the school's own task briefs, the student's own drafts and published criterion descriptors are both legitimate and more useful, because that is the material being marked.

process.title: Name the discipline, not just the subject group
process.description: Send the current unit's statement of inquiry or task brief. Either names whether this is history, geography, economics, business or civics, which decides who should teach the sessions. Asking for a tutor for Individuals and Societies without that detail is how a capable tutor ends up being the wrong one.

process.title: Send two marked tasks with their criterion sheets
process.description: The criterion sheets tell us which of the four criteria is costing marks and which strand inside it. Two tasks are usually enough. A description of the problem is far less diagnostic than one annotated script, and reading them beforehand means the first session is teaching rather than questions.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the discipline-matched tutor
process.description: One free trial per student, taught by the tutor who would continue, with no card details taken and no obligation. It is a working session on the current task, ending with one small piece of work set. If the discipline match is wrong, a different tutor is proposed at no cost.

process.title: Start with the research question if one is live
process.description: When an investigation is underway, the question comes first regardless of what else looks weak. Everything downstream, the plan, the sources, the argument and the evaluation, inherits the question's faults. Fixing it late means rebuilding work the student has already done.

process.title: Weekly sessions, one small marked task between each
process.description: A single short piece of work set at the end of every session, marked against the named strand and returned with annotations before the next lesson. Small enough to come back: one source evaluation, one paragraph, one action plan. A task that does not come back costs the next session its purpose.

process.title: Switch discipline when the school does
process.description: When the class moves from a history unit to a geography or economics one, the tutor can change with it rather than the student making do. That is only possible because nobody is travelling, and it is the main practical advantage of online delivery in this subject group.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the discipline, not to the subject-group label
whyPoints.description: History source evaluation and economics diagram explanation are different teaching jobs. Because lessons are online, the tutor is chosen from a discipline pool rather than from whoever is within driving distance of your community, which is the specific thing in-home arrangements cannot offer in this subject group.

whyPoints.title: The research question is taught, never supplied
whyPoints.description: Criterion B rewards the student's own question and their explanation of its relevance. We interrogate it, model alternatives on questions they are not using, and send them back to write it. A question handed over by a tutor compromises every mark built on it.

whyPoints.title: Source evaluation taught as a habit with a hinge word
whyPoints.description: Origin, purpose, value and limitation, each written as a consequence rather than a label, with because doing the work. Two or three sessions on this moves criterion D across every unit that follows, which is why we teach it early rather than before a deadline.

whyPoints.title: The UAE mandatory subjects explained accurately
whyPoints.description: Social Studies and Moral Education are separate from MYP Individuals and Societies, required by KHDA, and governed by content rules that limit what any tutor may substitute. We tell families what those rules say rather than selling support that would breach them.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, because we hold none
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and has no office or centre in the UAE. We explain what those bodies do because it is useful; we do not imply they endorse us.

faqs.question: What is actually inside MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: History, geography, economics, business management, civics and global politics, with sociology, anthropology or psychology appearing in some schools. Units are framed by key concepts such as time, place and space, systems, change and global interactions, and reported under one subject-group heading. The content changes shape every term while the four assessment criteria stay fixed, which is why students who revise content alone perform unevenly. For a parent arranging support, the subject-group name on the report is far less useful than the discipline of the current unit, which the statement of inquiry or task brief will name directly.

faqs.question: Is MYP Individuals and Societies history, geography or economics?
faqs.answer: All of them, at different points in the year, which is the single most common misunderstanding about this subject. A Dubai school might run a history unit in the autumn, a geography unit in the spring and an introductory economics unit in Year 4 or 5, reporting one set of criterion marks across the lot. That means a tutor who is excellent for one unit can be the wrong choice for the next. Before booking anything, find the current unit's task brief and establish which discipline it belongs to. Schools that separate the disciplines from MYP Year 4 make this easier, and many Dubai IB schools do.

faqs.question: What does criterion B, investigating, require in MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: Four things, each a separate strand. Formulating a clear and focused research question and explaining its relevance. Formulating and following an action plan to investigate it. Using research methods to collect and record appropriate, varied and relevant information. And evaluating the process and results of the investigation. Most students lose marks on the first and the last. They write a topic instead of a question, which leaves nothing to plan towards, and they skip the evaluation because it feels like admitting failure when it is in fact an explicitly marked strand. Both are quick to fix once someone shows them the shape.

faqs.question: How is a source-analysis answer marked in MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: Under criterion D, which asks students to analyse and evaluate sources or data in terms of origin and purpose, recognising value and limitations. Summarising the content earns nothing, and asserting that a source is reliable or biased earns nothing either, because neither is an evaluation. The mark comes from stating value and limitation as consequences: because this was written by a participant shortly afterwards, it shows how the decision was understood at the time; because the author was defending their own conduct, the account of alternatives is probably incomplete. The word because is doing the work, and teaching students to demand it of themselves is the fastest gain in the subject.

faqs.question: Do Dubai home tutors cover MYP Individuals and Societies or only exam subjects?
faqs.answer: The in-home market in Dubai is strongest in mathematics and the sciences, and thinner in humanities, thinner still if you need a specific discipline. Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and visits are usually sold as two-hour sittings because travel has to be recovered. The practical problem is not price but matching: finding someone within a reasonable drive who can mark a historical source evaluation this term and an economics diagram next term is unlikely. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; lessons are one-to-one over live video, which is what makes the discipline match possible.

faqs.question: How does MYP Individuals and Societies sit alongside the UAE Social Studies my child must take?
faqs.answer: They are separate subjects, separately taught and separately reported. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with content set by the Ministry of Education. MYP Individuals and Societies is the IB course, assessed on four criteria out of eight each. Families regularly read a weak Social Studies mark as a humanities problem, or the reverse. They need different responses. KHDA's guidelines also state that different or additional content for the mandatory subjects requires prior MoE permission, so legitimate support there works from the school's own materials.

faqs.question: Where do MYP Individuals and Societies students lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: In five predictable places, one per discipline. In history, reading a source for content rather than asking who produced it and why. In geography, describing a pattern when the task asked for the process behind it. In economics, drawing and labelling a diagram without the written account of what shifted. In business management, describing the company instead of applying a concept to it. In civics and politics, writing a persuasive one-sided case where the command term asked for a discussion. Each has a short fix that transfers to the rest of the course, which is why a diagnostic read of two marked tasks is worth more than a term of general revision.

faqs.question: What is a research question in MYP Individuals and Societies and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It is the sentence the student writes to define their own investigation, and criterion B marks both the question and an explanation of its relevance. It matters because everything downstream inherits its faults. A topic rather than a question leaves nothing to plan towards, no rational basis for choosing sources, and no honest evaluation to write. A workable question names something specific, names how it will be measured or judged, and is bounded in time or place so that the available evidence is sufficient. The test: can the student say what evidence would change their answer. If not, it is still a topic.

faqs.question: Does MYP Individuals and Societies lead anywhere in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Directly into History, Geography, Economics, Business Management, Global Politics, Psychology and Digital Society, each of which draws on the same four MYP skills in different proportions. A student strong on criterion D and ordinary on criterion A usually suits History or Global Politics, where argument carries the paper; the reverse profile often does better in Geography or Business Management. Every one of those Diploma courses has an internally assessed component that is essentially a longer, stricter MYP investigation, so criterion B independence is the skill that transfers most. No subject choice guarantees any university outcome, and entry requirements should be checked on the institution's own admissions pages.

faqs.question: How much writing does MYP Individuals and Societies actually involve?
faqs.answer: More than most Dubai families expect, and the volume rises sharply from MYP Year 3. A typical year includes two or three extended investigations, several source-based responses, at least one case study or data analysis, and in Year 5 the Personal Project running alongside. Criterion C explicitly marks style appropriate to audience and purpose, structure appropriate to the format, and sources documented by a recognised convention, so written presentation is assessed rather than incidental. This is why a student weak in written English loses humanities marks that look like understanding marks, and why fixing the writing often lifts several subjects at once.

faqs.question: What are global contexts and key concepts in MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: They are the framing devices the MYP uses instead of a prescribed content list. Key concepts in this subject group include time, place and space, systems, change, global interactions and identity, and each unit also carries related concepts specific to its discipline, such as causation in history or sustainability in geography. Global contexts set the real-world lens, for example fairness and development or globalisation and sustainability. For a student the practical consequence is that unit titles describe a concept rather than a topic, so the same body of history can appear under quite different headings in two Dubai schools.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both MYP Individuals and Societies and the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a sensible pairing, because the Personal Project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, which are close relatives of criterion B. A tutor who has taught investigation design can coach the process journal, the goal setting and the reflection without touching the product. The boundary has to be explicit: Personal Project support is process coaching only. Nobody should be producing the outcome, writing the report or selecting the student's sources. The arrangement works best when the same person sees both pieces of work, because the habits that weaken one usually weaken the other.

faqs.question: Does my child need to memorise content for MYP Individuals and Societies?
faqs.answer: Some, but much less than in a content-examined system, and this surprises families arriving from Indian or British curricula. Criterion A asks for terminology used in context and for content and concepts demonstrated through description, explanation and example, so facts are needed as evidence rather than as recall for its own sake. The other three criteria reward investigation, communication and critical thinking. A student who memorises a unit and cannot frame a question or evaluate a source will sit in the middle of the range however much they know, which is the commonest profile in the marked work Dubai families send us.

faqs.question: How is criterion D, thinking critically, different from criterion A?
faqs.answer: Criterion A asks whether the student knows and understands the material: can they use the terminology correctly and explain the content with examples. Criterion D asks what they do with it: discuss concepts and issues, synthesise information into a valid argument, evaluate sources by origin and purpose, and interpret different perspectives and their implications. A student can score 7 on A and 3 on D, and that is the most common split in Dubai MYP humanities. It means the knowledge is there and the argument is not. The response is structural practice in weighing positions, not more content teaching.

faqs.question: What does a good MYP Individuals and Societies session actually do for 60 minutes?
faqs.answer: It opens with the tutor naming the criterion strand being targeted, having read the marked task beforehand rather than during the lesson. The middle forty minutes are the student writing: their own script on a shared screen, the strand descriptor read aloud, the student identifying what they have not met, then rewriting it live. Content is taught briefly where a real gap appears. The last ten minutes set one small task, deliberately small so it comes back, to be marked against the same strand before the next session. What it does not do is cover a topic, which is a lecture rather than a lesson.

faqs.question: Is MYP Individuals and Societies easier than IGCSE History?
faqs.answer: Different rather than easier, and students moving between them in Dubai feel the difference sharply in both directions. IGCSE History rewards content coverage and timed examination technique against a defined syllabus with past papers available. MYP Individuals and Societies rewards independent investigation, source evaluation and written communication across a shifting set of disciplines, assessed on four criteria with no past papers to work through. A student who thrives on structure and revision often finds IGCSE more comfortable; one who writes well and thinks independently usually prefers the MYP. Neither is a softer option, and the skills they build are only partly the same.

dubai/ib-myp-individuals-and-societies-t.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach MYP Individuals and Societies across the history, geography and economics disciplines, for MYP Years 1 to 5. Each marks against the published criterion strands, returns annotated work between sessions, and keeps a dated record of which strand was targeted and what it scored.

intro.heading: How you will know whether the tutoring is working
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements are judged on feeling. The sessions seem useful, the tutor is pleasant, the child is less anxious on Sunday evening. Three months later a report arrives with the same number on it as before and nobody can say what happened. For an IB MYP Individuals and Societies tutor in Dubai that is an avoidable outcome, because the MYP produces more written evidence of progress than almost any other secondary programme. The criterion sheets exist. The drafts exist. The question is whether anybody is keeping them in order.

Individuals and Societies is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, criterion B is investigating, criterion C is communicating, and criterion D is thinking critically. Each has its own strands, and a teacher awards a best-fit mark strand by strand on every assessed task. That means a Dubai MYP student generates, across a year, perhaps eight to twelve separate criterion judgements in this subject alone. Laid out chronologically, those judgements are a progress graph that costs nothing to assemble.

What that graph usually shows is not a smooth line. A student who starts weekly support in October with criterion D sitting at 3 might see D move to 5 by December while criterion A stays at 6 and criterion C drops a mark because they are experimenting with a harder structure. The overall grade on the January report may be identical to the November one. Nothing has gone wrong. A grade is a band derived from a 32-mark total, and a four-mark gain inside band 5 does not become a 6. Without the criterion record, that term looks like a waste of money. With it, it looks exactly like what it is.

The second kind of evidence is the drafts themselves. An MYP investigation is not a one-pass piece of work, and the research question a student starts with is almost never the one they should end with. A tutor's annotations on draft one, draft two and draft three are the clearest record of teaching that exists: you can see the research question narrow, the action plan acquire dates, the sources acquire an evaluation of origin and purpose, the argument acquire a counter-position. Parents who ask for one thing from a tutor should ask for the annotated drafts to be kept.

The third kind is the between-session work, and it is the one that distinguishes support that moves marks from support that fills an hour. One small task, set at the end of a session, marked before the next one, against the same strand the school uses. Small tasks come back; large ones do not. Over twelve weeks that produces a dozen marked pieces, each with a strand name attached, and the pattern in them tells a family whether to continue, reduce or stop long before a school report arrives to confirm it.

All of this happens over live video, one-to-one, with the student's own documents shared on screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. The practical benefit for this subject is specific: Individuals and Societies covers history, geography and economics, and a tutor who can mark a historical source evaluation is not necessarily the right person for an economics investigation. Choosing by discipline rather than by driving distance is what makes the evidence worth reading.

programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools vary widely in how much of the portfolio parents actually see. Families moving towards the MYP should ask to look at it before Year 6 ends, because the research and reflection habits recorded there are the ones MYP criterion B will later mark formally, and the gap between a strong PYP exhibition and a weak first MYP investigation is usually one of format rather than ability.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The most measurable of the four programmes from a parent's point of view. sections.heading: The evidence a Dubai MYP family already has, and what each piece proves
paragraphs: Before any tutoring begins, a Dubai MYP household typically holds five kinds of document, and together they answer most questions a parent has about Individuals and Societies. The returned assessed task with the teacher's annotations. The criterion sheet attached to it. The unit's statement of inquiry and task brief. The termly or semester report with the four criterion grades or a single subject grade. And, in Year 5, the Personal Project process journal. Very few families have these in one place, and almost none have them in date order.

Putting them in order is the first hour of useful work, and it does not require a tutor. Chronological order reveals trends that individual documents conceal. A criterion D mark of 4, 3, 5, 3 across four tasks is not a weakness, it is a volatility, and volatility usually means the student does well on units that interest them and poorly on the rest. A criterion C mark of 6, 5, 4, 4 is a decline, and declines in communicating almost always track a change in task format rather than a loss of ability.

What each document can and cannot prove is worth being precise about. A report grade proves which band a 32-mark total fell into and nothing else; it cannot show movement inside a band, which is where most of a term's progress lives. A criterion sheet proves which strands a teacher judged met and unmet on one task. An annotated draft proves what changed between versions, which is the only direct evidence that teaching had an effect. And a between-session task marked by a tutor proves whether the teaching transferred to new work, which is the question that actually matters.

sections.heading: Reading a criterion sheet for Individuals and Societies
paragraphs: The four criteria in this subject group are specific enough that a parent can work out what went wrong from the strand wording alone. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, asks the student to use terminology in context and to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of subject-specific content and concepts through descriptions, explanations and examples. Criterion B, investigating, asks them to formulate a clear and focused research question and explain its relevance, to formulate and follow an action plan, to use research methods to collect and record appropriate and varied information, and to evaluate the process and results of the investigation.

Criterion C, communicating, asks for information and ideas communicated in a style appropriate to audience and purpose, structured appropriately to the specified format, with sources documented using a recognised convention. Criterion D, thinking critically, asks the student to discuss concepts, issues, models and theories, to synthesise information to make valid arguments, to analyse and evaluate a range of sources or data in terms of origin and purpose while recognising value and limitations, and to interpret different perspectives and their implications.

Read those four together and the diagnostic pattern is clear. A student can be strong on A and weak on D, which means they know the material and are not yet arguing with it. They can be strong on D and weak on C, which means they think well and present badly, usually a referencing and structure problem rather than a thinking one. They can be strong on everything except B, which means they can respond to a question someone else set but cannot yet frame their own. Each of those three profiles needs entirely different teaching, and each is visible on a single criterion sheet.

The strand language also tells you what evidence to demand from a tutor. If criterion D's weakest strand is analysing and evaluating sources by origin and purpose, then the between-session task should be a source evaluation, marked against that strand, and the improvement should be visible as a sentence that names provenance and limitation. Anything vaguer than that, from either the school or a tutor, is not evidence of progress on criterion D.
