sections.heading: Five years, not five sessions: what each MYP year actually costs
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme runs five years, and a family that budgets it as one is nearly always surprised twice: once in MYP 3, when the criteria stop being forgiving, and once in MYP 5, when the Personal Project and the sixteen-plus decision arrive in the same term. The table below spreads the spend across the sequence using the mid-market qualified rate, because that is the tier most Dubai Middle Years families end up on, and because using the specialist rate across five years produces a number nobody should pay.

The pattern that falls out of it is worth stating plainly. MYP 1 and MYP 2 are cheap years in which small amounts of the right support prevent expensive years later; the work is written stamina, note-taking and learning what a descriptor is. MYP 3 and MYP 4 are the content years, where subject knowledge starts to carry real weight and where a weekly slot in one or two subject groups is the standard shape. MYP 5 is the most expensive year in the programme, and it is the one families routinely under-budget because it looks like the end rather than the pivot.

Two caveats about reading the monthly column. First, it assumes one subject group, not three; a household running maths and sciences together is doubling or tripling it. Second, it assumes a term of consistent weekly sessions rather than a panic block, which costs the same per hour and less in total. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai, read in October 2026, run AED 240-600 at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, which brackets the figures below.

sections.heading: Buying by criterion rather than by hour
paragraphs: An hour is a unit of selling. A criterion is the unit the school reports on. Every Middle Years subject group is marked against four criteria, each on a nought-to-eight scale, and the grade your child brings home is a conversion of those totals rather than an average of test scores. If you buy hours, you cannot tell whether the money worked. If you buy against a criterion, you can: the next marked task either moves a band or it does not, and the task sheet names which criterion it was.

This reframing is the cheapest improvement available to a Dubai Middle Years family, and it costs nothing. Before booking, ask the school which criteria the next assessed task covers. Then brief the tutor on that criterion and nothing else. The table below gives the shape across the four letters as they appear in most subject groups, with the characteristic Dubai failure and a realistic number of sessions to move one band. The letters carry different names in different subject groups; the structure holds.

Confirm the criterion letters and the current grade boundaries with your child's subject teacher or the school's IB coordinator, because task-specific descriptors are written by the school and bands are set against the programme's published conversion. We are describing the mechanism, not publishing your school's figures. That distinction matters for the same reason the rate table names its sources: a number without a date and an owner is worth less than no number at all.

sections.heading: Eight subject groups, one timetable, and where a tight budget should go first
paragraphs: Dubai Middle Years students carry eight subject groups plus interdisciplinary units plus the mandatory UAE subjects their school is required to teach. No family can tutor all of that and none should try. The question is not which subject is weakest but which subject's criteria respond fastest to coaching, because a band gained in six weeks changes the student's confidence and a band gained in six months does not.

The honest ranking is roughly this. Language and Literature moves first, because criterion A analysis is teachable in marked paragraphs and the feedback loop is a week long. Mathematics moves next, because criteria C and D are structural and the content is usually already there. Sciences take longer because criterion B is a design skill rather than a knowledge gap. Individuals and Societies sits with Sciences. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education rarely justify paid hours in isolation, though they routinely drag a composite report down and are worth one session to diagnose.

Interdisciplinary units deserve a line of their own. They are separately reported, they are owned by no single teacher, and they are the mark most commonly left to chance in a Dubai Middle Years report. Thirty minutes of explicit synthesis practice before each unit deadline is one of the highest-return half-hours a family can buy in the whole programme, and almost nobody buys it because nobody tells parents the strand exists. Ask the school when the next interdisciplinary unit is assessed and which two subject groups it draws on; both facts are usually on the unit planner and neither tends to reach the parent.

sections.heading: What else the same Dubai evening could buy
paragraphs: Tutoring is bought against alternatives, and most Dubai families compare it against nothing. The table below sets one-to-one online support beside the other things that occupy a Middle Years student's weekday evening and a household's monthly outgoings, using figures published by the providers themselves and read in October 2026. The point is not that one is better. It is that AED 800 a month is a choice between things, and the choice should be made with the numbers visible.

The context number that belongs in this conversation is school fees. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a Middle Years family that is a genuinely useful planning fact: the largest education line in the household budget is flat for a year, which is the year to decide whether a weekly tutoring slot is affordable on a stable base rather than a rising one.

The second context number is the market's own shape. Dubai had 387,441 private school students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. The Middle Years cohort is therefore a minority inside a very large market, which is precisely why local in-home tutor supply for MYP-specific criterion work is thinner than it is for International GCSE, and why the online pool matters more here than the neighbourhood pool.

sections.heading: Gulf Standard Time, the school run, and the cost of a badly placed slot
paragraphs: The least discussed driver of Middle Years tutoring cost in Dubai is the clock. A session at 4pm competes with nothing and tends to be available at the lower end of whatever tier you are buying. A session at 7.30pm competes with every working parent in the emirate, and the price follows the scarcity. If your child can be at a desk by 4.15pm two days a week, you are shopping in a cheaper market than a family that can only do 8pm, for exactly the same teaching.

Villa communities with long bus routes and apartment households with two commutes end up at the expensive end of the evening by default. There are two ways out of it that cost nothing. The first is the weekend: Saturday mornings are the most underused hours in the Dubai tutoring week and the easiest slot to hold for a whole term. The second is the split session: two 45-minute slots a week outperform one 90-minute slot for criterion work, because the feedback loop closes twice.

Online delivery also widens the tutor pool across time zones, which is where availability stops being a local supply problem. A Middle Years sciences specialist working from India or the United Kingdom can take a 5pm Gulf Standard Time booking without travelling, which is the mechanism behind the gap between the online and in-home columns in the rate table. Ramadan shifts the whole pattern: sessions move to late morning or after Iftar, and families who plan that in advance keep their slot rather than losing the term.

sections.heading: The Personal Project year is a separate budget line
paragraphs: In MYP 5 every student completes the Personal Project: a self-directed piece of work with a process journal and a report, assessed against its own criteria and reported separately from any subject group. It is the single most common reason a Dubai family who had never bought tutoring suddenly needs some, and it is also the piece of work where the boundary between help and malpractice is narrowest.

What a tutor may legitimately do is teachable and specific. They may help the student choose a goal that is achievable in the time available. They may teach project management, research method, note-taking and referencing. They may ask the questions that make a vague goal measurable. They may read the student's own draft and give feedback against the criteria, and they may teach the student to self-assess against those criteria. They may coach the oral presentation and the reflection.

What a tutor must never do is supply any part of the assessed work. Not a paragraph of the report, not an entry in the process journal, not a product the student then presents as their own. The IB's academic honesty rules make that an expulsion risk for the student and it is not a service we sell at any price. One competitor in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure sum; that is not a cheaper version of tutoring, it is a different and much more expensive mistake. Budget the Personal Project as three to five sessions of process coaching, spread across the checkpoints the school sets.

sections.heading: The second bill: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's published requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Middle Years family this is not a footnote. It is three subjects that sit outside the eight subject groups, are reported on, and are the most common source of a tutoring bill that was never budgeted.

The organisational rules are specific and they explain why finding help is harder than it looks. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further constraints matter for anyone buying support. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. In practice that means tutoring in these subjects is school-material work: a tutor supports the student with the content the school is required to use, rather than importing a parallel scheme. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes.

sections.heading: Is the money working? What to check at six weeks
paragraphs: Six weeks is roughly six sessions, and it is long enough to tell. The check is not whether your child says the tutor is nice, and it is not whether the homework is done. It is whether a marked task has moved a criterion band, and if it has not, whether you can see what the tutor was working on and why it should have. Either answer is useful. The one unacceptable state is not knowing.

Four things should exist by week six. A written diagnosis from the first session that names criteria rather than topics. Session notes that reference the criterion letter and the task. At least two marked pieces of the student's own work with the descriptor visible beside the feedback. And a stated next step that is specific enough to be wrong. If all four exist and nothing has moved, the diagnosis was probably wrong and the fix is a different subject group or a different criterion, not more hours.

If none of the four exist, you are paying for company rather than teaching, and that is true at AED 45 an hour and at AED 650 an hour. This is also the point at which a Dubai family should ask the question nobody asks at the start: is the tutor legally permitted to teach privately here? Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, the official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service with a two-working-day completion time, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so nobody should be quoting you an amount.
bullets: A written diagnosis naming criteria, produced after the first session
Session notes that reference the criterion letter and the assessed task
Two or more marked pieces of the student's own work with feedback against the descriptor
A next step specific enough that you could tell if it failed
A straight answer about the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit

sections.heading: How these lessons actually run, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Sessions are one-to-one, live, over video, on a shared screen with a writing surface both people can use. The student works and the tutor watches them work, which is the part that cannot be replaced by a recording or a worksheet. Scheduling is on Gulf Standard Time against your child's own school calendar, and the material is your child's own unit planner, task sheet and marked work. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India, and this page's comparison tables exist so that the trade is visible rather than buried.

There are things this page will not tell you, and the omissions are deliberate. We do not publish an IB exam or results date, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date on a landing page that turns out to be wrong is worse than no date. Confirm every IB session date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. We do not hold KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, approval or partnership, and we do not describe ourselves as if we did; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific document issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and we do not operate premises in the UAE.

We also make no promises about any grade, publish no satisfaction percentages, and show no star rating we cannot evidence with real, dated, attributable reviews. What we will commit to is narrower and checkable: a diagnosis in writing, work against the criterion the school is about to assess, feedback on your child's own drafts, and a straight answer when no specialist is available for a niche subject group rather than a match made to fill a slot. If a Middle Years subject has no suitable tutor free in the window you need, we will say so, say when that changes, and not take the booking in the meantime.

process.title: Send the report and the task sheet
process.description: Not a description of the problem: the actual documents. A Middle Years report with criterion marks and the task sheet for the next assessed piece tell a tutor more in five minutes than a half-hour phone call. If the school publishes the unit planner, send that too.

process.title: Take the trial lesson
process.description: One lesson at no charge per family, with no card required to book it. It is a diagnostic rather than a sample lesson: the tutor works the student through a task and reports which criteria are actually costing marks, which is frequently not the subject the parent named.

process.title: Agree the scope and the price in writing
process.description: Session length, number of sessions, which criterion is being targeted, cancellation terms and whether VAT applies to the quoted figure. Put all five in a message before the second session. A quote that cannot survive being written down is not a quote.

process.title: Hold one fixed slot across the term
process.description: Consistency outperforms intensity in the Middle Years, because criterion work needs a feedback loop rather than a cram. Pick the earliest hour your household can actually sustain, which is usually cheaper as well as better attended, and defend it against everything short of exams.

process.title: Review at six weeks against the criteria
process.description: Read the marked work, not the invoice. Has a criterion band moved, and if not, does the tutor's own reasoning explain why? Change the target or the tutor at that point rather than at the end of the year, when the term you paid for is already gone.

process.title: Rescope at each MYP boundary
process.description: What worked in MYP 2 is wrong for MYP 4, and MYP 5 needs its own plan for the Personal Project and the sixteen-plus decision. Treat each boundary as a fresh diagnosis rather than a continuation, and expect the budget shape to change with it.

whyPoints.title: Prices with owners and dates attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six best-ranking competitor pages for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A number without a source is not information.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-led, not topic-led
whyPoints.description: Middle Years grades come from four criteria marked nought to eight against task-specific descriptors, so that is what sessions target. Buying topic revision when the loss is in criterion B or D is the most common way Dubai families waste tutoring money without noticing.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. You are told that before you book, not after, and the cost consequence is in the tables above.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty as a boundary, not a disclaimer
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own draft. Assessed work stays the student's own, which on the Personal Project is the difference between support and an expulsion risk. We say where the line is rather than leaving it to be discovered.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, including when it is bad
whyPoints.description: If no suitable tutor is free for a niche Middle Years subject group in your window, we say so and say when that changes. Filling a slot with whoever is available costs a family a term and is the failure mode nobody in this market admits to.

whyPoints.title: Regulator facts cited, never borrowed as credentials
whyPoints.description: KHDA, MoHRE and Ministry of Education requirements are described with their source so a parent can check them. We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them and operate no premises in the UAE, which is why none of this page claims otherwise.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP online tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai span roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, and Middle Years work usually sits in the AED 150 to AED 300 band. Tutopiya lists from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the platform end; Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200; TutorChase lists AED 270; BartyED lists AED 650 at the premium end. All read October 2026, all theirs rather than ours. Middle Years tutoring rarely needs the specialist tier, because MYP 1 to MYP 4 carry no external examination. Our own quote depends on subject group, year and session count, and is agreed in writing after the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start Middle Years tutoring in MYP 2 or wait until MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Starting earlier is cheaper in total and almost always cheaper per band moved. MYP 1 and MYP 2 problems are mechanical: no system for eight task sheets, weak written stamina, no idea what a descriptor is. Those take a handful of sessions. The same student in MYP 5 is carrying four years of the same habits into the Personal Project and the sixteen-plus decision at once, which is why MYP 5 is the most expensive year in the programme. Waiting does not avoid the spend; it concentrates it into the year with the least room to absorb it.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours does one MYP criterion realistically need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the letter. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is usually the student's strongest and often needs nothing. Criterion C, communicating, typically moves a band in two or three sessions because the problem is form rather than knowledge. Criterion B, investigating, takes three or four, since designing an inquiry is a skill rather than a fact. Criterion D, thinking critically, is the slowest at three to five, because evaluation has to be built as a habit. Those are working estimates across subject groups, not guarantees, and the band your school awards depends on its own task-specific descriptors.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject group gives the best return on tutoring spend?
faqs.answer: Language and Literature, in most cases. Criterion A analysis is teachable in marked paragraphs, the feedback loop is a week long, and movement shows on the next assessed task rather than next term. Mathematics is second, because the content is usually already present and the loss sits in communication and interpretation. Sciences and Individuals and Societies take a term, since the weak criterion is a design or evaluation skill. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education rarely justify paid hours alone, though one diagnostic session is worth buying when a composite grade drops without explanation.

faqs.question: Do I pay more for a tutor who has read my child's school unit plans?
faqs.answer: No, and you should expect it as standard rather than as a premium. Working from the live unit planner and task sheet is what makes Middle Years tutoring effective, because the descriptors are task-specific and written by the school. What reading them does change is the number of paid hours you need: a tutor who already has the document spends the first session teaching rather than diagnosing. Send the report, the task sheet and the unit planner before the trial lesson. It is the cheapest thing you can do to lower the total bill.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project year cost more in tutoring than MYP 4?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for three reasons that stack in the same year. The Personal Project is a separate assessed strand needing its own process coaching, typically three to five sessions across the school's checkpoints. Subject groups are simultaneously at their heaviest. And the sixteen-plus decision between continuing to the Diploma or moving to International GCSE or A Level often needs its own diagnostic work. Budget MYP 5 as the peak year of the programme rather than its wind-down. A tutor may coach process, method and self-assessment, but may never supply any part of the assessed work itself.

faqs.question: What does eAssessment preparation add to a Dubai family's tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: Only some Dubai schools enter students for end-of-programme eAssessment, so the first step costs nothing: ask your school's IB coordinator whether your child is being entered, and for which subject groups. Where it applies, it introduces on-screen examinations and ePortfolio requirements that differ in format from everything the student has done for four years, and format practice is the spend. Expect a short block rather than a term, concentrated in the months before the window. Where the school does not enter students, the programme remains internally assessed and no separate preparation budget is needed.

faqs.question: Do we have to pay separately for Arabic and Islamic Education support?
faqs.answer: If you need it, yes, and it is the most commonly unbudgeted line in a Dubai Middle Years household. All Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies whatever their licensed curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of 2025-26. These sit outside the eight subject groups and are reported separately. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes, so support has to match the right stream and work from the school's own prescribed material.

faqs.question: Is a 45-minute online session cheaper per criterion than a 90-minute one?
faqs.answer: Two 45-minute sessions a week usually outperform one 90-minute session at the same total cost, for criterion work specifically. The reason is the feedback loop: the student attempts something, gets it marked against the descriptor, revises it and attempts again. That cycle closes twice in two short sessions and once in one long one. Ninety-minute sessions earn their place for investigations, Personal Project work and anything needing a long run at one document. For weekly descriptor coaching in MYP 1 to MYP 3, split the time.

faqs.question: Why does a 7pm slot in Dubai cost more than a 4pm one?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, not quality. Every working parent in the emirate wants the same two hours of the evening, so the late slots fill first and clear at the top of whatever tier you are buying. A 4.15pm start competes with almost nothing. The two cheapest moves available to a Dubai household are therefore the earliest sustainable weekday hour and Saturday morning, which is the most underused window in the Dubai tutoring week. Online delivery also removes travel from the equation entirely, which is why the online column in our rate table sits below the in-home one.

faqs.question: Can two siblings in different MYP years share one tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: They can share a tutor and a weekly rhythm, but not a session. Criterion coaching is descriptor work on one student's own task sheet, and two children in MYP 2 and MYP 4 are working to different descriptors in different subject groups. What does work across a household is sequencing: one sibling on a weekly slot while the other runs deadline blocks, then swapping as the terms demand. Families in mixed-curriculum neighbourhoods like Mirdif and Al Warqa often run this pattern, because one tutor can hold both children's calendars without pretending the programmes are the same.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai 2026-27 fee freeze change what tutoring should cost?
faqs.answer: It does not change tutoring rates, but it changes the planning. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a Middle Years family that means the largest education line in the household budget is flat for a year, which makes it a sensible year to commit to a steady weekly slot rather than panic blocks. It is also useful context for judging a quote: a tutoring bill is being set against a stable fee base, not a rising one.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Dubai better value than one-to-one online?
faqs.answer: Per head, a group of two to four costs roughly a third to a half of the one-to-one rate, which is real money. Per criterion, it is usually slower, because descriptor work depends on one student's own task sheet and a group has to share attention. Groups suit content revision and exam-style drilling. They suit Middle Years criterion coaching badly. A centre also adds travel at the Dubai hours when travel is slowest, and a centre with premises needs a different permission from an individual tutor, which is worth asking about before paying.

faqs.question: What should I put in writing before paying a Dubai Middle Years tutor?
faqs.answer: Five things, in one message, before the second session. The session length and the rate for it. The number of sessions you are committing to. Which criterion or criteria the work is targeting, named by letter. The cancellation and rescheduling terms. And whether the quoted figure includes VAT. Ask separately whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which individuals providing private lessons in the UAE require under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and which is granted free of charge for two years. A quote that cannot survive being written down is not a quote.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether MYP tutoring is actually worth the money yet?
faqs.answer: Check at six weeks, and check the marked work rather than the invoice. Four things should exist: a written diagnosis naming criteria rather than topics, session notes referencing the criterion letter and the assessed task, at least two marked pieces of your child's own work with feedback against the descriptor, and a next step specific enough that you could tell if it failed. If all four exist and nothing has moved, the target was wrong and should change. If none exist, you are paying for company rather than teaching, at any hourly rate.

dubai/ib-myp-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then decide what to spend
dubai/ib-myp-online-tutor.closingBody: The useful order is diagnosis, then budget, then hours. Send your child's Middle Years report, the task sheet for the next assessed piece and the unit planner if the school publishes it. Take the trial lesson, which is one per family and needs no card, and read what comes back: which criteria are actually costing marks, in which subject groups, and what it would take to move them. Then set a figure against the year your child is in rather than against the whole programme. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the terms go in writing before a second session is booked.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below have supervised or taught MYP year five students through the Personal Project and the MYP subject groups that feed it. Each profile names the subject groups the tutor teaches and whether they work on projects, reports or both, so you can match on the part of the project that is actually stuck.

intro.heading: The product is not the project
paragraphs: Almost every Dubai family who searches for Personal Project help arrives at the same point in the year with the same problem. The product exists. There is a website, a short film, a prototype, a recipe book, a fundraising event that happened, a coded app that runs. And the mark is going to be low, because none of the three criteria the Personal Project is assessed against asks whether the product is good. They ask whether the student planned it, applied identifiable skills to it, and can reflect on it with evidence. A beautiful product with an empty process journal scores badly, and a modest product with a rigorous journal scores well.

That is counter-intuitive for a fifteen-year-old and for most parents, and nobody explains it clearly in the first term. The Personal Project is the culminating piece of the Middle Years Programme, usually completed in MYP year five, which in a Dubai school is Year 11 or Grade 10 depending on the school's naming. It is assessed against criterion A for planning, criterion B for applying skills, and criterion C for reflecting. Each is marked from zero to eight, giving twenty-four marks that the school converts to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries.

Where the project goes wrong is predictable enough to list. The learning goal is too broad to measure, so criterion A cannot be awarded in the top band. The success criteria are written after the product is finished, which the process journal gives away. The journal has four entries, all from the final fortnight. The report describes what happened rather than evaluating it against the criteria the student themselves set. And the global context is chosen because it sounded relevant, not because it frames the inquiry.

All of that is fixable, and it is fixable faster than parents expect, because it is not a knowledge problem. A student who can explain their own project out loud usually has the material for a strong report and has never been shown what the report is for. Two or three sessions on criterion wording, one on restructuring the journal evidence, and one on the reflection section tends to be the whole intervention.

What a tutor will not do is write it. The Personal Project must be the student's own work, every school requires an academic honesty form signed by the student and the supervisor, and the IB treats work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice with the consequence falling on the student. A tutor here reads, questions, explains a criterion in plain words and comments on a draft. The student does the writing, every time.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video with the document on a shared screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, because that is an India-only service, and for project work the online format is genuinely better: the journal, the draft and the criteria are on the screen in front of both people and the comments stay in the file afterwards.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.programmesIntro: The Personal Project sits at the end of a continuum, and what a Dubai student brings to it depends on where they joined. The three programmes below are the stages the project draws on, with the part of each that shows up in a project report.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP ends with the Exhibition, a collaborative inquiry presented to the school community. Students who did a real Exhibition arrive at the Personal Project already understanding that an inquiry has a question, evidence and a presentation. Students who joined later have usually never been assessed on process at all, which is the gap worth naming early.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run the full IB continuum from PYP through to the Diploma, and others admit students into the MYP from British or Indian curricula at Year 7 or Year 9. A student who arrived in Year 9 is attempting the Personal Project with two years of criterion marking rather than eight, and that is a scheduling fact rather than a weakness.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked zero to eight, plus the Approaches to Learning skills framework that the Personal Project is built to demonstrate. The project is the only piece of MYP work where the student chooses the goal, which is exactly why planning and reflection carry the marks rather than content knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools the Personal Project is normally completed across MYP year five with a submission date set well before the end of the academic year, so the real deadline sits in the second term. Schools entering students for MYP certification send a sample of projects for external moderation, so the school's internal mark is not always the final one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Extended Essay is four thousand words of independent research, assessed against criteria, with a supervisor and a reflection requirement. It is the Personal Project again with higher stakes, which is why a student who learned to keep a journal in MYP year five has a measurable advantage.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai IB schools frequently use Personal Project performance as part of the conversation about Diploma subject levels, not as a formal entry requirement but as evidence of whether a student can run an independent piece of work. A student heading for Higher Level sciences and an Extended Essay benefits more from a well-journalled project than from a polished product.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.subjectsIntro: A Personal Project is not in a subject, but it draws on one or two, and the skills it has to demonstrate come from the eight MYP subject groups. Below is what each group contributes and the kind of project goal it supports well.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The group that trains the writing the report depends on. Projects anchored here include a short story collection, a bilingual anthology or a podcast series. The common failure is a student who writes well describing their process beautifully and never evaluating it against their own success criteria.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Phases rather than years, so a Dubai student may sit Arabic, French or Spanish at a different phase from their year group. Projects here work when the goal is a measurable language outcome, such as a recorded interview series conducted entirely in the target language.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography, economics and civics. The strongest source of assessable Personal Project goals, because the group trains the use of sources and the framing of a question. A project on labour conditions, water use or urban heat in the Gulf sits naturally here.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion B in the sciences already demands a method and controlled variables, which transfers directly. A science-led project needs a measurable outcome rather than an experiment for its own sake: a tested prototype, a measured result, a documented iteration.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Undervalued as a project base. A data-led project with a real dataset, a stated method and an honest account of what the numbers cannot show scores well on reflection, because the limitations are concrete rather than invented at the end.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Visual art, music, drama and film. The group where products are most often excellent and journals most often thin, because artists tend to work rather than document. Fixing that is usually a matter of photographing stages and dating them as the work happens.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Supports goals built on a training plan, a nutrition study or a coaching programme run for younger students. The assessable element is the plan and the measured change, not the personal fitness result, and that distinction is where marks are usually recovered.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The closest subject group to the Personal Project in structure, with its own inquiry, development, creation and evaluation cycle. A design-led student usually understands iteration and needs help only with the reflection criterion and the report's word discipline.

subjects.name: Approaches to Learning skills
subjects.description: The ten ATL skill clusters across thinking, communication, social, self-management and research. Criterion B asks for evidence of skills applied, so naming which ATL skills the project used and showing them in the journal is the practical route to that mark.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.regionsIntro: The Personal Project runs in the second term, which in Dubai collides with mock exams and with Ramadan in some years. Where a family lives shapes only one thing here, which is when an uninterrupted ninety-minute drafting session can realistically happen.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Several of the city's full-continuum IB schools sit within this corridor, so Personal Project deadlines in one household often match a neighbour's. Shared study sessions are common and work badly for journal evidence, since two identical journals raise an honesty question.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Dense school provision and short commutes, so a 16:30 slot is realistic here. Useful for the fortnightly ninety-minute drafting sessions the report needs, rather than a weekly hour that never reaches a full section.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Villa communities feeding both British and IB schools, which means siblings on IGCSE coursework and a Personal Project in the same term. One shared calendar matters more than two separate tutors here.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: A long eastern commute into several IB schools, so students are often home after 16:30. Weekend morning sessions tend to hold better than weekday evenings during the project's drafting weeks.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Sports City
regions.note: Apartment communities with a high share of recent arrivals, so students joining MYP in Year 9 or Year 10 are common. Those students need the criterion vocabulary explained from scratch rather than revised.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf, Downtown and Business Bay
regions.note: Central towers close to two continuum IB schools. Short commutes but small apartments, so a quiet ninety minutes is scarcer than time; a tutor can work in two shorter blocks where that is the constraint.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: The university belt, with staff families whose children sit MYP locally. Project goals here skew technical, and technical projects need the hardest discipline on documenting failed iterations rather than only the version that worked.

schoolClusters.city: The continuum schools: Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: These schools run the IB continuum, which means the Personal Project arrives at the end of eight years of criterion marking. Students here usually know what a criterion is and still lose marks on the journal, because documenting as you go is a habit rather than a concept.

schoolClusters.city: The eastern and central MYP schools: Mirdif, Al Jaddaf and Festival City
schoolClusters.note: A mix of continuum schools and schools that admit into the MYP from British and Indian curricula. The second group produces the students who most need the criterion vocabulary built from nothing, and they often do very well once it is explained in plain language.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.modesIntro: Project work does not fit a weekly hour, because a report section needs a longer uninterrupted block than a maths topic does. These three formats reflect that, and all three are delivered online.

modes.title: Criterion clinic: three focused sessions
modes.description: The shortest useful intervention. Session one takes the learning goal and success criteria and rewrites them until they can be assessed. Session two audits the process journal and identifies which entries carry evidence for criterion B. Session three plans the reflection section against criterion C. The student writes between sessions and the tutor comments in the document.
bullets: Learning goal narrowed until it is measurable
Success criteria written in language the criteria recognise
Journal audited entry by entry for usable evidence
Written comments left in the student's own document

modes.title: Fortnightly supervision across the project
modes.description: A ninety-minute block every two weeks from the start of the project to the school's submission date. The student brings whatever has happened since; the tutor checks it against the criteria and sets the next fortnight's documentation task. This is the version that produces a journal with real dates in it, because the dates are generated by the sessions.
bullets: Ninety minutes every fortnight, dated and recorded
A documentation task set between each session
Progress measured against the school's own deadlines
The supervisor at school remains the decision-maker

modes.title: Report drafting and word discipline
modes.description: For students whose project is complete and whose report is either far too long or far too thin. The work is structural: mapping sections to criteria, cutting narrative that earns nothing, and finding the evaluation that is already in the student's head and not on the page. The limits are fixed by format and the tutor holds the student to them.
bullets: Section-by-section mapping to criteria A, B and C
Narrative description cut in favour of evaluation
Format limit enforced, whether words or minutes
No sentence written for the student at any stage

sections.heading: What the Personal Project is actually assessed on
paragraphs: Three criteria, each marked from zero to eight, for a total of twenty-four. Criterion A is planning: the student states a learning goal and a product, defines success criteria for the product, and plans the work. Criterion B is applying skills: the student shows how the Approaches to Learning skills they selected were used to achieve the goal and the product. Criterion C is reflecting: the student evaluates the quality of the product against their own success criteria and reflects on what they learned about the global context and about themselves as a learner.

Read that list again and notice what is absent. There is no criterion for how impressive the product is, how much money the fundraiser raised, how many views the video got, or how long the student worked. Those things can be evidence inside a criterion, but they are never the mark. A student who built a working robot and cannot say which research skill produced which decision will score below a student who knitted a scarf and documented every iteration against stated criteria.

The twenty-four marks are then converted by the school to a grade from one to seven using the published MYP boundaries, and schools entering students for MYP certification submit a sample for external moderation by the IB. That matters because a school's internal mark can move. It also matters because the criteria are not a local invention; they are the same descriptors a moderator anywhere will read, which is why rewriting success criteria in the language the descriptors use is worth real marks.

The table below sets out the three criteria with the strands inside them and the loss that is most common in each. Work through it with your child in front of the actual draft rather than in the abstract, because every one of these failures looks fine until it is checked against the descriptor.

sections.heading: Where the twenty-four marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The single largest loss is a learning goal that cannot be assessed. I want to learn about climate change is not a goal; it is a topic. I want to learn how to measure and reduce the electricity a single Dubai apartment uses in a month, and produce a guide other residents can follow, is a goal, because it tells you what success would look like and therefore what the success criteria must be. Rewriting the goal is a thirty-minute job that often moves criterion A by two bands, and it is the first thing a session does.

The second loss is success criteria that describe intentions rather than standards. My website will look professional cannot be evaluated by anyone. My website will load in under three seconds on a phone, will be readable at arm's length without zooming, and will be understood by three test users aged over sixty can be evaluated, and the evaluation writes itself in criterion C. Students resist specific criteria because specific criteria can fail, which is exactly why they earn marks.

The third loss is in criterion B, and it is a documentation failure rather than a skills failure. Students use research, organisation and self-management skills constantly and record none of it. A screenshot of a search that returned nothing useful, dated, with one line about what the student changed next, is stronger evidence than a paragraph in the report claiming that research skills were developed. Evidence has to exist at the time; it cannot be remembered into existence in April.

The fourth loss is the reflection. Criterion C asks for evaluation against the stated criteria and reflection on the global context, and most drafts give a narrative of events plus a sentence about enjoying the project. The fix is mechanical: take each success criterion in turn, state whether it was met, give the evidence, and say what you would change. Then separately address what the global context revealed. Done that way, the section is shorter and scores higher.
bullets: Goal rewritten until success and failure are both describable
Success criteria measurable by somebody other than the student
Journal evidence dated at the time, not reconstructed later
Reflection organised criterion by criterion, not as a story

sections.heading: The process journal is the evidence, not the paperwork
paragraphs: Students treat the process journal as an administrative burden the school has invented, and schools rarely have time to correct that impression. The journal is where criteria A and B are actually proved. Nothing in the report can be awarded on assertion: a claim that the student planned carefully is worth nothing without an extract showing a plan being made and revised. The report selects from the journal, so a thin journal caps the report regardless of how well it is written.

A journal does not need to be long or beautiful. It needs to be dated, varied in form, and honest about what did not work. Photographs of a prototype at three stages, a screenshot of a rejected design with two lines about why, a voice note transcribed, a printed email asking a professional a question, a crossed-out plan with the revision beside it. Five minutes after each working session is enough, and the five minutes have to happen on the day rather than at the end.

Where a journal is already thin and the deadline is close, there is an honest route and a dishonest one. The dishonest route is to write undated entries pretending to be old, which moderators recognise immediately and which the academic honesty form makes a declaration problem. The honest route is to document the remaining weeks properly, and in the report to be explicit that the early stages were under-documented and to say what the student would do differently. Criterion C rewards exactly that kind of honest self-assessment.

In sessions, the journal is the first thing opened and the last thing checked. A tutor reads it with the criteria beside it and says which entries carry weight, which are decorative, and what kind of entry is missing. The student then creates the entries from their own work, in their own words, because an entry written by anyone else is not evidence of the student's skills.

sections.heading: Report formats and the limits that come with them
paragraphs: The report is a separate assessed artefact from the product, and it may be submitted in several formats. The limits differ by format and they are not advisory. A written report runs from fifteen hundred to thirty-five hundred words. An electronic format such as a website or blog carries the same word range. An oral format such as a podcast or recorded presentation runs thirteen to fifteen minutes. A visual format such as a slide sequence has its own stated limit, and your school will confirm which formats it accepts.

Choosing the format badly costs marks for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. A student who speaks fluently and writes slowly often does better with a recorded report, provided they script the criterion coverage rather than improvising; an unscripted fifteen minutes usually spends twelve of them on narrative. A student who writes well can be undone by the upper word limit, because the evaluation ends up compressed into the final two hundred words after three thousand words of description.

The practical discipline is to allocate the limit to the criteria before writing anything. A rough split of a third to planning, a third to skills evidence, and a third to reflection keeps criterion C from being squeezed, which is the most common structural fault in a long report. Appendices and journal extracts generally sit outside the main count, but the rules on that are set by your school's reading of the current guide, so ask rather than assume.

sections.heading: Choosing a global context your inquiry can actually be framed by
paragraphs: Every Personal Project is framed by one of the six MYP global contexts, and most students pick one at the end to satisfy a box on the form. Chosen properly, the global context does real work: it gives criterion C something to reflect on beyond the student's own performance, and it keeps the inquiry from drifting into a hobby. Chosen badly, it produces a paragraph of invented significance that a reader can see through immediately.

The six are identities and relationships; orientation in space and time; personal and cultural expression; scientific and technical innovation; globalisation and sustainability; and fairness and development. The test for a good match is simple. If you can state, in one sentence, what question the context makes you ask that you would not otherwise have asked, the match is real. If the context only describes the topic, it is decoration.

Dubai gives students unusually good material here, and it is the material competitors never use. Water and energy consumption in a desert city, construction labour and migration, the preservation of pearl-diving and Bedouin heritage inside a city rebuilt in forty years, Arabic and English coexisting in one household, extreme summer heat and who it falls hardest on, a population drawn from more than a hundred nationalities in a few square kilometres. Any of those gives a context genuine traction.

The table pairs each context with a project goal that works in this city and explains why it is assessable. Use it as a prompt rather than a menu: a goal a student has not chosen for themselves tends to produce a journal nobody wants to keep.

sections.heading: Working backwards from your school's submission date
paragraphs: The Personal Project has no external exam date, which is precisely why it slips. The only fixed point is the date your school has set for submission, and in Dubai that usually sits in the second term, months before the end of the academic year. Everything else is a school-internal milestone: a goal approval, a supervisor meeting, a first draft, a journal check. If your child cannot tell you those dates, that is the first task rather than a tutoring question.

Once the date is known, the plan runs backwards. The report needs two to three weeks of drafting with the journal already complete. The product needs to be finished before the report begins, not alongside it, because evaluation of an unfinished product is guesswork. The journal needs to span the whole project, so the start date is dictated by how much documented process the criteria expect rather than by how long the product takes to make.

Two Dubai-specific collisions are worth planning around. The second term contains mock examinations for students also sitting IGCSE or starting Diploma courses, and in some years Ramadan falls across part of it, shifting family routines and school hours. Neither is a reason to delay; both are reasons to put the journal-heavy weeks before them and the drafting weeks after, which is a conversation to have in the first term rather than the week before submission.

sections.heading: What a supervisor does, what a tutor may do, and the boundary between them
paragraphs: Every Personal Project student has a supervisor at school. That person approves the goal, holds the official meetings, signs the academic honesty form and submits the mark. A tutor does not replace them and should never try to. The most useful thing a tutor can do early is make sure the student goes to their supervisor meetings with questions written down, because a supervisor with thirty projects to run gives the best attention to the student who arrives prepared.

Inside that structure a tutor can do a great deal. A tutor can interrogate a learning goal until it is measurable. A tutor can explain, in plain English, what a criterion descriptor means and show what the difference between two bands looks like using an example from another topic. A tutor can read a journal and say which entries would count as evidence. A tutor can read a draft and leave comments naming the criterion, the band and what the band above requires.

A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of the project or the report, and cannot produce the product. That is not a cautious house rule; it is what the academic honesty declaration says, and the consequence of breaching it falls on the student. One site competing for these searches advertises completed coursework for a fee. A family paying for that is buying a malpractice finding, and the student loses the qualification rather than the money.

Being explicit about this helps the student rather than restricting them. When a tutor says, I will not write this sentence, but I will tell you that the evaluation of your second success criterion is missing and here is what a moderator would look for, the student learns something that transfers to the Extended Essay two years later. That is the actual product of good supervision, and it is also why written comments in the student's own document are better evidence of honest support than an undocumented conversation.

sections.heading: What Personal Project support costs in Dubai, and what you are paying for
paragraphs: Published rates for one-to-one tutoring in Dubai give the shape of the market. Budget online sessions are advertised from around AED 45 to 65 an hour by EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with TutorChase at AED 270 and a premium named tier reaching AED 650 at BartyED. Those are the providers' own published figures, not IB Gram's.

Project supervision prices differently from subject tutoring, and it is worth understanding why before comparing hourly numbers. Most of the value sits in reading time outside the session: a journal audit and a draft read with criteria beside them take longer than the session that follows. A rate that covers only live minutes will either exclude that reading or absorb it invisibly, and the difference shows up as comments you can or cannot point at afterwards.

Volume also differs. A full fortnightly supervision across a project is perhaps eight to ten contact hours spread over a term, which is far less than a subject plan running weekly for the same period. A criterion clinic is three sessions. Families often assume project help is the expensive option because the project feels large, when in practice the hours are fewer and more concentrated than exam-subject tutoring.

IB Gram quotes its own rate after the free trial lesson, stating the session length and whether document reading and written comments are included. No price on this page is ours, every figure is attributed to whoever published it, and no claim is made here about outcomes, because a Personal Project mark depends on a student's own documented work and nobody can honestly promise a band.

process.title: Send the goal, the deadline and the journal
process.description: Three things get a useful first session: the learning goal as currently written, the school's submission date, and whatever the process journal contains right now however thin. A tutor can read all three in ten minutes and tell you which criterion is at risk, which is a more honest starting point than a general conversation about the project.

process.title: A free trial session with the tutor who would continue
process.description: The trial is a real session with the person who would supervise, not a sales call. No card details are taken beforehand. Most trials are spent on the learning goal, because a goal that cannot be assessed makes every later session harder and rewriting it is the fastest available improvement.

process.title: Criterion-by-criterion audit
process.description: The tutor reads the goal, criteria, journal and any draft against the three descriptors and produces a short written note: where the project currently sits, what is missing, and in what order to fix it. You keep that note. It is also the document to take to the next school supervisor meeting.

process.title: Documentation tasks between sessions
process.description: Each session ends with a specific documentation task rather than a general instruction to work on the project. Photograph the three stages and date them. Write two lines on why the second design was abandoned. Test the success criteria on one person outside the family. Tasks that produce evidence are the only ones worth setting.

process.title: Draft comments, then the student rewrites
process.description: Drafts come back with comments naming the criterion letter, the band the section currently sits in, and what the band above requires. Nothing is rewritten for the student. The comments stay in the document so there is a visible record of what support was given, which is useful if the school asks.

whyPoints.title: The criteria come first, not the product
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from the three descriptors and work back to the project, which is the opposite of how most students approach it. That reordering is where the marks are, and it is why a modest product with disciplined documentation outperforms an impressive one without.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a parent can read
whyPoints.description: You get the written audit, the comments in the draft and the documentation tasks. None of it requires knowing the subject. A parent can see whether the journal has dated entries spanning the project, and that single check predicts the mark better than any progress conversation.

whyPoints.title: Dubai material rather than generic examples
whyPoints.description: Global context work uses this city: cooling loads, water use, heritage inside a rebuilt city, Arabic and English in one household, heat and who it affects. A student with local material writes a reflection that is theirs rather than one assembled from a template.

whyPoints.title: A stated and enforced honesty line
whyPoints.description: A tutor here will question, explain and comment, and will not write any part of the project, the report or the product. The line is stated before booking and it holds in submission week, which is when it matters and when most people negotiate.

whyPoints.title: No invented numbers and no band promises
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it, and no success rate or average mark is claimed because none could be produced with a sample size and a method. Nobody can promise a Personal Project band, since the mark rests on the student's own documented work.

faqs.question: What exactly is the MYP Personal Project marked on?
faqs.answer: Three criteria, each from zero to eight, for twenty-four marks in total. Criterion A covers planning: a learning goal, a product, success criteria for that product, and a plan. Criterion B covers applying skills, meaning evidence that the chosen Approaches to Learning skills were actually used. Criterion C covers reflecting: evaluating the product against the student's own success criteria and reflecting on the global context and their learning. Nothing in the three criteria asks whether the product is impressive, which is why a well-documented modest project can outscore a spectacular one.

faqs.question: What grade does twenty-four marks turn into?
faqs.answer: The school converts the total to a grade from one to seven using the published MYP boundaries, so a mark in the high teens is a strong grade and a mark in single figures is not. Schools entering students for MYP certification send a sample of projects for external moderation by the IB, which means an internal mark can move either way. Ask your child's coordinator for the boundaries the school is applying, because knowing how many marks sit between the current position and the next grade changes where the remaining effort should go.

faqs.question: Which report format should my child pick, and what is the limit on each one?
faqs.answer: A written report, or an electronic one such as a website or blog, runs from fifteen hundred to thirty-five hundred words. A recorded oral format such as a podcast or presentation runs thirteen to fifteen minutes. Visual formats have their own stated limit. Your school confirms which formats it accepts and how it treats appendices and journal extracts, so ask before drafting. The practical advice is to allocate the limit across the three criteria before writing, because the most common structural fault is three thousand words of narrative and two hundred of evaluation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or edit my child's Personal Project report for them?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor cannot write the Personal Project report, rewrite sections of it, or produce the product. The project must be the student's own work and both student and supervisor sign an academic honesty declaration confirming it. What a tutor can legitimately do is interrogate the learning goal, explain what a criterion descriptor requires, audit the process journal for usable evidence, and leave comments on a draft naming the criterion and the band. The student does every piece of writing, which is also what makes the support defensible if the school asks what help was received.

faqs.question: What is a global context and does my child have to choose one?
faqs.answer: Yes, every Personal Project is framed by one of six MYP global contexts: identities and relationships; orientation in space and time; personal and cultural expression; scientific and technical innovation; globalisation and sustainability; and fairness and development. The useful test is whether the student can say in one sentence what question the context makes them ask that they would not have asked otherwise. If the context only restates the topic, it is decoration and criterion C will read as thin. Dubai offers unusually strong material: cooling and water use, heritage in a rebuilt city, and a hundred-plus nationalities in one neighbourhood.

faqs.question: My child's product is finished but the process journal is almost empty. What now?
faqs.answer: There is an honest route and a dishonest one. Writing undated entries that pretend to be older is recognisable to a moderator and sits badly against a signed honesty declaration. The honest route is to document the remaining weeks properly, select whatever real evidence exists from earlier, and then say explicitly in the report that early stages were under-documented and what the student would do differently. Criterion C rewards exactly that kind of self-assessment. It will not recover full marks, but it recovers more than a reconstructed journal and carries no integrity risk.

faqs.question: Is the Personal Project moderated outside the school or only marked internally?
faqs.answer: Schools register students for MYP certification submit a sample of Personal Projects for external moderation by the IB, so the internal mark is not automatically final. Practically, this means the criteria matter more than a particular teacher's preference: the descriptors a moderator reads are the same everywhere. It also means writing success criteria in language the descriptors recognise is worth real marks. Schools that do not enter students for certification mark internally, and their process still follows the same three criteria, so the preparation does not change.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project affect Diploma admission at a Dubai IB school?
faqs.answer: Not as a formal entry requirement in most schools, but it is read as evidence. A coordinator deciding whether a student can carry three Higher Level subjects and an Extended Essay is looking for someone who can run an independent piece of work to a deadline, and the Personal Project is the only evidence of that in the file. A well-journalled project with a modest product often reads better than a polished product with no documented process. Ask your child's school directly how it uses the project in Diploma course counselling, because practice varies between schools.

faqs.question: How much does Personal Project supervision cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from around AED 33 to 65 an hour for budget online sessions, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialist work, with a premium named tier reaching AED 650. Those are the providers' own figures. Project work tends to be fewer hours than subject tutoring, often three sessions for a criterion clinic or eight to ten across a whole project. Ask specifically whether reading a journal and commenting on a draft outside the session is included, because most of the work sits there.

faqs.question: When in the year should Personal Project support start?
faqs.answer: Before the goal is approved, if you have the choice. The learning goal and the success criteria set the ceiling for criterion A and shape everything criterion C can later evaluate, and they are much easier to get right at the start than to repair in the drafting weeks. A realistic second-best moment is the point where the product is roughly half built and the journal can still be filled honestly. The worst moment is three weeks before submission with an empty journal, which limits honest help to the reflection section.

faqs.question: What makes a good learning goal rather than just a topic?
faqs.answer: A goal describes a measurable outcome and implies its own success criteria. I want to learn about marine plastic is a topic. I want to learn how to survey plastic debris on one stretch of Dubai coastline and produce a method other students can repeat is a goal, because you can tell whether it was achieved. The test is whether failure is describable. If there is no version of the project that counts as not having worked, the success criteria will be vague and criterion C will have nothing to evaluate against.

faqs.question: Do you come to our villa in Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills for project sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and every session is delivered online over live video. For project work this is genuinely the stronger format. The journal, the draft and the criteria sit on a shared screen in front of both people, comments are typed into the student's own document and stay there afterwards, and the written record of what support was given is available if the school asks. A kitchen-table session leaves none of that behind.

faqs.question: What does the academic honesty form actually require?
faqs.answer: The student confirms the project is their own work and the supervisor confirms, from their own knowledge, that it is. The form records that supervision meetings took place, which is why going to those meetings and having them logged matters more than students assume. Filling the form in during submission week with no record of meetings is a weak position, and it is one a moderator can question. Keep a simple dated note of each supervision meeting and what was discussed; it takes a minute and it supports the declaration you are both signing.

faqs.question: Can the Personal Project be a business, a fundraiser or a charity drive?
faqs.answer: Yes, and these are among the most common choices in Dubai, but they carry a specific trap. The amount raised or the sales made is not the mark. Criterion C evaluates the product against the student's own success criteria, so a fundraiser that raised a large sum with no stated criteria scores poorly while one that set a target, a reach measure and a cost ceiling and then missed two of them can score well. Write criteria that could fail, document the planning, and treat the money as evidence rather than as the achievement.

faqs.question: What if our tutor and my child's school supervisor give different advice?
faqs.answer: The supervisor wins. They approve the goal, hold the official meetings, sign the honesty declaration and submit the mark, and they know the school's own reading of the current guide. Where a tutor disagrees, the useful move is to turn the disagreement into a question the student takes to their next supervision meeting, written down. That usually resolves it and has the side benefit of a student who arrives at meetings prepared. A tutor who encourages a student to work around their supervisor is creating a problem rather than solving one.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.closingHeading: Start with the goal, not the product
dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-help.closingBody: If your child's Personal Project is stuck, send three things: the learning goal as it is currently written, the school's submission date, and the process journal however thin it is. A tutor can read all three quickly and tell you which of the three criteria is actually at risk, which is more useful than a general conversation about the project. Book the free trial session and spend it on the goal and the success criteria, because those two paragraphs set the ceiling for every mark that follows. Everything else on this page, from the format limits to the backwards schedule, exists so you can check the advice rather than take it on trust.

intro.heading: You cannot watch a project happen, so ask what it leaves behind
paragraphs: A Dubai parent paying for Personal Project help is in an awkward position. Subject tutoring produces marked past papers and a test score three weeks later, and you can see whether anything is working. Project coaching produces none of that. There is no paper, no percentage and no weekly quiz. The project is marked once, months from now, by the school, against criteria most parents have never read. So the question that matters is not whether your child enjoyed the session. It is what the session left behind that you can look at tonight.

That is the whole basis of this page. An IB MYP Personal Project home tutor in Dubai is typically hired on trust and reviewed on feeling, and both are poor instruments. The better instrument is a stack of artefacts: dated journal entries in the student's handwriting or typing, a plan with revisions visible, a draft paragraph with a strand named against it, a test of the product against a success criterion the student wrote themselves. Those things either accumulate week by week or they do not, and either way you can tell within a month.

Dubai makes the evidence question sharper than it would be elsewhere. The emirate had 387,441 pupils across its private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, per the Dubai Media Office, and IB programmes account for a minority of that roll. Many families here have moved school systems at least once, which means parents are routinely reading a report format they have never seen before. An MYP report that gives criterion numbers out of eight, with no percentage anywhere, offers very little to a parent trying to judge whether paid help is working. The session artefacts fill that gap months before the report does.

There is a second reason to care about evidence specifically on this component. The Personal Project carries an academic integrity declaration signed by the student and countersigned by the school supervisor. A coaching relationship that produces visible student artefacts is self-policing: if the journal entries are in the student's own voice and the drafts show the student's own revisions, the declaration is straightforward. A relationship that produces only polished output and no working record is the one that should worry a family, and it is exactly what the essay-selling end of this market supplies.

What follows is the mechanics. What arrives after a session and when. What an annotated draft looks like, with the strand named rather than the sentence rewritten. A ten-week log of the kind of change that is realistic. How to read a mid-year project grade that has gone down. When the evidence says the coaching should stop. And an honest comparison of a visiting tutor in your Dubai community against one-to-one live video, because the search term says home tutor and the answer deserves to be direct: IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, and the reasons are worth reading before you decide.
