process.title: Tell us the deadline and the stage
process.description: Send the school's project deadline, the current stage, and the topic if there is one. If there is a booklet from the school, that tells us more in two minutes than a long conversation. We will say plainly whether the time left suits a planning block, check-ins, or a report clinic.

process.title: Free trial lesson, 45 minutes
process.description: One lesson at no cost, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards. The coach reads whatever exists, asks the student questions, and ends by naming the single biggest gap against the criteria. Parents are welcome to listen. If the fit is wrong, say so and nothing further happens.

process.title: Match to a subject-aware coach
process.description: We match on the project's subject area rather than on who is nearest, because delivery is online for every UAE family. A sciences project goes to someone who has supervised investigations; an arts project to someone who has marked process documentation. If nobody suitable is free, we tell you that instead of substituting.

process.title: Agree the block and the milestones
process.description: You get the number of sessions, their placement against the school's milestones, and what each one is for, in writing before anything is paid. There is no fixed-term commitment and no minimum number of weeks. Blocks can be paused for mock examinations or shifted for Ramadan timings.

process.title: Work between sessions, reviewed at the next one
process.description: Every session ends with one task the student does alone: a journal entry, a test against a success criterion, a paragraph rewritten. The next session starts by looking at it. This is the mechanism that keeps the work the student's own, and it is the part a ghostwriting service cannot imitate.

process.title: Hand back to the school supervisor
process.description: The school supervisor owns the project relationship and signs the integrity form. We prepare the student to arrive at those meetings with questions and evidence, and we stay out of the correspondence. After submission we offer a short bridge block for students continuing into DP1.

whyPoints.title: The criteria are read out loud, strand by strand
whyPoints.description: Most students have never heard the strand wording applied to their own paragraphs. We read a strand, then read what the student wrote, then ask which words in the paragraph satisfy it. It is slow for ten minutes and then it changes how the rest of the report gets written.

whyPoints.title: Subject-aware coaching, not general homework help
whyPoints.description: A project on bridge load testing and a project on a community radio episode need different questions. We match on subject background, which an online-only model makes possible across the whole UAE rather than within driving distance of one Dubai community.

whyPoints.title: A boundary we will state in writing
whyPoints.description: The student writes every word of the report, keeps the journal, and makes the product. A coach questions, reads and names gaps. We put that in writing before the first paid session, because the alternative sitting in this market is an integrity problem the student carries.

whyPoints.title: Blocks timed to your school's own milestones
whyPoints.description: Dubai schools set different project deadlines, often between December and February. Sessions are placed against your child's dates, not a standard package, and the planning block is deliberately front-loaded because that is where criterion A is won or lost.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: If no coach with the right subject background is free in the week you need, we say so rather than putting a generalist in the slot. For a project in an unusual area that may mean a short wait or a coach outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no regulator endorsements, no statistics without a source. Every AED figure on this page is somebody else's published rate with the source and reading date attached, and every IB detail should be confirmed against your school's current project guide.

faqs.question: My daughter's Dubai school has set the report deadline in February - when should support actually start?
faqs.answer: Count backwards from that date. For a February report, the product should be finished and tested by early January, which means the main build runs through November, which means success criteria and a dated plan need to exist in late September or early October. Starting in September buys structure, which is what criterion A rewards. Starting in late January buys editing, which is the least valuable help available and the most expensive per mark. If you are reading this in January, the sensible move is a short report clinic plus an honest reflection on what the journal can support, not an attempt to rebuild the plan retrospectively.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Personal Project out of, and does the product itself get a grade?
faqs.answer: The project is assessed against three criteria, each marked from 0 to 8, for a total of 24 that the school converts to a reported grade. Confirm the current criterion wording and conversion bands with your child's MYP coordinator, since the project guide has been revised and schools apply the current version. The product does not receive a mark of its own. It appears in the report as evidence: photographs, extracts, test results, user feedback. This surprises most families, and it explains why a beautiful outcome with a thin journal lands mid-band while a modest outcome with a rigorous record scores well.

faqs.question: What exactly is the process journal, and is it handed in with the report?
faqs.answer: It is the student's own dated working record, kept while the project happens: what was attempted, what happened, what changes next and why. Format varies by school, from a notebook to a shared document to a captioned photo folder. Schools differ on whether the whole journal is submitted or whether extracts are selected for the report, so check the booklet. Either way, it is the only source of evidence for criterion B. Four sentences a fortnight across the project year gives roughly fifteen dated decisions to cite, which is more than enough for a strong case.

faqs.question: Can a coach read my son's journal and still stay inside IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes. Reading the student's own record and asking questions about it is ordinary teaching, and it is what a school supervisor does at every meeting. What a coach cannot do is write entries, dictate the reasoning, or reconstruct months of thinking the student never had. Our sessions ask the student to write the entry during the lesson while the thinking is live, then read it back aloud. That keeps authorship unambiguous and produces something defensible in a supervisor meeting. If a provider offers to maintain the journal for your child, that is the signal to stop the conversation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a learning goal and a product goal, in plain terms?
faqs.answer: The product goal is the thing that will exist at the end, with a test that says it is finished: a working planter, a printed recipe book, a fifteen-minute documentary. The learning goal is what the student intends to understand or be able to do that they could not before: irrigation control, recipe testing with real users, interview technique. The criteria assess both and the final reflection judges each separately. Written as one fused sentence in September, a product that underperforms reads as a failed project. Written apart, an honest report can show the learning happened anyway.

faqs.question: How long does the written Personal Project report have to be in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: The written format is commonly 1,500 to 3,500 words, and most Dubai schools restate that range in their own project booklet. Alternative formats exist, typically an oral or multimedia presentation of around 13 to 15 minutes, and some schools allow a choice. Confirm the format and limit with your child's coordinator before drafting, because a report written to the wrong length is a painful rewrite. The practical issue is rarely reaching the word count. It is that students spend 2,000 words narrating the term and leave 400 for the reflection that carries criterion C.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project count towards the IB MYP certificate?
faqs.answer: At schools that register for the MYP certificate, a satisfactory Personal Project is part of what the IB requires, alongside subject results and end-of-programme eAssessment where candidates are entered. Many Dubai schools do not register for the certificate and simply report the project grade on the school transcript. Both are normal. Ask your child's coordinator which applies, because it changes nothing about the work required but quite a lot about how the result travels if your family moves school or country during the Diploma years.

faqs.question: My son wants to build an app and nobody in our family codes - is that project realistic?
faqs.answer: Often yes, with the scope cut hard. A student with no prior programming can realistically build something small and genuinely working in a project year, and the learning goal then becomes the programming itself, which is excellent evidence for criterion B. What fails is an ambitious specification copied from a commercial app. The practical Dubai advantage is mentors: parents and neighbours working in the free zones around Dubai Internet City and Dubai Silicon Oasis will often answer a specific technical question, and a cited half-hour conversation with a working developer is a legitimate source.

faqs.question: How many supervisor meetings should my child be having, and what if they are not happening?
faqs.answer: Schools set their own schedule, and three or more meetings across the project year is a common pattern. If meetings are not happening, that is worth raising with the coordinator politely and early rather than at the deadline, because the meeting record is part of how criterion A evidence gets built. A coach can prepare your child to arrive with questions and a journal rather than apologies, which tends to make supervisors more available. We do not contact the school ourselves; the relationship is the student's to manage.

faqs.question: What does the academic integrity form actually commit my child to?
faqs.answer: It is a declaration, signed by the student and countersigned by the supervisor, that the work and the thinking behind it are the student's own. Paid coaching is not excluded by that statement and many Dubai families use it. What the form rules out is help that replaces the student's work: text written by someone else, a journal kept by someone else, a product made by someone else. A student with a genuine dated journal signs it without anxiety. A student whose record was assembled in the last fortnight should think carefully.

faqs.question: Is project coaching worth paying for when the project carries no exam mark?
faqs.answer: Judge it on the next two years rather than on this grade. The Extended Essay in the Diploma assumes a student can hold one question for months, keep a reading record, meet a supervisor prepared and write a self-critical account. Those are the project's habits exactly, and the Dubai students who struggle most in DP1 are usually the ones for whom the project was a January panic. If the budget is tight, buy the planning block in the autumn and skip the rescue work. Front-loaded structure is worth more per dirham than late editing.

faqs.question: How much should project support cost in Dubai, and is it priced by the hour or the project?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates we read in October 2026 range from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, through AED 150 to 270 for qualified and specialist support, to AED 650 for premium named tutors. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. Project support is usually bought in blocks rather than a standing weekly slot, which often puts the total project year below one term of weekly subject tuition. Ask any provider for the number of sessions, what each is for, and the cancellation terms in writing before paying anything.

faqs.question: Can my child change the product goal halfway through if the first idea stops working?
faqs.answer: Yes, and handled properly it can improve the mark rather than damage it. Plans are expected to be adapted, and criterion A explicitly looks for evidence that a plan was used and adjusted. What matters is that the change is recorded at the time, with the reason, in the journal, rather than quietly rewritten in the final report. A student who can explain why a hydroponic design was abandoned for a wicking bed, with dated evidence of the failed test, is demonstrating exactly what the criterion asks for.

faqs.question: Will the project help when my child reaches the Extended Essay in Dubai's Diploma years?
faqs.answer: It is the closest preparation the programme offers. Both ask a student to define a researchable question, sustain it over months, keep a record of sources and decisions, work with a supervisor and write a critical account at the end. The difference is scale and formality, not kind. We offer a short bridge block immediately after project submission for exactly this reason: converting fresh project habits into Extended Essay habits while the student still remembers what went wrong is far easier than restarting the conversation a year later in DP1.

faqs.question: Our Dubai school moves students into International GCSE in Year 10 - is there still a Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Usually not in the same form. Schools that switch from the Middle Years Programme to Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE at Year 10 generally do not run the full Personal Project, though some keep a community project or an extended research task in Year 9. If your child is in that position, the useful preparation is the underlying skills rather than the component: a research question with defined scope, a dated record of decisions, and referencing habits. Those transfer directly into coursework and later into a Diploma Extended Essay.

faqs.question: What happens if no coach with the right subject background is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We say so. For an unusual project area, that sometimes means a short wait or a coach based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, and we will tell you which before you commit. What we will not do is put a generalist into a specialist slot and let you discover the mismatch in session three. Lessons are online one-to-one for every UAE family, so availability is a question of subject match and timetable rather than driving distance from your community.

dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the deadline, not with the topic
dubai/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.closingBody: Send us your child's school project deadline and whatever exists so far, even if that is a half-finished product and an empty document. The free 45-minute trial lesson is a diagnosis: the coach reads what there is, asks the student questions, and names the single biggest gap against the three criteria before anything is paid for. If the right answer is a four-session planning block in October rather than a term of weekly lessons, that is what we will tell you. Lessons are one-to-one on live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the student does every piece of the work that carries their name.

intro.heading: Most MYP physics problems are arithmetic problems in a physics costume
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai hires a physics tutor because a test came back at 11 out of 25 and the topic was motion. The reasonable assumption is that the student does not understand motion. In practice, perhaps one error in five on that script is about motion. The others are a gradient read as a single coordinate pair divided, a speed in metres per second calculated from a distance left in centimetres, an equation rearranged by pattern rather than by operation, and an answer written with no unit at all. The physics was understood. The arithmetic underneath it was not.

This matters because it changes what you should buy. Four operations carry most of MYP physics: rearranging an equation, converting units before substituting, reading a gradient as a change over a change, and handling standard form. A student fluent in those four can be taught any MYP physics topic in a few sessions. A student who is not will present as weak in every topic in turn, and will be tutored topic by topic for a year while the obstacle goes untouched. The mapping in this page exists so a parent can check which of the two is happening.

The home-tutor question deserves a direct answer as well, because it is the phrase that brings most families here. In-home physics tuition exists in Dubai and the published rates for it run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with the travel inside the fee; advertised monthly packages run around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits against about AED 799 for eight online sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. In-home teaching is a service we run in India only, and everything for UAE families is one-to-one over live video.

The reason we are comfortable saying that on a page targeting this search is that the in-home arithmetic in this city does not favour the parent. A tutor crossing from Al Qusais to Arabian Ranches for a 5pm appointment is in traffic for ninety minutes on the outbound leg, which is why they will not take a one-hour booking and why the rate carries the drive. The practical effect is a shortlist of tutors defined by geography. A family in The Springs ends up choosing between whoever can reach The Springs, rather than between people who have marked MYP physics criterion tasks.

What follows is the physics. A table mapping each MYP topic to the operation beneath it. The three questions a student must be able to answer about any motion graph. Why the resistance investigation goes wrong in the same way in every MYP 4 cohort. The calculation order that costs marks in efficiency questions. What the explain command term wants in a waves answer. How to design a physics investigation that can be marked in the upper bands. And what to fix in the final two MYP 5 terms before DP Physics or A Level.

dubai/ib-myp-physics-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics is taught under three different labels across a Dubai school career, and the mathematical demand rises faster than the physics does. Here is what each stage expects numerically, which is the part families are rarely warned about.

programmes.name: Physics inside integrated sciences
programmes.description: Forces, energy, light, sound and simple circuits, with the numbers kept small and the units usually consistent. The mathematical demand is low, which is exactly why gaps hide here: a student can reach the end of MYP 3 having never rearranged an equation, because every question gave the unknown on the left.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai cohorts arrive in MYP 1 from the PYP and from British, Indian and American primaries, with mathematics backgrounds that differ far more than their science backgrounds. We check ratio, decimal place value and simple rearrangement in the first session, because those three predict MYP 4 physics better than any science test at this age.

programmes.name: MYP Physics as a separate subject
programmes.description: Motion and graphs, forces and Newton's laws, work, energy and efficiency, waves, and electricity including series and parallel circuits. Unknowns now appear in denominators, units are mixed deliberately, and graphs must be processed rather than described. This is where the four operations stop being optional.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai continuum schools split the sciences at the start of MYP 4, so physics arrives with its own teacher, rubric and deadline in the same fortnight as chemistry and biology do. Families who ask for the physics task sheet in the first half term usually find the arithmetic problem before the first report does.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Standard or Higher Level, with uncertainties propagated, relationships linearised, and an internal assessment the student designs from their own research question. Logarithmic plotting and significant-figure discipline are assessed explicitly, so a student who reached MYP 5 without secure standard form meets two problems at once.
programmes.countryNote: The DP Physics decision in Dubai is often made on timetable availability rather than on evidence. The useful evidence is the MYP criterion C record: independent data processing is the first thing the internal assessment demands, and it is visible in marked MYP work two years earlier than any mock paper.

programmes.name: A Level and Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Many Dubai students leave MYP at 16 for IGCSE Physics, such as Cambridge 0625, and then A Level. The content overlaps substantially with MYP physics; the assessment does not, because terminal examinations test design and evaluation indirectly while MYP marks them directly against criteria.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools hold 37 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, so transfers in both directions are routine here. Cambridge runs June and November series with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the zone timetable governs your child's dates, so a move in Year 10 needs the receiving school's exams officer involved early.

dubai/ib-myp-physics-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below is MYP physics written as topics with their mathematical prerequisite attached, because that is the pairing that determines whether a topic lands. Take any line to your child's marked script and check whether the symptom described is the one on the page.

subjects.name: Speed, distance and time
subjects.description: Needs unit conversion and division fluency before anything else. The symptom when it is missing is an answer of the right magnitude in the wrong unit, or a speed calculated from centimetres and seconds and reported in metres per second without conversion.

subjects.name: Distance-time and velocity-time graphs
subjects.description: Needs gradient as a rate of change, and area under a line for velocity-time work. The symptom is a student dividing one coordinate pair, which is only correct through the origin, and treating a horizontal line on a velocity-time graph as stationary.

subjects.name: Forces, resultants and free-body diagrams
subjects.description: Needs vector addition in one dimension and the discipline of stating direction. The symptom is a diagram with equal-length arrows for unequal forces, or a resultant given as a number with no direction, which loses the mark even when the arithmetic is right.

subjects.name: Newton's laws and acceleration
subjects.description: Needs rearrangement with the unknown in any position. The symptom is a student who can state the relationship between force, mass and acceleration and then divides the wrong way when mass is the unknown, which is a rearrangement failure rather than a physics one.

subjects.name: Work, energy and efficiency
subjects.description: Needs percentage calculation and a fixed order of operations. The symptom is useful and total energy inverted in the efficiency fraction, or a percentage above 100 accepted without comment, which shows the student is not checking the physical sense of an answer.

subjects.name: Waves, sound and the wave equation
subjects.description: Needs standard form and consistent prefixes, since wavelengths arrive in nanometres and frequencies in kilohertz. The symptom is an answer out by a factor of a thousand, accepted because the student has no sense of the expected magnitude.

subjects.name: Light, reflection and refraction
subjects.description: Needs ray-diagram geometry and the explain command term. The symptom is refraction described as light bending, which is the observation rather than the mechanism; the mark requires the change of speed between media to be stated.

subjects.name: Electricity, current and resistance
subjects.description: Needs rearrangement with the unknown in the denominator and careful scale reading. The symptom is a correctly stated relationship between potential difference, current and resistance followed by the wrong division, plus ammeter readings taken off the wrong interval.

subjects.name: Series and parallel circuits
subjects.description: Needs reciprocal arithmetic for parallel combinations and the habit of tracking what stays constant. The symptom is a student who knows current divides in parallel and cannot predict what happens to the ammeter reading when a second resistor is added.

subjects.name: Measurement, resolution and significant figures
subjects.description: Needs place value and an understanding of instrument limits. It carries few MYP marks directly and predicts DP Physics difficulty strongly, so it belongs in the final MYP 5 terms whether or not the current rubric rewards it.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP physics home tutor in Dubai costs, and what the travel buys
paragraphs: Published in-home rates in Dubai run from roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 table, with independent home tutors advertised up to AED 500, while online bands for a qualified subject tutor sit closer to AED 150 to AED 300. Monthly packages in this market show the same gap plainly: about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car, an evening and a city with a rush hour that lasts three hours.

That is also why visiting tutors rarely accept a single-hour booking in the outer communities. A two-hour minimum is the only way the economics work for them, which means a family needing forty-five focused minutes on gradient reading pays for two hours and watches a tired student in hour two. The table below sets out the arithmetic community by community, using the drive times families themselves report for a weekday evening appointment.

IB Gram does not provide home visits in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For UAE families, teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The honest case for it is not that it is a cheaper version of the same thing. It is that the travel premium buys nothing a physics student needs, while removing it buys two things they do need: a tutor selected for having marked MYP physics work, and a session short enough to be fully attended.

sections.heading: Every MYP physics topic has a mathematical prerequisite: here is the map
paragraphs: The useful diagnostic question in MYP physics is not which topic is weak. It is which operation is missing, because one missing operation makes several topics look weak at once. A student who cannot rearrange with the unknown in a denominator will fail at acceleration, at resistance and at density, and a topic-by-topic plan will treat those as three problems. They are one problem presenting three times, and it is cheaper and faster to fix at the source.

The table maps the topics most Dubai MYP 4 and 5 students are taught against the operation each one sits on, the symptom when the operation is missing, and what a session does about it. Read it with your child's last marked script beside you. If the errors cluster in one column, you have found the plan. If they are scattered across the mechanism row, the problem genuinely is physics and the sessions should be topic teaching instead.

What makes this worth publishing is that it is the cheapest possible intervention, and almost nobody sells it. Six to eight sessions on four operations, drilled inside physics questions rather than as abstract mathematics, usually resolves the majority of a script's errors. The sessions are not glamorous: they are mixed-unit calculations, rearrange-before-substituting discipline, and gradients read off axes with two widely spaced points marked in pencil. They are, however, the work that makes every subsequent physics topic teachable, and they are the reason a student can look transformed in a single half term without anyone having taught them new physics at all.

sections.heading: Motion graphs: three questions a student must be able to answer about any graph
paragraphs: Motion graphs produce more lost marks in MYP 4 than any other physics topic, and the reason is that two different graphs look alike. A distance-time graph and a velocity-time graph can have identical shapes and mean opposite things, and a student who has not internalised which axis they are reading will describe a horizontal line as stopped on both. That single confusion costs marks every time graphs appear, which in MYP physics is constantly.

The three questions we drill are deliberately mechanical. First: what is on the vertical axis, in words and units, read aloud. Second: what does the gradient of this particular graph physically represent, speed on a distance-time graph and acceleration on a velocity-time graph. Third: what does a flat line mean on this graph specifically. A student who answers those three before interpreting anything stops making the error, and it takes two sessions rather than a term.

Then the gradient itself. Reading it correctly means marking two points far apart on the line, not two data points, reading the change in the vertical quantity and the change in the horizontal quantity off the axes, and dividing one by the other with units carried through. Students taught gradient as rise over run in a mathematics lesson often do not transfer it, because in physics the axes have units and the answer has a physical name. We teach it in the physics context, using the student's own graph from their last investigation, and the transfer stops being an issue.
bullets: Read the vertical axis aloud, in words and units, before interpreting
Say what the gradient physically represents on this graph
Say what a flat line means on this graph specifically

sections.heading: Why the MYP 4 resistance investigation goes wrong in the same way every year
paragraphs: Nearly every MYP 4 cohort in Dubai runs an investigation into the resistance of a wire, and nearly every cohort loses the same marks. The practical is straightforward and the design is not. The student varies the length of the wire, measures potential difference and current, calculates resistance and plots it against length. Criterion C then goes reasonably well and criterion B falls apart, because the plan said nothing about the wire's thickness or material.

The control-variable omission is the central failure. A student who varies length while silently using the same reel of wire has in fact controlled thickness and material, but the plan does not say so, and criterion B marks the plan. The second failure is heating: current through a thin wire raises its temperature and therefore its resistance, so readings taken with the circuit left closed drift upward. A plan that does not mention switching off between readings has a validity problem the evaluation ought to name.

The third is the processing step. Plotting raw potential difference against length instead of calculating resistance first is unprocessed data, which costs criterion C marks regardless of how neat the graph is. In a session we work through all three on the student's own plan: the thickness and material controls written explicitly with the method of control, the switching-off procedure added with the reason, and the resistance column calculated before anything is plotted. The same three corrections then transfer to the next investigation, which is why this work is worth more than its topic suggests.
bullets: Name thickness and material as controlled variables, and say how
Switch off between readings and say why, or address heating in the evaluation
Calculate resistance before plotting; raw readings are unprocessed data
Identify anomalies on the graph rather than quietly smoothing them

sections.heading: Energy and efficiency: the order of operations that costs the marks
paragraphs: Efficiency questions look easy and are marked harshly, because there are three places to go wrong and only one of them involves understanding energy. The first is inverting the fraction, putting total energy over useful energy, which produces a figure above 100 per cent that the student then writes down without noticing. The second is mixing units, usually joules with kilojoules. The third is forgetting to multiply by a hundred, or multiplying twice.

The fix is procedural and it holds. Write the quantities with units, identify useful and total explicitly and label them, convert both to the same unit, divide useful by total, then multiply by a hundred, then check the answer is below a hundred and makes physical sense. Written as six steps on a card the student produces themselves, it becomes automatic in two or three weeks of short drills. The sense-check at the end is the step that matters most, because it catches every one of the three errors.

Work and energy transfer questions fail differently, usually on the distance in the direction of the force rather than the total distance moved, and on confusing the energy transferred with the force applied. These are conceptual and need teaching rather than drilling. Separating the two kinds of error is exactly what an error tally does: if efficiency questions are wrong and work questions are right, nothing conceptual is missing and the fix is the six-step card. If both are wrong, the session teaches energy transfer properly before any procedure is introduced.
bullets: Label useful and total energy explicitly before calculating anything
Convert to a common unit before dividing
Multiply by a hundred once, then check the result is below a hundred
Work questions use distance in the direction of the force, not total distance

sections.heading: Waves and light: what the explain command term actually wants
paragraphs: Waves is the MYP physics topic where command terms do the most damage, because the observations are easy to describe and the mechanisms are not. A student asked to explain refraction writes that the light bends as it enters the glass. That is a description of what is seen, it is correct, and it earns nothing against an explain command term, which requires a reason or mechanism. The mark wants the change in speed between media, and the resulting change in direction as a consequence of it.

The same pattern repeats across the topic. Why does sound travel faster in water than in air, why does a wave diffract through a narrow gap, why does a red object look red: each has a describable observation and an underlying mechanism, and the command term decides which one is wanted. Students who learn to annotate the command term before writing, and who keep a short list of the mechanisms the syllabus expects, stop losing these marks almost immediately.

The wave equation adds a numerical trap on top. Wavelengths arrive in nanometres or centimetres, frequencies in kilohertz or megahertz, and speeds in metres per second, so an answer out by a factor of a thousand is the most common wrong answer in the topic. We teach a magnitude estimate before calculating: what order of size should this answer be. A student who expects a number near three hundred million for the speed of light in a vacuum notices immediately when their calculator produces three hundred thousand, and that habit is worth more than any formula sheet.
bullets: Explain wants a mechanism; describe wants the observation
Keep a short list of the mechanisms the topic expects
Convert prefixes before substituting into the wave equation
Estimate the order of magnitude before calculating

sections.heading: Designing a physics investigation that can be marked in the upper bands
paragraphs: Criterion B asks for a problem explained, a hypothesis supported by scientific reasoning, variables identified with their handling described, and a safe, replicable method. In physics the giveaway between a middle-band and an upper-band plan is almost always the variable section, because physics investigations have more plausible confounds than biology ones and students mention none of them.

Take a pendulum investigation, which many MYP 4 cohorts run alongside the resistance practical. The student varies length and measures period. The upper-band plan names the mass of the bob and the amplitude of swing as controlled variables, says how each is held constant, and explains why amplitude matters at large angles. It also specifies timing ten oscillations and dividing, because a single period is comparable to human reaction time. That last sentence is a validity argument, and it is the kind of detail the upper bands describe.

A session on this does not involve teaching pendulums. It involves taking the student's own plan, following the method literally while asking what happens next, and stopping at every point where a reader would have to guess. Then each guess becomes a sentence. The student writes all of them; a tutor questions, challenges and gives written feedback, and never supplies text for submission. That boundary matters in the MYP as much as in the Diploma, and a tutor who blurs it is exposing the student to an academic-honesty finding that outlasts any grade. The useful side effect of working this way is that the student learns to read their own plan as a stranger would, which is the skill the Diploma Programme internal assessment will ask for in two years' time.
bullets: Name every plausible confound, not just the obvious variable
Say how each control is maintained, and with what
Time ten oscillations and divide, with the reaction-time reason stated
The student writes every word submitted; the tutor questions and feeds back

sections.heading: From MYP 5 physics to DP Physics or A Level: what to fix in the final two terms
paragraphs: At the end of MYP 5, Dubai families choose between Diploma Programme Physics at Standard or Higher Level and A Level Physics, and the decision is too often made on which school has a place. The better evidence is the criterion record. Strong criterion A with weak criterion C means secure recall and shaky independent data handling, and that profile finds the first DP year hardest, because the internal assessment arrives before the content is finished being taught.

The table compares the two routes on the things that actually differ for a student who found MYP physics hard: how much independent design is required, when it is required, how uncertainty is treated, and how much of the grade rests on a single terminal sitting. Neither route is easier in general. They are differently shaped, and the shape interacts with the student's own profile.

Whichever route is chosen, four things are worth fixing in the last two MYP 5 terms, and all four are cheap compared with remediation later. Significant figures and instrument resolution, because both routes assess them explicitly. Writing a research question answerable with school apparatus, which is the most common internal assessment failure. Processing data without being told which calculation to apply. And linearising a simple relationship, which is a mathematics skill that arrives in DP Physics early and unannounced. Twelve sessions across two terms covers all four and removes most of the first-year shock. Doing them in MYP 5, while the stakes are low and the timetable still has room, costs a fraction of remediating the same gaps in the middle of a Diploma year when five other subjects are competing for the same evenings.

The tutor works on the script you sent and finishes by naming which of the four operations is weak and what a six to eight session block would address. The written note is yours whether you continue or not.

process.title: Fix the operations before the topics
process.description: Where the errors cluster on rearrangement, conversion, gradient or standard form, we drill those inside physics questions rather than teaching topics in sequence. The student writes their own one-page reference sheet. Most scripts improve across several topics at once, because one operation was making several topics look broken.

process.title: Then follow the school's physics sequence
process.description: Once the operations hold under timed conditions, the weekly slot follows whatever unit the school is teaching, with simulators for circuits and motion and a marked piece every second session. Send the task sheet whenever an investigation is set, so sessions can be scheduled backwards from the school's internal deadline.

process.title: Review at half term and plan the interruptions
process.description: At half term we compare the error tally with the baseline and decide whether to continue, change focus or reduce to fortnightly. School examination weeks are pause weeks. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar or a late weekend morning and shorten to forty-five minutes. Planning that in advance is what keeps a term's plan intact.

whyPoints.title: The arithmetic is diagnosed before the physics is taught
whyPoints.description: Four operations carry most MYP physics marks, and a script dominated by rearrangement and conversion errors does not need a year of topic teaching. We count the error types first and will say when the useful purchase is a short operations block rather than a term of weekly physics.

whyPoints.title: The in-home premium is published, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Dubai in-home bands run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 online for a qualified subject tutor. whyPoints.title: Work on the student's own graphs and circuits
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on the graph the student drew and the resistance plan they submitted, not on a worksheet. A shared screen holds the rubric, the marked script and a live spreadsheet together, which is where gradient and processing corrections actually get made rather than merely explained.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory
whyPoints.description: Practical work belongs at school with school apparatus and supervision, and no tutor replaces it. What a tutor contributes is the design beforehand and the processing afterwards, which is where criteria B and C are marked. Anyone offering to run your child's MYP practicals has misread the programme.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval from KHDA, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. We publish no IB examination dates, because the IB's own site cannot be verified automatically. And no tutor can promise a grade on a programme whose boundaries the school itself applies.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor come to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. For Dubai families everything is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Visiting tutors do exist in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with the travel inside the fee, and they usually require a two-hour minimum in the outer communities because of the drive. The practical cost of that model is a shortlist defined by geography rather than by who has marked MYP physics work.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics in class and still fail the calculations?
faqs.answer: Because classwork is scaffolded in ways that hide arithmetic. On the board the equation is already rearranged and the units are already consistent. In a test the student must rearrange before substituting and convert first, and those two operations are where most errors live. The test for this takes ten minutes: give six mixed-unit calculations with the unknown in the denominator, untimed. If accuracy collapses, the obstacle is one of four operations rather than the physics, and that is a six to eight session fix.

faqs.question: What are the four operations MYP physics depends on?
faqs.answer: Rearranging an equation with the unknown in any position, including a denominator. Converting units before substituting rather than afterwards. Reading a gradient as a change in the vertical quantity divided by a change in the horizontal one, both read off the axes. And handling standard form with prefixes, since wavelengths arrive in nanometres and frequencies in kilohertz. A student fluent in those four can be taught any MYP physics topic quickly. A student missing one will look weak in several topics at once, which is why topic-by-topic tutoring so often disappoints.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child is reading motion graphs properly?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions about any graph in their book. What is on the vertical axis, in words and units. What does the gradient of this particular graph physically represent. What does a flat line mean on this graph specifically. A student who cannot answer the third will describe a horizontal line on a velocity-time graph as stopped, which is wrong and costs marks whenever graphs appear. All three are drillable in about two sessions, using the student's own graphs rather than textbook examples.

faqs.question: Why did my child lose criterion B marks on the resistance of a wire investigation?
faqs.answer: Almost always the controlled variables. A student who varies length while using one reel of wire has controlled thickness and material in practice but said nothing about it in the plan, and criterion B marks the plan. The second common loss is heating: current warms a thin wire and raises its resistance, so a plan that does not mention switching off between readings has a validity gap. The third is plotting raw potential difference against length instead of calculating resistance first, which costs criterion C marks for unprocessed data.

faqs.question: What makes an efficiency calculation go wrong so often?
faqs.answer: Three things, and only one involves understanding energy. Inverting the fraction, so total goes over useful and the answer exceeds 100 per cent without the student noticing. Mixing joules with kilojoules. And multiplying by a hundred either twice or not at all. A six-step procedure written by the student fixes all three: label useful and total, convert to one unit, divide useful by total, multiply by a hundred once, then check the answer is below a hundred and physically sensible. Two or three weeks of short drills makes it automatic.

faqs.question: My child writes that light bends during refraction and gets no marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because bending is the observation and explain asks for the mechanism. The mark wants the change in the speed of light between the two media, with the change in direction following from it. This is a command-term problem rather than a physics one, and it recurs across the whole waves topic: why sound travels faster in water, why a wave diffracts, why a red object looks red. Each has an easy description and a required mechanism. Annotating the command term before writing resolves most of these within a few weeks.

faqs.question: Can physics really be taught well without apparatus in the room?
faqs.answer: The apparatus part is not the tutored part. MYP practical work happens at school, supervised, with school equipment, and nothing replaces that. Tutoring covers the design beforehand and the processing afterwards, which is precisely where criteria B and C are marked. A shared screen holds the task sheet, the rubric and a live spreadsheet at once, and a circuit simulator lets a student predict an ammeter reading before changing a resistor, which demonstrates variable control better than most table-top demonstrations manage.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to hire a physics tutor who lives in our community?
faqs.answer: Sometimes marginally, and it usually costs more in other ways. Published Dubai in-home bands sit above online bands precisely because travel is inside the fee, and in the outer communities a visiting tutor typically requires two hours for the economics to work. A family needing forty-five focused minutes on gradient reading pays for two hours and watches a tired student in hour two. The larger cost is the shortlist: proximity becomes the selection criterion instead of whether the tutor has marked MYP physics criterion tasks.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a MYP 4 physics student usually need?
faqs.answer: If the error tally is dominated by operations, six to eight sessions is often the whole intervention, after which a fortnightly check is enough. If the tally shows genuine mechanism errors in electricity or waves, add a weekly slot through the term the school teaches those units. What rarely works in Dubai is three weekly sessions across biology, chemistry and physics at once: the week does not contain them, and the plan is usually abandoned by half term and paid for in full.

faqs.question: Should we choose DP Physics or A Level Physics after MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Read the criterion record rather than the overall grade. DP Physics requires an internal assessment designed by the student from their own research question, often before the content is finished, so a student strong on recall and weak on independent data processing meets the hardest part first. A Level concentrates more weight in terminal papers and generally places the independent work later. Neither is easier in general. Ask the MYP coordinator for the strand marks and decide from the shape of them.

faqs.question: What should we fix in MYP 5 before physics gets harder?
faqs.answer: Four things, roughly twelve sessions across two terms. Significant figures and instrument resolution, because both post-16 routes assess them explicitly. Writing a research question that can actually be answered with school apparatus, which is the most common internal assessment failure. Processing data without being told which calculation to use. And linearising a simple relationship, which arrives early in DP Physics and is a mathematics skill rather than a physics one. Doing these in MYP 5 is far cheaper than remediating them in the first post-16 term.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat specific figures with caution. Since the permit is free, there is no reason not to ask to see it.

faqs.question: Can the tutor help write up my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor questions the plan, challenges the variable list, follows the method literally to find the gaps, processes the data alongside the student and gives written feedback on a draft. What a tutor must never do is supply any part of the text that is submitted. Every word of an MYP investigation has to be the student's own. That boundary is not a formality: outsourced work is an academic-honesty breach whose consequences for the student last far longer than a low criterion mark would.

intro.heading: How to tell, by half term, whether physics tutoring is working
paragraphs: Most families in Dubai judge tutoring by two signals, and both arrive too late to act on. The first is the school report, which lands at the end of a term and reduces an entire semester of physics to a number and a sentence about engagement. The second is the student's own account, which is cheerful in week two and vague by week seven. Neither tells you whether the money is buying anything, and by the time a report says otherwise, a term has gone.

There is a better signal available and it costs nothing to ask for. MYP physics generates marked artefacts continuously: criterion A question sets, criterion B investigation plans, criterion C data processing, end-of-unit tests. A tutor working properly accumulates those artefacts, names the error type on each one, and can show you the same error type disappearing across four pieces of work. That is a record a parent can read in five minutes without knowing any physics, and it is the record this page is built around.

The reason physics lends itself to this is that its failure modes are unusually well defined. A student does not go wrong on physics in general. They go wrong on rearranging an equation with the unknown in the denominator, or on converting centimetres to metres before substituting, or on reading a gradient as a ratio of single values rather than as a change over a change, or on dropping units entirely, or on writing a conclusion that describes a graph instead of answering the hypothesis. Six recurring types cover most of a Dubai MYP physics script. Each can be counted, and counts can fall.

Grade movement needs the same honesty. The MYP does not award percentages. Each of the four criteria is marked from 0 to 8, those four marks sum to a total out of 32, and the school converts the total to a 1 to 7 grade using the boundary table it applies, which the MYP coordinator can give you. So a 5 becoming a 6 is not a few extra per cent; it is specific strand marks moving, usually on criterion C or on the upper bands of criterion A. Tutoring that cannot say which strand it is targeting cannot explain what a grade change would even consist of.

What follows is the operational version of that argument. An evidence pack by week four, eight and twelve. The marked-script loop that produces it. The error inventory with frequencies and fixes. A twelve-week plan counted backwards from a summative. What a session note should contain. How physics is taught without a laboratory on screen, and what honestly stays at school. And the three questions that establish whether a tutor in this market is permitted to work and experienced in this programme.

dubai/ib-myp-physics-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics appears under three different names across a Dubai student's school career, and the evidence a parent should look for changes with each. Here is what each stage produces that can actually be inspected, and what it predicts about the next one.

programmes.name: Integrated sciences, physics strand
programmes.description: Forces, energy, light, sound and simple electrical circuits taught inside integrated sciences, usually with the arithmetic kept gentle. The evidence worth collecting at this stage is unit discipline and graph conventions, because a student who leaves MYP 3 writing bare numbers without units carries that habit into every quantitative subject afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students arrive in MYP 1 from the PYP and from British and Indian primaries across the city, and their mathematics backgrounds differ more than their science backgrounds do. We check decimal and ratio fluency in the first session, because a physics problem in MYP 2 is usually an arithmetic problem wearing physics clothing.

programmes.name: MYP physics as a separate subject
programmes.description: Motion and graphs, forces and Newton's laws, energy transfers and efficiency, waves, and electricity including series and parallel circuits. Criterion tasks are now unscaffolded, so an investigation plan has to name and control its own variables, and data processing has to choose its own calculation. The scripts produced here are the most informative evidence in the whole programme.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai continuum schools split the sciences at MYP 4, which means a physics teacher, a physics rubric and a physics deadline all appear at once alongside two other sciences doing the same. Families who collect the marked physics work from the first term find the pattern long before the report does.

programmes.name: MYP 5 on-screen assessment
programmes.description: Where a school registers for it, MYP 5 sciences are assessed on screen, with data supplied in the paper and answers typed. Physics suffers more than biology from screen format, because students lose the margin they would normally use for a sketch or a quick rearrangement. Practice has to be timed, typed and on screen to be worth anything.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the MYP coordinator whether your child's cohort is registered for eAssessment or sitting internal examinations, because the two need different preparation. We publish no IB dates on these pages: the IB's own site cannot be verified automatically, so confirm every date with the school or on ibo.org before planning around it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Physics at Standard or Higher Level, with uncertainties handled quantitatively, logarithmic and linearised relationships, and an internal assessment designed by the student from a research question of their own. The MYP criterion C record is the best available predictor of how the internal assessment will go, and better than any mock paper mark.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students choosing between DP Physics and A Level Physics at the end of MYP 5 often decide on timetable availability. The more useful evidence is the strand record: strong recall with weak independent data processing is the profile that finds DP year one hardest, and it is visible in marked MYP work two years earlier.

dubai/ib-myp-physics-tutor.subjectsIntro: The list below is the MYP physics content Dubai families ask about, written with the specific place marks are lost in each. Every line is checkable against your child's own marked scripts, which is the point.

subjects.name: Motion, speed and distance-time graphs
subjects.description: Reading a gradient is the skill, and it is the one most often faked. Students take a single pair of coordinates and divide, which gives the right answer only through the origin. Teaching change in y over change in x, with both read off the axes, repairs several criterion C marks at once.

subjects.name: Forces, Newton's laws and free-body diagrams
subjects.description: The common loss is a diagram with arrows of equal length for unequal forces, or a resultant stated without direction. Marks here are mostly presentational, which makes them cheap to recover once a student is shown what the mark scheme actually looks for in a labelled diagram.

subjects.name: Energy transfers, work and efficiency
subjects.description: Efficiency calculations fail on units and on which energy goes on top. Students who can state the formula still divide the wrong way round under time pressure. A short drill of six calculations with mixed units, repeated weekly, moves this permanently within a month.

subjects.name: Waves, sound and light
subjects.description: Wave diagrams needing amplitude and wavelength marked correctly, the wave equation applied with consistent units, and refraction explained as a change of speed rather than as bending. The last of those is a mechanism, so it belongs to the explain command term and is marked accordingly.

subjects.name: Electricity, circuits and resistance
subjects.description: Series and parallel behaviour, Ohm's law, and the practical investigation of resistance that nearly every MYP 4 cohort runs. The errors cluster on rearranging the equation when the unknown is in the denominator and on reading an ammeter scale with the wrong interval.

subjects.name: Criterion B physics investigation design
subjects.description: A testable hypothesis with a physical mechanism, variables named with the method of control for each, and a replicable procedure. Physics plans usually fail on control: a student varying the length of a wire who says nothing about keeping the thickness and material constant has designed an uncontrolled experiment.

subjects.name: Criterion C data processing in physics
subjects.description: Repeat readings averaged, a derived quantity calculated rather than raw values plotted, a line of best fit judged rather than joined, anomalies identified, and a conclusion that names the hypothesis. This is where the largest number of recoverable marks sits in a physics script.

subjects.name: The mathematics underneath physics
subjects.description: Rearranging equations, standard form, significant figures, unit conversion and gradient work. A student who is behind in MYP mathematics presents as weak in physics, and the sessions that help most are frequently mathematics sessions aimed at four specific operations.

subjects.name: Measurement, uncertainty and significant figures
subjects.description: Instrument resolution, repeat spread, and answers quoted to a sensible number of figures. This carries few MYP marks directly and predicts DP Physics difficulty strongly, so it is worth teaching in MYP 5 even when the current rubric barely rewards it.

subjects.name: Command terms in physics questions
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, calculate, determine and evaluate each demand a different answer shape. Calculate and determine both want working shown; explain wants a mechanism. Students who annotate the command term before writing lose fewer marks to misreading than to any gap in content.

sections.heading: What evidence of progress in MYP physics looks like at weeks four, eight and twelve
paragraphs: A parent who cannot read physics can still audit physics tutoring, provided the tutor produces the right artefacts. The question to ask is not whether the sessions are going well. It is: show me the last marked piece, tell me which error types you counted, and tell me how that count compares with week one. If those three answers exist, the arrangement is working or visibly not working, and either way you can act. If they do not exist, the only available evidence is the student's mood.

The table sets out what should be in the folder by each checkpoint. Week zero is a baseline, which matters because without it no later improvement can be demonstrated. Week four should show the first error type falling. Week eight should show a redrafted criterion task beside its original, which is the single most persuasive artefact in MYP science tutoring because the change is visible to anyone. Week twelve should show a school-marked piece, not a tutor-marked one, since the school's mark is the one that counts.

That last distinction matters more than it sounds. A tutor marking their own student's work is a useful teaching device and weak evidence. The strong evidence is a school-set, school-marked task scoring better on the strand the tutoring targeted. In MYP physics that usually arrives in the second half of a term, which is why twelve weeks is the right unit for judging an intervention rather than four. Four weeks is enough to tell whether the diagnosis was right; twelve is what it takes to see the school's own marks move.

sections.heading: The marked-script loop: how one session uses last fortnight's work
paragraphs: The loop is simple enough to describe in four steps and rare enough in practice to be worth describing. The student does a piece of work. The tutor marks it against the school's rubric and names each error by type rather than circling it. The next session opens by making the student correct two of those errors themselves, out loud, explaining why the original was wrong. Then the session teaches whatever the errors revealed, and sets the next piece. Repeat fortnightly.

The step that does the work is the third one. A student who is told they forgot to convert centimetres to metres learns nothing durable, because being told is not the same as noticing. A student who is handed their own script and asked to find the two unit errors in it starts checking units unprompted within a few weeks. The same applies to gradients: a student who recalculates their own wrong gradient, reading the change in y and the change in x off the axes, stops taking single coordinate pairs.

The loop also produces the audit trail almost incidentally. Six marked pieces across a term, each with a typed error tally, is a record of exactly what changed and when. We send the tally in the session note so it accumulates in your inbox rather than in a folder nobody opens. Parents in Dubai are often at work while lessons run, and this is the only honest substitute for sitting in on one. It is also what makes a conversation with the school's physics teacher productive, because you arrive with specifics instead of an impression.

sections.heading: The MYP physics error inventory: six types, with frequencies and fixes
paragraphs: Across the marked MYP physics work we see from Dubai schools, six error types account for the large majority of lost marks, and only one of them is a knowledge problem. That proportion is the single most useful thing a parent can know before buying tutoring, because it means a plan built on re-teaching topics is aimed at the smallest part of the problem. The table lists the six with the root cause and the fix, so you can match them against your child's own scripts this evening.

Two deserve particular attention. Unit and conversion errors are the most frequent and the fastest to fix, and they are also the ones most often dismissed as carelessness. They are not carelessness; they are a missing habit, namely writing the unit next to every number as it is written rather than at the end. The habit takes about three weeks to install and then holds for years. Gradient misreading is the second, and it matters disproportionately because it corrupts criterion C on every graph-based investigation the student will do.

The one knowledge-shaped error on the list is the mechanism error: explaining refraction as light bending rather than as a change of speed, or explaining a series circuit by restating the observation. That is genuine physics teaching and takes longer, which is why it is worth knowing how little of a typical script it accounts for. Count the types on your child's last two marked pieces before you buy anything, and the right purchase usually becomes obvious: often a short block on arithmetic habits rather than a year of physics content.

sections.heading: What a grade change in MYP physics actually consists of
paragraphs: Parents often ask how many marks a tutor will add, and the question cannot be answered honestly in that form, partly because nobody can promise a grade and partly because the MYP does not work in marks the way the question assumes. Physics is assessed against four criteria, each marked from 0 to 8. The four scores sum to a total out of 32, and the school converts that total into a 1 to 7 grade using the boundary table it applies. Ask the MYP coordinator for that table; it is the only accurate way to see how far your child is from the next grade.

What follows from this is useful. Because each criterion is scored separately, a student can be two marks from a grade change on one strand and nowhere near it on another, and the cheapest route up is almost always the strand with the most mechanical losses. In physics that is nearly always criterion C. A student scoring 5 on criterion C because their conclusions describe graphs and their data is unprocessed can realistically address both inside a term, and those are strand marks rather than a vague improvement.

It also follows that some targets are not worth buying. Moving criterion A from 7 to 8 is expensive, slow and depends on handling genuinely unfamiliar applications under time pressure. Moving criterion D from 4 to 6 may be a referencing exercise. No tutor can promise any of it, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching. What a tutor can do is name the strand, show the marks that are mechanically recoverable, and produce the fortnightly evidence that lets you judge whether the recovery is happening.

sections.heading: A twelve-week physics plan, counted backwards from the summative
paragraphs: Plans fail when they are counted forwards from the day you hire someone. Count backwards from the date the school assesses, and the sequence organises itself: revision of marked work in the final fortnight, no new content in the last three weeks, the redraft at week eight while there is still time for it to matter, and the diagnosis done early enough to be wrong without costing the term. The table is the version we use, and it assumes a single weekly session with a marked piece every fortnight.

Two features are deliberate. The mid-point review at week six exists because first diagnoses are sometimes wrong, and a plan with no scheduled opportunity to change direction will simply continue in the wrong one. And the last three weeks teach nothing new, because new content introduced late competes with consolidation and generally loses. Students arrive at a physics summative better prepared by rehearsing six familiar calculation types than by meeting a seventh.

The plan also survives the Dubai calendar, which is the practical test. School examination weeks are pause weeks, not extra weeks. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar or a late weekend morning and shorten to forty-five minutes. Half term is used for the redraft, since no new school content is arriving to compete with it. Families who plan those three interruptions at the start of the term almost always complete the twelve weeks; families who do not usually finish eight of them and then wonder why the evidence pack is thin.

sections.heading: What a session note should say, and what to do when it says nothing
paragraphs: A session note is a short written record sent after each lesson, and it is the mechanism that makes everything above auditable. A useful one has four elements: what was worked on, named by strand or error type rather than by topic; what the student did with it, including what they got wrong during the session; what has been set; and what the next marked piece should show. Four lines is enough. It takes a tutor three minutes and it is the difference between a record and an impression.

A note that says we covered forces and motion and he is improving contains no information. Nothing in it can be checked, compared with last fortnight or taken to a physics teacher. If that is what arrives twice in a row, ask directly for the error tally and the strand name. A tutor working from marked evidence will produce them immediately, because they already exist in their marking. A tutor working from a textbook sequence will not, and that answer is itself the information you needed.

For Dubai households this matters more than it might elsewhere, because the parent is frequently not in the room. Sessions run at six or seven in the evening while one or both parents are still at work in Business Bay or DIFC, and the student's report of the lesson is not a reliable instrument. The accumulated notes also make the parent-teacher conversation at school far more productive: arriving with three specific error types and the dates they were last seen gets a far better conversation with a physics teacher than asking how he is doing in physics.

sections.heading: Teaching physics without a laboratory, and what honestly stays at school
paragraphs: Physics is the science where the online question gets asked most, because it is the one with apparatus in the room. The honest answer is in two parts. Practical work belongs at school, supervised, with the school's equipment, and no tutor of any kind replaces that. Nothing on this page suggests otherwise, and a tutor who offers to run your child's MYP practicals is offering something the programme does not want.

What a tutor does is the design before and the processing after, and both are better on a shared screen than at a table. Before: the plan is read, the hypothesis is pushed for a mechanism, the variable list is challenged for controls, and the method is tested by having the student read it aloud while the tutor follows it literally and asks what happens next. After: the data goes into a spreadsheet the student keeps, repeats are averaged, a derived quantity is calculated, and a line of best fit is drawn and argued about.

Simulations cover the rest usefully. A circuit simulator lets a student change one resistor while predicting the ammeter reading, which demonstrates control far better than a demonstration with real wires and a flat battery. A motion simulation can be run twice with one variable altered while the student narrates what is being held constant. None of this is a substitute for a school laboratory and none of it needs to be. It is the part of physics where the marks are, and it happens to be the part that a shared screen does well.
bullets: Practical work stays at school, supervised, with school apparatus

sections.heading: Checking a physics tutor in Dubai: the permit and three other questions
paragraphs: Start with the legal position, because it is checkable and most families never ask. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any circulating figure with scepticism. Since the permit costs nothing, ask to see it.

Then three questions about the teaching. First: which MYP physics criterion strands have you marked, and at which year? A tutor who has marked criterion C work will answer with specifics about data processing; one who has not will talk about topics. Second: will you work from our school's task sheet and rubric? Schools write their own MYP tasks, so the answer has to be yes. Third: what written record arrives after each session? If the answer is nothing, there is no way to audit the arrangement.

One further caution worth knowing in this country. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That rule has been press-reported rather than read here from ADEK's current document, so verify it with ADEK before relying on it. The practical conclusion holds regardless: an arrangement where your child's own physics teacher tutors them privately for a fee is one to decline, however convenient it looks.
