Cost: granted free of charge, valid for two years
Route: MoHRE private tutor licensing service, two working days, no fee listed
Ask directly to see the permit before the first paid session

sections.heading: The MYP 4 science split, and what it does to a household budget
paragraphs: The single largest change in MYP science spending happens at the start of MYP 4, and it catches almost every family that has not been warned. Until then, one teacher taught integrated sciences and one tutor could cover it. From MYP 4, most Dubai IB continuum schools run biology, chemistry and physics separately, with three teachers, three sets of criterion tasks and three sets of deadlines that do not coordinate. The tutoring question changes from who can teach science to which of the three is costing marks, and why.

In practice the three sciences fail for different reasons, which is why a single tutor across all three is usually the wrong purchase at this level. Biology loses marks on vocabulary and on the precision of written explanation. Chemistry loses them on quantitative work, particularly mole arithmetic and the processing of mass and volume data. Physics loses them on algebra and graph gradients. A tutor who is strong on one of those three is not automatically useful on the other two, and paying one rate for all three usually means paying a specialist rate for generalist teaching.

A workable approach is to spend on the weakest subject weekly and treat the other two diagnostically. Ask for one session in each of the other two sciences at the start of term, with a written note afterwards of what the marked work shows. If the note says habits rather than content, the fix belongs in the weekly session you are already paying for. If it says a genuine content gap, add a short block rather than a retained slot. That keeps the MYP 4 figure closer to the single-subject bands in the table above than to three times them.

sections.heading: When the cheapest option is the wrong one: coverage and the honest fallback
paragraphs: No platform covers every subject and level in every time slot, and claiming otherwise is how families end up with a mismatched tutor two weeks before a summative. MYP sciences at MYP 4 and 5 level is one of the narrower requests in this market, and the narrowest of all is a specific criterion task in a specific science at a specific evening hour. It is better to say that plainly than to accept a booking and improvise.

What happens here when the exact match is not free: we say so, we say when the slot is likely to open, and we offer the nearest honest alternative, which is usually a different evening with the right specialist rather than the right evening with the wrong one. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche MYP science request, the tutor may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before you book rather than discovered afterwards. Delivery is online either way, so the tutor's location affects the timetable and nothing else.

The thing not to buy is a cheap hour that does not address the named criterion. An AED 60 session on general science revision in the fortnight before an MYP 5 on-screen assessment is cheaper than an AED 250 session on the student's own marked script, and it is also worth less than nothing, because it consumes an evening that the marked script needed. Spend against a diagnosis, start with the trial lesson, and increase only when a marked piece of work says the current plan is not enough.
bullets: Coverage limits are stated before you book, not afterwards
A tutor outside the UAE teaching into Gulf Standard Time is disclosed in advance
Delivery is online one-to-one in every case, so location changes only the timetable

process.title: Tell us the criterion, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is short and specific: MYP year, which science, which criterion the last two summatives scored lowest on, and the school. If you do not have the criterion breakdown, ask your child's science teacher for it, or send a photograph of the last marked task sheet and we will read it from there.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the condition stated
process.description: The trial is one forty-five-minute online session at no charge, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel afterwards. It is a teaching session rather than a sales call: the tutor works on the actual task or marked script you send, and you get a written note of what the work showed and what a term of sessions would target.

process.title: Agree a shape and a slot that survives the term
process.description: Pick the pattern from the options above that fits the MYP year and the household. The slot matters more than the rate, because a session that collides with a school bus or a weekly commitment gets rescheduled twice and then quietly dropped. Choose a time you can hold through examination weeks and Ramadan.

process.title: Work on marked evidence, every fortnight
process.description: Every second session uses a piece of the student's own marked or drafted work rather than a worksheet. The tutor questions the plan, points at the strand that lost the marks, and sends a written note. That note is what tells you whether the hours are working, which no hourly rate can tell you on its own.

process.title: Change the dosage when the evidence says to
process.description: Reduce to fortnightly when the marked work stabilises, and add a short block before an on-screen assessment or an end-of-year summative. Pause rather than cancel during school examination weeks. The aim is the smallest sustained intervention that keeps the named criterion moving, not the largest package the budget will bear.

whyPoints.title: The AED figures come with sources
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A parent in Dubai transacts in dirhams and deserves to see the market before being sold inside it.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level teaching, not general science support
whyPoints.description: MYP marks are awarded against four criteria out of 8 each, so support that is not aimed at a named criterion is aimed at nothing in particular. Sessions start from the student's own marked task and the school's own rubric, which is why the first message we ask for is the criterion breakdown rather than a list of topics.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, with the travel premium removed
whyPoints.description: Published in-home bands in Dubai sit well above online bands because an evening of Sheikh Zayed Road is inside the fee. Teaching over live video removes that cost and the geographic limit behind it, so a family in Arabian Ranches can work with an MYP chemistry specialist rather than the nearest available generalist.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered openly
whyPoints.description: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a MoHRE permit issued free for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. We explain what it is, who is eligible and how to ask to see one. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none; what we can do is tell you exactly what to check.

whyPoints.title: Honest boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has written. No part of a criterion task, a Personal Project or any assessed piece is ever supplied on a student's behalf, and we will tell a parent plainly when a request crosses that line. The alternative is an academic-honesty finding that follows the student much longer than a poor grade would.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP sciences tutor in Dubai charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online tier to AED 650 for a premium named tutor. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; Unitors lists IB support from AED 200; TutorChase quotes around AED 270; BartyED publishes AED 650. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. For MYP 4 and 5 sciences specifically, expect the qualified online band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300 rather than the entry tier.

faqs.question: Why is MYP science tutoring priced above IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Supply, mostly. The International Baccalaureate accounts for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against 37 per cent for British curricula, so a tutor who has marked MYP criterion tasks is drawn from a much smaller pool than one who has taught Cambridge IGCSE. The work also differs: MYP marks reward hypothesis design, variable control and evaluation, which cannot be taught from a past-paper bank the way a terminal IGCSE syllabus largely can. A tutor who quotes the same rate for both without asking which criterion is weak is usually pricing IGCSE work and planning to deliver it.

faqs.question: Is the hourly rate lower if my two children share one MYP science session?
faqs.answer: Group rates in this market do sit lower per student, typically around AED 40 to AED 90 an hour each at the MYP 1 to 3 level and AED 70 to AED 130 at MYP 4 and 5. Whether that is good value depends on the work. Two siblings in the same MYP year with the same weak criterion can share an hour productively. Two children in different years, or one needing criterion B design help and the other needing graph work, cannot, and the hour ends up half-useful to both. Criterion task coaching on a student's own draft is not shareable at all.

faqs.question: Do MYP science tutoring rates in Dubai go up before the MYP 5 on-screen assessments?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, though it shows up as scarcity rather than a published increase. Supply of MYP-experienced science tutors is fixed in the short term and demand concentrates in the weeks before internal deadlines and on-screen eAssessment sittings, so the affordable evening slots disappear first and what remains is the specialist end of the band. The practical response is to book a regular slot early in the academic year, even fortnightly, rather than trying to buy a block six weeks out when the only availability left is at the AED 300 and above end.

faqs.question: Does the price we are quoted for tutoring in Dubai include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing before the first paid session. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition depends on the provider's own registration status and the nature of the service, and we do not state the tax position of other providers as fact here. What a parent should insist on is simple: whether the figure quoted is the figure payable, whether it is per hour or per session, and whether a session shorter than sixty minutes is billed as a full hour. Those three answers remove almost every billing dispute families report in this market.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours does an MYP 4 science student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: About eighteen hours across a term covers most students, structured as one weekly session in the weakest of the three sciences plus a fortnightly review of the second weakest. Three weekly sessions across biology, chemistry and physics looks thorough and generally collapses by half term, because it leaves no evening for homework. In MYP 1 to 3 a single weekly session for one term, aimed at one habit such as graph conventions or unit discipline, is usually enough and holds its value for years afterwards.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper private tutor in Dubai legally allowed to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Only with a permit. Private tuition in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you read with scepticism. Because the permit is free, ask to see it; a tutor who deflects has given you the answer.

faqs.question: What does an MYP sciences grade out of 32 mean on my child's report?
faqs.answer: It is the sum of four criterion scores, each marked from 0 to 8: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The school converts that total into a 1 to 7 grade using the MYP boundaries it applies, so ask the MYP coordinator for the exact table rather than assuming a percentage. The useful figure for buying tutoring is not the total but the four parts: a student on 7 for criterion A and 3 for criterion C has a specific, cheap problem, while flat scores of 5 across all four need something broader.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover MYP biology, chemistry and physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: For MYP 1 to 3 integrated sciences, yes, and it is the sensible purchase. From MYP 4, when most Dubai schools split the three, it is usually the wrong one. The three fail for different reasons: biology on vocabulary and written precision, chemistry on mole arithmetic and quantitative data handling, physics on algebra and graph gradients. A tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in the other two. Buy a specialist for the weakest subject weekly, and treat the other two with a diagnostic session and a written note at the start of term.

faqs.question: What does it cost if we only need help with one criterion B investigation?
faqs.answer: Criterion task coaching sits in the specialist band in this market, roughly AED 200 to AED 350 an hour online, and the usual shape is two to four sessions from the task brief to the student's final draft. The tutor reads the school's rubric and task sheet, interrogates the hypothesis and the variable list, and gives written feedback on the student's own draft. The student writes every word. It is more expensive per hour than general support and often cheaper overall, because the corrections apply to every investigation the student writes for the rest of the programme.

faqs.question: Is online MYP science tuition genuinely cheaper than a home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the published bands show why. Online one-to-one in Dubai sits at roughly AED 45 to AED 300 an hour depending on qualification, while in-home one-to-one sits at roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with advertised monthly packages of about AED 799 online against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 in-home. The difference is travel, not teaching. A tutor crossing the city at 5pm commits an evening for one paid hour. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits in the UAE at all; our lessons are one-to-one over live video, with in-home teaching offered only in India.

faqs.question: Do we pay for a session we cancel the night before?
faqs.answer: Our own slots can be moved up to the previous evening without a charge, and we would rather move a session than have a tired student sit through one after a late school event. What matters more generally is asking the question before you commit anywhere in this market, because cancellation terms are where quoted hourly rates quietly become real monthly costs. Ask three things in writing: the notice period, whether a missed session is forfeited or banked, and what happens to a prepaid block if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze for 2026-27 change our tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For many households that is a flat school line for the first time in several years, which makes this a reasonable year to spend deliberately rather than reactively. Spending deliberately means a diagnosed criterion and a sustainable fortnightly or weekly slot from September, rather than an emergency block of specialist hours in the spring.

faqs.question: What happens if no MYP sciences specialist is free at the hour we want?
faqs.answer: We say so, and we say when the slot is likely to open. The usual honest alternative is a different evening with the right specialist rather than your preferred evening with the wrong one, because a mismatched tutor two weeks before a summative costs more than a week of waiting. Where no UAE-based tutor covers a narrow MYP science request, the tutor may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before you book. Delivery is online one-to-one in every case, so the tutor's location affects only the timetable.

dubai/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, then look at the rate
dubai/ib-myp-sciences-tutor.closingBody: Dubai's tutoring market prices an hour anywhere from AED 45 to AED 650, and the number on its own tells a parent almost nothing. What tells you something is the criterion breakdown on the last two marked summatives, the MYP year your child is in, and whether the three sciences have split yet. Send those three things with a photograph of a marked task sheet, take the free trial lesson, and read the written note that follows it. If the note does not name a criterion and a change to make, you have learned something useful about the tutor and spent nothing. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school week.

intro.heading: Why families ask for a home tutor, and what they are really asking for
paragraphs: The phrase parents type is 'home tutor'. The thing they want is visibility. A tutor in the room feels verifiable in a way a grade on a report card three months from now does not: you can hear the lesson from the kitchen, you can see the books open, you know the hour happened. That instinct is sound. The problem is that presence is weak evidence. An hour of friendly conversation in Spanish looks and sounds identical to an hour that moves a Criterion C mark, and from the kitchen you cannot tell which one you paid for.

Marked work can tell you. MYP Language Acquisition is scored on four criteria of eight marks each, and every assessed task in the subject carries one or two of them. A tutor working properly can hand you, each week, a piece of your child's own writing or a recording of their own speaking, marked against a named criterion, with strand-level comments. Four weeks of that is a readable record. Three months of 'she's doing much better' is not. The difference is not effort or warmth; it is whether anyone wrote anything down.

This is where the in-home model starts to cost you rather than reassure you. A Dubai in-home rate of AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is what the market charges, is partly a mileage charge. The tutor who can reach Dubai Marina or Al Sufouh by half past five on a Tuesday is selected by geography first and by MYP Spanish expertise second. For a subject as thinly staffed as Language Acquisition, that ordering is the whole problem: there are far more Spanish speakers within a twenty-minute drive of any Dubai community than there are tutors who can tell you what separates a five from a seven on Criterion D.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around a Dubai school run. What that buys is a wider pool and a better record. Written work is annotated live on a shared screen and sent back afterwards. Speaking tasks are recorded, replayed and marked while the student listens, which is something neither a living room nor a classroom of twenty-two usually manages.

The rest of this page is built around that record. There is a table of what the Dubai market charges and how much of the hour is travel. There is a twelve-week evidence log showing exactly which task lands in which week and what a parent can check. There is a section on reading a Dubai MYP report card against a tutor's marking, and one on what to do when twelve weeks of evidence shows no movement, because that happens and the honest answer is not another term of the same thing.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-home-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three school-age IB programmes. The evidence question changes shape in each of them, because what gets written down about a student changes shape too.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP reporting is descriptive, which makes progress hard to track numerically and easy to track in artefacts. For an additional language the readable evidence is a short recording every few weeks and a page of the child's own writing. Three such pairs across a term show more than any comment bank entry, and they cost nothing to keep.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP schools vary widely in how much additional-language time they timetable, and many offer French and Arabic without Spanish. Families aiming at Spanish in MYP 1 should ask in Year 5 what the language offer will be, then decide whether a short run of groundwork is worth it rather than discovering a Phase 1 start at eleven.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · Years 7-11, labelled MYP 1 to MYP 5
programmes.description: The programme this page is about. Criterion-referenced marking means the evidence is already structured for you: four criteria, eight marks each, a named strand behind every mark. A tutor who returns work in that format produces a record that lines up with the school's own, which is what makes comparison possible rather than aspirational.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP cohorts turn over heavily, and a student who joined in MYP 3 often has no marking history at the school at all. In those cases the tutor's own first four marked tasks become the baseline, which is a reason to start the record early rather than wait for a first report card in November.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Criteria give way to assessment components with published weightings, and the internal assessment in Spanish becomes an individual oral. Evidence becomes predicted-grade shaped: timed papers marked to component boundaries, and recorded orals. The habit of keeping marked work from MYP pays off here, because a DP1 predicted grade conversation goes better with a folder than with a memory.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set option blocks for DP1 in the spring of MYP 5, so a student's MYP Spanish record is the document that argues for or against a Spanish B place. Phase evidence beats enthusiasm in that meeting, and it has to exist before the meeting rather than be assembled after it.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Language Acquisition strands and neighbouring courses Dubai families ask us for, described by what the marked evidence looks like in each rather than by syllabus content.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish listening, Criterion A
subjects.description: Evidence is a transcript-free score on an unseen audio task, repeated monthly on comparable material. Criterion A moves faster than the other three because it responds to listening volume, so a month-on-month comparison on similar-length audio is the clearest early sign that a weekly session is doing anything.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish reading, Criterion B
subjects.description: Evidence is a marked unseen text task with the inference questions circled. The characteristic failure is a blank where the answer was implied rather than stated, and it shows up identically in September and in March unless somebody names it. Keep the first and fourth attempts; the gap is visible without reading Spanish.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish response tasks, Criterion C
subjects.description: Evidence is the plan as well as the response. A tutor working on Criterion C should be handing back a three-idea planning frame alongside the written answer, because the frame is where the mark is won or lost. Parents can read the frame even without Spanish and see whether format and audience were addressed.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish production, Criterion D
subjects.description: Evidence is two pieces of writing side by side with range marked rather than errors marked. Criterion D rewards variety of structure and register, which is why a careful student who has learned to write safely stalls. The marking should show what was attempted, not only what was wrong.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish speaking and interaction
subjects.description: Evidence is audio. A ninety-second recorded interaction from the trial lesson, repeated every four to six weeks, is the single most persuasive record available in this subject, and it is the one thing an in-home hour almost never produces. Families keep the files; we do not need them afterwards.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required for non-Arab students in Dubai private schools and marked on the same four criteria as Spanish. Because the criteria are identical, marked Spanish work doubles as diagnostic information about Arabic. Families running both subjects often find one tutor's criterion work lifts the other grade without extra Arabic lessons.

subjects.name: MYP French
subjects.description: Dubai's other common MYP additional language, and the usual fallback when a Spanish set does not fill. The evidence format is the same because the criteria are the same, which makes a mid-year language switch less disruptive than it sounds if the record has been kept properly.

subjects.name: DP Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: Evidence becomes component-shaped: timed writing to a prescribed theme and a recorded individual oral on a visual stimulus. For a student arriving from Phase 1 or 2 this is the realistic route, and the MYP recordings are what justify the choice to a DP coordinator.

subjects.name: DP Spanish B
subjects.description: Five prescribed themes, timed text-type writing and an individual oral. The MYP-to-DP gap shows up in the record as strong Criterion D work that collapses under time pressure. Timed tasks from MYP 5 onwards are what close it, and they also produce the evidence a predicted grade rests on.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: The evidence here belongs entirely to the student: a process journal and a report they write themselves. A tutor's contribution is questions, deadlines and feedback on what has already been produced. We put that limit in writing at the start, because an academic-honesty finding under IB rules follows the student rather than the tutor.

sections.heading: What a home tutor costs in Dubai, and how much of that hour is the drive
paragraphs: Start with the number, because every other decision hangs off it. Rates read across Dubai providers in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The gap between the online band and the in-home band is not a quality premium. It is the car. A tutor crossing from Al Barsha to Dubai Marina at five in the afternoon spends forty to fifty minutes each way in term time, and that time is inside the rate whether it is itemised or not. On a two-hour in-home booking the travel is diluted; on a single sixty-minute session it can be more than half of what you pay for. Palm Jumeirah, Dubai South and the outer Dubailand communities sit at the top of every in-home band for this reason and no other.

The second cost is invisible and larger. An in-home tutor is drawn from whoever will make that drive, which for MYP Spanish in Dubai is a short list. You are choosing from Spanish speakers in a radius rather than from Language Acquisition specialists in a market. The hour may be perfectly pleasant and still not touch the criterion that is holding the grade, because the person teaching it has never been shown the phase descriptors.

For context on the household budget: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the emirate valued at AED 1.5 billion. School costs are flat. Tutoring is the discretionary line, which is exactly why it is worth asking what a rate buys in marked work rather than in contact minutes. sections.heading: The evidence file: what you should be able to read after four weeks
paragraphs: Four weeks is long enough to judge a tutoring arrangement and short enough that stopping costs little. By the end of it you should be holding five things, none of which requires you to speak Spanish. A baseline recording of your child speaking Spanish for ninety seconds, made in the trial lesson. Four pieces of their own work, each marked against a named criterion with strand-level comments. A written note of which criterion was chosen as the focus and why. At least one planning frame showing how a response was built before it was written. And a sentence from the tutor about what has not moved.

That last item is the one that separates a record from a sales document. Every honest four-week report has something in it that has not improved, because four weeks is not long enough to fix four criteria. A tutor who tells you everything is going well has either not been marking or is not telling you what the marking says. Ask which criterion was the focus and what the first and fourth marks on it were. Two numbers and a date are a harder thing to fudge than a paragraph of encouragement.

Compare the tutor's marking with the school's. Dubai MYP report cards give four separate numbers for Spanish, one per criterion. If the tutor says Criterion C has moved from four to six and the school's next report still shows four, that is a conversation worth having with both. Sometimes the tutor is marking generously. Sometimes the school assessed a different task type. Either way you have found something out, which you cannot do without two sets of numbers.

Keep the files. Parents consistently underestimate how useful a September recording is in March, and how persuasive a folder of marked work is in a DP option-block meeting where a Spanish B place is being argued for. The record costs nothing to keep and it is the only part of the arrangement that remains yours after the lessons stop.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of MYP Spanish, week by week, with the evidence each one leaves behind
paragraphs: Below is the actual shape of a twelve-week block for an MYP 4 student placed at Phase 3 or 4 whose Criterion C has been flat. It is not a syllabus; it is a schedule of evidence. The point of publishing it is that you can hold any tutor, including ours, against it, and that you can tell in week three whether the arrangement is producing a record or just producing hours.

The first three weeks deliberately produce no visible grade movement. Weeks one and two are baseline and task-reading, which feel slow and are the reason the rest works. A parent who expects improvement by week two will cancel a block that was about to deliver. A parent who expects a baseline, a planning frame and a first marked response by week three has the right expectation and can hold the tutor to it.

Weeks four to eight are where the marks move, and the evidence is comparative rather than absolute: the same task type, attempted twice, five weeks apart, both marked. Weeks nine to twelve shift to timed conditions, because a student who can plan a Criterion C response in unlimited time and not in thirty-five minutes has half the skill. The final week produces a second recording and a written review, which is the document the next decision gets made from.

Adjust the subject matter to whatever your child's school is teaching; the tutor should be asking for the unit plan and the internal assessment calendar in week one precisely so this table can be mapped onto the school's own sequence rather than run alongside it. What should not change is the evidence column. If a block produces nothing in that column for three consecutive weeks, something has gone wrong with the arrangement and not with your child.

sections.heading: Reading a Dubai MYP report card against a tutor's marking
paragraphs: A Dubai MYP report card for Spanish usually shows four numbers out of eight and a one-to-seven grade. Parents new to the programme read the one-to-seven and ignore the four, which is the wrong way round. The four are the diagnosis; the one-to-seven is a conversion applied by the school using its own grade boundaries. That last point surprises people: the boundaries are not fixed across the IB, so a total of nineteen out of thirty-two at one Dubai school and the same nineteen at another can land on different grades.

Which means two things in practice. Comparing your child's grade with a friend's at a different school in the same community tells you very little. And asking your MYP coordinator for the boundary table is a reasonable, routine request that most schools will meet. With the boundaries in hand, the four criterion marks become usable: you can see exactly how many marks sit between the current grade and the next one, and which criterion is the cheapest place to find them.

Set the tutor's marking next to it. The pattern of agreement matters more than the absolute numbers. If both sets of marks are low on the same criterion, you have a confirmed target. If the tutor is consistently two marks above the school, the tutor is marking to a different standard and you should ask to see the strand language behind a mark. If the school is low on a criterion the tutor never assesses, the tutor is working on the wrong thing and the session plan needs changing this week, not next term.

One honest caveat about criterion marks on a report card: they are often a best-fit judgement across several tasks rather than a single score, and different teachers weight recency differently. Treat the four numbers as a direction rather than a measurement. The direction across three reporting cycles, read alongside twelve weeks of dated marked work, is about as much certainty as this subject offers anyone.

sections.heading: Recorded speaking: the one piece of evidence a living room rarely produces
paragraphs: Ask any parent how they would know their child's spoken Spanish had improved and you get the same answer: they would hear it. Almost nobody does, because the moments when a child speaks Spanish are in a classroom or in a lesson, and neither keeps a copy. The result is that spoken progress, which is half of Criterion C and most of Criterion D, is the part of this subject families have the least information about and the most anxiety over.

Recording fixes it cheaply. A ninety-second task in the trial lesson, repeated at week six and week twelve, on comparable material, produces three files that answer the question directly. You do not need Spanish to hear the difference between hesitant single clauses and connected speech with recovery when a word goes missing. That is the honest comparison, and it is more informative than any mark out of eight because it bypasses the question of whether the marking was generous.

It is also better practice than the live version. A recording can be replayed and marked against the Criterion D strands while the student listens, which almost never happens in a classroom of twenty-two or in an in-home hour running to a schedule. Students hear their own fillers, their own tense slips and their own recovery strategies, and in our experience that single exercise does more for spoken accuracy than a term of correction in the moment.

Two practical notes for Dubai families. Use headphones and a decent connection, because a poor line ruins a listening task and makes a recording useless as evidence. And keep the files yourself rather than relying on us to hold them, both because they are your child's and because they belong in the folder you take to a DP option-block meeting. We ask only for what we need to mark the task, and we say so in plain terms when any personal data about a student is collected, in line with the UAE's personal data protection law.

sections.heading: When twelve weeks of evidence shows nothing moving
paragraphs: It happens, and the way a provider handles it tells you more than any claim on a website. There are four common explanations and they call for different responses, which is why the question 'what has not moved?' belongs in every six-week review rather than only in a cancellation email.

The first is that the wrong criterion was chosen. A student whose real problem is Criterion A listening stamina will not improve if three months went on Criterion C planning, and the marked record makes that visible in about ten minutes. The second is phase mismatch: a child sitting in a Phase 4 set while working at Phase 2 produces accurate, thin work and a stable five, and no amount of tutoring inside the wrong phase changes that. The fix there is a conversation with the MYP coordinator, armed with the placement note, not more lessons.

The third is the match itself. Some pairings do not work, and in a language subject where the student has to be willing to be wrong out loud, that matters more than in maths. Asking for a different tutor is a normal request and not a complaint; we would rather rematch at week six than have a family quietly stop in week fourteen. The fourth is that nothing is wrong and the expectation was off: a grade moving from five to six in MYP Spanish typically takes two reporting cycles, not one, and a tutor who promises faster than that is selling something.

There is also the case where we should not have taken the work. MYP Spanish is a thin pool, and if we cannot staff a request with someone who knows the phase descriptors, saying so at the start is cheaper for everyone than a term of general conversation practice. No tutor, however experienced, can promise a particular grade, and nobody in this market should be offering one. What can be promised is a record you can read and a decision point you can act on.

sections.heading: Who is allowed to tutor privately in Dubai, and how a parent checks
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and u.ae states plainly that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anybody, including us.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. The published list includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing', available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no fee listed.

Two limits matter when you are hiring. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct pointing the same way. If a provider offers you your child's own class teacher privately, that is a problem rather than a perk.

What to do with this as a Dubai parent: ask whether the person teaching your child holds a current private tuition work permit, ask who employs them, and ask what happens if the match is wrong. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership of any kind; where you see those words used as a selling point, ask to see the permit or centre number behind them.

sections.heading: Scheduling an online Spanish session into a Dubai week
paragraphs: The practical window in Dubai is narrower than families expect. Buses from the Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Nad Al Sheba school clusters deliver students home between four and a quarter to five, and a child who walks in at half past four is not ready for an unseen Spanish text five minutes later. Sessions for Dubai MYP students sit overwhelmingly between half past five and half past seven Gulf Standard Time, with a second cluster on Saturday mornings.

Ramadan reorganises the week rather than suspending it. School days shorten, late afternoons become a poor time for language work, and families plan around iftar. The two slots that work are early afternoon, newly free because school finished earlier, and after iftar, when the student is alert and the household has settled. Book the change a fortnight ahead; post-iftar slots across the Gulf fill quickly and the good ones go first.

The internal assessment calendar is the other fixed point. Dubai IB schools stack Language Acquisition tasks into defined assessment weeks and most publish the dates at the first parents' evening. A family that has those dates in September can book a short intensive block against them rather than discovering a portfolio task three days out. Ask for the calendar, then ask the tutor to map the twelve-week log onto it.

Two smaller advantages of the online format are worth stating because they are the reasons families stay rather than the reasons they start. Travel is normal in this city, and a slot held over live video survives three weeks in Europe or India without rebooking. And moving a session by a day costs nobody a commute, so a school trip or a sports fixture is a message rather than a negotiation about mileage.

process.title: Send the four criterion marks, not just the grade
process.description: A short form: MYP year, school, the one-to-seven grade and the four criterion marks from the last report. Those four numbers are the diagnosis and they determine which tutor we match. If your report card does not show them, say so and we will work them out in the trial lesson instead.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a baseline
process.description: Sixty minutes, no payment, four short tasks and a ninety-second recording. You keep the recording and receive a written placement note referencing the phase descriptors. If the tutor is not the right fit, you have lost an hour and gained a baseline, which is more than most first lessons leave behind.

process.title: Agree the focus criterion and the twelve-week log
process.description: One criterion is named as the focus, because four at once moves none of them. The twelve-week log on this page is adapted to your child's school unit plan and internal assessment calendar, and the dates are written down. Week six is set as a review point before anything starts.

process.title: Marked work back before the next session
process.description: One piece of your child's own work each week, marked against the named criterion with strand-level comments in the school's own vocabulary. It arrives before the following lesson, not at the end of the month. Twelve weeks of this is the record the next decision gets made from.

process.title: Week six: review, switch or stop
process.description: A written review naming what has moved and what has not, plus a second recording. Three outcomes are on the table: continue, change the focus criterion, or change tutor. Stopping is also an outcome and we would rather you took it at week six than drifted to week twenty.

process.title: Week twelve: a decision with evidence behind it
process.description: Third recording, the final marked tasks and a written review that compares week one with week twelve on the same task types. Blocks do not roll over automatically. If the evidence supports another block, you will be able to see why; if it does not, you keep the folder either way.

whyPoints.title: A record instead of a reassurance
whyPoints.description: Twelve dated, marked artefacts and three recordings per term, in the same criterion vocabulary your Dubai school report uses. The point is not that we mark; it is that you can read the marking and compare it with the school's. Nothing else in this market gives a parent a way to check the claim.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium does not appear on your invoice
whyPoints.description: Dubai in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour carry forty to fifty minutes of term-time driving each way. Online delivery removes that cost and the geographic filter behind it, so the tutor is chosen for knowing MYP phase descriptors rather than for living near Dubai Marina.

whyPoints.title: Spoken progress you can actually hear
whyPoints.description: Recorded ninety-second tasks at weeks one, six and twelve, marked against the Criterion D strands while the student listens. Families consistently report this as the most convincing evidence they receive, and it is the piece an in-home hour almost never produces.

whyPoints.title: A week-six exit built in
whyPoints.description: The review at week six can end the block, change the focus criterion or change the tutor, and asking for a different tutor is treated as a normal request. Arrangements that cannot be ended cleanly are how families end up paying for a year of pleasant conversation.

whyPoints.title: Limits on coursework stated up front
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has already produced. For the MYP Personal Project and every assessed Spanish task, the student writes every word themselves. An IB academic-honesty finding follows the student, which is why this boundary is in writing before the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: Figures and rules with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated October 2026. Permit facts come from u.ae and MoHRE, school-fee context from KHDA. IB session dates are left off these pages because they could not be verified from the IB directly.

faqs.question: What does a Spanish home tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Rates read across Dubai providers in October 2026 put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist. Advertised monthly packages include AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. The gap between the in-home and online bands is mostly the car: forty to fifty minutes of Dubai term-time driving each way sits inside that rate whether anyone itemises it or not.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our villa in Dubai Marina instead of teaching online?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For MYP Spanish the trade favours you twice over: the tutor is chosen for knowing Language Acquisition phase descriptors rather than for living within a drive of the Marina, and the session produces marked work and a recording instead of an hour nobody kept a copy of.

faqs.question: How will I know my child's Spanish is improving before the next report card?
faqs.answer: By reading the marked work and listening to the recordings. After four weeks you should hold a ninety-second baseline recording from the trial lesson, four pieces of your child's own work marked against a named criterion with strand-level comments, a note of why that criterion was chosen, at least one planning frame, and one sentence about what has not moved. None of that requires you to speak Spanish. Two marks on the same task type five weeks apart is harder information than any progress summary.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Dubai report card show four numbers for Spanish?
faqs.answer: Because MYP Language Acquisition is marked on four criteria of eight marks each: comprehending spoken text, comprehending written text, communicating in response, and using the language in spoken and written form. The four add to thirty-two, and your school converts that to a one-to-seven grade using its own boundaries. The four numbers are the diagnosis and the single grade is the summary, so read them in that order. Ask your MYP coordinator for the boundary table; it tells you how many marks sit between the current grade and the next.

faqs.question: Do you mark my child's work between lessons or only during them?
faqs.answer: Between them, and that is the part of the arrangement that produces the record. One piece of the student's own written or recorded work goes back each week marked against the named focus criterion, with comments at strand level in the vocabulary the school's report uses, and it arrives before the next session rather than at the end of the month. Twelve weeks of a weekly slot therefore leaves twelve dated artefacts. A tutoring arrangement that produces nothing between sessions gives you no way to check it.

faqs.question: How long does it take for an MYP Spanish grade to actually move?
faqs.answer: Typically two reporting cycles rather than one. Criterion A listening moves fastest, often within a term, because it responds to listening volume. Criterion C response work takes about four sessions to restructure and then a full assessment cycle for the school to see it. Criterion D is cumulative and slowest. Anyone offering a faster timetable than that is selling rather than teaching, and no tutor can promise a particular grade in any case. What can be shown is movement on the same task type, marked twice.

faqs.question: What happens if twelve weeks of marked work shows nothing changing?
faqs.answer: There are four usual explanations and they need different responses. The wrong criterion was chosen as the focus, which the record makes visible quickly. The phase placement is wrong, in which case the fix is a conversation with the MYP coordinator rather than more lessons. The match between tutor and student is not working, which is a rematch and not a complaint. Or the expectation was faster than the subject allows. We would rather name which of the four it is at week six than let a block run to week twenty.

faqs.question: Can we change tutor without starting the whole arrangement again?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the week-six review exists partly for that. The record travels: the new tutor receives the placement note, the marked tasks, the recordings and the focus criterion, so the first session continues the block rather than restarting it. In a language subject where a student has to be willing to be wrong out loud, the pairing matters more than in most subjects, and asking for a different tutor is treated as a normal request rather than as a complaint about anyone.

faqs.question: How do I check a Dubai tutor is permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask for their MoHRE private tutor work permit. Private tuition in the UAE runs under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and u.ae states that individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine amounts are published, so treat any figure quoted at you with suspicion. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's own school deadlines in Dubai?
faqs.answer: That is the intention, and it is why the tutor asks for the unit plan and the internal assessment calendar in week one. Dubai IB schools stack Language Acquisition tasks into defined assessment weeks and most publish the dates at the first parents' evening. The twelve-week log on this page is then mapped onto those dates rather than run alongside them. A tutor working to a generic syllabus while the school assesses something else produces marks that do not transfer to a report card.

faqs.question: We have two children in MYP Spanish. Can one tutor take both?
faqs.answer: One tutor, two separate sessions, is what works. A shared hour sounds efficient and fails in practice unless the two are in the same phase and working on the same criterion, which siblings rarely are. The same tutor across both does help: they hold the comparison, spot that one child's Criterion B problem is the other's too, and can reuse planning frames. Each child still gets their own marked work, their own recordings and their own focus criterion, because the record is individual or it is useless.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's MYP Personal Project if it involves Spanish?
faqs.answer: A tutor can question the goal, help plan the process, discuss sources and give feedback on what the student has already produced. The student writes every word of the report and the process journal themselves. We put that in writing before the first session because parts of this market do not, and because an academic-honesty finding under IB rules attaches to the student rather than to the tutor. A provider offering to produce the project for you is telling you something useful about itself.

faqs.question: What exactly happens in the trial lesson, and what do we keep?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes with a Spanish specialist, no payment and no obligation. Four short tasks, one per criterion, plus a ninety-second recorded interaction. You keep the recording and receive a written note placing the evidence against the published phase descriptors, which you can take to your MYP coordinator. If the tutor is not right for your child you have spent an hour and gained a baseline, which is more than most paid first lessons leave behind in this market.

faqs.question: Does a poor internet connection make online Spanish lessons unworkable?
faqs.answer: A weak line ruins listening tasks and makes recordings useless as evidence, so it is worth sorting before the trial rather than after. Headphones matter more than a camera: a laptop microphone across a room picks up the room, not the student, which defeats the point of a recorded speaking sample. A wired connection or strong Wi-Fi in the room where the lesson happens is enough. Dubai household connections are generally well up to it; the failures we see are microphones and distance, not bandwidth.

faqs.question: Is small-group Spanish tutoring better value than one-to-one for MYP?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per student, and weaker on exactly the thing this page is about. Group rates in the Dubai market sit well below one-to-one, but a group is set by the group's level rather than the student's, and individual criterion diagnosis is hard to extract from shared work. For a student whose problem is a specific criterion, group work tends to produce activity rather than evidence. For general exposure and speaking confidence at Phase 1 or 2, it can be a reasonable use of money.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-home-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the record before you ask for the rate
dubai/ib-myp-spanish-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing an in-home Spanish tutor in Dubai against an online one, the question that settles it is not the hourly figure. It is what you will be holding in four weeks. Ask any provider, including us, for the marked work, the named criterion, the planning frame and the recording. Then compare their answer with the twelve-week log on this page. IB Gram's first lesson is free, produces a baseline recording and a written placement note you keep, and commits you to nothing. Send us the MYP year, the school and the four criterion marks from the last report, and we will match a Spanish specialist for the trial.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Spanish inside the MYP framework rather than as a general language course. That means criterion-referenced marking, phase-appropriate texts, and feedback written in the strand language a Dubai MYP report card uses.

intro.heading: What MYP Spanish is actually marked on, and why that changes what a tutor does
paragraphs: Spanish in the Middle Years Programme is not graded on vocabulary tests or on how much of the textbook a class has covered. It is graded against four published criteria, each carrying eight marks. Criterion A asks whether the student comprehends spoken and visual text. Criterion B asks the same of written and visual text. Criterion C is about communicating in response to what has been heard or read. Criterion D is about using the language in spoken and written form, which is where accuracy, range and register live. Thirty-two marks in total, converted to a one-to-seven grade by boundaries the school applies. A tutor who does not work in those four columns is tutoring a different subject.

That matters in Dubai more than in most places, because the city's MYP cohort is unusually mixed. A single MYP 3 Spanish class in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills can hold a child who has spoken Spanish at home since birth, a child who arrived last August from a British school in the UK with no Spanish whatsoever, and a child who did two years of Spanish in Singapore under a different phase structure. MYP handles this with phases rather than year groups, and the phase a student sits in should reflect what they can do, not how old they are. In practice, placement gets decided in the first week of term and then rarely revisited.

The commonest problem we are asked about is not weak Spanish. It is a mismatch. A student placed in Phase 4 who is genuinely working at Phase 2 will produce writing that is accurate but thin, score steadily in the fours, and never understand why. A student placed in Phase 2 who is genuinely at Phase 4 will coast, hit the mark ceiling built into Phase 2 descriptors, and lose interest. Both show up as a flat grade across three reporting cycles. Both are fixed by looking at a piece of real work against the phase descriptors rather than by adding more vocabulary drills.

The second commonest problem is Criterion C. Students treat it as a comprehension question with a Spanish wrapper: read the text, answer in Spanish, done. Criterion C is a response task. It wants an interpretation, an opinion, a connection, in the target language, with a format and an audience. A Dubai MYP student who writes a grammatically clean paragraph that only restates the source text will sit at four or five out of eight indefinitely, however much grammar they revise. The fix is structural, it takes about four sessions, and it is invisible if nobody looks at the criterion strands.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing for texts and audio. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a language subject that trade turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. A Dubai family gets a Spanish specialist who knows MYP phase descriptors, instead of whichever Spanish speaker is willing to drive to their community at five o'clock on a Tuesday. Speaking tasks can be recorded and replayed, written work can be annotated live, and a session can be moved by a day without anyone recalculating a commute.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram supports all three school-age IB programmes for Dubai families. This page is about the middle one, but the phase a student reaches in MYP Spanish decides which Diploma route is open to them, so the three are worth reading together.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP has no Language Acquisition phases and no criteria out of eight. Additional-language learning sits inside the transdisciplinary units and is reported in descriptive terms. For Spanish, the useful question at PYP is exposure: how many minutes a week, taught by whom, and whether the child is reading in Spanish at all. That answer predicts the MYP 1 phase placement more reliably than any test.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB continuum schools usually run a single additional language through PYP, then widen the choice at MYP 1. Families who want Spanish specifically often discover in Year 6 that their school offers French and Arabic only, and that Spanish starts from Phase 1 in MYP. Six to eight weeks of groundwork before MYP 1 removes most of that cliff.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · Years 7-11, labelled MYP 1 to MYP 5
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and criterion-referenced marking throughout. Language Acquisition is one subject group and Spanish is one of the languages offered inside it. The four criteria stay the same from MYP 1 to MYP 5; what changes is the phase, and with it the complexity of text a student is expected to handle and the independence expected in Criterion D.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP years collide with two local realities. Arabic and Islamic Education are required in every private school regardless of curriculum, which compresses the option block Spanish sits in. And mobility is high, so an MYP 4 Spanish class often contains students who joined in MYP 3 from an IGCSE school with no MYP marking experience at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subject groups, three core components. Spanish appears as Language ab initio at SL, as Language B at SL or HL, and for strong bilinguals as Language A: Language and Literature. The jump from MYP marking to DP marking is real: criteria are replaced by assessment components with published weightings, and the internal assessment becomes an individual oral.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are large enough that most IB schools run Spanish B SL, but ab initio and HL groups depend on numbers each year. Families planning a Spanish B HL route should ask the school in MYP 4, not MYP 5, because a group that does not fill is not offered and the alternative is a different language entirely.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-tutor.subjectsIntro: Spanish sits inside one MYP subject group, but a tutor is usually asked about the phase above and the phase below as well. These are the Language Acquisition strands and the adjacent courses Dubai MYP families ask us for most often.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish, Phases 1 and 2
subjects.description: Short, familiar texts and highly scaffolded response tasks. The mark ceiling is built into the phase descriptors, so the work here is accuracy, present and near-future tenses, and enough listening stamina to hold a two-minute recording. Most late arrivals into a Dubai MYP class start here whatever their year group says.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish, Phase 3
subjects.description: The phase where Criterion C starts to separate students. Texts become unfamiliar, and a response has to interpret rather than repeat. Past tenses appear in production rather than only in recognition. Sessions here are usually half comprehension strategy and half structured writing against a format and an audience.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish, Phase 4
subjects.description: The most common placement in Dubai MYP 4 and MYP 5 Spanish classes. Students handle authentic text, argue a position, and are expected to show register awareness in Criterion D. Subjunctive appears. This is where a flat five becomes a seven, or does not, depending on whether the student can plan a response before writing it.

subjects.name: MYP Spanish, Phases 5 and 6
subjects.description: Literary and journalistic text, abstract topics, and sustained spoken interaction. Criterion D rewards range and idiom rather than error avoidance, which catches out careful students who have learned to write safely. Phase 6 students are usually heading for Spanish B HL or Spanish A and benefit from DP-style tasks a year early.

subjects.name: DP Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: The route for a student who finishes MYP at Phase 1 or 2, or who picks Spanish up at DP1. Prescribed themes, a narrow grammar list, and an individual oral based on a visual stimulus. Dubai students often choose this to protect a science-heavy timetable, which is sensible if the phase evidence supports it.

subjects.name: DP Spanish B SL
subjects.description: The standard destination for a Phase 4 MYP finisher. Receptive, productive and interactive skills across five prescribed themes, with an individual oral on a visual stimulus linked to a theme. The MYP-to-DP gap here is mostly about writing to a text type under timed conditions rather than about new grammar.

subjects.name: DP Spanish B HL
subjects.description: Adds two literary works and a markedly higher expectation of fluency and nuance. Suited to Phase 5 and 6 finishers. In Dubai the practical constraint is group size: a school needs enough HL candidates to timetable it, so interest has to be registered early in MYP 5.

subjects.name: MYP Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in Dubai private schools for non-Arab students and marked on the same four Language Acquisition criteria as Spanish. Families frequently ask for both, and the criteria transfer: a student who learns to plan a Criterion C response in Spanish does better in Arabic within a term without any extra Arabic teaching.

subjects.name: MYP French
subjects.description: The other widely offered MYP language in Dubai, and the usual alternative when a Spanish group does not fill. Worth tutoring in parallel only where a school genuinely runs two additional languages; otherwise the criteria work done in one language carries across.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature, English
subjects.description: A different subject group with its own four criteria, including analysing and organising. Students who struggle with Criterion C in Spanish very often struggle with the analytical criterion in English too, because the underlying skill is reading a prompt and planning a response. Diagnosing both at once saves a term.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Not a Spanish course, but a Spanish-themed Personal Project is common in Dubai MYP 5 cohorts. A tutor coaches the process, questions the goal, and reviews the student's own report against the criteria. The student writes every word of the report and the process journal themselves; that boundary is not negotiable.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities where MYP Spanish families reach us
dubai/ib-myp-spanish-tutor.regionsIntro: Dubai's MYP schools cluster, and so do the questions. Below are the areas we hear from most for MYP Language Acquisition, with the detail that actually changes how a weekly Spanish session gets scheduled.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Home to one of the longest-running IB continuum cohorts in Dubai, so MYP phase placement here is usually done carefully and early. The practical issue is timetable density: students carrying Spanish plus Arabic plus a music commitment can only take a 7pm slot.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: The highest concentration of IB World Schools in one district. Spanish groups are large enough to run at several phases, which also means a misplaced student is easy to overlook. School-run traffic on Umm Suqeim Street pushes realistic session starts to 5.30pm or later.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed Indian, British and IB enrolment, with families who often add a language after arriving. A high share of our Phase 1 and Phase 2 MYP Spanish requests come from here, usually from students who joined an IB continuum school mid-MYP.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan
regions.note: Villa communities feeding two large IB schools, with long school-bus routes. Students are frequently home only by 4.30pm, so Spanish sessions land at 6pm on weekdays or move to Saturday morning during assessment weeks.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Fast-growing, apartment-heavy, and served by schools that added IB programmes recently. Spanish is often newly offered here, which means Phase 1 cohorts with teachers also new to MYP criteria. Parents ask more questions about marking than about grammar.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park and Dubai South
regions.note: Spread out, with the longest commutes in the city for many families. In-home tutoring is least practical here on pure travel arithmetic, and it is where the online format saves the most time. Evening slots after 6.30pm are the norm.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah
regions.note: Older villa districts with a mix of IB continuum and British schools. Spanish requests here skew to Phases 4 and 5 and to DP transition planning, because many students have had the same additional language since PYP.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Umm Suqeim
schoolClusters.note: The densest cluster of IB World Schools in Dubai. Students we support in this cluster sit MYP Language Acquisition at several phases in the same year group, and the schools here are the ones most likely to register for MYP eAssessment at the end of MYP 5.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Nad Al Sheba and Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: Villa-belt IB schools with established continuum cohorts. Students we support here tend to have had a single additional language since PYP, which makes Phase 4 and Phase 5 Spanish the normal MYP 5 position and the DP route conversation an MYP 4 one.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Investments Park, JVC and Dubailand
schoolClusters.note: Newer IB provision in the southern and western communities. Students we support here often joined mid-MYP from a different curriculum, so Phase 1 to Phase 3 Spanish dominates and criteria literacy matters as much as language teaching.

dubai/ib-myp-spanish-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every MYP Spanish request we take from Dubai. All three are delivered online over live video; the difference is cadence and what the time is spent on.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-time
modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week through the school year, sequenced against the school's own unit plan. The tutor marks one piece of student work against a named criterion each week and returns it before the next session, so the parent sees a strand-level trail rather than a monthly verdict. This is the format that moves a Criterion C score.

modes.title: Phase placement and diagnostic block
modes.description: Three to four sessions to establish where a student actually sits against the Language Acquisition phase descriptors, using a listening task, a reading task, an unseen response and a short recorded interaction. The output is a written placement note the parent can take to the MYP coordinator. Families use this before deciding whether to commit to weekly lessons at all.

modes.description: Two sessions a week for a fixed four to six weeks, timed to a school's internal assessment window or to an MYP eAssessment ePortfolio deadline. Work is on task conditions, planning time and register rather than on new content, because new content this late rarely converts to marks. Sessions pause afterwards rather than rolling on.

sections.heading: The four criteria, what each one is really testing, and where the marks go missing
paragraphs: MYP Language Acquisition carries four criteria of eight marks each. A student's Spanish grade is a conversion of those thirty-two marks, and every piece of assessed work in the subject is tagged to one or two of them. If you have ever looked at a Dubai MYP report card and seen four separate numbers next to Spanish with no explanation, that is what they are.

The criteria are not equally hard to move. Criterion A, comprehending spoken and visual text, responds quickly to listening volume: a student who listens to twenty minutes of Spanish audio a week for a term will move a band, and that is the cheapest mark on the page. Criterion B, comprehending written text, responds to strategy rather than volume, because the failure is usually reading every word rather than scanning for the question's target. Criterion C, communicating in response, is where most Dubai MYP students stall, and it needs a structural fix. Criterion D, using language in spoken and written form, is the slowest to move because it is cumulative.

The table below is what a tutor works from in the first month. It is worth reading next to your child's own report card, because the pattern of which criterion is low tells you what kind of problem you have. Low A and B with healthy C and D means an input problem. Healthy A and B with low C means a response-planning problem. Low D alone usually means the student is writing safely to avoid errors and losing the range marks as a result.

One practical note for Dubai families: schools here apply their own grade boundaries to the thirty-two marks, and those boundaries differ between schools. A nineteen out of thirty-two is not a fixed grade. Ask the MYP coordinator for the boundary table rather than comparing your child's total with a friend's at another school in the same community.

table.caption: MYP LANGUAGE ACQUISITION CRITERIA — SPANISH, MARKS AND FAILURE MODES
columns: Where Dubai MYP students lose them
rows: A
Comprehending spoken and visual text
Listening stamina. A student who copes with two minutes of audio fails at four. Fixed by volume, not by technique.
B
Comprehending written and visual text
Reading every word instead of locating the answer. Inference questions are left blank because the literal answer is absent.
C

Restating the source text instead of responding to it. Format and audience ignored. The single biggest score leak.

sections.heading: Phases, not year groups: finding out where your child actually sits
paragraphs: Language Acquisition runs on six phases rather than year groups, and this is the part of MYP that confuses new arrivals to Dubai most. A student can be in MYP 4 and Phase 2, or MYP 2 and Phase 4. The phase describes capability; the MYP year describes age. Schools group students into teaching sets by phase where numbers allow, and where numbers do not allow, a single Spanish class covers two phases at once with differentiated tasks.

Placement is normally decided in the first fortnight of term, often from a short written task and a conversation. That is a reasonable method under time pressure and a poor method for a child who was quiet in week one, or who had three weeks of Spanish tutoring over the summer and tested above their real level. Once placed, students are rarely re-tested, because re-setting a class in November is disruptive for everyone.

A diagnostic that takes four short tasks, one per criterion, usually settles it. The useful output is not a label but a written note: here is the student's listening performance on a Phase 3 text, here is the same student on a Phase 4 text, here is a recorded ninety-second interaction, and here is where the phase descriptors place that evidence. A parent can take that to the MYP coordinator as a basis for a conversation rather than an assertion.

The table maps the six phases onto what they look like in a Dubai MYP classroom. The descriptor bands are the IB's; the classroom column is ours, drawn from the work we see from students in Dubai IB schools. Use it to sanity-check a placement, not to self-diagnose: two students at the same phase can look very different depending on whether their strength is receptive or productive.

table.caption: MYP SPANISH PHASES — WHAT EACH ONE LOOKS LIKE IN A DUBAI CLASSROOM
rows: Phase 1
Emergent communicator
Recognises familiar words and short phrases. Produces single sentences with heavy scaffolding.
Sound-to-spelling mapping, present tense, and listening to short authentic audio daily.
Phase 2
Emergent communicator
Handles short familiar texts. Writes a guided paragraph. Speaks in memorised chunks.
Moving from memorised chunks to generated sentences, and past-tense recognition.
Phase 3
Capable communicator
Copes with unfamiliar text on familiar topics. Attempts an opinion. Past tenses appear in production.
Criterion C response structure: prompt, format, audience, then language.
Phase 4
Capable communicator

Planning under timed conditions, subjunctive in production, range for Criterion D.
Phase 5
