sections.heading: The five things that move a Dubai quote for the same student
paragraphs: Two families can receive quotes two hundred dirhams apart for apparently identical work, and the difference is almost never arbitrary. Five variables do most of it. The first is the year group: MYP 1 and 2 work is quoted lower than MYP 5, because the content is narrower and the pool of competent tutors wider. The second is the criterion being targeted. Criterion A content teaching is the commonest skill in the market; criterion B investigation coaching is the rarest, and the price reflects scarcity rather than difficulty.

The third is session length. A 90-minute session is rarely priced at exactly 1.5 times a 60-minute one, because the fixed costs of preparation and marking are the same. For standard-route work in Years 7 to 9, two 45-minute sessions a week often beat one 90-minute session on outcome and cost close to the same, which makes the comparison a scheduling decision rather than a financial one.

The fourth is how late you start. A deadline block booked three weeks out is ordinary work; the same block booked four days out requires a tutor to clear other slots, and the market prices that. More importantly, late work is less effective: criterion B coaching four days before submission cannot rebuild the generalisation skill, only tidy the draft. The fifth is continuity. One tutor across a year costs less in real terms than three tutors across a year, because each new tutor spends the first session doing diagnosis you have already paid for.

One variable that should not move the price, and sometimes does: the standard versus extended distinction. Extended attracts higher quotes in this market because the tutor pool is thinner, not because the hour is harder to deliver. If you are quoted a standard-route rate with an extended-route surcharge attached, ask what in the brief changed. The table lists all five variables with the direction and the size of the effect, expressed against published market bands rather than against our own prices.

sections.heading: What a year of standard-route support actually totals
paragraphs: A rate is half a price. The other half is the quantity, and this is where published market figures become useful rather than decorative: multiply the band by a realistic session count and the decision becomes visible. A term in a Dubai school rarely yields twelve usable weekly sessions. Assessment weeks, a school trip, two travel weeks and a public holiday take the realistic figure to nine or ten, which means an academic year of weekly support is twenty-eight to thirty-two sessions rather than the thirty-eight the calendar suggests.

Three plan shapes cover most standard-route families. The light plan is two deadline blocks and one habit block a year, about ten to fourteen sessions, and it suits a student whose criterion A marks are sound and whose losses are in communication and evaluation. The medium plan is one weekly slot across two terms plus a deadline block, roughly twenty-two to twenty-six sessions, which is the usual Year 9 or Year 10 shape. The heavy plan is weekly across the full year with blocks layered on, which is a Year 11 or Diploma-year commitment and should be entered deliberately.

Run those session counts against the published bands and the spread is instructive. At the mid-market qualified band, a light plan is a fraction of what a heavy plan at specialist rates costs, and for a standard-route student with sound content knowledge the light plan frequently produces more grade movement per dirham, because it is aimed at the criteria with the widest mark ranges. The expensive mistake is not buying the wrong band. It is buying the heavy plan when the evidence called for two blocks.

sections.heading: Standard is not the cheap route: what it actually covers
paragraphs: The phrase standard mathematics invites a misreading, and Dubai parents arrive with it regularly. Standard is one of two routes through the same framework, covering number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, and statistics and probability, assessed against the same four criteria on the same 0 to 8 scales. It is not a reduced subject with a lower ceiling on the report. A student on the standard route can score at the top of every criterion, and the grade that results is the same grade a student on the extended route would receive for the same marks.

What the extended route adds is additional content, aimed at students heading towards higher-level Diploma mathematics, delivered at a faster pace. The standard route uses that time for consolidation instead, which for most students is the better bargain. The group that suffers is the one placed on the standard route and then asked to pick up higher-level Diploma mathematics anyway, because the gap is real and has to be closed in the summer between MYP 5 and the Diploma.

The cost consequence runs in both directions. Standard-route support is quoted lower because the tutor pool is wider, but a standard-route student intending to take Analysis and Approaches at higher level needs a bridging plan that is priced like extended work. Conversely, an extended-route student who will take Applications and Interpretation is paying extra for content the Diploma course will not require. The question that actually decides the bill is the Diploma route, and it should be asked in Year 10, not Year 12.

This is also why a single diagnostic session on route choice is good value. A specialist reading four criterion marks and three marked tasks can say whether the extended route is survivable, whether the bridging plan is needed, and what it would cost in hours. Families who buy that one session and nothing else have still made the most financially significant decision in the whole five years.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees, the freeze and what else the money buys
paragraphs: A tutoring figure in isolation sounds either trivial or alarming depending on the day. In context it is easier to judge. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 private school pupils in 2024-25, across 17 curricula, with the British curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, the Indian curriculum at 26, the American at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. That is the market a Dubai family is buying in, and it is both deep and competitive on price.

The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, as part of Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For 2026-27 the emirate also added seven new private schools, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. A frozen fee line plus new capacity is a buyer's market at school level, which is exactly when discretionary spending moves into tutoring.

Against that backdrop, the comparison worth making is not tutoring against nothing but tutoring against the alternatives for the same money. A term of weekly one-to-one at the mid-market band sits in the same range as a set of holiday camps or a year of a single extracurricular activity. Judging it fairly means attaching a measurable outcome to the tutoring, which is why every plan on this page carries a checkpoint stated as what should appear on the next school-marked task.

The table gathers the published figures a Dubai family actually weighs, each with its source. Where a figure is ours, we say so; none of the money figures here are. Two deliberate omissions: we publish no school fee figures for individual schools, because those are set per school and change, and we state nothing about the tax treatment of tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority source we do not have.

sections.heading: Where standard-route families in Dubai waste money
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the wasted spend we see, and all four are avoidable with one diagnostic session. The first is buying content when the loss is in communication. A student with a 6 on knowing and understanding and a 4 on communicating does not need more topic teaching; they need a dozen notation habits corrected on their own work. Families who buy a year of content teaching for that profile pay a great deal and watch the report not move, which then reads as the tutoring having failed.

The second is paying specialist rates for generalist work. Number fluency repair in Year 7 does not require an examiner-level specialist, and the market will happily sell one. The third is the optimistic second weekly session. Dubai Middle Years timetables carry eight subject groups plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies stream, and the second session is the one that gets cancelled from October onwards, often after it has been paid for in a package.

The fourth is late booking against deadlines. A criterion B block four days before submission can tidy a draft and cannot build the generalisation skill the mark depends on, so the family pays for coaching at a premium and receives proofreading. Booking the same block three weeks out costs less and does the actual work. The pattern repeats every term because the task sheet arrives earlier than parents notice it.

One more, less common but more expensive: continuing past the checkpoint without asking the question. A plan with no stated measure runs indefinitely because nobody can say it has failed. Ours state the measure in advance, which is as much a protection for the family as for us. If a provider will not tell you what should appear on the next marked task, the plan has no checkpoint and the spending has no natural end.

sections.heading: The permit, the invoice and what to put in writing
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the regulation affects what a legitimate quote looks like. Individuals providing private lessons need a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with scepticism.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different matter: that requires an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with initial approval first and annual renewal. The distinction matters because the phrase approved tutor circulates loosely in this market. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination board approval, accreditation or partnership, and anyone claiming one should be asked for the permit number.

On the invoice itself, four things belong in writing before money moves: the rate and what the unit is, whether it is per hour or per session; the number of sessions and what happens to unused ones; the notice period for cancelling or pausing, which matters in a city where families relocate mid-year; and whether the quoted figure includes value added tax, together with the provider's tax registration number if they charge it. We do not state the general tax treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation.

Two further questions are worth asking any provider. Who specifically will teach, and what happens if that person becomes unavailable? And what is collected about your child, why, and how it is deleted on request, since a lead form for a minor collects personal data and the UAE's personal data protection law applies. A provider who answers all six of these in writing is probably also keeping records of the teaching.

sections.heading: How these lessons run, and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard the student writes on and a recording the family keeps. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and that is true of every emirate rather than a limitation on this page. The published in-home figures above are market context for a service we do not sell, included because the question deserves an answer rather than a redirect.

The commercial consequence is in your favour on a criterion-marked subject. Removing the drive removes the radius, and the radius is what otherwise decides which tutor your child gets. A standard-route Year 10 student in International City can work with the same specialist available to a family in Emirates Hills, at the same band, which is not true of any visiting model in this city.

Where no suitable tutor is free in the slot you want, we say so and offer the honest alternatives: a different time with the right specialist, a different profile at your time, or a short wait. We do not fill a slot with a generalist and let a family discover the mismatch at the next reporting point. The constraint bites hardest at 5pm on weekdays, which is when every family in Dubai wants a session.

What we will not claim: approval, accreditation or partnership from any regulator, school or examination board; any grade outcome, because no honest tutor can promise one; any statistic about our own students without the sample size, date and method attached; and no price of our own dressed up as a market average. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider or survey named beside it and was read in October 2026. What we offer is a free 45-minute trial lesson, one per family, no card details taken, and a written plan with hours and a checkpoint in it.

faqs.question: What does standard-route Middle Years maths tutoring cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this emirate put budget online platforms at AED 33 to AED 65, qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to AED 300, subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 with individual listings reaching AED 500. Those figures belong to the providers and rate surveys that published them and were read in October 2026. A standard-route brief usually belongs in the qualified middle band: framework knowledge and descriptor fluency are the requirement, and examiner-level specialism is rarely proportionate before the Diploma years.

faqs.question: Why is standard route maths sometimes quoted lower than extended?
faqs.answer: Because the tutor pool is wider, not because the hour is easier to deliver. Both routes cover the same four branches against the same four criteria on the same scales; extended adds content aimed at higher-level Diploma mathematics and moves faster, which narrows the number of tutors confident teaching it. If you are quoted a standard rate with an extended surcharge attached, ask what in the brief changed. The genuinely expensive case is a standard-route student who intends to take higher-level Analysis and Approaches, because that needs a bridging plan priced like extended work.

faqs.question: How many sessions should I budget for an academic year?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar suggests. A Dubai term rarely yields twelve usable weekly sessions once assessment weeks, a school trip, travel and public holidays are deducted, so nine or ten is realistic and a full year of weekly support is twenty-eight to thirty-two. Light plans of ten to fourteen sessions suit students whose content is sound and whose losses are in communication and evaluation. Medium plans of twenty-two to twenty-six are the usual Year 9 and Year 10 shape. Anything heavier should be a deliberate Year 11 decision rather than a default.

faqs.question: Is an eight-session monthly package better value for standard-route maths than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: It is a quantity decision rather than a discount, and should be judged that way. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide by the hours and compare against the band, then ask the two questions that decide whether the package is good value for you: what happens to unused sessions, and what the notice period is for pausing. In a city where families relocate mid-year and timetables tighten after October, an unused session is a real cost.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school fee freeze change what we should spend on tutoring?
faqs.answer: It changes the context rather than the price. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, and the emirate added seven schools and 16,846 places for the same intake. A frozen fee line and new capacity usually move discretionary education spending towards tutoring, which means demand rather than cost pressure. Treat any provider who cites rising costs as a reason for a higher rate with ordinary scepticism.

faqs.question: Which single purchase gives a standard-route student the most movement?
faqs.answer: Usually a short notation and reasoning block followed by one bounded investigation block. Criterion C losses are habits, correctable in three or four sessions on the student's own work, and criterion B carries the widest mark range in the subject while being the least rehearsed in homework. Together that is seven or eight sessions aimed at the two criteria most likely to be holding the grade down. A year of weekly content teaching costs several times as much and, for a student whose knowing-and-understanding mark is already sound, frequently moves nothing.

faqs.question: Should I pay more for a tutor who has read my child's school unit plans?
faqs.answer: You should expect it rather than pay extra for it. The task-specific clarification sheet and unit sheet are what tell a tutor what the marker will accept, and a session that opens by reading them against your child's draft changes what the student does more reliably than extra content teaching. Those documents come from you, not from the tutor, which is why we ask for them before the first session. If a provider quotes a premium for familiarity with your school, ask what specifically they will have read and when.

faqs.question: Should a Dubai tutoring invoice show value added tax separately?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly, and ask for their tax registration number if they charge it. We do not state the general tax treatment of tuition fees on this page because that requires a Federal Tax Authority source, and a tutoring website is not the right authority for a tax position. What a parent can reasonably insist on is clarity: whether the quoted figure is inclusive or exclusive, which unit it applies to, and whether the invoice will show the breakdown. Vagueness on that question is itself a useful signal about how the rest of the arrangement will be run.

faqs.question: Is a tutor without a UAE permit cheaper, and what is the risk?
faqs.answer: Sometimes cheaper, and the risk sits with the tutor rather than with you, which is precisely why it is worth asking. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to eligible applicants. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published. Since the permit costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained one is telling you something about their record-keeping.

faqs.question: How much does a route-choice conversation cost at the end of Year 9?
faqs.answer: It can be the free trial lesson. A specialist reading four criterion marks and three marked tasks can give an honest view on whether the extended route is survivable for your child, what the standard route closes off, and what a bridging plan to higher-level Diploma mathematics would cost in hours. Families who buy nothing else have still made the most financially consequential decision of the five years, because the wrong route produces either a year of unnecessary extension content or a summer of expensive catch-up before the Diploma starts.

faqs.question: Does a 90-minute session cost 1.5 times a 60-minute one?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because preparation and marking are fixed costs whatever the live duration. That makes the comparison a scheduling question rather than a financial one. For Years 7 to 9 on the standard route, two 45-minute sessions a week usually outperform one 90-minute session, because the habits being built are small and benefit from frequency. For Year 11 retrieval work the longer session wins, since a full past task or a complete modelling write-up does not fit into 45 minutes. Price both and choose on the maths, not on the per-minute figure.

faqs.question: What happens to the money if the tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Get the answer in writing before you start, from any provider. The questions are who specifically will teach, what happens if that person becomes unavailable mid-term, and whether a replacement repeats the diagnostic work at your expense. Continuity has a real price: every new tutor spends the first session doing diagnosis the family has already paid for once. We also make no promise to return money on the strength of a grade, because such promises are commitments no honest tutor can keep and the published terms usually say so in the detail.

faqs.question: Can two children in different programme years share the spend?
faqs.answer: Not a session, usefully, but a plan yes. Two students in different Middle Years years are working on different content and often different criteria, so a shared live session shortchanges both. What can be shared is the diagnostic review, a single evidence file the family reads once, and an evening: staggered slots back to back are far easier for a Dubai household to protect than two separate commitments on different nights. Ask any provider whether they price a household review rather than two independent intakes, since the second intake is largely repeated work.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class in Dubai cheaper for standard-route maths?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, and a different product, so compare on what each hour contains. A centre class follows the centre's sequence at a shared pace and will not open your child's task sheet or clarification. Most Dubai centres advertise monthly, so divide by the hours before comparing with an hourly band. Where the need is broad revision in an exam year, a class can be reasonable value. Where it is one criterion or one inherited gap, one-to-one is shorter and usually cheaper in total even at a higher hourly figure.

faqs.question: When is the honest answer that we should not buy tutoring at all?
faqs.answer: More often than the market admits. Three cases come up regularly: a student whose criterion marks are all moving upwards already and who needs time rather than teaching; a student whose problem is a timetable or sleep issue that no tutor can fix; and a family whose real question is about set placement, which is a conversation with the school rather than a purchase. The free trial is where we say so. A provider unwilling to reach that conclusion in any circumstance is not giving you advice, only a quotation.

dubai/ib-myp-standard-mathematics-tutor.closingHeading: Get the band, the hours and the checkpoint in writing
dubai/ib-myp-standard-mathematics-tutor.closingBody: Send the year group, the route and three recent marked mathematics tasks. In a free 45-minute trial lesson, one per family and no card details taken, a specialist tells you which market band your brief belongs in, how many sessions the work realistically takes across a Dubai school year, and what should appear on the next school-marked task if the plan is working. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Every market figure quoted here belongs to the provider or survey named beside it, and none of them is a price of ours.

intro.heading: Why Middle Years reports confuse parents who had no trouble reading a British one
paragraphs: A Dubai family that has moved from a British or Indian system meets the Middle Years Programme report card and stops being able to read it. There are no percentages. There is no class rank. Instead there are four letters per subject, each with a number out of eight beside it, and then a single figure from 1 to 7 that appears to have come from somewhere else entirely. The usual first question an IB MYP tutor in Dubai is asked is not about content. It is what those numbers mean.

Here is the architecture. The programme covers five years, from roughly ages eleven to sixteen, which in a Dubai school maps to Year 7 through Year 11. There are eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, and each criterion is marked on a scale of 0 to 8 against published descriptors. Four criteria at eight marks each gives a maximum criterion total of 32, and that total is converted into the single grade from 1 to 7 using a boundary table.

The criteria are not interchangeable between subjects, and this is where most parental confusion starts. Criterion A in Mathematics is knowing and understanding. Criterion A in Design is inquiring and analysing. Criterion A in Sciences is also knowing and understanding, but criterion B in Sciences is inquiring and designing while criterion B in Mathematics is investigating patterns. A tutor who treats all four criteria as generic effort scores is not teaching to the assessment, and the student's marks will not move.

What this means practically is that two students with the same grade 5 can need completely different lessons. One has 7 on A, 7 on B, 4 on C and 3 on D: strong content, unable to communicate it or apply it to an unfamiliar context. The other has 4 across all four: a genuine content gap. The first student does not need re-teaching, they need to be taught to write to a descriptor. The second does. Reading the criterion profile rather than the grade is the single most useful thing a parent can learn to do, and it takes about ten minutes.

The Dubai context adds two further wrinkles. The first is that this programme sits in the densest private-school market in the country: the Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment against 37% for UK curricula. The second is that a significant number of Dubai schools teach the Middle Years Programme to Year 9 and then switch to Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE for Years 10 and 11, which means a Year 9 student may be preparing for an assessment system they will never sit.

Everything that follows is written around the assessment rather than around the city. The criteria by subject group, how 32 marks become a 1 to 7, where the marks actually go missing, what the published command terms demand, what end-of-programme eAssessment involves, how the Personal Project is marked and where a tutor's involvement must stop, and what the step into the Diploma or into International GCSE really requires. Lessons are one to one over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: The five programme years behave like three distinct phases, and the useful tutoring question changes at each boundary. What follows is the phase structure rather than a year-by-year syllabus, because the content varies by school while the assessment model does not.

programmes.name: Middle Years 1 to 3
programmes.description: The habit-forming phase. Content load is moderate, no external assessment exists, and the criteria are introduced gradually, often with only two or three of the four reported in a given unit. The skills being built are the ones that pay off later: writing to a command term, structuring an investigation, recording a method so that someone else could repeat it, and reflecting in a way that says something.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Dubai parents most often decide to wait, and where waiting costs most. A student who reaches Year 10 without ever having written to a criterion descriptor is not behind on content; they are behind on the thing every mark in the programme depends on. Short, early, criterion-focused support is cheaper than remediation in an examination year.

programmes.name: Middle Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Content depth rises sharply, Mathematics splits into standard and extended routes, Sciences may separate into Biology, Chemistry and Physics, and all four criteria are reported in every subject. The Personal Project runs through the final year. Students meet genuinely unfamiliar application tasks for the first time, and the gap between knowing material and performing on an assessment task becomes visible.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this phase is forked. Some schools continue the programme to the end of Year 11 and may enter students for end-of-programme eAssessment; others switch the cohort to Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at the start of Year 10. The first question we ask a Dubai family is which of those two their school does, because the answer changes the entire preparation.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project carried out across the final year, assessed against three criteria rather than four: planning, applying skills, and reflecting, each marked out of eight for a total of 24. It is externally moderated. The product itself is not what earns the marks; the process journal, the evidence of skill application and the quality of reflection are.
programmes.countryNote: The most common Dubai failure here is a beautiful product with a thin process journal, which scores poorly because two of the three criteria are about process and reflection. A tutor can teach what each criterion rewards and ask the questions that produce usable reflection. A tutor cannot select the goal, develop the product or supply written text for submission.

programmes.name: Interdisciplinary learning
programmes.description: Units that deliberately combine two or more subject groups, assessed on the student's ability to evaluate and synthesise across disciplines and to reflect on what the combination produced. Schools timetable these differently, and because the task sits between subjects it is frequently the assessment students prepare for least.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students often treat an interdisciplinary unit as a double dose of homework rather than as a separate assessment with its own criteria. Where a school enters students for the end-of-programme interdisciplinary on-screen examination, that misunderstanding is expensive, and a couple of focused sessions on what synthesis actually looks like in writing is usually enough to correct it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: The eight subject groups below are listed with the criteria each one is marked against, because that is the information a parent cannot find on a report card and cannot get from a subject name. The criterion letters are what a lesson is built on.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marked on analysing, organizing, producing text and using language. Dubai students reading in English as an additional language typically score well on organizing and lose marks on analysing, where the task is to say what a writer's choice does rather than what the text contains.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Marked on comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students placed in too high a phase appear weak when the real problem is placement, which is worth checking before paying for anything.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the lowest-scoring criterion in this group almost everywhere: students describe sources instead of evaluating their origin, purpose and limitations.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5; integrated or separate in MYP 4-5
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B and C are where marks vanish, because a hypothesis without a variable table and a graph without an evaluated method cap the mark no matter how good the content is.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5; standard and extended in MYP 4-5
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students arriving from a computational system score strongly on A and poorly on B and D, because pattern generalisation and modelling an unfamiliar context are not skills their previous school assessed.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Marked on investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. Three of those four criteria reward the workbook rather than the finished piece, which is why a strong performer with a thin process folder lands on a grade 4.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Marked on inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so students who build first and document afterwards lose criterion A and B marks they cannot recover later in the unit.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Half the available marks are written rather than physical, which regularly surprises families whose child is a strong athlete with a grade 4.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting across two or more subject groups. The common error is writing two separate subject answers side by side rather than one answer that could only exist by combining them.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of eight for a total of 24, and externally moderated. The process journal carries the marks. A student who starts the journal after finishing the product has already lost most of two criteria.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP tutor in Dubai does in the first three sessions
paragraphs: The short answer: reads the criterion profile, finds which of the four criteria is actually costing marks, and teaches to that descriptor using the school's own tasks. An IB MYP tutor in Dubai who opens by re-teaching content has skipped the diagnosis, and for roughly half of the students who come to us the content was never the problem.

Session one is the report card and a piece of the student's recent work, side by side. We look for the shape of the profile rather than the headline grade. High on A, low on C and D is a communication and application problem. Low on B in Sciences or Mathematics is an investigation-design problem. Flat 4s across all four criteria in every subject is usually a genuine content and confidence issue, and that is a different plan entirely.

Session two takes the school's own unit sheet, including the statement of inquiry and the task instructions, and unpacks what the marked task is really asking. Students are given these documents and almost never read them, which is understandable and expensive, because the criterion strands printed on them say exactly what an 7 to 8 band answer contains. A tutor's job here is to make the student read the descriptor before they write, every single time.

Session three is a rehearsal. The student produces a response under something close to real conditions, the tutor marks it against the published descriptor rather than giving a percentage, and the annotated version comes back with the strand that was missed named explicitly. From that point the lesson has evidence to work from, and a parent has something concrete to compare against the next report.

sections.heading: The four criteria in every subject group, by letter
paragraphs: This table is the thing that no competing page in this market publishes, and it is the single most useful reference a Middle Years parent can have. The criterion letters are not generic. They mean different things in each subject group, and the mark a student loses on criterion C in Design has nothing in common with the mark they lose on criterion C in Mathematics.

Read across your child's subject group and the report stops being mysterious. A 3 on criterion D in Individuals and Societies means they described sources rather than evaluating origin, purpose and limitations. A 3 on criterion D in Mathematics means they could not apply a technique to an unfamiliar real-life context. Both read as a 3 on a report card and they need completely different lessons.

Two notes before the table. Schools do not report all four criteria in every unit, particularly in the first three years, so a report may show only two letters for a subject in a given term. And criterion strands are revised by the IB from time to time, so the strand wording a school uses is the authoritative version for that cohort. Ask the coordinator for the current subject guide criteria if the wording differs from what you read here.

Used properly, this is a conversation tool. A parent who walks into a parents' evening able to ask why criterion B is sitting at 4 in Sciences is having a different and much shorter conversation than one who asks how their child is doing. Teachers respond well to it, because it is the language the assessment is actually written in.

sections.heading: How 32 criterion marks become a grade from 1 to 7
paragraphs: Four criteria, each out of eight, gives a criterion total out of 32. That total is then converted to a single grade from 1 to 7 using a boundary table. The conversion is not a percentage and it is not linear in the way a parent expects, which is why a student can gain two criterion marks and not move a grade, or gain one and move two.

The arithmetic matters for planning. If a student sits at 18 out of 32 and needs a 5, the question is not how to improve in general; it is which single criterion can realistically rise by two marks in a term. Moving one criterion from 4 to 6 is a defined teaching job with a known descriptor. Moving everything by one mark each is four teaching jobs, costs four times as much, and usually produces less.

This also explains the complaint we hear most often from Dubai parents: a fortnight of hard revision produced no grade change. That is entirely consistent with the model. Revision raises criterion A, which was often already the student's strongest criterion, and leaves C and D untouched. The total barely moves and the grade does not. Teaching the criterion that is low is the only thing that reliably shifts the number on the report.

Schools publish the boundary table they use and the IB publishes the authoritative version, so confirm the exact bands with your child's coordinator rather than relying on a table copied from a tutoring site, including this one. What is worth taking from the table below is the shape of it: the bands are uneven, the gaps between the middle grades are the widest, and the final jump to a 7 is narrower than most families assume.

sections.heading: Where Dubai Middle Years students lose marks, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Lost marks in this programme are unusually diagnosable, because the descriptors tell you exactly what an 8 contains. After several hundred Dubai Middle Years requests the pattern is consistent, and it clusters in the later criteria rather than the first.

Criterion B in Sciences and Mathematics is the most common single loss in the city. In Sciences the task is inquiring and designing, which means a testable hypothesis, identified and controlled variables and a method someone else could follow. Students write a prediction, list equipment and start. In Mathematics criterion B is investigating patterns, which requires generalising a rule and then justifying it, not spotting the next term in a sequence.

Criterion C and D losses are about writing. Processing and evaluating in Sciences needs a graph with the right axes, a stated trend, a quantified comparison and an evaluation of the method's weaknesses. Thinking critically in Individuals and Societies needs origin, purpose and limitation of a source rather than a summary of it. Applying mathematics in real-life contexts needs the student to say why the model is reasonable and where it breaks. All three are teachable in a term; none of them improve by rereading notes.

The second pattern is specific to Dubai's transfer population. Students arriving from computational or recall-heavy systems score highest on criterion A and lowest on B and D, often with a gap of three or four marks between them. That profile is not a weakness in the subject. It is a mismatch between what the previous school assessed and what this one does, and it closes faster than parents expect once it is named.
bullets: Sciences criterion B: no variable table, no controlled variables, no repeatable method
Mathematics criterion B: spotting a pattern but never generalising or justifying a rule
Sciences criterion C: a graph without a stated trend or an evaluated method
Individuals and Societies criterion D: describing a source instead of evaluating it
Arts and Design: a strong final product with almost no documented process
Physical and Health Education: strong performance, missing written planning and reflection

sections.heading: Command terms: the words that decide the shape of an answer
paragraphs: Every assessed task in this programme uses published command terms, and each one demands a specific structure. A student who answers describe, explain, analyse and evaluate in the same way is throwing away marks they already have the knowledge to earn. This is the highest-yield hour of teaching available in the whole programme, and it is almost never taught explicitly.

The reason it works so well is that command terms are a closed set. There are not hundreds of them. A student who learns the handful that appear repeatedly in their subject group, and learns what each one's top band looks like, carries that into every future task including the Diploma, where the same terms reappear with higher expectations.

The teaching method is mechanical and effective. Take a past task, cover the content, and ask the student to write only the skeleton the command term demands: for explain, a statement plus a causal mechanism; for evaluate, two weighed positions plus a justified judgement; for analyse, components identified plus the relationship between them. Three rounds of that usually changes how a student reads a question permanently.

Parents can check this at home without any subject knowledge. Ask your child what the command term in their task is, and then what structure it requires. If they can name the term but not the structure, that is the lesson to buy. If they cannot name the term, they have not read the task instructions, which is a different and even cheaper fix.

sections.heading: End-of-programme eAssessment: on-screen examinations and ePortfolios
paragraphs: Not every school uses it, and a Dubai parent's first job is to find out whether theirs does. The programme offers an optional external assessment at the end of the final year, leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and schools choose whether to enter their cohort. Many Dubai schools do not, because they switch students to International GCSE for the final two years instead.

Where it is used, the structure splits two ways. Several subject groups are assessed through on-screen examinations sat under examination conditions, with Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics and the interdisciplinary assessment taking that form. Other subject groups are assessed through ePortfolios of the student's work, moderated externally, which is the route for Language Acquisition, Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education. The Personal Project is externally moderated alongside them.

Preparation differs completely between the two. An on-screen examination rewards the same things a written paper does, plus confidence with the on-screen interface and with reading extended source material on a display rather than on paper. An ePortfolio rewards curation: the right pieces, with the process evidence attached, assembled to the criteria across the year rather than in the fortnight before submission.

The requirements for the certificate itself are set by the IB across the required results, including a minimum standard in each subject group as well as an overall total, and those thresholds are the kind of thing that should be read from the IB's own current documentation or confirmed with the school's coordinator rather than taken from a tutoring page. What we will say is that an ePortfolio assembled in the final fortnight rarely meets the standard that the same student's work across a full year would have met.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and exactly where a tutor has to stop
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed against three criteria, not four: planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight for a total of 24, and it is externally moderated. Two of those three criteria are about process. That single fact explains almost every disappointing Personal Project result in Dubai.

A student who builds a drone, choreographs a performance or codes an app and then writes the report afterwards has evidence for one criterion out of three. The planning marks required a documented goal, defined success criteria and a workable plan recorded as it happened. The reflection marks required evidence of how the student's thinking and skills changed, written while they were changing. Neither can be reconstructed convincingly at the end, and moderators recognise reconstruction immediately.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial. Teach the three criteria and what their top bands contain. Explain what a process journal entry should capture and how often. Ask the questions that turn an account of what happened into genuine reflection. Review a draft the student has written and point to the strand it has not yet addressed. Set milestones backwards from the school's internal deadlines so the work is spread across the year.

What a tutor must not do is equally clear. Not select the goal. Not develop the product. Not supply text for submission or rewrite a passage into its final form. Not write a journal entry for the student to adopt. One site visible in this market sells completed internal assessments outright; under IB rules that is malpractice, and it is the student who faces the consequence, not the seller. Our working test is whether the student could explain every sentence of their own document, unaided, after the session. If not, the line has been crossed.

sections.heading: Global contexts, key concepts and why the unit sheet is the whole game
paragraphs: Every unit in this programme is framed by a key concept, related concepts, a global context and a statement of inquiry, all printed on the unit sheet the school issues. Students treat that sheet as administrative decoration. It is in fact the specification for the assessed task, and reading it is free.

The six global contexts are identities and relationships; orientation in space and time; personal and cultural expression; scientific and technical innovation; globalization and sustainability; and fairness and development. The chosen context tells a student what lens the task expects. A Sciences unit framed by globalization and sustainability will ask criterion D questions about impact in those terms, and a student who writes about laboratory accuracy instead has answered a different question well.

The statement of inquiry is more useful still. It is a single sentence combining the key concept, the related concepts and the global context, and a good extended answer is very often a defence or interrogation of that sentence. We teach students to copy it to the top of their draft and check, paragraph by paragraph, whether what they have written speaks to it. The improvement in criterion C and D marks from that one habit is disproportionate to the effort.

This is also the place where a tutor working online has a structural advantage over one working from memory of a different school's course. We ask for the actual unit sheet, the actual task instructions and the actual criterion strands the school is using, because programme content varies between schools in a way the Diploma's does not. Teaching a generic version of a Middle Years topic is the most common way to waste a term.

sections.heading: The fork at sixteen: continuing the programme or switching to International GCSE
paragraphs: This is the Dubai-specific decision that most affects what tutoring is worth buying, and it is made by the school rather than the family. Some Dubai campuses run the programme through Year 11 and may enter students for end-of-programme eAssessment. Others teach the programme to the end of Year 9 and then move the whole cohort onto Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE for Years 10 and 11 before the Diploma or A Levels at sixteen.

Both routes work and both reach the same destinations, but they assess almost opposite things. The programme rewards investigation design, process documentation and reflection. International GCSE rewards precise recall and structured answers to tightly specified questions under timed conditions. A Year 9 student heading for International GCSE needs timed written practice and past-paper technique more than they need further criterion work, and a Year 9 student continuing in the programme needs the opposite.

The transition itself is where the avoidable grade losses happen. Students moving from the programme into International GCSE find that method marks are awarded for specific steps shown in a specific way, and that no credit exists for process documentation. Students moving in the other direction, into the Diploma, find that internal assessments reward exactly the process skills the programme was building, and the students who took the programme seriously arrive with an advantage they did not know they had.

Dubai's market keeps changing underneath this. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority reported seven new private schools for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six openings during 2025-26 and a 6% rise in enrolment. More continuum provision tends to mean fewer cohorts switching at sixteen, but the only answer that matters is the one your own school gives, in writing, for your child's year group.

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory UAE subjects and the crowded Middle Years timetable
paragraphs: A Dubai student in this programme is not only studying eight subject groups. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies sit on the timetable alongside them, because private schools in the UAE must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to teach, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations.

The Knowledge and Human Development Authority publishes the detail for Dubai, and its requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies must be taught in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from the authority to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about.

For tutoring there is one hard constraint. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic as an additional language therefore works from the school's own material and the student's own exercise book, builds vocabulary, grammar and writing through practice, and does not substitute an alternative syllabus. It is the most commonly requested non-programme subject in Dubai and the one where the rules are tightest.

sections.heading: How the lessons happen, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Every UAE lesson is one student with one tutor over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and there is no office or centre in the country to visit. For a Dubai family the practical consequence is that the match is made on subject group and criterion need rather than on which side of Sheikh Zayed Road somebody lives.

In the lesson the student joins from a laptop or tablet, the tutor shares a whiteboard, and the student's own unit sheet, task instructions, draft or marked work sits on screen. Written work is photographed, uploaded, marked against the published criterion descriptors and returned annotated with the strand that was missed named explicitly. For Design and the Arts the tutor works through the process journal and workbook, which is where three of those four criteria live anyway.

Some things are genuinely harder over video and it is better to say so. A practical performance in Physical and Health Education cannot be coached remotely, although the written planning and reflection criteria that carry half the marks can. A Design build needs hands and a workshop; the design cycle documentation does not. Younger students need an adult within earshot for the first few weeks, and a student who will not turn a camera on learns less, because a tutor who cannot see the working cannot correct it.

What we will not do is claim status we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, by the Ministry of Education or by the International Baccalaureate, and no tutoring service in this market should imply otherwise. We do not publish satisfaction percentages, star ratings or student headcounts, because none could be produced with a method and a date attached. Where a tutor teaches privately from inside the UAE, the relevant permit is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years.

process.title: Send the last report and one piece of marked work
process.description: Not a description of how things are going. The criterion profile on the report plus a marked task tells us in ten minutes what two terms of conversation would not: whether this is a content problem, a structure problem or a placement problem. Add the subject group and the year group.

process.title: Ask the school for the unit sheet
process.description: The unit sheet carries the key concept, the global context, the statement of inquiry and the criterion strands being assessed. It is the specification for the task your child will be marked on, and it varies between schools, so a tutor working without it is teaching a generic version of the topic.

process.title: Take the free first lesson
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and carries no obligation to continue. The tutor works through one piece of the student's own work, marks it to the descriptor, and sends a short written note naming which criterion is costing marks and why. If the match is wrong we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot that survives the Dubai school run
process.description: Bus catchments in Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City routinely put students home after 16:30, while Al Barsha families can often start at 16:00. We set the time against your actual arrival, not an ideal one, and hold Friday afternoon for longer sessions and Personal Project work.

process.title: Track criterion marks, not vague improvement
process.description: Progress is reported the way the school reports it: criterion marks out of eight, measured against the previous report. If the targeted criterion has not moved by the next reporting cycle, we change the approach or the tutor rather than asking for more weeks at the same thing.

whyPoints.title: We teach to the criterion, not to the grade
whyPoints.description: A grade 5 can mean strong content with weak communication or a flat profile across all four criteria, and those need opposite lessons. Reading the criterion profile first is why some students need six weeks of writing structure rather than two terms of re-teaching.

whyPoints.title: Your school's own task, not a generic version
whyPoints.description: Programme content varies between Dubai schools in a way the Diploma's does not. We work from the unit sheet, the statement of inquiry and the task instructions the school issued, so practice matches what will actually be marked.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: A closed set of command terms decides the structure of every assessed answer, and almost no student is taught them directly. It is the highest-yield hour in the programme and it transfers intact into the Diploma, where the same terms reappear.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project stays the student's
whyPoints.description: We coach the process, teach the three criteria and question a draft the student wrote. We do not select the goal, develop the product or supply text for submission, and we say why: under IB rules the consequence of that help falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals and no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate and does not imply any. Every figure on this page is attributed to the body that published it, and nothing is quoted without a source.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one student, over live video
whyPoints.description: No travel time in the price, no tutor pool limited to a twenty-minute drive, and the same tutor across the whole course including through Ramadan. The limits are stated too: a practical build or a physical performance cannot be coached remotely, though their written criteria can.

faqs.question: What does criterion B actually assess in Middle Years Sciences?
faqs.answer: Inquiring and designing. A top-band answer states a testable hypothesis with scientific reasoning behind it, identifies the independent, dependent and controlled variables, and describes a method in enough detail that another student could repeat it. What most students submit is a prediction, a list of equipment and a set of instructions. That caps the mark regardless of how good the rest of the write-up is, and it is why criterion B is the most common single loss we see in Dubai. It is also one of the fastest to fix, usually within four or five sessions.

faqs.question: Which criterion letters does Middle Years Mathematics use?
faqs.answer: Criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is investigating patterns, C is communicating and D is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Each is marked out of eight. Students arriving in Dubai from a computational curriculum score highest on A and lowest on B and D, often with a three or four mark gap, because generalising a rule and justifying it, and modelling an unfamiliar context, are not things their previous school assessed. That profile is a mismatch rather than a weakness, and it closes faster than most parents expect once somebody names it.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need my child's school unit sheet to be useful?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first thing we ask for. The unit sheet carries the key concept, the related concepts, the global context, the statement of inquiry and the criterion strands being assessed in that unit. Programme content varies between Dubai schools in a way Diploma content does not, so a tutor working without it is teaching a generic version of the topic rather than the task your child will actually be marked on. Students are issued these sheets and almost never read them, which is the cheapest fix available in the whole programme.

faqs.question: The school has put my daughter into extended mathematics for Year 10 - what changes?
faqs.answer: Content depth and the kind of question she will meet, more than the criteria themselves. The extended route carries additional topics and sets investigation tasks with less scaffolding, which pushes criterion B and D harder than the standard route does. The criteria and the 0 to 8 marking are identical. In practice the students who struggle with the move are not weaker mathematicians; they are students who were succeeding on criterion A alone, and extended material exposes that quickly. Six to eight weeks of pattern-generalisation and modelling work usually settles it.

faqs.question: What is a statement of inquiry and does it matter for revision?
faqs.answer: It is a single sentence on the unit sheet combining the key concept, the related concepts and the global context, and it matters more than almost anything else on the page. A strong extended answer is very often a defence or interrogation of that sentence. We teach students to copy it to the top of their draft and check paragraph by paragraph whether what they have written speaks to it. The gain in criterion C and D marks from that one habit is disproportionate to the effort, and it costs nothing.

faqs.question: Are the command terms in Middle Years tasks the same as the Diploma ones?
faqs.answer: Largely yes, which is why teaching them in Year 8 pays off in Year 13. Describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify, suggest, compare and contrast all reappear in Diploma papers with higher expectations attached. The set is closed and small, and each term demands a specific structure: explain needs a stated mechanism, evaluate needs weighed positions plus a judgement, analyse needs components and the relationship between them. A student who can name the term but not its structure has found the lesson worth buying.

faqs.question: How long is a Middle Years on-screen examination and what is it like?
faqs.answer: Where a school enters students for end-of-programme eAssessment, the on-screen examinations are timed papers sat under examination conditions on a screen rather than on paper, covering Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics and the interdisciplinary assessment. The duration and the current format are published by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's coordinator. The practical preparation point is that students who have only ever practised on paper meet the interface cold, and reading extended source material on a display is a skill worth rehearsing.

faqs.question: What are the three criteria the Personal Project is marked against?
faqs.answer: Planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight for a total of 24, and the project is externally moderated. Two of those three are about process rather than product, which explains most disappointing results in Dubai. A student who builds something impressive and writes the report afterwards has evidence for one criterion out of three. Planning marks required a documented goal, success criteria and a plan recorded as it happened; reflection marks required evidence of changing thinking, written while it changed. Neither reconstructs convincingly at the end.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my son's Personal Project process journal?
faqs.answer: Yes, and reading it is one of the most useful things a tutor does. The tutor can check the journal for evidence against each of the three criteria, explain what a journal entry should capture and how often, and ask the questions that turn an account of events into genuine reflection. What a tutor cannot do is select the goal, develop the product, write a journal entry for the student to adopt, or supply text for submission. Our test: after the session, could he explain every sentence of his own document unaided?

faqs.question: My son's report shows 6, 5, 7 and 4 - which number should we act on?
faqs.answer: The 4, almost always, and not the subject overall. That profile totals 22 out of 32, which sits in the grade 5 band on most boundary tables. Moving the 4 to a 6 lifts the total to 24 and will usually move the grade; raising the 6 and the 5 by one each costs twice the teaching and may not. Find out which criterion the 4 belongs to, read its descriptor, and buy teaching for that one thing. It is the cheapest grade movement available in this programme.

faqs.question: Does the Knowledge and Human Development Authority inspect how the programme is taught?
faqs.answer: It inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and that inspection covers teaching and learning across the school rather than auditing a specific international programme's internal assessment, which the IB handles through its own processes. The authority also sets the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies requirements that sit alongside the programme. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from the authority and does not claim any; we name it because it is the body whose published reports a parent can read.

faqs.question: How many Dubai schools actually run the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, given how visible the IB name is here. The Dubai Media Office reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment against 37% for UK curricula and 26% for Indian. Continuum provision is concentrated in Al Barsha, the coastal belt, Emirates Hills and the eastern education districts. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

faqs.question: Why do so many Dubai schools stop the programme at Year 9?
faqs.answer: Because International GCSE at sixteen is the dominant route in this market and offers an externally certificated qualification that universities and employers recognise immediately, which the final Middle Years years do not provide unless the school enters students for eAssessment. UK curricula accounted for 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment against 7% for the International Baccalaureate, so the pull is commercial as much as pedagogical. What matters for a parent is simply knowing which route their school takes for their child's year group, in writing, because the preparation differs completely.

faqs.question: Can Design and the Arts be taught properly over video?
faqs.answer: Three of the four criteria in each, yes. In Design, inquiring and analysing, developing ideas and evaluating all live in the documentation, which is exactly what a tutor can work through on a shared screen; creating the solution needs hands and a workshop. In the Arts, investigating, developing and evaluating sit in the workbook, while the performance or final piece does not. Since the documentation carries three criteria out of four, remote work covers most of the available marks. We say plainly where it cannot help rather than overclaiming.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai family budget for weekly support across a school year?
faqs.answer: Using published market figures rather than our own price list: a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour works out at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one weekly session, per the Bestimate 2026 bands, and a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above lands nearer AED 1,000 to 2,000 a month. Middle Years work usually sits in the first band rather than the second, because it is not examination-year teaching. Our own pricing conversation starts with the free first lesson rather than a quote.

faqs.question: Is Year 8 too early for one-to-one support, or should we wait?
faqs.answer: Early is cheaper, and the reason is structural. There is no external assessment in the first three years, so parents reasonably decide to wait. But the criteria being introduced in those years are the ones every later mark depends on: writing to a command term, designing an investigation, documenting a process, reflecting usefully. A student who reaches Year 10 having never written to a descriptor is not behind on content, they are behind on the entire assessment model. Six weeks of early criterion work costs less than a term of remediation later.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Send the report and the unit sheet, and we will tell you which criterion to buy
dubai/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: The useful first conversation about Middle Years support is short. Send the most recent report with its criterion marks, one piece of marked work, and the unit sheet for the task your child is working on now. We will tell you which criterion is costing the marks, whether that is a content problem or a writing problem, and how many weeks it should take to move. The first lesson is free and carries no obligation to continue; it ends with a written note rather than a sales call. Every UAE lesson is one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed around your real school run.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barari.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Middle Years Programme subjects for Al Barari and the Dubailand communities around it. Each one works from the criteria your child's school is actually assessing against, rather than from a general sense of the subject.

intro.heading: The report says 5 in Sciences. What does that mean?
paragraphs: It means a criterion total somewhere in the middle of a band, and almost nothing else that a parent can act on. The Middle Years Programme assesses each subject against four criteria, each marked out of eight, giving a total out of thirty-two which is converted to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. A pupil with a strong knowledge criterion and a weak investigation criterion can carry the same final grade as a pupil whose profile is reversed, and the two need entirely different help.

That is the single most useful thing to understand before hiring an MYP tutor in Al Barari. The number on the report is a sum. The actionable information is the four components, and most schools publish them if asked even when the headline report does not show them clearly. A tutor who begins by asking for the criterion breakdown is doing the right thing; one who begins by asking which topics your child finds difficult is working from the least reliable source available, which is a thirteen-year-old's self-assessment.

Al Barari families face a second complication, which is why this page also compares systems. The community has no school inside its gates, so pupils commute out — north to Nad Al Sheba, west towards Motor City and the Arabian Ranches, or across to Al Barsha South. Some of those schools run the IB continuum through to the Diploma; others run the British curriculum and sit IGCSE at sixteen. Children from neighbouring villas are therefore in genuinely different assessment systems at the same age, and parents compare reports that are not comparable.

Those two systems reward different things, and the difference is not cosmetic. The MYP marks investigation, communication and reflection alongside knowledge, and it collects marks across the year from set tasks rather than resting on a final paper. IGCSE marks a terminal written paper against a mark scheme. A pupil who thrives in one may struggle in the other, and a family choosing a school or considering a move at fourteen should understand which demands their child meets more easily.

The third thing this page covers is MYP5 and the Personal Project, because it is where the programme most often goes wrong in Dubai. It is assessed against three criteria, and the marks sit substantially in the process rather than in the finished product. Students who do the project first and write the journal afterwards lose marks they could have had for work they already did.

One fact stated plainly. IB Gram delivers Middle Years tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For MYP-age pupils we will say honestly where a screen is the wrong format — a distractible eleven-year-old who needs an adult in the room is better served in person, and we do not offer that here.

The gaps that matter are written stamina and number fluency, because the programme assumes both and spends little time building either explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this is also when many families arrive mid-programme from another country or another curriculum, so a pupil may meet criterion assessment for the first time at thirteen.
