programmes.name: MYP Year 3
programmes.description: The year in which patterns set. Criterion profiles become stable and visible across subjects, and a pupil who consistently scores well on knowing and understanding and poorly on investigating has a transferable weakness rather than a subject problem. This is also where the Community Project falls in many schools.
programmes.countryNote: For families near Al Barari this is the decision year if a move to a British-curriculum school for IGCSE is being considered, since most such schools begin the IGCSE course in Year 10. The comparison table further down this page is written for that decision.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: The final two years, ending with the Personal Project in MYP5 and, in some schools, IB eAssessment. The workload rises sharply and the Personal Project competes with subject deadlines for the same evenings, which is the single most common reason an MYP5 pupil's grades dip across several subjects at once.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools enter candidates for IB MYP eAssessment, producing the formal MYP certificate, while others award school-based grades only. These are materially different arrangements and you should know which your child's school uses, because it changes what the final year is working towards.

programmes.name: The move into the Diploma
programmes.description: MYP5 pupils moving into the Diploma arrive strong on investigation and reflection and often light on the executional fluency the Diploma assumes, particularly in mathematics. The Diploma Internal Assessment also rewards differently from MYP criteria, and students who assume the skills transfer directly tend to be surprised.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Al Barari is concentrated in a small number of schools. If your child is continuing on the continuum, the useful preparation during MYP5 is algebraic fluency and extended written argument, both of which the Diploma assumes and the MYP does not drill.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups with their four criteria named, because the criteria are what is actually being assessed. Compare them against your child's report and the weak component usually becomes obvious.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the criterion most pupils score worst on, because it rewards generalising and justifying rather than calculating, and arithmetic practice does not improve it.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is where marks concentrate and where pupils stop at the result rather than discussing what the data does and does not show.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Pupils who write fluently frequently score low on analysing, because they describe what a text says instead of examining how it achieves an effect. That is a teachable distinction and it moves one criterion out of four.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. A pupil can move phase mid-programme, which changes the standard they are measured against, and parents often read a lower grade as a decline when it reflects a harder phase.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the criterion that separates grades at the top, and it rewards evaluating sources and weighing interpretations rather than presenting more content.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The subject most dependent on documented process: a strong final product with no design folder behind it cannot score well, which surprises capable pupils every year.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. Responding carries marks for reflecting on one's own and others' work, and it is routinely the lowest criterion for talented practitioners who do not write about what they make.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written rather than physical, which is why able athletes sometimes bring home a grade their family cannot explain.

subjects.name: Arabic in the MYP
subjects.levels: Language and literature or language acquisition, plus mandated strands
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must deliver Arabic alongside the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring splits the same way: literary and grammatical work on one side, script and spoken fluency on the other.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Three criteria — planning, applying skills, and reflecting — each marked out of eight for a total of twenty-four. Most of the available marks reward documented process rather than the finished product, which is why a journal written afterwards scores badly.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Research, thinking, communication, social and self-management skills, taught across subjects rather than separately. Weak self-management shows up as missed deadlines across several subjects simultaneously, which looks like a motivation problem and is usually a planning one.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria, combining two subject groups. Pupils often score lower here than in either parent subject, because the assessment rewards synthesis explicitly and nobody has shown them what synthesis looks like in writing.

sections.heading: How a criterion total becomes a grade
paragraphs: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight on a set of level descriptors. The four marks are summed to a total out of thirty-two, and that total is converted to a grade from one to seven using boundaries the IB publishes. Schools apply the same mechanism, though they differ in how often they report and in whether they show the component marks to parents.

The consequence is the thing worth understanding. Two pupils can hold the same subject grade with opposite profiles. One might score seven and seven on knowing and understanding and communicating and three and three on investigating and reflecting. Another might be the reverse. Both appear identical on a report and neither needs the same tutoring. Asking for the criterion breakdown is therefore not a nicety: it is the difference between targeted help and generic help at the same hourly rate.

The second consequence is about timing. Because marks accumulate from assessed tasks through the year rather than resting on a terminal paper, a weak criterion identified in an autumn report is still inside the final grade in the summer unless something changes. That cuts both ways. It means a problem does not go away on its own, and it means there is more opportunity to influence the outcome than in a system where everything rests on one paper.

Ask your child's school three questions: what were the four criterion marks in each subject, which criterion is weakest across subjects, and what task is next assessed against it. That third question is what converts a report into a plan, because an MYP criterion is only improved on an actual task. A tutor with those three answers can do useful work in the first session; one without them is guessing.

sections.heading: The MYP against IGCSE, for a family choosing between them
paragraphs: Around Al Barari this is a genuine decision rather than a thought experiment, because the school clusters within a single drive include both continuum schools running the MYP to sixteen and British-curriculum schools sitting IGCSE. Parents compare reports across the fence and reach the wrong conclusions, because the two systems reward different things and report on different scales.

The MYP assesses four criteria per subject across the year, with investigation, communication and reflection carrying equal weight to knowledge. It rewards a pupil who can plan an inquiry, explain their reasoning and evaluate their own work, and it penalises one who can only answer questions. It also spreads the assessment load, which suits pupils who work steadily and disadvantages those who perform best under a single deadline.

IGCSE assesses a terminal written paper against a mark scheme, usually with tiering that caps the grade on the lower route. It rewards precise, concise answers that match a command term, accurate calculation and the ability to finish a paper under timing. It suits pupils who revise well and perform on the day, and it disadvantages those whose strength is extended independent work rather than recall under pressure.

Neither is harder in the abstract and both are well recognised. The practical questions are: which does your child demonstrably do better, which does the school you can actually get into offer, and what does the sixth form that follows expect. If your child is moving from MYP3 into a British-curriculum Year 10, budget a transition block aimed at paper format rather than content, because the content gap is usually small and the format gap is not.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and why the journal is the mark
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP5 is assessed against three criteria — planning, applying skills, and reflecting — each marked out of eight for a total of twenty-four. Confirm the current criteria with your child's school, since the IB revises its guides. The structural point is the one that matters and it surprises almost every family: the bulk of the available marks reward the documented process rather than the finished product.

That is why the commonest Personal Project failure in Dubai schools is a strong product with a thin process journal. A pupil builds something genuinely impressive, writes the journal in the fortnight before submission, and scores in the middle because the evidence of planning, of skills being developed, and of reflection along the way simply is not there. The work happened; the record of it did not. Nothing can be done about that afterwards, because reconstructing a journal is both obvious to a reader and not what the criteria ask for.

The fix is a cadence rather than an intervention. A short entry each week recording what was attempted, what went wrong, what was learned and what changes next, maintained from the start, produces the evidence the criteria want as a by-product of doing the project properly. A tutor's useful role is to hold that cadence, check that the product criteria the student set for themselves are actually being addressed, and give feedback on the student's own report.

On the boundary: a tutor does not choose the project, make any part of the product, write the journal or write the report. Those are the student's, and the criteria are explicitly about the student's own planning and reflection, so work the student did not do scores badly even before the honesty question arises. Where a draft report needs changing, the tutor says what is not working and the student rewrites it.

sections.heading: Why the same criterion is weak in six subjects
paragraphs: Look across a full MYP report rather than subject by subject and a pattern usually appears. A pupil weak on investigating patterns in mathematics is frequently also weak on inquiring and designing in sciences and on investigating in individuals and societies. Those are different criteria in different subject groups and they reward the same underlying skill: forming a question, planning how to answer it, and justifying the approach.

This is the most useful observation available in MYP tutoring and almost nobody acts on it. A family seeing three mediocre subject grades books three subject tutors. What the report is actually showing is one transferable weakness appearing three times, and one tutor working on the skill — through whichever subject the pupil likes most — will lift all three. That is a third of the cost and usually a better outcome, because the pupil is not spending three evenings a week being tutored.

The same logic applies to the communication criteria. A pupil who scores low on communicating in mathematics, producing text in language and literature, and communicating in individuals and societies has a writing problem rather than three subject problems. It may be structure, it may be not knowing what a justification looks like in prose, or it may be simple written stamina. All three are addressable, and none of them is addressed by more content teaching in any individual subject.

The third common pattern is self-management, which shows up not as a criterion but as missed deadlines across several subjects at once. Because MYP marks come from set tasks, a missed task is a missing mark, and a pupil who is coping academically but drowning organisationally loses grades for work they could have done. That looks like motivation and is usually planning, and it is worth addressing before anybody buys subject tutoring at all.

sections.heading: eAssessment, school-based grades, and knowing which you have
paragraphs: Some Dubai schools enter MYP5 candidates for IB eAssessment, which produces the formal IB MYP certificate through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios. Others award school-based MYP grades without external assessment. These are materially different arrangements and a surprising number of parents do not know which one their child's school uses, which makes planning the final year difficult.

If your child's school uses eAssessment, the final MYP year has external deadlines and an examination component, and preparation has a recognisable shape: practising the on-screen format, working to the ePortfolio requirements, and meeting submission dates set outside the school. If it uses school-based grades, the final year is an internal matter and the grades are moderated by the school rather than externally examined, so the useful preparation is simply doing each assessed task well.

Ask the school directly, and ask what the final MYP grade will be used for. In some schools it informs Diploma course and level placement, which makes it consequential; in others it is reported and then largely superseded. Either way, knowing changes how much weight to put on MYP5 and whether to spend the final year on MYP criteria or on building the fluency the Diploma will assume.

For families continuing onto the Diploma at the same school, there is a case for doing both: securing the MYP grades that affect placement while using some of the year to build algebraic fluency and extended written argument. Those two are what MYP pupils most often lack on arrival in the Diploma, and MYP5 is the last moment they can be built without a Diploma deadline competing for the time.

sections.heading: Tutor supply for the MYP around Al Barari
paragraphs: Here the picture is more favourable than in the Diploma, and it is worth saying so. Middle Years subject support is the best-served tutoring need in this part of Dubai: there are many competent teachers across the Dubailand communities, plenty will travel, and group tuition centres cover the common subjects. A family looking for general mathematics or science support for a Year 8 has real local choice.

Two things are genuinely scarce. The first is a tutor who works from the criteria rather than from the topic, and who can tell you what a level descriptor for investigating patterns actually asks for. Most tutors in this market have never read an MYP subject guide, and they will teach a competent lesson on the mathematics while leaving the criterion that produced the low grade untouched. The second is Personal Project coaching, which requires knowing that the marks sit in the process and holding a student to a weekly cadence for months.

What differs between the communities is scheduling. A Nad Al Sheba pupil can start at half past four; an Al Barari or Mudon pupil realistically starts at five. For this age group that matters, because an eleven- or twelve-year-old at six in the evening after a commute and a full school day has limited useful attention. The adjustment that works for younger MYP pupils is a shorter session — forty-five minutes rather than an hour — kept weekly, rather than a long session that loses the last third.

One honest limit. For a distractible pupil in the early MYP years who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, a screen is the wrong format, and we do not offer in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE. In that case the right provider is one who does, and saying so costs us a booking and saves a family a term.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and where not to spend
paragraphs: Market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026: EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, BartyED at AED 650. Bestimate's table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

For the Middle Years Programme the honest advice is that the top band is usually unnecessary. A premium Diploma specialist at AED 450 an hour is not three times as useful to a Year 8 as a capable qualified teacher at AED 150, because the content is not where the difficulty lies. What the Middle Years actually needs is someone who knows the criteria and will work on the school's real tasks, and that is available in the AED 150 to AED 300 band.

Where spending is genuinely well targeted is in two places. Criterion coaching, because improving one criterion lifts every subsequent assessed task in that subject and often in others. And Personal Project process coaching through MYP5, because the marks sit in documentation that cannot be recovered later and a fortnightly slot across six months is a small total commitment against a component that carries its own grade.

Where spending is usually wasted is three parallel subject tutors for what a full report shows to be one transferable weakness, and premium rates for early Middle Years content. IB Gram publishes no hourly rate here because the right figure depends on subject, year and whether the work is criterion coaching or project process, but the market band above lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free.

sections.heading: Regulation, honesty and the things we will not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

No fine amount appears on this page. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and the figure circulating online could not be verified. IB Gram is also not approved, accredited or licensed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, and no provider should claim such a thing without a permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai.

On assessed work, the boundary is firm and matters more in the MYP than families expect, because so much of the assessment is coursework rather than examination. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards, discusses an approach, teaches the content or skill required, and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write, make, assemble or complete any part of an assessed task, a Personal Project product, a journal or a project report. Where something needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student does the work.

There is a practical reason as well as an ethical one, and it is worth explaining to a fifteen-year-old directly. The criteria reward planning, skill development and reflection — the student's own thinking, documented over time. Work produced by someone else reads exactly as such and loses precisely those marks, which are the majority. The students who score well on a Personal Project are the ones who kept the journal from week one, not the ones with the most impressive product.

faqs.question: What does a grade of 5 in an MYP subject actually tell me?
faqs.answer: That the criterion total fell within a particular band, and very little else. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, giving a total out of thirty-two that is converted to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. Two pupils can hold the same grade with opposite profiles: one strong on knowledge and weak on investigation, the other the reverse. They need completely different tutoring. Ask the school for the four criterion marks, because that is the only part of the report a tutor can act on.

faqs.question: Why is my child weak on the same criterion in several MYP subjects?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria across subject groups reward overlapping skills. Investigating patterns in mathematics, inquiring and designing in sciences, and investigating in individuals and societies all ask the pupil to form a question, plan how to answer it and justify the approach. A pupil weak in one is frequently weak in all three. That is a single transferable weakness appearing three times, and one tutor working on the skill through the pupil's favourite subject will usually lift all of them.

faqs.question: How are the Personal Project's 24 marks divided up?
faqs.answer: Against three criteria — planning, applying skills, and reflecting — each out of eight for a total of twenty-four, converted to a grade. Confirm the current criteria with the school, since the IB revises its guides. The structural point that catches families out is that most of the marks reward documented process rather than the finished product. A pupil who builds something impressive and writes the journal in the final fortnight scores in the middle, because the evidence of planning, skill development and reflection along the way is not there.

faqs.question: Should we move from the MYP to IGCSE at Year 10?
faqs.answer: It depends on which system your child demonstrably does better in, what the schools you can actually access offer, and what the sixth form afterwards expects. The MYP rewards planning an inquiry, explaining reasoning and evaluating one's own work, with marks spread across the year. IGCSE rewards precise answers matched to a command term, accurate calculation and finishing a paper under timing. Neither is harder in the abstract. If you do move, budget a transition block aimed at paper format, because the content gap is usually small and the format gap is not.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to an Al Barari home?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For this age group we will also say honestly when a screen is the wrong format: a distractible eleven- or twelve-year-old who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is better served in person, and since we do not offer that here the useful thing we can do is point you elsewhere.

faqs.question: Why did my child's language acquisition grade drop?
faqs.answer: Check whether the phase changed. Language acquisition is assessed by phase rather than by year group, with six phases across the programme, and a pupil who moves up a phase is measured against a harder standard. A grade that falls from six to four can reflect a phase change rather than any decline in ability, and families frequently read it as a collapse. Ask the school which phase your child is in now and whether it changed this year, before concluding that anything has gone wrong.

faqs.question: My MYP5 child's grades dipped across several subjects at once. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually the Personal Project competing for the same evenings as subject deadlines, which is the commonest MYP5 pattern in Dubai schools. Because MYP marks come from assessed tasks, a task done badly because the project was due is a mark permanently in the final grade. The fix is sequencing rather than more tutoring: deal with the project process on a fixed weekly cadence so it stops consuming whole weekends, and the subject tasks recover. Missed deadlines generally, rather than content, are the second common cause.

faqs.question: Does my child's school enter them for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the answer changes what the final year is working towards and a surprising number of parents do not know. Some Dubai schools enter MYP5 candidates for IB eAssessment, producing the formal MYP certificate through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios with externally set deadlines. Others award school-based grades moderated internally. Also ask what the final MYP grade is used for: in some schools it informs Diploma course and level placement, which makes it consequential, and in others it is largely superseded.

faqs.question: What should an MYP5 student do to prepare for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Build algebraic fluency and extended written argument, which are the two things MYP pupils most often lack on arrival. The programme develops investigation and reflection well and drills execution lightly, so a student can design an excellent inquiry and then lose Diploma marks rearranging an equation or sustaining a four-paragraph argument. MYP5 is the last point at which both can be built without a Diploma deadline competing for the time, and a holiday block is a good shape for it.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP tutoring session be?
faqs.answer: For the early years, forty-five minutes held weekly beats an hour that loses its final third. An eleven- or twelve-year-old at six in the evening, after a commute from a Dubailand school and a full day, has limited useful attention, and a longer session simply adds time rather than learning. From MYP4 onwards an hour is usually productive. Frequency matters more than duration in either case, because criterion improvement happens on actual tasks and tasks arrive weekly.

faqs.question: Which rate band is right for Middle Years support in Al Barari?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for specialists. Monthly at one session a week that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. For the Middle Years the top band is usually unnecessary, because content is not where the difficulty lies. What you need is someone who knows the criteria.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Personal Project?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes, and that is where the marks are. A tutor can hold a weekly cadence of documented steps, check that the success criteria the student set are actually being addressed, teach any skill the project requires, and give feedback on the student's own report. A tutor cannot choose the project, make any part of the product, write the journal or write the report. Those are what the criteria assess, so work the student did not do loses precisely the marks it was meant to gain.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class useful for MYP subjects?
faqs.answer: For content reinforcement, often yes, and it costs considerably less per hour. Where it falls short is criterion work, because a group cannot stop to examine one pupil's investigation against a level descriptor, and criterion improvement is what moves an MYP grade. If your child's difficulty is keeping up with taught content, a group is reasonable. If the report shows a weak criterion while knowledge is fine, a group will not touch it and one-to-one criterion coaching will.

faqs.question: Why is Arabic on my child's MYP timetable?
faqs.answer: Because Dubai requires it regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and prohibits combined classes, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. The timetable therefore carries subjects beyond the eight MYP groups, and Arabic is among the most requested tutoring streams in the emirate.

faqs.question: Do tutors for Middle Years pupils need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the requirement does not depend on the age of the student. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of quoted amounts, and ask to see the permit rather than accepting an assurance.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barari.closingBody: The most useful email you can send your child's school asks for the four criterion marks out of eight in each subject, which criterion is weakest across the whole report, and what task is next assessed against it. Those three answers turn a grade from one to seven into a plan, and they often reveal that three mediocre subjects are one transferable weakness appearing three times. If your child is in MYP5 and the Personal Project journal has not been started, that is the first job, because the marks sit in documented process and cannot be recovered later. Al Barari sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits in the UAE and promise no grades.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below support Middle Years Programme subjects from MYP 1 to MYP 5, working to the four published criteria in each subject group. Matching takes account of where a student sits in the programme's year, because a first-term unit and a final-term reporting point need different work. All sessions run online.

intro.heading: A programme with no examination to count down to
paragraphs: Parents in Al Barsha arriving from an examination-driven system find the Middle Years Programme calendar genuinely disorientating, and that confusion costs money. There is no public examination in MYP 1 to MYP 4 to count down to. There is no syllabus a parent can read and tick off. What there is instead is a rolling cycle: units of work, each with a small number of criteria assessed inside it, feeding a reporting schedule the school decides. A family who treats that as a slow run-up to something external will buy support at the wrong points and misread every report they receive.

The programme's real calendar has three layers. The first is the unit cycle: a unit of work runs for some weeks, assesses two or three of the four criteria in that subject, and closes. The second is the reporting cycle, usually two or three reporting points a year, which aggregate whatever criteria have been assessed by then. The third is the programme arc: five years in which MYP 1 to 3 build habits and MYP 4 and 5 carry real assessed consequence, ending in the Personal Project and the decision about what comes next.

Reading those three layers changes what a parent does with a report. An interim report is partial by construction, because not every criterion is assessed in every unit. A student showing a four on criterion D in November may have been assessed on it once, on one task, in one unit. That is information, and it is not a verdict, and treating it as a verdict is how families end up buying three subjects of weekly support in response to a provisional picture.

A second consequence follows for how a household budgets. An examination course invites a long commitment because the target sits at a fixed distance and gets closer every week. The Middle Years Programme does not work that way, and a year-long weekly slot bought in September will spend many of its hours in weeks where no criterion is being assessed in that subject at all. It also changes when support is worth buying. The useful moments in an MYP year are not the moments a report arrives; they are the weeks before a unit's assessed task, and the start of MYP 5. The first is where a tutor can actually affect a criterion level, because the task has not been attempted yet. The second is where the programme's one genuinely time-bound piece of work begins, and where the option decisions for the following year get made.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. On a calendar-led page that matters practically: MYP support is better bought in short, movable blocks placed against unit cycles than as a fixed year-long commitment, and short movable blocks are straightforward to operate when nobody has to build a driving route around them.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha.programmesIntro: The five MYP years do different work, and support in each is worth a different amount. The notes below describe them by what the calendar actually demands rather than by difficulty.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the first two years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked from zero to eight against published descriptors, with units running on a cycle and interdisciplinary work linking subjects. Nothing feeds an external qualification. The calendar is therefore gentle and the value of support is entirely in habit formation: generalising rather than noticing, structuring a communication, evaluating rather than describing.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Barsha this is the band families skip, and the saving is illusory. A student who has not learned to structure a criterion C communication at twelve meets the same weakness at fifteen in the Personal Project and again in a Diploma internal assessment, by which point a deadline is doing the teaching and the sessions cost more and achieve less.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the middle years
programmes.description: Assessed tasks become substantial and the criteria are applied at more demanding descriptors. In many schools MYP 4 is where subject choices begin to narrow and where mathematics splits into standard and extended routes. Reporting carries more weight because it starts to inform the following year's placements, which makes the second and third terms of MYP 4 a genuine decision point.
programmes.countryNote: The mathematics route decision in MYP 4 is the one that reaches furthest forward in this catchment, because extended mathematics is the path that prepares a student for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. A family who wants that door open should know the school's placement criteria and timing before the decision is taken, not afterwards.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the final year
programmes.description: The only genuinely time-bound year in the programme. The Personal Project runs through it, assessed on three criteria of planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked zero to eight for twenty-four marks in total, with a product, a process journal and a report. Option choices for the next programme are made. Where a school uses MYP eAssessment there are on-screen examinations and ePortfolios; where it does not, reporting stays internal.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South schools differ on the eAssessment question and most parents here do not know which applies to their own child. The answer changes the final year's plan completely, because an on-screen examination needs timed practice while an internally reported year does not. The MYP coordinator can answer it in a sentence.

programmes.name: What MYP 5 leads into
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme, A Levels, or in some schools a one-year IGCSE route or a career-related programme. The two main destinations read MYP attainment differently: a Diploma school looks at the spread across subject groups because a candidate cannot drop the weak one, while a sixth form looks at the two or three subjects to be continued.
programmes.countryNote: Both destinations are available within a short drive of Al Barsha, with British-pathway schools in Al Barsha 1 and Al Sufouh and IB provision in Al Barsha South and Emirates Hills. That makes the MYP 5 option decision a real choice here, and it is a decision with a school-set deadline attached.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: Each subject group has its own four criteria, and the assessment cycle inside each is what a calendar-led plan works against. The entries below name the criteria and note when in a year each tends to be assessed.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion A is assessed most frequently through the year because it fits a routine task; criterion B usually appears in a dedicated investigation once or twice a year, which makes those weeks the highest-leverage moments in the subject.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. B and C are typically assessed together in a practical investigation once or twice a year. Those are the tasks worth preparing for, and they are the direct ancestors of the Diploma scientific investigation.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Assessed tasks are spread more evenly than in the sciences, so the leverage is in the weeks before each extended piece. Criterion A rewards analysis of how a text achieves its effect rather than a summary of what happens.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, with students placed in a phase rather than a year. Speaking is usually assessed in a scheduled window each term and is the criterion least rehearsed, because it cannot easily be practised alone. Those windows are worth knowing in advance.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion B investigations are scheduled and substantial, and criterion D is what separates a five from a seven. Source work and referencing conventions are reliable marks that can be taught once and reused.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design cycle runs across weeks, so the calendar inside a unit is unusually visible here. Students who build a good solution without documenting the development lose heavily on criterion B, whatever the product looks like.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. The process journal is the assessed artefact as much as the finished work, and it has to be kept while the work is being made rather than assembled before a deadline. Performance criteria are assessed in scheduled windows.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. The written components surprise families who assumed the subject was practical only, and criterion B rewards a plan with stated targets rather than a description of training done.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and service as action
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary units are assessed in their own right with criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection, and they usually sit at a fixed point in the year. Students treat them as an extra piece of one subject and lose the synthesis marks. Service as action carries a reflection expectation rather than an hours target.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in every Dubai private school. KHDA calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

sections.heading: The MYP year, term by term
paragraphs: The table below maps a typical UAE academic year, running in three terms from roughly September, onto what the Middle Years Programme actually does in each phase and what is worth buying. Reporting points and assessment windows are set by the school, so the specifics belong to your own school's calendar; the shape, however, is stable across MYP schools in this catchment.

The pattern that matters is that the leverage sits before the assessed tasks and not after the reports. A unit of work runs for some weeks and assesses two or three of the four criteria inside it. Once that task is submitted, the level is awarded and the only remaining value is learning for next time. Two or three sessions in the weeks before it, working against the descriptor for the level above, is where a criterion level can still move. Two or three sessions after the report arrives are two or three sessions aimed at a task that has closed.

The second pattern is that reports in this programme are partial by construction. Not every criterion is assessed in every unit, so an interim report aggregates whatever has been assessed by that point, which may be a single task on a single criterion. A family treating a November interim as a full picture will over-respond, which in this catchment typically means buying weekly support in three subjects in response to provisional information.

The third is that the third term in MYP 4 carries a decision most families do not see coming: subject and route placements for MYP 5 and, in mathematics, the standard or extended split that reaches all the way into Diploma Higher Level eligibility. That deadline is school-set and worth asking about in the second term rather than the third.

sections.heading: Which criteria get assessed when, and why that matters
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group has four criteria, each marked from zero to eight against published descriptors, and the four are not assessed at the same frequency. That single fact explains most of what confuses parents about MYP reporting and most of what makes timing decisive.

Criteria that fit a routine classroom task get assessed often. Knowing and understanding in mathematics and in the sciences, using language in language and literature, applying and performing in physical and health education: these appear repeatedly across a year because they can be assessed within an ordinary piece of work. Criteria requiring an extended, designed task get assessed rarely, often once or twice a year. Investigating patterns in mathematics, inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating in sciences, investigating in individuals and societies: these need a scheduled investigation.

The consequence is sharp. A student's level on a rarely assessed criterion rests on one or two pieces of work in a whole year. That makes the weeks before each of those tasks the highest-leverage moments in the subject, and it also means a disappointing level on such a criterion is thinner evidence than a parent assumes. The right response is not twelve weeks of weekly support; it is two or three sessions before the next one of those tasks.

The table below sets out the pattern. It is a guide to where to look rather than a claim about any school's scheme of work, and the subject teacher can confirm when each criterion is next being assessed. That question, asked in a parents' evening, is more useful than almost anything else a parent can ask, because it converts a vague worry into a date.

sections.heading: MYP 5 counted backwards
paragraphs: MYP 5 is the one year in the programme that can genuinely be planned backwards, because it contains deadlines rather than only cycles. The Personal Project runs through it, assessed on three criteria of planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked zero to eight for twenty-four marks in total, and comprising a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, supervised by a school-appointed supervisor. Option choices for the next programme are made during the year. Where a school uses MYP eAssessment there are on-screen examinations and ePortfolios with their own entry and submission dates.

The sequence that fails is always the same. A goal is agreed in September, work begins in November, the journal is not kept, the product is finished in February and the report is written in three weeks with the journal reconstructed backwards. Two-thirds of the available marks sit in planning and reflecting rather than in the product, and a reconstructed journal reads as reconstructed. This is not a difficult failure to avoid and it is the commonest one in this catchment.

The table below counts the year backwards from a school-set final deadline. The dates belong to your school and the MYP coordinator will supply them; what the table provides is the order and the realistic spacing. The highest-value intervention is the earliest and the cheapest: testing whether the goal is scoped to be completable and to generate enough evidence of applying skills. That is one conversation and it changes the ceiling on the whole project.

Running alongside it is the option decision, which has its own school-set deadline, usually earlier than families expect. A Diploma school reads MYP attainment across subject groups because a Diploma candidate cannot drop the weak one; a sixth form reads the two or three subjects to be continued. Which evidence a student needs therefore depends on the destination, and gathering it is work that has to happen before the deadline rather than in an appeal afterwards.

sections.heading: The five-year arc, and where each year's work lands
paragraphs: Stepping back from a single year, the programme has a shape that is worth planning across rather than reacting to annually. MYP 1 and MYP 2 are habit years. Nothing feeds an external qualification and the whole value of support is in learning to generalise rather than notice, to structure a communication, and to evaluate rather than describe. Those are the three behaviours every later criterion rewards, and they are cheap to build at eleven and expensive to build at sixteen.

MYP 3 is where assessed tasks become substantial enough that habits show. A student who built them earlier starts producing fives and sixes on the rarely assessed criteria without extra effort; a student who did not starts producing threes and fours and nobody can see why, because the content knowledge is fine. This is the year in which a parent most often first sees a problem, and the problem was formed two years earlier.

MYP 4 carries the decisions. Subject placements for the final year, and in mathematics the standard or extended split that determines whether Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level stays available later. Those are school-set and evidence-based, and the evidence is the criterion marks accumulated across the year. Support in MYP 4 therefore has a concrete use beyond the grades themselves, which is unusual in this programme.

MYP 5 carries the Personal Project, the option choices and, where a school uses it, eAssessment. It is the busiest and most time-bound year. A family who has done nothing earlier and starts here is buying a scramble; a family who built habits in MYP 1 to 3 and gathered placement evidence in MYP 4 is buying a project supervision block and little else. The arithmetic across five years favours the early spend substantially, which is the least popular advice on this page.

sections.heading: No mocks: what replaces the diagnostic
paragraphs: Families arriving from examination systems look for the mock, find nothing comparable in MYP 1 to 4, and lose their main diagnostic tool. There are three substitutes and all three are free.

The first is the criterion marks themselves. The school holds a level from zero to eight for each of the four criteria in every subject and will provide them on request. The pattern across those marks is the diagnosis. A student consistently strong on A and C and weak on B and D knows the material and communicates it and is not yet investigating independently or thinking critically about it, which is a specific and fixable problem. A flat five across all four is a different problem entirely, usually engagement rather than skill.

The second is the descriptor for the level above. The school holds those too. Reading the written statement for the level a student is achieving next to the written statement for the level above produces a precise, short list of what the work is missing. That comparison is the whole of criterion-referenced teaching, and a tutor who does not do it is teaching topics in a programme that does not assess topics.

The third is the assessed task itself. An MYP assessed task, returned with the criterion levels awarded, is better evidence than a mock because it is real assessment against the real descriptors. Collecting those tasks rather than only the reports gives a parent a running record, and in this catchment that record is the single most useful thing to bring to a first tutoring conversation. Ask the subject teacher when the next assessed task on the weak criterion falls, and the diagnostic becomes a plan.
bullets: Ask for the criterion marks, not the grade; the pattern is the diagnosis
Read the descriptor for the level above next to the one being achieved
Collect returned assessed tasks, which are real evidence against real descriptors
Ask when the next assessed task on the weak criterion falls

sections.heading: Ramadan, breaks and keeping an MYP habit alive
paragraphs: The MYP calendar is less deadline-driven than an examination course, which makes it more vulnerable to interruption rather than less. There is no looming date to pull a student back into a routine, so a habit broken in February frequently stays broken until the summer. Three predictable interruptions sit in the UAE academic year and all three can be planned for in September.

Ramadan falls within the academic year and shortens school hours, with family routines moving around Iftar. For MYP 1 to 3 an earlier, shorter session usually works better than a post-Iftar one, since a younger student's evening attention is limited. For MYP 4 and 5 a post-Iftar slot works well. The point is to keep something running rather than to pause for a month, because restarting a habit costs more than maintaining a reduced one.

End-of-term breaks are the second. MYP students lose the thread across a long break more than examination students do, because there is no revision task holding it. Two sessions in the final week of a break, previewing the unit the next term opens with, restores the working method cheaply. Two sessions in the first week of a break, by contrast, are usually two sessions nobody wants to attend.

The third is the co-curricular calendar, which most schools publish a term ahead. Clubs, squad training and performance commitments move termly, and a slot chosen against last term's timetable will collide with this term's. Reading the published timetable before fixing a slot removes the commonest cause of a cancelled MYP session. All three of these adjustments are easier to make when nobody is building a driving route around them, which is one practical consequence of online delivery.
bullets: No looming date means a broken habit stays broken; keep something running
MYP 1-3 usually do better earlier and shorter in Ramadan; MYP 4-5 post-Iftar

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units and service as action on the calendar
paragraphs: Two parts of the programme sit at fixed points in the year and are routinely under-prepared because they do not belong to a single subject. Both are worth knowing about in advance.

Interdisciplinary units are assessed in their own right, with criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection, and in most schools they sit at a defined point in the year. The characteristic student error is treating the unit as an extra piece of whichever subject they find easier, which produces work that demonstrates one discipline well and shows no synthesis. Synthesis is the thing being assessed. Explaining what it means, with an example, takes one session and is a conversation very few students have had.

Service as action runs across the programme and carries a reflection expectation rather than an hours target, which parents from other systems frequently misread as an hours requirement. What matters is that the student can account for what they did and what it changed in their own words. The reflection has to be the student's, and it is one of the places where a well-meaning parent or tutor can cross a line without noticing.

Both of these land in terms where subject assessed tasks are already running, which is why they appear on a calendar page rather than a content page. A family who knows in September that the interdisciplinary unit falls in the second term, and that a service reflection is due at the end of the year, can place support around them. A family who does not meet both as surprises in the same fortnight, usually alongside a scheduled science investigation.
bullets: Interdisciplinary units assess synthesis, which is the part students skip

sections.heading: What MYP support costs by phase, and the checks that apply all year
paragraphs: Because MYP support is better bought in short blocks against the calendar than as a year-long commitment, cost is clearest expressed per block. Market rates read in October 2026: Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, usually delivered by current university students. Unitors publishes from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB for qualified online subject tutors. TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate places specialist work at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Bestimate quotes in-home visits including travel at AED 180 to AED 350, independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are the providers' own figures, not an IB Gram price list.

Applied to the MYP calendar at the mid band of AED 150 to AED 300, a pre-task block of three sessions is roughly AED 450 to AED 900. A weekly habit slot for MYP 1 to 3 at forty-five minutes a week across a term is roughly AED 1,500 to AED 3,000. A Personal Project block of six sessions across MYP 5 is roughly AED 900 to AED 1,800. A single diagnostic hour is AED 150 to AED 300. The useful observation is that the calendar-aligned blocks are small, because the MYP rewards timing more than volume.

Two free checks apply whatever the phase. The permit: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

The accreditation check: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and regulates schools rather than tutoring platforms. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; that is a numbered document. IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB, and claims none. And on the Personal Project specifically: a tutor questions, reviews and gives feedback, writes no part of the project, journal or report, and the student signs whatever authenticity declaration the school requires.

process.title: Ask when the next assessed task falls
process.description: The subject teacher can say which criteria the next unit assesses and when the task is due. That single answer converts a worry into a date and makes a pre-task block possible. It is also the question that reveals how rarely some criteria are assessed, which is why a disappointing level can be thinner evidence than it looks.

process.title: Get the criterion marks and the next descriptor
process.description: The school holds a level from zero to eight for each criterion and holds the published descriptors. Reading the statement for the level being achieved next to the statement for the level above produces a short, precise list of what the work is missing. That comparison is the entire method, and it costs nothing.

process.title: Ask the coordinator about eAssessment and the project dates
process.description: Whether the school enters students for MYP eAssessment or reports internally changes the final year completely, and the Personal Project milestones are school-set and published nowhere a parent can search. Both answers come from the MYP coordinator in one message, and both reshape the MYP 5 plan.

process.title: Check the MYP 4 placement deadline early
process.description: Subject placements for MYP 5, and in mathematics the standard or extended split, are decided on criterion evidence accumulated across the year, with a school-set deadline usually earlier than families expect. Asking in the second term leaves time to build evidence; asking in the third leaves time only to appeal.

process.title: Buy in blocks, not in years
process.description: The MYP rewards timing more than volume, so short blocks placed against assessed tasks beat an open-ended weekly commitment. Three sessions before a scheduled investigation is roughly AED 450 to AED 900 at the mid band and is usually worth more than twelve sessions aimed at nothing in particular.

whyPoints.title: Timed to assessed tasks, not to reports
whyPoints.description: A criterion level can only be affected before the task is attempted. Support is placed in the weeks before a scheduled assessed task rather than in the weeks after a report, which is when most families buy it and when the task in question has already closed.

whyPoints.title: Interim reports read as partial
whyPoints.description: Not every criterion is assessed in every unit, so a mid-year report aggregates whatever has been assessed by then, sometimes a single task on a single criterion. Saying so prevents the three-subject response to provisional information that is the commonest overspend in this programme.

whyPoints.title: MYP 5 planned backwards from real dates
whyPoints.description: The Personal Project milestones, the option-choice deadline and any eAssessment dates are school-set and obtained before planning begins. Two-thirds of the project's marks sit in planning and reflecting rather than in the product, which is why scoping the goal early is the highest-value session in the year.

whyPoints.title: Habit work priced for the years it belongs in
whyPoints.description: MYP 1 to 3 is where generalising, structuring and evaluating are cheap to build, and MYP 5 is where their absence is expensive. Short weekly sessions in the early bands are the lowest cost per unit of long-term benefit available anywhere in the programme.

whyPoints.title: Blocks rather than open-ended commitments
whyPoints.description: Frequency moves with the unit cycle: two or three sessions before a scheduled investigation, little in between, more in MYP 5. That is simple to operate when nobody is building a driving route around it, and it keeps total spend proportionate to what the calendar actually demands.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project boundary stated up front
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions the goal, interrogates the plan, reviews the journal and gives feedback on the student's own draft report. No part of the project, journal or report is written or produced by a tutor, and the student signs the school's authenticity declaration. That is said to the student at the first session.

faqs.question: When in the MYP year is it actually worth hiring a tutor?
faqs.answer: In the two or three weeks before a scheduled assessed task, because that is the only point at which a criterion level can still be affected. Once the task is submitted the level is awarded and the remaining value is learning for next time. Most families buy support after a report arrives, which is aimed at a task that has closed. Ask the subject teacher which criteria the next unit assesses and when the task is due, and the timing follows from that.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report look incomplete in November?
faqs.answer: Because it is, by construction. Each subject has four criteria and not every criterion is assessed in every unit, so an interim report aggregates whatever has been assessed by that point. A level on a rarely assessed criterion may rest on a single task in a single unit. That is information rather than a verdict, and treating it as a verdict is how families end up buying weekly support in three subjects in response to a provisional picture.

faqs.question: Which MYP criteria are assessed only once or twice a year?
faqs.answer: The ones needing an extended designed task. Investigating patterns in mathematics, inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating in sciences, investigating and thinking critically in individuals and societies, and the analysing and organizing criteria in language and literature all tend to be assessed in scheduled pieces of work rather than in routine tasks. Those weeks are the highest-leverage moments in each subject. The subject teacher can confirm when the next one falls, which is the most useful question at a parents' evening.

faqs.question: How should we plan the Personal Project year in Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Backwards from the school's own milestones, which the MYP coordinator sets and which are published nowhere a parent can search. The project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, each from zero to eight for twenty-four marks, so two-thirds of the marks sit outside the product. The highest-value session is the earliest: testing whether the goal is completable and able to generate enough evidence of applied skills. A goal abandoned in January costs most of the reflecting marks.

faqs.question: Does our school use MYP eAssessment, and does it change the plan?
faqs.answer: Ask the MYP coordinator, because schools in Al Barsha and Al Barsha South differ and most parents here do not know which applies. Where a school enters students for eAssessment there are on-screen examinations and ePortfolios with their own dates, and timed practice becomes genuinely useful in the final year. Where a school reports internally, the year is entirely criterion-referenced and timed examination practice is largely wasted effort. The answer changes the MYP 5 plan completely.

faqs.question: What replaces mock examinations as a diagnostic in the MYP?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. The criterion marks themselves, which the school holds for each of the four criteria in every subject and will provide on request. The published descriptor for the level above the one being achieved, which turns a level into a short list of what the work is missing. And the returned assessed tasks, which are real assessment against real descriptors and better evidence than a mock. Collecting the tasks rather than only the reports gives a parent a running record.

faqs.question: When is the MYP 4 subject placement decision made?
faqs.answer: On a school-set deadline, usually in the second or third term of MYP 4, and on the criterion evidence accumulated across the year. In mathematics this is where the standard and extended split happens, and extended is the route that prepares a student for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level later. Asking the school in the second term leaves time to build evidence; asking in the third leaves time only to appeal. It is the decision in this programme that reaches furthest forward.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying MYP support in Years 7 and 8 when nothing is examined?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest support per unit of long-term benefit in the whole programme, precisely because no deadline is distorting it. The work is three habits every later criterion rewards: generalising rather than noticing, structuring a communication, and evaluating rather than describing. A student who builds them at eleven produces solid levels on the rarely assessed criteria at fourteen without extra effort. A student who does not will be building them at sixteen against a Personal Project deadline.

faqs.question: My child's levels dropped in MYP 3. What usually causes that?
faqs.answer: Habits formed two years earlier becoming visible, rather than a new problem. MYP 3 is where assessed tasks become substantial enough to separate students who can investigate and evaluate independently from students who know the content and cannot yet do those things. The content knowledge usually looks fine, which is why the drop seems inexplicable. The diagnosis is in the pattern of criterion marks: strong on knowing and understanding, weak on the investigating and thinking criteria.

faqs.question: How should MYP sessions work around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Keep something running rather than pausing for the month, because the MYP has no looming date to pull a student back into a routine and a habit broken in Ramadan often stays broken until the summer. School hours shorten and family routines move around Iftar. For MYP 1 to 3 an earlier and shorter session usually works better; for MYP 4 and 5 a post-Iftar slot works well. Agree the arrangement in the first term rather than in the second week of the month.

faqs.question: Are school breaks a good time for MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: The end of a break is, and the start generally is not. MYP students lose the thread across a long break more than examination students do, because no revision task holds it. Two sessions in the final week, previewing the unit the next term opens with, restores the working method cheaply and costs roughly AED 300 to AED 600 at the mid band. Two sessions in the first week of a break are usually two sessions nobody wants to attend.

faqs.question: What is an interdisciplinary unit and when does it fall?
faqs.answer: A unit assessed in its own right, with criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection, and in most schools it sits at a defined point in the year. The characteristic student error is treating it as an extra piece of whichever subject is easier, producing work that shows one discipline well and no synthesis, which is the thing being assessed. Explaining what synthesis means with a worked example takes one session, and very few students have had that conversation.

faqs.question: Does service as action have an hours requirement?
faqs.answer: It carries a reflection expectation rather than an hours target, which parents from other systems frequently misread. What matters is that the student can account for what they did and what it changed, in their own words. That reflection has to be the student's, and it is one of the places where a well-meaning parent or tutor can cross a line without noticing. A tutor can ask what the student thinks and cannot supply the answer.

faqs.question: How much should a calendar-aligned MYP block cost?
faqs.answer: At the mid band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers who publish it, a pre-task block of three sessions is roughly AED 450 to AED 900. A Personal Project block of six sessions across MYP 5 is roughly AED 900 to AED 1,800. A weekly forty-five minute habit slot across a term for a younger student is roughly AED 1,500 to AED 3,000. The blocks are small because this programme rewards timing more than volume.

faqs.question: My child joined an Al Barsha MYP class mid-year. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask which criteria have already been assessed in each subject and on what tasks, because a mid-unit arrival means levels exist for work the student was not present for. Mid-year arrivals are frequent in Dubai Hills and Al Barsha South. One diagnostic session that maps the assessed criteria so far against the descriptors, and identifies which upcoming tasks give the student a chance to be assessed on the weak ones, is the cheapest way to turn a confusing first report into a plan.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with an MYP student need a permit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with MYP students across Al Barsha South and the districts either side of it. Each one teaches to the four published criteria for the relevant subject group, because a student who does not know what Criterion B rewards cannot be marked well against it.

intro.heading: Why an MYP question in Al Barsha South is really a question about sixteen
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme runs from MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages eleven to sixteen, and it is assessed in a way that looks nothing like the exam system most parents in Al Barsha South grew up with. Every subject is marked against four criteria, lettered A to D, each scored from 0 to 8. The four add to 32, and published grade boundaries convert that total into a single number from 1 to 7. There is no terminal paper in most schools. There are tasks, and each task is marked against one or two criteria rather than against a percentage.

This produces a specific kind of parental confusion. A report comes home with a 5 in Sciences and a 4 in Mathematics, with no percentage and no rank, and a comment about Criterion C. It is genuinely hard to tell from that whether the child is in difficulty or doing fine. The useful response is not to find the nearest tutor; it is to find out which criteria are low, what those criteria actually reward, and whether the task types the school uses are being read correctly. That is a short diagnostic job, and it often ends with a parent deciding no tutoring is needed.

The second reason families in Al Barsha South search for MYP support is the fork at sixteen. Some schools near here run the MYP to MYP 5 and then the Diploma. Others run the MYP to the end of MYP 3 and move to IGCSE in Year 10. Others never run the MYP at all. A child in Al Barsha South, a child in Al Barsha 1 and a child in Dubai Hills Estate can be in the same year group on three different trajectories, and the right MYP tutoring plan depends on which one they are on.

Dubai's market makes this more varied than most cities. KHDA counted 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for roughly 7% of private enrolment. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places, and enrolment rose 6% during 2025-26. More IB provision is arriving, which means more MYP students and more families facing the sixteen decision without a clear reference point.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school, group or examination board. Tutoring for families in Al Barsha South, Arjan, Dubai Science Park and Jumeirah Village Circle is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because MYP support is long and relational work and nobody should start it on a false premise about how it will be delivered.
