dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.programmesIntro: Al Barsha South sits in reach of schools running three different middle-years models. Knowing which one your child is on decides what MYP tutoring should actually be doing between now and sixteen.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, MYP 1 to MYP 5
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, assessed through tasks rather than terminal papers. The framework is organised around key and related concepts, six global contexts and a statement of inquiry per unit, with approaches to learning skills taught explicitly alongside content. Students also complete service as action and at least one interdisciplinary unit assessment each year.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near Al Barsha South run the full five years and enter students for MYP eAssessment at the end of MYP 5, leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Others run the framework internally without external assessment. The two produce very different MYP 5 years, and it is worth asking the school which it does before planning any support.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, as the destination after MYP 5
programmes.description: Six subject groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service as the core. Assessment moves to timed external papers plus one internal assessment per subject, which is the format shift that catches MYP students out in their first Diploma term.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP 5 student in Al Barsha South moving into DP1 at the same school has continuity of philosophy and a sharp change in assessment. The students who struggle are rarely the weakest; they are the ones who were strongest at extended criterion-marked tasks and have never sat a timed paper against a mark scheme.

programmes.name: IGCSE from Year 10, the other fork at fourteen
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson two-year courses ending in terminal papers, with codes such as 0580 for Cambridge Mathematics, 0620 for Chemistry and 4MA1 for Pearson Mathematics A. Tiering at entry sets the grade ceiling in many subjects, and the whole assessment logic differs from criterion-related marking.
programmes.countryNote: A student leaving MYP 3 for a Year 10 IGCSE cohort in Al Barsha 1 or JVC needs timed-paper technique and command-term reading more than content. We plan that as a defined block with the specification document open, and we say so when the gap genuinely needs two terms rather than six weeks.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.subjectsIntro: MYP subjects are grouped rather than listed, and each group has its own four criteria. These are the eight groups with the criterion that most often holds an Al Barsha South student back.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria are A analysing, B organising, C producing text and D using language. Criterion A is where most marks go missing: students summarise a text where the task asked them to analyse the effect of a writer's choices, and the descriptor pays for the second.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and a student in the wrong phase will look weak against descriptors written for a different level of fluency.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria are A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating and D thinking critically. Criterion D is the usual gap: students describe sources rather than evaluating their origin, purpose and limitations, which is the specific move the descriptor rewards.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria are A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating and D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B is lost on variables and controls rather than on the science, and Criterion C on graphs drawn without uncertainty or a stated trend.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria are A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating and D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B requires a general rule and a justification of it, and students who find the pattern but never prove or test it stop at the middle band.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria are A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution and D evaluating. The marks are in the documentation rather than the artefact: a strong product with thin design specification and no testing against stated success criteria scores poorly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria are A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing and D evaluating. The process journal carries a large share of the available marks, and students who work well but record nothing lose marks they genuinely earned in the studio.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria are A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing and D reflecting and improving performance. Written reflection is the weak point for athletic students, who are routinely surprised that half the criteria are not physical.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed separately on disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Schools entering students for eAssessment sit an on-screen interdisciplinary examination, which is unfamiliar to students who have only met single-subject tasks.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Marked on three criteria, planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of 8. Supervised at school and supported externally only as coaching and feedback on the student's own work and process journal.

sections.heading: Al Barsha South against its neighbours, judged on what happens at sixteen
paragraphs: The comparison families actually need is not about tutor supply. It is about which middle-years model each community's schools run, because that decides what an MYP tutor should be preparing a child for. In the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh cluster there are IB continuum schools that take students through MYP 5 and into the Diploma, and British-curriculum schools that end the middle years at fourteen and move to IGCSE. In the Dubai Hills, JVC and Motor City cluster, British provision dominates and the IGCSE route is the norm.

That means two MYP 3 students living a few minutes apart can face completely different next two years. One will continue with criterion-marked tasks, interdisciplinary units and a Personal Project. The other will be handed a Cambridge or Pearson specification, a tiering decision and a terminal paper. A tutor who treats them identically is useful to neither.

The table below compares the communities on that axis. It avoids ranking them, because ranking a neighbourhood on tutoring quality would be meaningless: lessons here are delivered online and the available pool is the same from every address in New Dubai. What the table does show is which question a family in each community should be asking their school this term.

The one genuine local difference is timing, and for MYP it matters more than for Diploma students. Criterion-marked task work needs sustained attention rather than adrenaline, and a twelve-year-old off a 16:00 bus from Al Barsha South is not in a state to produce a Criterion B investigation. For MYP 1 to 3 a 17:30 slot usually outperforms a 19:30 one, which is the reverse of the advice we give Diploma families.

sections.heading: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, and the letter that is actually low
paragraphs: MYP reporting names criteria rather than topics, and a parent who learns the four letters for one subject group can read a report properly for the first time. In Sciences they are A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, and D reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics they are A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, and D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Each is scored 0 to 8.

The diagnostic value of this is high, because the letters separate ability from technique. A Sciences student scoring 7 on Criterion A and 3 on Criterion B does not have a science problem; they have a variables-and-controls problem, which is a two-lesson fix. A Mathematics student scoring well on A and poorly on B is finding patterns and never generalising or justifying them, which is a specific habit rather than a gap in knowledge.

Most Al Barsha South families arrive without this information, because the report gives a single 1-7 figure per subject and a comment. Ask the teacher for the criterion scores behind the grade, in writing. Schools hold them, the request is routine, and the answer converts a vague worry into a defined piece of work. We ask for the same thing in the first lesson, so a parent who has it already saves themselves the session.

The table lists all eight groups with their criteria and the one that most often holds a student in Al Barsha South back. It is worth reading even for subjects your child is doing well in, because the pattern across subjects is usually consistent: a student weak on investigation criteria tends to be weak on them everywhere, and that is one problem rather than five.

sections.heading: How 32 criterion marks become a grade from 1 to 7
paragraphs: Each of the four criteria is marked out of 8, so a subject carries 32 marks in total. Those 32 are converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries, and the boundaries are not quarters. This is the arithmetic that explains most of the confusion on an MYP report card.

The practical consequence is that the four criteria are not interchangeable. A student with 7, 7, 7, 3 carries the same total as a student with 6, 6, 6, 6, and both land in the same band, but the first student has one defined weakness worth a few lessons while the second has a general pattern worth a term. Reading only the final grade cannot tell those two apart, which is why the criterion breakdown is the thing to ask for.

It also explains why panic about a single low grade is usually premature. Criteria are not all assessed in every task, and a subject grade published in the middle of the year may rest on two criteria out of four. A 3 in Mathematics in November can mean Criterion B was assessed once, in an unfamiliar investigation, and the student mishandled the format. That is diagnosable in one conversation and does not call for a weekly commitment.

The reverse case is the one we take seriously. A student scoring consistently at the lower end of every criterion in two or more subject groups is usually struggling with a reading or organisational demand rather than with the subjects. That pattern is worth a diagnostic lesson, and it is sometimes worth a conversation with the school about learning support rather than with us about tutoring.

sections.heading: MYP 5, eAssessment and the schools that do not sit it
paragraphs: At the end of MYP 5 some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations in several subjects with moderated ePortfolios in subjects such as Language Acquisition, Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education, plus the moderated Personal Project, and leads to the IB MYP Certificate. Other schools run the MYP framework internally for five years without external assessment and report their own grades.

That difference changes MYP 5 completely, and parents in Al Barsha South frequently do not know which their school does. A student facing on-screen examinations needs timed-assessment practice, because an on-screen MYP examination is an unfamiliar object to a child who has only ever submitted tasks. A student in a school without eAssessment has a Personal Project and a set of internal tasks, and timed-paper practice would be a waste of their year.

The interdisciplinary assessment is the component that surprises most students in schools that do sit eAssessment. It asks for disciplinary grounding from two subjects, a synthesis of them, and reflection on the process, in one on-screen sitting. Students who are strong in individual subjects can perform poorly because nothing in their school year has required them to combine two disciplines under time pressure.

Ask the school one question this term: does our cohort sit MYP eAssessment, and if so in which subjects. The answer determines whether the right support for your MYP 5 child is criterion coaching or timed-assessment practice, and buying the wrong one is the commonest way a Dubai family wastes a term of MYP tutoring.

On-screen examinations need timed practice; internal task assessment does not
ePortfolio subjects are judged on process evidence, so the journal is the work

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the three criteria it is marked on
paragraphs: The Personal Project sits in MYP 5 and is marked against three criteria: planning, applying skills, and reflecting, each out of 8. It is the first piece of genuinely independent extended work most students have done, and it is the one where the gap between effort and marks is widest.

The reason is that the marks are not in the product. A student can build something impressive and score in the middle bands because the planning criterion wants a clear goal with stated success criteria, the applying-skills criterion wants evidence of transferring approaches-to-learning skills, and the reflecting criterion wants evaluation of the product against those stated criteria plus reflection on the learning. The process journal is where all of that is evidenced, and students who work hard and record nothing lose marks they earned.

The boundary for external support here is firm and worth stating precisely. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a goal is specific enough to be evaluated, teach a skill the student needs, and give feedback on journal entries and drafts the student has written. A tutor must never write, make, produce or complete any part of the project or its report. The IB treats that as malpractice and the consequence falls on the candidate, not on the tutor who offered it.

Deadlines belong to the school supervisor. MYP coordinators set internal dates for goal approval, journal checkpoints and final submission, and those are the only dates a support plan should work to. We take them from your child's supervisor rather than publishing dates here, and no IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page because none could be verified from the IB's own site.

sections.heading: What Middle Years support costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Middle Years tutoring tends to be bought by the term rather than by the crisis, so the monthly figure is the one worth starting from. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above a month for specialist exam-year work. An MYP student is usually in the first two of those three, not the third, and a provider pushing exam-year intensity at an MYP 2 child is selling the wrong product.

Translated to hourly figures, the published bands run as follows. Budget online tuition sits at roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate showing 200 to 450 plus. BartyED advertises AED 650 at the premium end.

In-home visiting rates sit on their own logic because travel is inside the hour: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Advertised monthly packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of those figures belong to the providers that published them in 2026, with their sources named; none is an IB Gram price.

For an MYP family the useful conclusion is about duration rather than rate. Criterion work is slow: a student learning what Criterion B actually demands in Sciences needs several marked tasks to internalise it, which is a term rather than a fortnight. A mid-band weekly arrangement sustained for two terms is better value than a premium block in April, which is the opposite of the advice an exam-year family should take. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so for most households the tutoring line is the flexible one this year.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies inside an MYP timetable
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. An MYP timetable in Al Barsha South therefore carries these alongside the eight subject groups, and they take real hours out of the week.

KHDA's rules on how they run are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can reasonably ask about. For the mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so no external provider should be offering an alternative syllabus for them.

The practical point for an MYP support plan is capacity. A student carrying eight subject groups, mandatory UAE subjects, service as action and a Personal Project has less homework headroom than the number of tutoring hours a worried parent might want to buy. One well-targeted weekly session that produces a better task is worth more than three sessions that add volume to an already full week.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Barsha South, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A good MYP enquiry contains the year group, the subject group, the criterion letters that are low, and whether the school sits eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. With those four facts a match takes a short conversation. Without them the first lesson goes on establishing information the school would have supplied by email.

The first lesson is free and diagnostic. The tutor reads a recent marked task, compares the student's own re-marking against the teacher's, and identifies whether the problem is understanding the criterion, reading the task, or the content itself. You get a written summary either way, naming the criteria and the specific move that would lift them. If the honest answer is that your child is performing normally and the report is simply hard to read, that is what the summary will say.

The delivery position does not change and is better said once, clearly. Lessons to Al Barsha South, Al Barsha 1, Arjan, Dubai Science Park, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and no tutor will arrive at a Dubai address; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we have no UAE office, centre or branch.

On availability, MYP Sciences, Mathematics and Language and Literature are usually matched within a few days. Design, Arts and specific Language Acquisition phases are narrower and can take longer, and occasionally we cannot cover a combination at all; we say so at the enquiry rather than matching you to somebody who has never read the relevant criterion descriptors. The enquiry form collects the student's year group, school, subject group and a parent contact, is used only to make the match, and can be deleted on request.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion scores
process.description: Request the A to D breakdown behind each reported 1-7 grade, in writing. Schools hold it and the request is routine. It converts a vague worry into a named piece of work, and it is the single most useful thing a parent can do before paying anyone.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one session at no cost. The tutor works from a recent marked task, has the student re-mark it against the published descriptors, and identifies whether the gap is criterion understanding, task reading or content. You receive a written summary regardless of what you decide next.

process.title: Target one or two criteria, not a subject
process.description: Support aimed at Criterion B in Sciences is a defined job with a visible outcome. Support aimed at science in general is open-ended. We name the criteria at the start so that progress can be checked against something other than a feeling.

process.title: Measure on a re-marked task
process.description: Every few weeks the student submits a task, marks it themselves against the descriptors, and the two marks are compared with the teacher's. Agreement between student and teacher is the signal that the criterion has been internalised.

process.title: Plan the sixteen decision early
process.description: By MYP 3 we talk about whether the child is heading for MYP 5 and the Diploma or for IGCSE in Year 10, because the preparation differs. That conversation belongs a year before the option forms, not after them.

whyPoints.title: Criterion descriptors, used openly
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach from the published criterion descriptors for the relevant subject group and MYP year, and students see them. A child who can predict their own criterion score within a band has learned the thing that lifts it.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the subject group and phase
whyPoints.description: A Language Acquisition student in phase 3 and one in phase 5 need different people. Online delivery means the pool is everyone who has taught that group and phase, rather than everyone within a short drive of Al Barsha South.

whyPoints.title: The sixteen decision taken seriously
whyPoints.description: We ask early whether your child is heading into MYP 5 and the Diploma or into a Year 10 IGCSE cohort, because the two need opposite preparation. Most providers never ask, and the resulting plan fits whichever route they assumed.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: Coaching on planning, skills and reflection, and feedback on the student's own journal and drafts. No tutor will write, make or produce any part of the project. The malpractice consequence lands on the student, which settles the question.

whyPoints.title: Figures sourced, claims absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or source that published it in 2026. We publish no success rate, star rating or grade guarantee, because a number that cannot be evidenced should not appear on a page a parent is planning around.

whyPoints.title: Honest about capacity
whyPoints.description: An MYP student carrying eight subject groups, the mandatory UAE subjects, service as action and a Personal Project has limited homework headroom. We will tell you when the answer is fewer hours better targeted rather than more hours.

faqs.question: What do the MYP criteria A, B, C and D on my child's report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each scored from 0 to 8, and the letters mean different things in different subject groups. In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Learning the four letters for one subject lets you read a report properly, because a low single letter is a defined technique problem while a flat profile across all four is something different.

faqs.question: How does a total out of 32 turn into a grade from 1 to 7?
faqs.answer: The four criteria add to 32 marks, and published grade boundaries convert that total into a single figure from 1 to 7. The boundaries are not simple quarters, which is why the arithmetic surprises parents. It also means two students on the same grade can be in very different positions: a profile of 7, 7, 7, 3 has one named weakness worth a few lessons, while 6, 6, 6, 6 is a general pattern worth a term. The final grade alone cannot distinguish them, so ask for the criterion scores.

faqs.question: My child's MYP grade dropped from a 6 to a 4 in one term. Should I be worried?
faqs.answer: Usually less than it feels. Not every criterion is assessed in every task, so a mid-year subject grade can rest on two criteria out of four. A drop can mean one unfamiliar investigation task was marked against Criterion B and handled badly, which is a format problem rather than a collapse. Ask which criteria the grade was based on and how many tasks fed into it. If the pattern repeats across two or more subject groups, that is a different signal and worth a diagnostic conversation rather than an immediate weekly commitment.

faqs.question: Does my school near Al Barsha South enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Some do and some do not, and it changes MYP 5 completely. Schools entering students sit on-screen examinations in several subjects, submit moderated ePortfolios in groups such as Language Acquisition, Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education, and have the Personal Project moderated, leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Schools running the framework internally report their own grades with no external assessment. Ask the coordinator directly this term, because a student facing on-screen examinations needs timed practice and a student without them does not.

faqs.question: What is the MYP interdisciplinary assessment and why do strong students do badly in it?
faqs.answer: It asks a student to show disciplinary grounding in two subjects, synthesise them into a single response, and reflect on the process, usually in one on-screen sitting for schools that sit eAssessment. Students who are strong in individual subjects can perform poorly because almost nothing in a normal school year requires combining two disciplines under time pressure. The preparation is practice at the task type rather than more content in either subject, and two or three rehearsed attempts make a visible difference.

faqs.question: Would a child in Al Barsha 1 or Dubai Hills get a better MYP tutor than one in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. None of these communities contains a concentrated supply of teachers who mark against MYP criterion descriptors; the IB cohort in Dubai is spread across many schools rather than clustered in a neighbourhood. What genuinely differs is the middle-years model the local schools run and therefore what the child meets at sixteen. Since lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, the tutor pool is identical from Al Barsha South, Al Barsha 1, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle, and the decision moves to subject group and phase.

faqs.question: Which is better at sixteen, staying in MYP 5 and the Diploma or moving to IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Neither is better in general, and anyone answering otherwise is guessing about your child. The Diploma route keeps criterion-related assessment for another year and then shifts to timed external papers with internal assessments. The IGCSE route moves to terminal papers and tiering at fourteen. The decision turns on whether your child performs better in extended independent tasks or in timed papers, on which subjects they want at sixteen to nineteen, and on what the school actually offers. Ask the school what each route looks like in practice before the option form.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on MYP Sciences Criterion B when they know the science?
faqs.answer: Because Criterion B is about inquiring and designing rather than about content. The descriptors reward a testable hypothesis with a reason, correctly named independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method another student could follow. A child who understands photosynthesis perfectly and writes a method with no stated controls scores in the lower bands. It is one of the fastest MYP fixes available, usually two or three marked tasks with the descriptor open, because the gap is a habit rather than knowledge.

faqs.question: What does Criterion B in MYP Mathematics want that my child is not doing?
faqs.answer: A generalisation, tested and justified. Students usually spot the pattern, write the next few terms and stop. The descriptor wants a general rule stated in algebra, verified against further cases, and then justified or proved, with the limits of the rule described. Reaching the top bands means doing all four of those things explicitly on the page. Most students have done the thinking and written only the conclusion, which is why Criterion B scores look low in students who are perfectly capable mathematicians.

faqs.question: How is the MYP Personal Project marked, and how much can a tutor help?
faqs.answer: It is marked on three criteria, planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of 8, with the process journal as the main evidence. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the goal is specific enough to be evaluated, teach a skill the student needs, and give feedback on journal entries and drafts the student has written. A tutor must never write, make or produce any part of the project or report. The IB treats that as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to a home in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for families in Al Barsha South, Arjan, Dubai Science Park, Dubai Hills Estate and Jumeirah Village Circle are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Other providers do sell in-home visits and publish them at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate. For criterion coaching, which depends on reading a marked task together on screen, the format loses nothing.

faqs.question: What does weekly MYP support cost monthly around Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market, with AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above reserved for specialist exam-year work that an MYP student does not need. Hourly, budget online tuition is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya, while qualified online tutors sit around AED 150 to 300. Those are other providers' published figures with their sources, not ours.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session run if we live in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Earlier than you would schedule a Diploma student. Buses here return between roughly 15:20 and 16:10, and a 16:45 to 17:30 slot generally works well for MYP 1 to 3. Criterion-marked task work needs sustained attention rather than last-minute energy, and a twelve-year-old at 19:30 produces a weaker Criterion B investigation than the same child at 17:00. Families in Arjan and Dubai Science Park where parents work until 18:00 often settle on 17:30 with homework supervision afterwards rather than a late evening lesson.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply to a student doing the MYP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those lessons occupy timetable space, which limits how much extra work an MYP week can absorb.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers my child's MYP subject group or language phase?
faqs.answer: We say so at the enquiry rather than matching you to somebody who has not read the relevant descriptors. MYP Sciences, Mathematics and Language and Literature are usually covered within a few days. Design, Arts and specific Language Acquisition phases are narrower pools and can take longer, and occasionally a combination cannot be covered at all. In that case you are better served looking elsewhere, and we will tell you that rather than filling the slot. A short wait for the right match is cheaper than a term with the wrong one.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.closingHeading: Ask for the letters, then decide
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-barsha-south.closingBody: Two requests will tell an Al Barsha South family more than a month of worrying. Ask the school for the criterion scores behind each 1-7 grade, and ask whether the cohort sits MYP eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. The first turns a vague report into a named piece of work. The second decides whether your MYP 5 child needs timed practice or criterion coaching. Bring both to a free diagnostic lesson, delivered online over live video, and you will leave with a written account of which criteria are low, what move would lift them, and whether tutoring is the right purchase at all this term.

intro.heading: Why MYP support is cheap now and expensive later
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is the stage where tutoring money goes furthest and is spent least. A student in MYP 3 or MYP 4 with a weekly session is building the habits the Diploma will assume, at a point when one session a week is enough. The same student two years later, in Diploma 2 with three Internal Assessment deadlines in a fortnight, needs several sessions a week to recover ground that was never gained. The arithmetic is not close.

What makes the Middle Years hard to act on is the absence of an external signal. There is no exam result to react to, only a report card carrying numbers out of eight against criteria with names like inquiring and designing or thinking critically. Parents read a 4 and reasonably conclude that their child is average at the subject. Very often the child understands the material and has never been shown what the criterion rewards.

That distinction is the whole value of a Middle Years tutor and the thing to test before paying anyone. Every MYP subject assesses four criteria, A to D, each marked out of eight, with published descriptors converted into a 1 to 7 grade by boundaries the school applies. A tutor who can name the four criteria in your child's subject group and read a marked task against the strand descriptors is doing the job. A tutor who talks about covering the topics is not.

In Al Furjan the practical side is straightforward, which is a relief after the Diploma pages on this site. Middle Years students are home earlier than their Diploma siblings: buses reach the villa districts between 15:20 and 16:10 depending on the district and the school, and most Middle Years children do not stay for the late revision clinics that push Year 12 and 13 students past 16:30. A 16:30 or 17:00 session fits comfortably.

IB Gram runs every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and no tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. For Middle Years work that matters mainly because it gives a wider choice of subject-group specialist, and because a session missed to a late bus moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

This page is costed rather than enthusiastic. It covers what Middle Years support is worth buying and at roughly what total, what the four criteria mean in each subject group, why a 4 is usually not a content problem, how the Personal Project and the optional MYP 5 eAssessments work, and where families in this corridor spend money on the wrong thing. Published AED figures are attributed to the providers who published them.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme runs across five years and changes character as it goes. These are the phases an Al Furjan family will meet, and what each one costs to support properly.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3, the early years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups taught through units with criteria assessed from the start, though schools often report in a simplified form at this stage. The habits that matter are reading the task instruction properly, structuring a written response, and showing a process rather than only a result. Content gaps here are small and easily closed; habit gaps compound for five years.
programmes.countryNote: Al Furjan students in these years are home earliest, often by 16:00, and rarely have late commitments, so a 16:30 session is routine. This is the cheapest and most effective place to spend. One session a week for two terms costs a fraction of a Diploma rescue block and changes what is possible in MYP 4 and 5, particularly in mathematics and the sciences.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5, the decision years
programmes.description: Criteria are applied at full demand and schools often split mathematics into standard and extended routes. Criterion B in mathematics, criterion C in the sciences, criterion D in individuals and societies and the process journal in design are the reliable places marks disappear. These two years decide whether Diploma Higher Level choices are realistic.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Al Furjan enquiries arrive, often after an MYP 4 report. Students may now stay for clubs or fixtures, pushing arrival to 16:30, so a 17:00 slot is the common fit. The useful intervention is a criteria diagnosis on marked work rather than a content review, and it typically takes one session to identify and a term to fix.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project completed in the final MYP year, supervised in school and externally moderated. It is assessed on the process as much as the product: the planning, the sources consulted, the record of decisions and the evaluation against the student's own stated criteria. Impressive outcomes with no documented process score below modest outcomes that are properly recorded.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Al Furjan families most often ask for late help, and where the money is least effective if the process journal was never kept. A tutor may read the criteria with the student, question the goal, teach research and reflection technique, and give written feedback on the student's own work. No part of the project is produced by the tutor.

programmes.name: MYP 5 eAssessments
programmes.description: Schools may enter MYP 5 students for optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Not every school does, and families should ask rather than assume. Where they are sat, the on-screen examinations reward applying knowledge to unfamiliar stimulus material rather than recalling taught content, which is a distinct skill.
programmes.countryNote: Whether your child's school enters these changes the shape of MYP 5 considerably, so it is a question worth asking the coordinator in September. Where a school does not enter them, MYP 5 ends with school-assessed criteria and the Personal Project, and the preparation that matters is the transition into the Diploma or into IGCSE at a new school.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria. Knowing the letters for your child's subject is what turns a report card into something actionable, so each note names them.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where capable students stall, because it asks for a general rule and a justification rather than correct answers. Students who find the pattern and never state the general form lose most of the strand.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is the consistent loss: processing data properly, evaluating the method and explaining anomalies. Criterion D is often rushed at the end and is worth the same as the others.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Students who write fluently often score well on C and D and poorly on A, because analysing means explaining how a text creates its effect rather than describing what happens in it. That distinction is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, assessed within phases rather than year groups. Speaking is the strand students most fear and most under-prepare, and the gap is usually fluency under timing rather than vocabulary. Arabic, French and Spanish are the common requests in this corridor.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is the one that separates grades: it asks for evaluation of sources and arguments, and a student who summarises evidence without weighing it caps out regardless of how much they know.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The process journal carries most of the marks, so a student who builds something impressive without recording iterations, tests and decisions scores below a student with a modest solution and a full record.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. As in design, documented process is assessed alongside the work itself. Students lose marks by treating the developmental workbook as an afterthought rather than as the main assessed artefact.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Written criteria carry real weight, which surprises families who assume the subject is assessed on sporting ability alone.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: The MYP assesses interdisciplinary learning, which asks students to bring two subject groups together on one task. Students accustomed to working inside one subject find this disorienting, and the marks go to explaining the connection rather than to covering both syllabuses.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills are taught explicitly and appear in criterion descriptors across subject groups. Self-management is the one that most often explains a report card full of 4s, and it is not a content problem at all.

subjects.name: Service as action
subjects.description: Students are expected to engage in service linked to their learning and to record reflection on it. It is not graded as a subject but it appears in reporting, and schools differ in how much documentation they require, so it is worth asking what your child's school expects.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. The process record decides the mark more than the product does. A tutor may question the goal, teach research and reflection technique and give written feedback on the student's own work, and may not produce any part of it.

sections.heading: What Middle Years support costs, and what the money is for
paragraphs: Dubai market rates are the same whatever the programme, so the figures a parent will be quoted for Middle Years work come from the same published bands as everything else. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300 per hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate's Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Those are market figures read in October 2026.

What changes at Middle Years level is the quantity needed, and that is where the real saving sits. A single diagnosis session on a marked task costs one hour. A weekly session through MYP 4 at mid-market rates across a thirty-six week year is roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800. Both are modest against the Diploma pattern of two or three sessions a week in the spring of Diploma 2 at specialist rates of AED 300 to 450.

The reason the earlier spending works harder is that it buys habits rather than content. Showing process, answering the criterion as written, documenting decisions, and structuring a written response are the skills every Diploma Internal Assessment later assumes. A student who arrives in Diploma 1 with them needs a weekly session; a student who arrives without them needs a block in every subject.

Bestimate's monthly estimates make the comparison concrete: AED 240 to 600 a month for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Middle Years work sits in the middle band and exam-year Diploma work in the top one. Spending in the middle band for two years is cheaper than spending in the top band for one, and it produces a better result.

sections.heading: Criteria A to D, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a parent can learn about the Middle Years Programme is that every subject group assesses four criteria, each marked out of eight against published descriptors, and the 1 to 7 grade on the report is derived from those totals. The criteria are not the same across subjects. Criterion B means investigating patterns in mathematics and organizing in language and literature, which are entirely different demands.

Once you know the letters for your child's subject, a report card becomes readable. A student with a 6 on criterion A and a 3 on criterion C in the sciences does not have a science problem; they have a data processing and evaluation problem. A student with strong C and D and weak A in language and literature writes well and does not analyse. Those are different interventions, and neither is addressed by revising the unit content.

This is also the test to apply to any Middle Years tutor before paying them. Ask them to name the four criteria in the subject group your child needs. Someone who teaches the programme answers immediately. Someone who teaches the subject generally will talk about topics, which tells you they will prepare your child for an assessment that does not exist in this programme.

The table below sets out the four criteria for each of the eight subject groups, which is information almost no competitor page in this market publishes. Taking it to a parent-teacher meeting with a marked task in hand changes the conversation from a general one about effort into a specific one about a strand descriptor and what it asks for.

sections.heading: Why a 4 is rarely a content problem
paragraphs: A Middle Years report card full of 4s is the most common reason an Al Furjan family contacts a tutor, and the most commonly misdiagnosed. A 4 in the MYP conversion is a respectable middling grade, and it is what a student receives when they demonstrate understanding without doing the specific thing the criterion descriptor asks for. The content is there. The evidence the criterion wants is not.

The pattern repeats across subject groups in recognisable forms. In mathematics, a student finds the pattern, gives the right answers, and never states a general rule or justifies it, which is most of criterion B. In the sciences, data is presented rather than processed and the evaluation section lists equipment complaints instead of analysing the method, which caps criterion C. In individuals and societies, evidence is summarised rather than weighed, which is criterion D.

None of those is fixed by covering the topic again, which is what a general tutor will do because it is what the student will ask for. They are fixed by reading one marked task against the strand descriptors, identifying the gap, and practising the specific behaviour the descriptor names. That is usually one diagnostic session and then a term of deliberate practice inside normal school work.

This is also why self-management belongs in this conversation. Approaches to learning skills are taught explicitly in the MYP and appear inside criterion descriptors, and self-management is the one that most often explains a flat report. A student submitting work that is complete but unplanned and unrecorded scores below their understanding in every process-assessed subject at once, which looks like a general ability problem and is not.
bullets: A 4 usually means understanding without criterion evidence
Mathematics criterion B needs a stated general rule and justification
Science criterion C needs processed data and real evaluation
Individuals and societies criterion D needs weighed evidence, not summary

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the process record that carries it
paragraphs: The Personal Project is completed in the final Middle Years year, supervised in school and externally moderated. It is the first substantial independent piece a student produces, and it is assessed on the process as much as the outcome: how the goal was set, what was researched, which decisions were taken and why, and how honestly the result was evaluated against the student's own stated criteria.

The failure mode is consistent. A student with an ambitious goal produces something impressive and keeps no record of how, then writes the report afterwards from memory. The result scores below a modest project with a full process journal, because the marks are available for the documented process and are not available retrospectively. Nobody can reconstruct six months of decisions in a fortnight, and markers can tell when it has been attempted.

That makes the highest-value session the earliest one, exactly as with the Diploma Internal Assessments this stage prepares students for. One hour spent asking whether the goal is achievable, what will be recorded, and how success will be judged protects more marks than five hours spent on the report. Al Furjan families who ask for help in the final term are usually asking too late for the money to work hard.

The boundary here is the same one that applies throughout the IB and we state it at the first session. A tutor may read the criteria with the student, question the goal, teach research and reflection technique, show how a documented process looks, and give written feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not produce any part of the project or the report, or outline it for the student to fill in.
bullets: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting
The process record cannot be reconstructed after the fact
One early hour on goal feasibility beats five late hours on the report
A tutor questions and teaches; the student produces everything

sections.heading: Which subject groups actually repay paid support
paragraphs: Not every Middle Years subject is worth paying a tutor for, and saying so is more useful than listing all eight as options. Mathematics and the sciences repay support most reliably, because their criteria are explicit, their gaps are diagnosable from a marked task, and the habits built there carry directly into Diploma Internal Assessments. These are also where an unaddressed weakness closes Higher Level doors two years later.

Language and literature repays support where the issue is criterion A, analysing. A student who writes fluently and describes rather than analyses has a specific, teachable gap worth a short block of sessions. Language acquisition repays support mainly for speaking, where the barrier is fluency under timing rather than vocabulary, and where practice with a patient specialist is genuinely hard to arrange otherwise.

Individuals and societies is worth supporting for criterion D, thinking critically, which is the strand separating grades and the one least often taught explicitly. Design and arts are different: their marks sit largely in documented process, so what the student usually needs is a habit and a template rather than a term of teaching. Two or three sessions on process journalling often does the whole job.

Physical and health education rarely needs paid support, though its written criteria surprise families who assume the subject is assessed on performance alone. Interdisciplinary units and service as action are generally school-managed and not sensible tutoring purchases. A provider willing to tell you which of the eight not to buy is giving you more information than one offering all eight equally.
bullets: Mathematics and sciences repay support most reliably
Language and literature: a short block on criterion A analysing

sections.heading: Where Al Furjan families overspend in the Middle Years
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is paying a subject rate for homework supervision. A Middle Years student who works steadily through set tasks with a tutor beside them is being invigilated at AED 200 an hour. If the household needs someone to make sure the work happens, that is a different and far cheaper service, and conflating the two is how a monthly invoice grows without a single criterion score moving.

The second is session length chosen for the invoice. Ninety-minute sessions feel substantial and are wrong for a twelve-year-old, who concentrates hard for forty-five minutes and then performs. Two forty-five minute sessions at the same weekly cost retain more and allow set work to be checked between them. Families buy the long session because it looks like better value per booking, which it is not.

The third is buying all four or five academic subjects at once because the report card was flat across them. A flat report is more often a self-management or process problem than four separate subject problems, and buying four tutors treats the symptom four times. One diagnosis session on two marked tasks from different subjects usually reveals the common cause.

The fourth is the travel premium, which applies here as everywhere in this corridor. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online reflect the drive into the villa districts rather than any difference in teaching. For Middle Years students above about MYP 2 there is no pedagogical case for physical presence that outweighs having a wider choice of subject-group specialist.
bullets: Subject rates paid for homework supervision rather than teaching
Ninety-minute sessions bought for a child who concentrates for forty-five
Four tutors hired for what is usually one self-management problem
A travel premium that narrows rather than widens the choice of specialist

sections.heading: What MYP 5 leads into, and why that changes the spend
paragraphs: The end of the Middle Years Programme has two possible shapes and families should know which applies before planning MYP 5. Some schools enter students for the optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate; others end MYP 5 with school-assessed criteria and the Personal Project alone. The coordinator can confirm which, and the answer changes what the final year's support should target.

Where eAssessments are sat, the on-screen examinations reward applying knowledge to unfamiliar stimulus material rather than reproducing taught content. That is a distinct skill and it is the one to practise, which means working with unseen material under timing rather than reviewing units. Students who are strong in school assessments and weak on unfamiliar stimulus are common and the gap is trainable.

Where they are not sat, the useful work in MYP 5 is the transition ahead. For students continuing into the Diploma, that means the habits the Internal Assessments will assume: stating a method, processing data, documenting a process, evaluating honestly. For students moving to IGCSE at another school, which several families in this corridor do at 16, it means exam technique and the mark-scheme conventions the MYP never taught.

That second case is worth naming because it is specific to this part of Dubai. Full IB Diploma provision in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor is thinner than further north, so Al Furjan families frequently change schools after MYP 5, and some change curriculum as well. Four to six sessions over the summer on the conventions of the new system removes most of the first-term shock.
bullets: Ask the coordinator whether the school enters MYP 5 eAssessments
On-screen examinations reward applying knowledge to unseen stimulus
Without eAssessments, MYP 5 support should target the transition ahead
Families moving to IGCSE at 16 need mark-scheme conventions taught

sections.heading: What a Middle Years tutor will not do
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is assessed almost entirely on work produced in school, which puts the boundary on help at the centre of the arrangement rather than at its edge. An IB Gram tutor teaches technique, reads criteria with the student, questions a plan or a goal, demonstrates method, gives written feedback on the student's own work, and records what was covered. That is the territory, and in this programme most of the available marks sit inside it.

What a tutor will not do is produce work for submission. No written tasks, no Personal Project content, no process journal entries, no completed investigations, and no outlines for a student to fill in. At least one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments at a fixed price; submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student rather than on the seller.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, task banks or assessment criteria documents as downloads. Criteria are discussed and explained, and sessions work from the task sheets and marked work the school has issued. Reproducing published IB material is a copyright matter and there is no reason to take it when the school's own documents are the better basis anyway.

Two further limits worth stating. We do not predict or guarantee grades, including criterion scores, and any provider doing so is selling confidence. And we do not claim approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds none of them. We explain what those bodies do, which is a different and more useful thing.

process.title: Send a marked task, not a report card
process.description: The report tells us a score; the marked task tells us which criterion strand was missed. Send one or two marked pieces, the subject group, the MYP year, and the earliest time your child is at the desk after the Al Furjan bus. Middle Years students here are usually home earlier than their Diploma siblings.

process.title: We match by subject group and name the tutor
process.description: You are told who will teach and whether they work to the four criteria in that subject group. Ask them to name the criteria; it takes ten seconds and it is the clearest possible test. If we cannot match the subject group we say so rather than offering a general subject tutor.

process.title: Free diagnosis session on the marked work
process.description: Forty to sixty minutes reading the task against the strand descriptors, ending with a specific statement of which criterion is costing marks and why. No payment is taken and there is no obligation. Many Al Furjan families use exactly this session and nothing else, then talk to the school.

process.title: Decide whether a term is needed at all
process.description: Sometimes the answer is a weekly session for a term. Sometimes it is two sessions on a process-journal habit, or a conversation with the subject teacher. We will tell you which, including when the answer is that paid tutoring is not the right purchase for the problem we found.

process.title: Short sessions matched to attention, not to the invoice
process.description: For MYP 1 to 3, forty-five minutes twice a week retains more than ninety minutes once, at the same weekly cost. For MYP 4 and 5, sixty minutes weekly on one subject group. Local arrival times make a 16:30 start practical for most of this community.

process.title: Put the Personal Project session at the start
process.description: If MYP 5 is ahead, the goal and process conversation belongs before work begins, not when the report is due. One hour on whether the goal is achievable and documentable protects marks that cannot be recovered afterwards from memory.

whyPoints.title: Criteria read, not topics covered
whyPoints.description: Every MYP subject assesses four criteria out of eight against published descriptors. We work from a marked task and the strand it missed, because a report card full of 4s is usually understanding without criterion evidence rather than a content gap.

whyPoints.title: The cheapest stage, spent deliberately
whyPoints.description: A single diagnosis session costs one hour. A weekly session through MYP 4 costs a fraction of a Diploma 2 intensive at specialist rates, and it buys habits the Diploma will assume rather than exam technique after the internal marks are already submitted.

whyPoints.title: Honest about which subjects to skip
whyPoints.description: Mathematics and the sciences repay support reliably. Design and arts usually need a process habit rather than a term of teaching, and physical and health education rarely needs paid support at all. A provider offering all eight equally is not advising you.

whyPoints.title: Sessions sized for the student
whyPoints.description: Forty-five minutes twice a week for younger Middle Years students, sixty minutes weekly for MYP 4 and 5. Ninety-minute sessions are bought because they look substantial and are wrong for a twelve-year-old, who performs rather than works for the last half hour.

whyPoints.title: Slots that fit the early arrival
whyPoints.description: Middle Years students in Al Furjan are home between 15:20 and 16:10, earlier than Diploma siblings, so 16:30 and 17:00 sessions are genuinely available. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time and a missed one moves to the next evening.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary from the first session
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach and give written feedback on the student's own work. They do not produce tasks, project content or journal entries. Where completed internal assessments are sold in this market, having that in writing protects the student.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report is all 4s. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: Usually that they understand the material and are not producing the evidence the criterion descriptor asks for. Every MYP subject assesses four criteria, each out of eight against published descriptors, and the 1 to 7 grade comes from those totals. A 4 is what a capable student receives when, for example, they find a mathematical pattern and never state a general rule, or present science data without processing it. That is a criteria problem, and revising the unit content will not move it.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria in MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, and D applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each marked out of eight. Criterion B is where capable students stall, because it asks for a general rule and a justification rather than correct answers; a student who spots the pattern and stops there loses most of the strand. Criterion C rewards notation and clear presentation, which students treat as presentation rather than as assessed mathematical communication.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion costs science students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Criterion C, processing and evaluating. It asks for data processed properly, a method evaluated critically, and anomalies explained rather than noted. What students submit instead is raw data presented tidily and an evaluation section listing complaints about equipment. Criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science, is the other reliable loss, usually because it is written in the last twenty minutes despite being worth the same eight marks as the other three strands.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for an MYP tutor in Al Furjan when there are no external exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for less money than later. The absence of an external exam is exactly why the problem goes undiagnosed: there is no result to react to, only a number out of eight against a strand name. A single diagnosis session on a marked task, at published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 an hour, will tell you whether the issue is content, criteria or self-management. That is a cheaper and better-targeted purchase than a term of general support.

faqs.question: How much does a full year of MYP tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At the published mid-market online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, one weekly session on one subject group across a thirty-six week year is roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800. Bestimate's monthly estimates put mid-market provision at AED 600 to 1,200 a month. For comparison, a Diploma 2 spring intensive of twenty hours at specialist rates of AED 300 to 450 costs AED 6,000 to 9,000 and cannot reach internal marks already submitted. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: What is the Personal Project assessed on?
faqs.answer: Planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process record carrying more weight than most students expect. It is completed in the final Middle Years year, supervised in school and externally moderated. The usual failure is an ambitious product with no documented process, written up afterwards from memory, which scores below a modest project with a full journal. Six months of decisions cannot be reconstructed in a fortnight, and markers recognise the attempt when it is made.

faqs.question: When should Personal Project help be arranged?
faqs.answer: Before the goal is fixed, not when the report is due. One hour spent asking whether the goal is achievable, what will be recorded and how success will be judged protects marks that are unavailable retrospectively. Families in this corridor typically ask in the final term, when the money works far less hard. A tutor may question the goal, teach research and reflection technique and give written feedback on the student's own work, and may not produce any part of the project.

faqs.question: Which MYP subjects are not worth hiring a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Physical and health education rarely needs paid support, though families are often surprised that it carries written criteria rather than being assessed on performance alone. Service as action and interdisciplinary units are generally school-managed and not sensible purchases. Design and arts usually need two or three sessions on process journalling rather than a term of teaching, because their marks sit in documented development. Mathematics and the sciences are where support repays most reliably.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in class and badly on the criteria?
faqs.answer: Because class performance and criterion evidence are different things. A student can answer every question a teacher asks and still submit written work that never does what the descriptor names: stating a general rule, weighing evidence rather than summarising it, evaluating a method rather than listing equipment problems. Approaches to learning skills matter here too, particularly self-management, which appears inside criterion descriptors. Work that is complete but unplanned and unrecorded scores below the student's understanding in every process-assessed subject at once.

faqs.question: Does my child's school enter MYP 5 students for eAssessments?
faqs.answer: Ask the coordinator, because schools differ and it changes the shape of the final year. Where the optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the IB MYP Certificate are sat, the examinations reward applying knowledge to unfamiliar stimulus material rather than reproducing taught content, so the useful preparation is unseen material under timing. Where they are not sat, MYP 5 ends with school-assessed criteria and the Personal Project, and support should target the transition into the Diploma or into IGCSE instead.

faqs.question: What time do MYP sessions usually run for families in the villa districts?
faqs.answer: 16:30 or 17:00 for most. Middle Years students in Al Furjan are home earlier than their Diploma siblings, with buses arriving between 15:20 and 16:10 depending on the district and the school, and fewer late commitments. Children on Dubai Investments Park or Green Community routes can start at 15:50, which suits forty-five minute sessions before dinner. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and a session missed to a late bus moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

faqs.question: Should I hire four tutors if the whole report card is flat?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. A report that is uniformly middling across subjects is more often one self-management or process problem appearing four times than four separate subject problems. Buying four tutors treats the symptom repeatedly at four times the cost. One diagnosis session on two marked tasks from different subjects usually identifies the common cause, which is frequently planning, recording process, or not reading the task instruction properly before starting.

faqs.question: How does MYP work prepare a student for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Directly, which is the strongest cost argument for supporting it. The habits criterion-based assessment builds, stating a method, processing data, documenting a process and evaluating honestly, are exactly what every Diploma Internal Assessment later assumes. A student arriving in Diploma 1 with them needs one weekly session; a student arriving without them needs a block in every subject at exactly the point when every family in Dubai is competing for the same specialists in the same evening slots.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of an MYP task if my child has run out of time?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may read the criteria with the student, question a plan, demonstrate method, teach technique and give written feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not produce written tasks, project content, process journal entries or completed investigations, and may not outline a piece for the student to fill in. That boundary is stated at the first session and feedback is given in writing, so that a school asking what support was received gets a clear and defensible answer.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 to IGCSE at a new school. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Mark-scheme conventions, mostly, which the MYP never teaches because it does not use them. Showing method for method marks, answering a command term precisely, writing to a time limit, and the specific tabulating and graphing conventions of science papers are all new. Four to six sessions over the summer covers most of it. This is a common move in the Al Furjan corridor, because full IB Diploma provision nearby is thinner than further north, so families change school and sometimes curriculum at 16.

faqs.question: Is a long weekly session better for a Year 8 student than two short ones?
faqs.answer: No, and the reverse is usually true at that age. A twelve or thirteen year old concentrates hard for about forty-five minutes and then performs attention rather than using it, so the last half hour of a ninety-minute session produces little. Two forty-five minute sessions at the same weekly cost retain more and allow work set in one to be checked in the next. Parents buy the long session because it looks like better value per booking, which it is not.

intro.heading: The busiest child in the house is the one in the middle
paragraphs: Middle-school students in Dubai have the fullest days in the family. They finish later than their primary-aged siblings, they are expected at more after-school commitments than a sixth-former whose timetable has free periods, and in a neighbourhood like Al Garhoud they are travelling out of the area each morning — across the Creek to Dubai Festival City, down to Oud Metha, or east towards Al Qusais. The result is that a parent looking for MYP support is not short of willing tutors. They are short of hours.

The Middle Years Programme adds its own load on top of lesson time. Eight subject groups, all assessed. Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 against published descriptors, giving 32 marks that the school converts to a 1-7 grade. Approaches to Learning skills taught across subjects rather than in one. Service as Action expected throughout. At least one interdisciplinary unit a year with its own separate criteria. And in MYP 5, the Personal Project running quietly in the background for most of the year. None of that is optional and all of it generates work.

What that means in practice is that the honest tutoring question for a Garhoud MYP family is not which subject needs help, but which single hour in the week is genuinely free and what it should be spent on. A family who books two sessions into a week with one available evening loses one of them within a month. A family who identifies the free hour and uses it on the skill that is costing marks across several subjects — organisation, written explanation, investigation design — frequently finds that two subjects improve from one session.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We say that in the first part of every UAE page rather than the footer, because the format decides the scheduling and the scheduling is what this page is about. A visiting tutor needs a fixed arrival time on roads where arrival time is not fixed; an online slot can sit at 5:40pm on a Tuesday, move to Thursday when a fixture appears, and shift to early afternoon through Ramadan when Dubai schools shorten the day.

Below there is a table pairing MYP year groups with what their day actually contains and where a session fits. There is an Approaches to Learning table, because those five skill clusters are where most MYP marks are quietly lost and almost nobody teaches them directly. There is the decision Dubai families face at 14 — stay in the MYP or move to IGCSE — set out honestly rather than sold. There are the dirham market rates with sources. And there is a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with MYP coursework, which matters in a search result containing people who sell finished work.
