dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-garhoud.programmesIntro: The MYP sits between two very different experiences, and a Garhoud family's tutoring needs change sharply depending on which end of it their child is at. MYP 1 is a transition problem; MYP 5 is a decision problem.

programmes.name: MYP 1 and 2, the transition years
programmes.description: The first contact with criterion assessment, subject specialists instead of one class teacher, and homework set by eight different people with no coordination between them. Content is rarely the issue. Organisation, note-taking and writing to a command term are, and all three are teachable in a term.
programmes.countryNote: Garhoud families moving a child from a primary in Oud Metha or Festival City into an MYP secondary often see a grade drop in the first reporting cycle that frightens them unnecessarily. It is usually the assessment system rather than the child, and the fix is criterion literacy rather than extra content.

programmes.name: MYP 3 and 4, the content years
programmes.description: Subject content deepens, the Extended route appears in Mathematics in many schools, and the first genuinely demanding investigations and written tasks arrive. This is where a gap opened in MYP 1 becomes expensive, and where most families in this area first look for help.
programmes.countryNote: It is also when Dubai families decide whether to stay in the MYP or move to a school running IGCSE at 16. The decision is easier with evidence, and the best evidence is criterion scores in Mathematics and the sciences rather than an overall grade.

programmes.name: MYP 5, the year with a project in it
programmes.description: The Personal Project runs across most of the year alongside normal subject assessment, and some schools enter students for the optional eAssessment leading to the IB MYP Certificate. The combination makes this the heaviest MYP year by a clear margin.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma subject choices are confirmed at the end of this year, and the Mathematics route decision — Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation — is the one with the longest consequences. Criterion B investigation marks are the most useful early signal of which route suits a student.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: All eight MYP subject groups are assessed, which surprises families who expect the core subjects to carry the weight. Below is each group with what it actually demands of a middle-school week.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Investigating patterns and applying mathematics to real contexts are the two criteria that separate students, and both require written work rather than calculation. Weekly homework load is the heaviest of the eight groups, and the Extended route decision in MYP 4 shapes Diploma options two years later.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Investigation design and data processing carry criteria of their own, so a student can know the content and still score poorly. The write-up is the assessment. A session spent on method, controlled variables and evaluation language moves marks faster than revising the topic again.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of how a writer achieves an effect, organised writing, and accurate language use. Students describe rather than analyse, which is a structural habit and responds quickly to a fixed paragraph frame built on one quotation and one technique.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Students sit in a phase rather than a year group, assessed across listening, reading, speaking and writing. Families often discover late that their child's phase is too low to reach Diploma language requirements. Short frequent sessions work far better than one long one.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content assessed partly through source investigation and critical thinking. Thinking critically is where marks vanish, because students summarise a source instead of weighing its origin, purpose and limitations.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The design cycle folder is the assessment, not the finished object, which is why Design is so often the lowest grade on an MYP report. Writing specifications that can actually be tested, then testing against them, is the highest-return intervention available in the subject.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: The process journal outweighs the finished piece. Support is about documenting intention and revision in enough detail and writing the reflective responses that the final criterion rewards, neither of which most students are shown how to do.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Includes planning and reflection components, not only performance. Marks are lost on training plans with no measurable targets and on reflections that describe rather than evaluate. A few sessions on goal-setting and data recording usually resolve a grade a family assumed was about fitness.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and Service as Action
subjects.description: At least one interdisciplinary unit a year, assessed against its own separate criteria, plus a Service as Action expectation running throughout. Both are rarely revised for because they sit outside the normal subject rhythm, and both appear on reports.

sections.heading: What a middle-school day actually leaves behind
paragraphs: Primary children finish early and arrive home with energy. Sixth-formers finish late but have free periods and some control over their time. Middle-school students have neither, and that is why scheduling tutoring for them is harder than for either group. In Dubai the secondary day typically runs to between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, co-curricular commitments two or three afternoons a week push that to 4:15pm or 4:30pm, and the journey back into Al Garhoud from any of the usual school destinations adds twenty to forty minutes at that hour.

Add food. A twelve-year-old who walks in at 4:20pm and is put in front of a tutor at 4:30pm produces perhaps twenty usable minutes, and the parent pays for sixty. The same child at 5:15pm, having eaten and changed, produces a full session. Families routinely buy the first version and then conclude that their child does not respond to tutoring, when what happened is that they bought the wrong hour.

The homework load is the other half of the arithmetic. Eight subject groups means homework set by eight teachers who do not coordinate, and in most Dubai MYP schools it arrives unevenly: two heavy nights and three light ones, with the heavy nights usually following the days when Mathematics and a science fall together. A tutoring session placed on a heavy night is competing with the homework rather than helping it.

sections.heading: Approaches to Learning: the five skill clusters nobody teaches directly
paragraphs: The MYP expects students to develop Approaches to Learning skills across five clusters — communication, social, self-management, research and thinking — and expects subject teachers to build them into units. In practice they are assessed implicitly through subject criteria and taught briefly, which means a student who is weak in one of them loses marks in several subjects simultaneously without anybody identifying the common cause.

This is the most useful diagnostic frame a parent can have. A child losing marks in Sciences Criterion C, Mathematics Criterion C and Language and Literature Criterion B is not weak in three subjects. They are weak at organising written material, which is one self-management and communication problem showing up three times. Teaching that once, on tasks from all three subjects, is both cheaper and more effective than three separate subject interventions.

The clusters that cause the most visible damage in Dubai MYP classrooms are self-management and research. Self-management shows up as long tasks started the night before, process journals with three entries, and homework handed in incomplete despite the content being understood. Research shows up as sources that are summarised rather than evaluated, bibliographies assembled at the end, and investigations designed after the data has been collected.

The table names what each cluster looks like when it is missing and what teaching it actually involves, so a parent can recognise the pattern on their own child's report before paying anybody. Take it to the parent-teacher meeting and ask which cluster the subject teachers would name; the answers usually converge, and when they do you have found the single thing worth buying.

sections.heading: The fork at 14: staying in the MYP or moving to IGCSE
paragraphs: Dubai is one of the few places where this is a live decision for a large number of families, because both routes are widely available and often within a few kilometres of each other. The UK curriculum accounts for 37 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 7 per cent on IB programmes, so for most families the IGCSE route is the default and the MYP is the deliberate choice. A Garhoud family comparing a Festival City IB school with a British-curriculum school in Oud Metha is making a real comparison, not a theoretical one.

The arguments are genuine on both sides and worth separating from school marketing. Staying in the MYP keeps a student inside one continuum, maintains breadth across eight subject groups including Design and the Arts, and builds investigation and extended-writing skills early. The cost is that the first external examination a student meets is in the Diploma, two years later, so examination technique has to be taught deliberately rather than absorbed. Moving to IGCSE produces a set of externally examined, internationally portable grades at 16 and narrows the subject count, at the cost of breadth and of the continuum.

The evidence that should decide it is the student's own criterion profile rather than a preference about systems. A student with strong Criterion A and weak Criterion B across subjects — good recall, weak investigation — often does better with the structure of IGCSE papers. A student with the reverse profile usually thrives in the MYP and struggles with the pace of IGCSE content coverage. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown rather than the grades before deciding.

Whatever the decision, it has consequences for post-16 and for equivalency. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB route there is no published points figure in that source, so confirm it on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on a tutoring website.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report when you have never seen one
paragraphs: The first MYP report a parent receives is usually incomprehensible, and that is not their fault. It contains letters, numbers out of 8, a converted grade out of 7, and no percentages, and a family arriving from a British or Indian system has no reference point for any of it. Several Garhoud families have told us they spent a term worried about a grade that turned out to be entirely respectable.

The structure is this. Each subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each marked out of 8 against published descriptors. The four add to 32, and the school converts that total into a 1-7 grade using IB grade boundaries. The criteria themselves differ by subject group, which is the detail that catches everybody: Criterion C is communicating in Mathematics, processing and evaluating in Sciences, producing text in Language and Literature, and creating the solution in Design. Reading a report without that mapping is guesswork.

Descriptors are written in two-mark bands, which is why progress happens in jumps rather than smoothly. A student sitting at 3 or 4 is being told they can do the thing in simple situations or with support. Reaching 5 or 6 almost always requires one specific addition — a justification, an evaluation, a generalisation — rather than more of the same. That is the sentence worth taking to a parent-teacher meeting: which single addition would move this criterion into the next band.

Ask for the task sheets as well as the report. Schools publish task-specific clarifications of the descriptors on each task, and those clarifications are what the teacher actually marks against. Any tutoring session that begins without the task sheet is working from a generic version of the assessment rather than the real one.

sections.heading: Service as Action, interdisciplinary units and the workload nobody counts
paragraphs: Families budgeting time for the MYP count eight subjects and stop. The programme contains at least two further commitments that generate real work and appear on reports, and leaving them out of the mental arithmetic is why middle-school weeks feel heavier than they look on paper.

Service as Action runs through all five years. It is not a box-ticking exercise in most Dubai schools: students are expected to identify a need, act on it, and reflect on what happened, with the reflection being the part that is assessed. Students who treat it as attendance at an activity produce thin reflections and lose marks that have nothing to do with their academic ability. The teachable part is the reflection structure — what was the need, what did I do, what changed, what would I do differently — and it takes one session, not a term.

Interdisciplinary units are the second. At least once a year two subjects are brought together and the student is assessed against separate interdisciplinary criteria on their ability to synthesise. These units are rarely revised for because they sit outside the normal subject rhythm and because parents have never heard of them. Knowing the interdisciplinary criteria before the task is set is most of the work, and asking the school when the unit falls is a two-minute email that prevents a surprise grade.

Then, in MYP 5, the Personal Project sits on top of everything else for most of the year. It is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, all evidenced through a process journal kept over months. A thin journal scores badly however good the product is, which means the workload is spread rather than concentrated and has to be scheduled from the start of the year rather than discovered in the spring.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in old Dubai
paragraphs: Middle-school support sits in the middle of the Dubai market in every sense, and the useful way to think about it is what the travel premium would buy if you spent it on teaching quality instead. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's rate work, with independent home tutors quoted as high as AED 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. The difference between those two bands is largely a car, and for a fifty-minute MYP session it is a significant share of the price.

Below that, Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For homework supervision in MYP 1 or 2 that band can be perfectly reasonable, because what is being bought is an adult sitting alongside a twelve-year-old keeping them on task. For criterion work it generally is not, since marking against MYP descriptors is a trained skill. Above the mid band, specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the premium end — a band rarely necessary for middle-school work.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget session, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Advertised packages show about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All figures read in October 2026 and attributed to their publisher.

None of those are IB Gram's prices. We quote after a free trial lesson, one per subject before any payment, against a written plan, because a six-week skills block for an MYP 2 student and a year of Personal Project support are not the same purchase and should not share a rate card.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with MYP coursework
paragraphs: Some of the pages competing for searches like this one sell completed coursework. The relevant fact for an MYP family is not that it is available but that the risk is one-sided: the student carries it, and the habit formed in MYP 4 is the habit that will be applied to an Internal Assessment and an Extended Essay two years later under a regime that checks carefully.

The line is drawn by whose thinking appears in the submitted work. A tutor may teach a skill, explain a concept, model a worked example on a different question, read the criteria with the student, mark a completed draft against descriptors, and ask the questions that make a student notice a gap. A tutor may teach referencing and show how to acknowledge a source. A tutor may hold weekly accountability so a process journal stays current rather than being written in one evening.

A tutor may not write any part of a submission, draft a Personal Project report, dictate sentences for transcription, make or assemble a product, invent data for an investigation, or edit a piece until the final text is theirs rather than the student's. The working test is whether the student can explain, without prompting, why each sentence and each decision is in the work. If they cannot, it should not be there.

Families sometimes worry this makes the help thinner. It makes it more durable. A twelve-year-old taught to structure an evaluation can do it in every subject for the next six years. A twelve-year-old handed an evaluation has bought one mark and learned nothing transferable, and has begun a pattern that becomes genuinely dangerous in the Diploma.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects inside a middle-school week
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are taught in every Dubai private school regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance states its requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. In a middle-school timetable these occupy periods that a parent counting eight MYP subject groups has not accounted for, and they appear on the report alongside criterion grades.

The organisational detail is worth knowing because it explains your child's week. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Non-Arab students take Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met and KHDA advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Schools must ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a concrete thing to ask about at a parents' evening. Using different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so tutoring in them stays inside the prescribed curriculum rather than importing outside material.

For a Garhoud MYP family the practical overlap is Arabic, which may appear twice in a week — once as the mandatory provision and once as a Language Acquisition phase within the MYP. Those are different assessments with different expectations, and it is worth asking the school which one a weak grade belongs to before buying any support.

sections.heading: Why our lessons are online, and what that fixes for a middle-schooler
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are part of our India service. For a middle-school family the reasons are more practical than philosophical, and they follow from everything above.

Fixtures move. A middle-school student's Tuesday is a football match one week and free the next, and a visiting tutor's weekly slot cannot absorb that without someone losing money. An online slot moves to Thursday with a message. Arrival home varies by half an hour on these roads depending on which crossing is working, and a slot set from the optimistic arrival fails on the weeks when it is the pessimistic one. Through Ramadan, when Dubai schools shorten the day, the session can move to the early afternoon — the best academic hour a Dubai middle-schooler gets all year — which is nearly impossible to arrange with a visiting tutor whose own day is also compressed.

Supply is the second reason. Design, Arts and Language Acquisition are the MYP subject groups where specialist tutors are genuinely scarce, because few tutors have marked a design cycle folder or a process journal or taught to a specific Language Acquisition phase. Matching online means a Garhoud student is choosing from everyone available rather than from the people who will drive over the bridge at 5pm, and across eight subject groups that difference is decisive.

Where a tutor in the room is better — a child who will not settle on screen, a household with no quiet corner — the Dubai market provides it at the rates listed above and a family should use it. We would rather be clear about not being that provider than let a parent find out after paying.

process.title: Send the afternoon, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us which school, which MYP year, which afternoons carry fixtures, and what time your child genuinely walks through the door. For a middle-school student that information decides more about whether the arrangement works than the choice of tutor does.

process.title: Bring the report and one task sheet
process.description: The report gives criterion scores; the task sheet gives the clarified descriptors the teacher actually marked against. With both, a tutor can name the gap in the first session. With neither, the first session is spent reconstructing what the school already told you.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one per subject
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject before any payment, taken at the proposed time so you can see whether that hour works for a tired thirteen-year-old. Fifty minutes rather than eighty for most MYP students, because the attention budget is different.

process.title: Skill first, subject second
process.description: If the report shows the same criterion weak across several subjects, we will propose a skills block rather than a subject block, because one well-aimed hour that fixes written organisation improves three grades. We will say so even though it means selling fewer sessions.

process.title: Review at the next summative
process.description: The review point is the next marked task with its criterion score, not a number of weeks. If the criterion moved, we pick the next target. If it did not, we change the approach or the tutor and tell you which we think it was.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for the middle-school day
whyPoints.description: Fifty-minute sessions, set from arrival home rather than dismissal, moveable when a fixture appears. Middle-school students are the busiest people in a Dubai household and most tutoring arrangements for them fail on timing rather than on teaching.

whyPoints.title: Skills diagnosis, not subject guessing
whyPoints.description: The same weak criterion appearing in three subjects is one skill problem, not three subject problems. We read the report for that pattern first, because fixing it once is cheaper and more durable than three separate interventions.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-literate tutors
whyPoints.description: The tutors matched to MYP work have marked against MYP descriptors, which is a different skill from knowing the content. Ask any prospective tutor which subject groups and criteria they have assessed; the answer separates a specialist from a well-qualified generalist.

whyPoints.title: The fork at 14 answered honestly
whyPoints.description: We set out the MYP and IGCSE routes with the real trade-offs and tell families the decision should rest on their child's criterion profile. We have no interest in either answer, which is more than can be said for the schools marketing each one.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names its publisher and is dated October 2026, given hourly and monthly. We quote our own number after the free trial against a written plan, because an MYP 2 skills block and a year of MYP 5 project support are not the same purchase.

whyPoints.title: Honesty boundaries stated in advance
whyPoints.description: We teach, model, mark and hold accountability. We do not write reports, draft journals or make products, and the section above says precisely where the line sits. In a search result containing sellers of finished coursework, that boundary is the first thing worth checking.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start for a child schooling in Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: Assume arrival home between 3:45pm and 4:15pm and book 5pm. Secondary dismissal is later than primary, the Creek crossing is slow at that hour, and a middle-school student needs food and a change of clothes before anything useful happens. A 4:30pm booking in that situation typically produces twenty usable minutes out of fifty. If that afternoon carries a fixture, move the session to a different day entirely rather than pushing it to 6:30pm, which is too late for most thirteen-year-olds.

faqs.question: Should an MYP session be fifty minutes or eighty?
faqs.answer: Fifty, for almost all middle-school students. Attention after a full school day and a commute is a finite resource, and a session that ends while the child is still engaged leaves them willing to come back next week. Eighty-minute sessions make sense for MYP 5 students working on a Personal Project or for weekend work, where the task genuinely needs sustained time. For MYP 1 to 3, shorter and more frequent beats longer and rarer in almost every case we have seen.

faqs.question: The same criterion is weak in three subjects. Is that three problems?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly one. The MYP expects Approaches to Learning skills to develop across subjects, so a student weak in organising written material loses marks in Sciences, Mathematics and Language and Literature simultaneously. That is one communication and self-management problem showing up three times. Teaching it once, using the student's own tasks from all three subjects, is cheaper and more effective than three separate subject interventions. Ask for the criterion breakdown rather than the grades and the pattern is usually visible immediately.

faqs.question: What are Approaches to Learning skills and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: Five clusters the MYP expects students to develop across all subjects: communication, social, self-management, research and thinking. They are assessed implicitly through subject criteria rather than directly, so a gap in one shows up as several subject grades without anybody naming the common cause. The two that damage Dubai MYP students most are self-management, which looks like long tasks started the night before and thin process journals, and research, which looks like sources summarised instead of evaluated.

faqs.question: My child's first MYP report makes no sense. How do I read it?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each marked out of 8 against published descriptors, giving 32 marks that the school converts into a 1-7 grade. There are no percentages, and 24 out of 32 is not 75 per cent of anything. The criteria differ by subject: Criterion C is communicating in Mathematics, processing and evaluating in Sciences, producing text in Language and Literature and creating the solution in Design. Ask for the task sheets as well, since they carry the clarified descriptors the teacher actually marked against.

faqs.question: Should we keep our child in the MYP or move to a school doing IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Decide on the criterion profile rather than on the systems. A student with strong Criterion A and weak Criterion B — good recall, weak investigation — often does better with the structure of IGCSE papers. The reverse profile usually thrives in the MYP. Staying keeps breadth across eight groups and builds investigation skills early, at the cost of meeting no external examination until the Diploma. Moving produces externally certificated grades at 16 and narrows the subject count. Both routes reach either post-16 destination.

faqs.question: What is Service as Action and does it actually affect grades?
faqs.answer: It is an expectation running through all five MYP years that students identify a need, act on it and reflect on what happened. The reflection is the part that carries weight, which is why students who treat it as attendance at an activity lose marks unrelated to their academic ability. The reflection structure is teachable in one session: what was the need, what did I do, what changed, what would I do differently. Ask the school how it is recorded and when, because the recording is usually the part that slips.

faqs.question: Nobody told us about interdisciplinary units. What are they?
faqs.answer: At least once a year an MYP school runs a unit bringing two subjects together, assessed against separate interdisciplinary criteria on the student's ability to synthesise across them. They sit outside the normal subject rhythm, which is why they are rarely revised for and why most parents have never heard of them. Email the school and ask when the unit falls and which criteria apply. Knowing the criteria before the task is set is most of the preparation, and it prevents a surprise grade on a report.

faqs.question: Is Design really worth paying for?
faqs.answer: It is often the lowest grade on an MYP report, so yes, if the grade matters to you. The reason it is low is almost never ability: students treat the design cycle folder as paperwork and the finished object as the assessment, when the folder is what is marked. The highest-return intervention is teaching a student to write specifications that can actually be tested, and then to test against them and record the result. Two or three sessions usually change the pattern, because the fault is procedural rather than conceptual.

faqs.question: How much does Middle Years Programme tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: budget online generalists AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; qualified subject tutors online AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270; in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 budget and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range for a weekly session. Those are market rates; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Al Garhoud for a middle-school lesson?
faqs.answer: Not from us. Every UAE lesson is online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is part of our India service. For a middle-school family the online format solves the two real problems: fixtures that move week to week, and arrival times that vary by half an hour depending on the route. In-home tutoring is available in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, so a family who needs it can find it.

faqs.question: Is a university student at the budget rate enough for an MYP 1 child?
faqs.answer: For homework supervision, frequently yes. What is being bought at AED 33 to 65 an hour is an adult sitting alongside an eleven-year-old keeping them on task, and that is genuinely useful. What it does not buy is criterion literacy, because marking against MYP descriptors is a trained skill. If your child's problem is organisation and completion, the budget band is good value. If it is a criterion score that will not move, buy fewer hours from somebody who has marked MYP work.

faqs.question: How early should MYP 5 students start the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because the assessment rests on planning, applying skills and reflecting, all evidenced by a process journal kept over months. A journal started late cannot score well however good the product is. Goal and context settled before the winter break, making and skill-building through the second term, and the report written after the spring break with the journal already complete is a workable shape. Your school's internal deadlines override any general timeline, so get those dates from the coordinator in the first term.

faqs.question: Does my child take Arabic twice in an MYP week?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and families find this confusing. Arabic appears as the mandatory provision every Dubai private school must deliver, and separately as a Language Acquisition phase within the MYP, assessed against its own criteria. These are different assessments with different expectations and different language-of-instruction rules — KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language and prohibits combined classes. Ask the school which of the two a weak grade belongs to before buying any support, because the teaching needed differs.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project process journal?
faqs.answer: With the habit, yes; with the content, no. A tutor may hold weekly accountability so the journal stays current rather than being written in one evening, teach the student how to write a reflection that names a decision, its reason and its consequence, and read the assessment criteria with them. A tutor may not draft entries, write the report, or make the product. The test is whether the student can explain any entry without prompting. Most journals fail on consistency rather than quality, so the accountability is the valuable part.

faqs.question: What happens to the session when my child has a fixture that week?
faqs.answer: It moves to another day rather than being cancelled or pushed to 6:30pm. Middle-school co-curricular commitments vary week to week — a match one Tuesday and nothing the next — and that variability is precisely what a visiting tutor's fixed weekly slot cannot absorb. Because lessons are online, a message is enough to shift the session. Tell us at the start which afternoons are likely to carry fixtures so the default slot avoids them, and keep one evening deliberately empty as the week's shock absorber.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingHeading: Tell us when your child actually gets home
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-al-garhoud.closingBody: For a middle-school student that single piece of information matters more than the subject does. Send the school, the MYP year, the afternoons that carry fixtures and the real arrival time, along with the most recent report and one task sheet, and we will propose a fifty-minute slot and say whether the first block should target a subject or a skill. The first lesson is free, one per subject, before any payment, and best taken at the proposed time so you can judge the hour as well as the tutor. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.
